https://help.sap.com/docs/business-netwo.content: 主页SAP Business Network for Procurement…默认交易规则 SAP Business Network 采购商管理指南版本: 2602Chinese Simplified (简体中文) Content on this page is relevant for customers who have not yet migrated to the SAP Business Network on BTP experience. If you have already moved to SAP Business Network on BTP, you can access the relevant documentation here. 提供有关搜索的反馈  搜索范围 更多 目录 PDF 收藏夹 共享 默认交易规则 在此页面上 规则类别 允许规则与要求规则 SAP Business Network 默认交易规则控制供应商如何提交符合采购商内容要求的交易文档。 采购商必须确保文档遵守其流程和过程。通过发票文档，采购商和供应商必须确保文档具有税务合规性并符合国家/地区特定规则。如果文档不合规，采购商和供应商都可能花费大量成本和时间来处理异常情况。 在 SAP Business Network 上配置业务规则时，采购商可以减少异常并确保文档合规，方法是在将文档发送到采购商的后端系统之前识别问题。供应商可以在其客户收到文档之前处理和解决问题。 注意 SAP Business Network 将规则应用于使用本地语言 cXML 的文档。最初未以此格式创建的文档将首先转换为 cXML，然后应用规则。 如果文档遵守采购商规则，则会通过特定于采购商的集成方法将文档实时发送给采购商。然后，这些规则可应用于供应商在 SAP Business Network 门户上手动输入的交易以及自动集成到网络中的交易。 对于在 SAP Business Network 门户上输入的文档，创建文档时将应用交易规则。如果存在错误或不完整的信息，用户将无法进入下一阶段，即无法向采购商提交文档。 对于集成文档，这些规则将在接收并处理文档后应用。如果供应商调查文档状态，则网络会在 SAP Business Network 门户和 SAP Integration Suite 面向支出管理的托管网关和 SAP Business Network 上以通知形式发送相关错误消息。 为确保一致性，采购商的测试和生产 SAP Business Network 帐户中配置的交易规则必须相同。 采购商可在其 SAP Business Network 帐户中（“帐户设置” “管理概要” “默认交易规则”）“默认交易规则”页面上配置默认交易规则。但是，他们可为特定供应商和供应商组覆盖默认交易规则。 对于发票，采购商还可为发送发票的国家/地区覆盖发票规则。有关详细信息，请转到基于国家/地区的发票规则。 规则类别 注意 有关 SAP Business Network 供应链 的其他默认交易规则信息，请参阅SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide。 “默认交易规则”页面有按以下类别分组的规则： 付款批次传输规则 订购单规则 一揽子订购单规则 计划协议版本设置规则 Ariba Buyer 合同站点设置规则 附件规则 SAP Business Network 供应商的快速激活 订单确认和发货通知规则 服务工作单规则 发票规则 发票归档 税款发票的长期归档 销售订单规则 D-U-N-S 编号规则 工单信息 质量协作规则 允许规则与要求规则 通常，交易规则有两种类型： 允许规则 - 当选中这些规则时，供应商可选择是否输入每个规则设置的值。如果没有选中这些规则，则强制实施此规则行为。 要求规则 - 当选中这些规则时，采购商要求供应商在文档上提供某些信息。当未选中这些规则时，供应商可选择不填写这些信息。 其他规则 - 下面是不以“允许”或“要求”开头的其他规则，但是也按“要求”规则处理： 配置默认交易规则 付款批次传输规则 订购单规则 一揽子订购单规则 计划协议版本设置规则 Ariba Buyer 合同站点设置规则 附件规则 SAP Business Network 供应商的快速激活 订单确认和发货通知规则 服务工作单规则 发票规则 发票归档 税款发票的长期归档 销售订单规则 D-U-N-S 编号规则 工单信息 质量协作规则 管理默认交易规则 此页面有帮助吗？  是 否

https://help.sap.com/docs/business-netwo.title: Guided Integration for Trading Partners | SAP Help Portal
https://help.sap.com/docs/business-netwo.content: HomeSAP Business Network for Trading Par…Guided Integration for Trading Partn… Guided Integration for Trading PartnersVersion: 2602English Provide feedback on our search  Search Scope More Table of Contents PDF Favorite Share Guided Integration for Trading Partners On this page Prerequisites Restrictions Workflow Guided Integration for Trading Partners streamlines and expedites the tasks needed for you to integrate with your existing buyers for additional business processes. Before Guided Integration for Trading Partners was available, supplier integration was a high-touch process involving the SAP integration team. It could take weeks, or even months, for you and your buyer to be fully integrated to transact business smoothly. Buyers could set default transaction rules in SAP Business Network to define their business processes, but you had no equivalent tool, which made it difficult for you to determine which buyers to integrate with. Guided Integration for Trading Partners gives you this capability. You can use Guided Integration for Trading Partners to discover which of your existing buyers you can easily integrate with for additional business processes. After discovering buyers, you can use Guided Integration for Trading Partners to integrate your business processes quickly and independently, and as a result, you become enabled for additional types of commerce collaboration with your existing buyers. Prerequisites You need one of the following permissions to use Guided Integration for Trading Partners: Integration Management Full Access Integration Management Read-Only Access Restrictions You must have a SAP Business Network Enterprise Platinum account to use Guided Integration for Trading Partners. Workflow Follow these steps to find existing buyers to integrate with for additional business processes: Go to Guided Integration for Trading Partners. See Entering Guided Integration for Trading Partners. Complete the questionnaire to define your business processes. See Questionnaire for Guided Integration for Trading Partners. Use the compatibility dashboard to search for buyers. See View Your Compatibility with Your Trading Partners. Compare and reconcile your template for a document type with a prospective buyer’s template. See Compare and Reconcile Templates with Guided Integration for Trading Partners. Use SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network to map and transform your template. See Mapping and Transforming Template Created with Guided Integration for Trading Partners. https://help.sap.com/docs/sisgw/sap-arib.title: Using Test Central for Buyer Regression Testing | SAP Help Portal
https://help.sap.com/docs/sisgw/sap-arib.content: HomeSAP Integration Suite, Managed Gatew……Using Test Central for Buyer Regress… SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview GuideVersion: 2602English Provide feedback on our search  Search Scope More Table of Contents PDF Favorite Share Using Test Central for Buyer Regression Testing With the Test Central framework, buyers can automate end-to-end testing of use cases using previously generated documents or transactions, re-run the test cases, and generate a report on results. Using Test Central benefits buyers in: Reducing testing timelines and accelerating regression testing Evaluating the impact of upgrades using support packs, customizations, and XSLT mapping changes The test regression functionality available on the Test Central page helps you perform regression testing of business flows and/or transactions. You can create and run regression tests based on documents or transactions you have created manually. This helps validate the regression scenarios or baseline use cases after you do the following: Perform system upgrade Update mapping Customization Note Test Central is supported for the SAP Ariba Commerce Automation subprocess of SAP Business Network. For example, you update the mapping of a transaction. Now, you want to check the output of the transaction based on the new mapping. For this, you must first choose an existing regression test suite containing a test case, such as purchase order, that impacts the mapping. Then, you must re-run the test suite. The latest test run would mark up the mapping changes in the baseline and target XML files. Running regression testing To perform regression testing in Test Central, you must first create a test suite. You can determine a business flow and/or a transaction that you have run manually, as the base for testing. Then, you can do the following and perform the search operation: Select the originating document type of the base transaction Enter the transaction number (document number) of the base transaction This will list the test cases for all the subsequent transactions. Note Currently, Test Central supports the following originating cXML document types: OrderRequest (for purchase order) InvoiceDetailRequest For more information about managing regression test suites, see Managing Regression Test Suites in SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Configuration Guide. After creating the test cases for all the transactions, you can load them to create the test suite. For a test suite that doesd not contain any test cases with manual steps, you can see that the test suite runs by default and creates the follow-on documents in the order of the original, manual transactions. Starting SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network 2208 (Q3 2022) release, the buyers can also include manual steps in one or more test cases loaded to the test suite. These manual steps are added through of the advanced configuration of the test suite. This configuration enables the buyers to perform a manual activity, which is an essential part of running a test case, outside Test Central. Test Central holds the step until the buyer completes the manual activity. After you run a test suite, you can view the following details of the test cases in the test suite: The order in which the test cases are run Document type of each test case The after-mapping file of the manual transaction. You can view this information in the BaseLine XML column. The current status of the test case. You can view the status Scheduled, In Progress, Passed, Update, Failed, and Canceled. The document number (transaction number) of the test case Error log. Only the updated or failed test cases display the error log. For the failed test cases, you can view the detailed error log. For the updated test case you can view the difference between the baseline and the target XML files. For more information about managing regression test cases, see, Managing Regression Test Suites Knowing essential concepts about Test Central Knowing the following terms and basic concepts will help you in managing test suites and test cases: BaseLine XML (also known as Source XML) The after-mapping file of the transaction that you have created manually. You can click and download the baseline XML file to your local system. Target XML The after-mapping file of the transaction that is generated in Test Central. Status of test suites and test cases In Test Central, you can view the following status of the tests suites and/or test cases Scheduled Indicates the test case that will start next in the sequence. Passed Indicates the test case that has finished running successfully. Update Indicates the difference between the after-mapping files of the manually created transactions and the transactions created in Test Central. You can view the details in the logs. Failed Indicates failures in test cases. You can view the details in the test logs. In-progress Indicates the test case that is currently running. Cancelled Indicates the test suite and/or test case canceled manually. After a test case is canceled manually, all the follow-on documents are canceled automatically. Test Log You can view the Test Log field in the details view of a test case in a test suite. In the Test Log field, you can view the differences between the baseline and target XML files of the updated or failed test cases. The following is the sample test log for the updated and the failed test cases: For an updated test case: Expected text value '<expected_value (value_in_BaseLine_XML)>' but was '<value_in_Target XML>' at /<hierarchical_order_of_XML_tags_to_change_location>/(for example, /cXML[1]/Header[1]/To[1]/Correspondent[1]/Contact[1]/PostalAddress[1]/Street[1]/text()[1]) Removed element '<value_in_BaseLine_XML (for example, 'State')>' from /<herarchical_order_of_XML_tags_to_change_location>/ (for example, /cXML[1]/Request[1]/OrderRequest[1]/OrderRequestHeader[1]/ShipTo[1]/Address[1]/PostalAddress[1]/State[1]) Added element '<value_in_baseline_XML (for example, 'Phone')>' at /<hierarchical_order_of_XML_tags_to_change_location>/ (for example, /cXML[1]/Request[1]/OrderRequest[1]/OrderRequestHeader[1]/Contact[1]/Phone[2]) For a failed test case: Failed to send document to "<destination (for example, ADDON)>" with status code, "<status_code (for example, 400)>" and error message, "<error_message (for examle, Please enter a partner role Instance <transaction_number> of object type <transaction_name (for example, PurchaseOrder)> could not be changed)> ". Difference between baseline XML and target XML files Under the Test Log section of the view that displays the details of passed or updated test cases, you can view the section Difference. This section helps you compare the difference between baseline XML and target XML files. At the top right of this section, you can see the total number of removals and additions between baseline XML and target XML files. You can also download the baseline and the target XML files from this section. The baseline XML file displays alongside the target XML file. You can use the vertical scroll bar on the left to go through the XML files displayed. The removals are marked up in red in the baseline XML file. The additions are marked up in green in the target XML file. Note The Difference section is not displayed for failed, canceled, or scheduled test cases. Update the baseline XML file Under the Difference section in the details view of an updated or a passed test case, you can see the Update BaseLine button. You can use the Update BaseLine button to replace the current baseline XML file with the target XML file. You can do so after you compare the baseline and the target XML files and ensure the accuracy of the updates. After updating the baseline XML file, you can use this file for re-running tests in the future. For more information, see Replacing the Baseline XML File with the Target XML File for an Updated Test Case Enabling Test Central To enable Test Central with SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network in your test environment, you must do the following tasks in the order they are listed: Configure global settings for Test Central Configure general settings for SAP Business Network in Test Central Configure transaction-specific settings for SAP Business Network in Test Central For more information, see Configuring Test Central. General recommendations You must consider updating baseline XML in the following scenarios: Transaction Scenario ERP-initiated invoice You observe a mismatch in alphabet cases in the SupplierpartID. Payment Proposal You observe differences in the sequence of the tax details order, but the values are intact. Purchase Order with split accounting (the change operation) You observe differences in the sequence of accounting distribution segment IDs. For rejecting an order confirmation (at the header level), apply SAP Note 890812 To understand the end-to-end process flow for creating a regression test suite in Test Central, see Process Flow to Test Transactions For more information about configuring and managing Test Central for buyer regression testing, see Using Test Central for Buyer Regression Testing in the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network configuration guide. Was this page helpful?  Yes No

file://SBN/split/Buyer Value Prop - Test.content: Managed Gateway for Spend and Network – Test Central Supplier Integration SAP 2025 -- 1 of 10 -- 2 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Agenda • Overview of the Managed Gateway for Spend & Network • Test Central Overview • Data Flow through the Managed Gateway for Spend & Network • Integration Project Overview • Considerations for Using Test Central • Overall Process, Roles and Responsibility for setting up Test Central -- 2 of 10 -- 3 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Overview of the Managed Gateway for Spend & Network Managed Gateway for Spend & Network is the supplier integration engine for the SAP Business Network • Primary Goal: To simplify integration management across multiple relationships and significantly decrease the integration timeline • Secondary Goals: • Provide a growing list of industry and regional standards • Provide flexibility in the context of standardization via an extension framework • Provide self-testing capabilities using Test Central • Provide robust monitoring and transaction tracking Network Effect and Scale • Eliminate point-to-point integration • Eliminate linear resource scale • Reduce new relationship connection to days • 100% of relationships are integrated once initially connected • Increase user experience and satisfaction -- 3 of 10 -- 4 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Test Central Introduction Test Central empowers suppliers to independently validate their integration with the SAP Business Network—streamlining and accelerating project timelines. By enabling self-service testing, suppliers can confirm key aspects of their setup without direct involvement from buyers. Key Capabilities • Connectivity Validation Verify system-level connectivity with SAP’s Managed Gateway for Spend & Network to ensure a stable technical handshake. • Schema Compliance Confirm that transaction files are properly structured and conform to industry standards and SAP’s data specifications. • Document Choreography Document choreography allows suppliers to self-test against document flow leveraging buyer specific requirements. • Buyer-Specific Transaction Rules Ensure your transactions align with the unique business rules and configuration requirements of each buyer on the network. By leveraging these features, suppliers can perform thorough, realistic testing and confidently move forward in the integration process— without waiting on buyer-side interaction. -- 4 of 10 -- 5 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Data Flow through the Managed Gateway for Spend & Network -- 5 of 10 -- 6 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Data Flow through the Managed Gateway for Spend & Network -- 6 of 10 -- 7 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Integration Project Overview -- 7 of 10 -- 8 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Considerations for using Test Central • Test Central is enabled individually for each Buyer account • Suppliers can only access Test Central POs if they have a Trading Relationship with Buyer • Test Central Purchase Orders validate against Buyer’s SAP Business Network Configuration only, not a Buyer’s B&I or ERP configuration • Test Central Documents will have a “TC_” Prefix • Purchase Orders from Test Central are not copied into Buyer’s ERP • You will see “test data” in the SAP Business Network • Invoices will be rejected in Buyer’s ERP, or treated as non-PO invoices (if supported) -- 8 of 10 -- 9 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Overall Process, Roles and Responsibility for setting up Test Central Task IS/IA/DS Buyer Supplier Discuss Test Central Process R/A C I Agreement to use Test Central C R/A I Enable Managed Gateway in Production and Test Manage Profile >> Managed Gateway >> Enable Managed Gateway A/C R I Create Test Plan with Buyer based on type of POs in scope C R/A I Work with Buyer to create/select specific PO examples for each PO type to be used in Test Central R A I Prep the Purchase Orders for Test Central R/A I I Load the Purchase Orders in Test Central R/A I I Submit JIRA ticket for tracking Test Central Setup R/A I I Confirm Test Central Ready for Supplier Use R/A I C R = Responsible -The person or people who actually do the work to complete the task. They are responsible for action/implementation. Responsibility can be shared. A = Accountable (or Approver) -The one ultimately answerable for the correct and thorough completion of the task. Whoever is Accountable must sign off or approve work that Responsible provides. There must be exactly one Accountable person per task. C = Consulted-Those whose opinions are sought before a decision or action is taken. Typically, they are subject-matter experts, and there is two-way communication. I = Informed -Those who are kept up to date on progress or decisions. They receive information but are not necessarily consulted or responsible for the work. Communication is usually one-way. -- 9 of 10 -- 10 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Thank you. -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/BuyerAdminGuide for BTP.content: SAP Business Network on BTP Buyer Administration Guide Generated on: 2026-05-06 06:48:45 GMT+0000 SAP Business Network for Procurement | Cloud Public Original content: https://help.sap.com/docs/ARIBA_NETWORK/3c2416ce48504cfdb28ae12258c367c6?locale=en- US&state=PRODUCTION&version=RTC Warning This document has been generated from SAP Help Portal and is an incomplete version of the official SAP product documentation. The information included in custom documentation may not reflect the arrangement of topics in SAP Help Portal, and may be missing important aspects and/or correlations to other topics. For this reason, it is not for production use. For more information, please visit https://help.sap.com/docs/disclaimer. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 1 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Introduction SAP Business Network on BTP for buyers introduce significant improvements to the site performance and operational efficiency. User experience of the Default Transaction Rules page, Notifications page, Email notifications, Invoice Details page, Purchase Order Details page, and System IDs and Endpoints page are enhanced.. SAP Business Network adapted SAPUI5 technology to improve user experience intuitiveness, navigation, content organization, and visual consistency across its applications. This release adapts SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP) thus offering the ability to compose end-to-end business processes. This guide applies to: SAP Business Network SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Restrictions Experimental features are not part of the officially delivered scope that SAP guarantees for future releases. This means that experimental features may be changed by SAP at any time for any reason without notice. Experimental features are not for productive use. You may not demonstrate, test, examine, evaluate, or otherwise use the experimental features in a live operating environment or with data that has not been sufficiently backed up. The purpose of experimental features is to get feedback early on, allowing customers and partners to influence the future product accordingly. By providing your feedback (e.g. in the SAP Community), you accept that intellectual property rights of the contributions or derivative works shall remain the exclusive property of SAP. For more information, see Disclaimers and Other Legal Information. SAP Business Network on BTP for Buyers Buying organizations use SAP Business Network to find suppliers from which they want to purchase products or services and invite suppliers to form trading relationships. After the supplier accepts the invitation, the buying organization can look at the supplier’s customer catalogs and place orders. Buyers can also easily search for suppliers and their products on the network catalog irrespective of the trading relationship between buyer and supplier. Suppliers receive the orders and return invoices. As a buying organization, you can do the following on SAP Business Network: Search for or invite suppliers that have the products and services you need to form trading partnerships. Send orders and receive invoices. Run reports on your suppliers.  Note The functionality remains the same compared to previous release. This document covers only the user interface changes that are part of this release. This document does not cover all the features, but only those features that are part of early customer access (EAC). The document will be updated as and when new features are delivered. This document should be read in conjunction with the classic SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 2 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Enhancements from Legacy SAP Business Network Buyer User Interface The following enhancements are made to the user interface, compared to the legacy SAP Business Network user interface The Default Transaction Rules page is improved for better organization, search, and user experience. You can easily find and configure rules in a structured and intuitive layout. Enhanced the look and feel of the Notifications page, supported multiple email addresses up to ten, and improved the information displayed in the email notifications. Configured notification alerts for the following: send a notification to the requestor when orders are not delivered to private suppliers. send a notification when orders are undeliverable. Redesigned the Invoice Details page, Purchase Order Details, and System IDs and Endpoints page with a clear layout and organized information with various sections to improve visibility and easy navigation. Simplified the navigation steps: To access the newly designed default transaction rules page, click the Configure transaction rules tile under the Setup Actions section on the SAP Business Network homepage. To access the newly designed notification settings page, click the Configure email notifications tile on the SAP Business Network homepage. The Settings page is redesigned and the tasks are grouped under different tabs. The existing Account settings Manage Profile Business Application IDs and End Points (cXML and OData Setup) link is renamed to System IDs and End Points (Document Routing). The new Display Invoice permission is added to the Permissions section of the Create Role page. The View All link on the Purchase Orders tile and Invoices tile is hidden as the Analytics dashboard features are not available for the first release of the Next Generation Cloud Platform for buyers. Also, the Reports Analytics menu option on the SAP Business Network homepage is not available for buyers. The existing Inbox and Order Access permission is renamed to Display Invoice permission. The Display Invoice permission allows you to view invoice tiles and lists and access the invoice details page. Users with Inbox and Order Access permission will have the Display Invoice permission automatically. Inbox and Order Access permission remains as is, for backward compatibility. The Purchase Order Details page has been redesigned for easier reading and with the ability to search for relevant fields so buyers and suppliers can act efficiently. Account Administrator Responsibilities One person in your organization acts as the account administrator. The administrator is responsible for: Setting configuration options. See SAP Business Network Configuration. (Optional) Adding additional users to the account. See SAP Business Network Users and Roles.  Note If any of these tiles are not visible on the screen, click View All Tasks and then select the appropriate option. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 3 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- (Optional) Creating a test account for testing document flow with suppliers. See Using Test Accounts on SAP Business Network. Getting Started with the SAP Business Network on BTP User Interface for Buyers The SAP Business Network application user interface for buyers has the following key components: 1. —The default page you see when you sign in to SAP Business Network. Click Home to access your home page from anywhere in the application. 2. Menu bar—Provides access to the various pages in the application. Some menus go directly to a page, while others provide a dropdown list of commands. The menu bar that you see may vary depending on your account’s entitlements. 3. Header bar—Provides helpful menus and commands. Use the dropdown on the top-left corner of the header bar to switch between different SAP Business Network web applications. Click the Account Settings icon to choose one of the following commands from the dropdown: ANID (Ariba Network ID)—A number that uniquely identifies your company on SAP Business Network. You might need this number to contact some support services. Company Profile—Review and manage your company profile on SAP Business Network. Manage Profile—Configure company settings such as locale settings, cXML settings, document routing preferences, system notifications, country/region-based invoice rules, payment settings, application end points, and quote automation rules. Settings—Access configurations for users and roles, self-service customization, the unit of measure master list, and your audit log. Also manage purge requests. Services—Manage your SAP Business Network services. Switch to Test Account—Change from production to test account modes. Saved Suppliers— View and remove suppliers that are saved. Admin can view the saved suppliers of all users. Announcements— Create and publish announcements. Logout—Exit SAP Business Network when you are done with your session. Click the Notifications icon to view the list of notifications for the logged in user. Click the Help  icon to navigate directly to the SAP Product Support Help Center. 4. Search bar—Provides capabilities to search for trading partners and network catalog products on SAP Business Network. Trading partners search. See Searching for Trading Partners on SAP Business Network. Discovery search. See Searching for Products in Network Catalog from Various Suppliers. This option is not available for RTC. 5. The Overview section displays the default tiles for your business role, or tiles that you have configured. 6. The Setup Actions section offers you recommended tasks and information resources for first time users. 7. The Highlights section provides widgets to show at a glance current information for your business activities.  Note 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 4 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Home Page You can navigate back to the SAP Business Network home page by clicking Home on the menu bar. Depending on your permissions, the Home dashboard can display the following content items. Only the Alerts and Messages content item is not permission-based. Notifications This content item displays important information about SAP Business Network, and reminders about your account. A yellow icon is shown for alerts that require your attention soon, and a red icon is shown for alerts that require your immediate attention. You can permanently delete any item that does not have an icon by clicking the trash can icon. Shipment Tracking. See Tracking Shipments from the Home Dashboard. Be sure to respond promptly to alerts in the Alerts and Messages content item. Overview Section The SAP Business Network Home page displays the all the configured tiles in the Overview section, by default. Depending on the configuration in Wrokbench, the tiles are displayed. You can reveal additional tiles with the More button. You can also configure which tiles are to be displayed from the Workbench. For more information, see The Workbench  Note The user interface now has the Feedback button on the right for users to share their feedback by means of a 1-minute survey. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 5 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Setup Actions The Setup Actions tile bar directs you to complete important configuration tasks for your account. For example, Update company profile, Upload company logo, Upload vendors, Manage active relationships, or Configure transaction rules, Add roles and users, or Configure email notifications. Click View All Tasks to view the list of actions that are not visible as tiles. Highlights Section The Highlights section displays role-based widgets. These widgets help you focus on important tasks, insights, key performance indicators, and benchmarks for your business. To customize the contents of your Home page, see Customizing Your Home Page Widgets. Shipment Tracking Widget The Shipment tracking widget allows you to quickly track the status of shipments. Enter a purchase order number and click Track to view shipment status information. Purchase Orders Widget The Purchase Orders widget shows you the total value of purchase orders you have created in each month of the selected year. Data is displayed in your preferred currency. Click View all to view additional details on the Analytics dashboard. You must have the Analytics dashboard access permission and the analytics functionality must be activated to access the Analytics dashboard. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 6 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Invoices Widget The Invoices widget shows you the total value of invoices you have received in each month of the selected year. Data is displayed in your preferred currency. Click View all to view additional details on the Analytics dashboard. You must have the Analytics dashboard access permission and the analytics functionality must be activated to access the Analytics dashboard. Supplier Enablement Widgets The Enablement summary, Full enablement progress, and Light enablement progress widgets enable you to quickly check the real-time enablement progress for your potential suppliers that are planning to use either an enterprise account or a standard account. To view the widgets, you must have at least one of the following permissions assigned to your account: Supplier Enablement Configuration, Supplier Enablement Program Administrator, Supplier Enablement Report Administration, or Supplier Enablement Task Management Update Company Profile The buyer company profile on SAP Business Network on BTP provides information about your company and its business. You can review and manage information in the Company Profile to help suppliers learn about your company. Your Company Profile page consists of the following sections: Section Description Quick Navigation Tabs Use the navigation tabs to go to different sections. About Us An overview of your company information is displayed at the top of your profile. You can edit details such as the company name, website, DUNS number, number of employees, year founded, annual revenue, legal form, address, and business type. Product and Services The data for Product and Service Categories and Receiving Locations are retrieved from SAP Business Network Discovery activities and cannot be edited. You can specify Industries for your company. Company Showcase You can showcase your company by adding marketing collateral in the form of attachments, customer presentations, case studies or external links. This helps suppliers learn more about your company.  Note Purchase order and invoice amounts specified in non-USD currencies are converted to USD for the purpose of aggregation using the currency exchange rate at the time the transaction document is created. The aggregated amount is further converted to your user-specified currency for display in widgets. Therefore, you may see a difference between the original amounts displayed in the workbench and the aggregated amount displayed in widgets. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 7 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Buyers with the Company Information permission can click Edit available at the top of each section to edit the information contained in the section. The options in the upper-right corner includes commands for viewing your public profile and obtaining a public profile URL. Edit the Company Profile Follow these steps to Edit your company profile: 1. Click Edit for the section that you want to edit information, enter or revise values as needed, and save your changes. 2. You can edit the following fields in the About Us section: Company Name—A name by which your company is to be known. DUNS Number—A nine-digit number issued by Dun & Bradstreet, Inc. to identify each corporate location of an organization. You can obtain a DUNS number or look up your company’s existing number on Dun & Bradstreet’s website, https://www.dnb.com . Address Information—Complete address of the company including country, region, city, along with the postal code. Short Description—A short description about your company. Long Description—A detailed description about your company. Business Type—Check the business types that apply to your company. Number of Employees—The approximate number of people who work for your organization. Founded—Enter the year when the company was founded in yyyy format. Revenue—Select a currency range. If you prefer not to state your annual revenue, scroll to the bottom of the list and select Contact company for information. Legal Form—Choose the type of business entity or legal status of your company from the dropdown. The list of values varies per country/region. Stock Symbol—A symbol that represents the stock of your company Legal Name—Name by which the company is legally registered. Website URL—Website URL of your company. 3. In the Product and Services section, you can edit only the Industries by selecting the industries your company serves. 4. In the Company Showcase section, you can either add an external link or an attachment. Choose Attachment to attach any files you want to make available to suppliers, such as customer presentations, case studies, and certifications. Choose External link to enter a URL and a description for each additional site. You must preface URLs with “https://”. For example: https://www.Your-Company.com/service. Additional Entities The Additional Entities page enables businesses to add organizational units—such as branches, affiliates, and subsidiaries—and manage business address types, including Sold From (supplier company address), Remit To (supplier remittance address), Sold To (buyer company address), and Bill To (buyer billing address), in one centralized location on their respective company profile. By centralizing address management, businesses ensure consistent and accurate address entities across invoicing, payments, and shipments. For more details, see Understanding Additional Entities 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 8 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Understanding Additional Entities In addition to showing your organizational structure, Additional Entities simplify address management. Instead of maintaining multiple addresses separately, you can centrally manage all address types—Sold From and Remit To (when acting as suppliers), or Bill To and Sold To (when acting as buyers). This helps ensure address information remains consistent and accurate across business processes like invoicing, payments, and shipments. When adding an entity, you’ll enter key details like the legal name, address, tax information (if applicable), and the network collaboration function—which defines how the entity participates in transactions. Available functions include: Sold From – A supplier entity selling goods to buyers. Remit To – A supplier entity where buyers remit payments after receiving an invoice. Bill To – A buyer entity to whom suppliers issue invoices. Sold To – A buyer entity that receives goods from suppliers. Assigning the correct function ensures addresses are used appropriately in transactions, improving operational accuracy and efficiency. How Additional Entities Are Used When Acting as Suppliers Country Configuration (formerly Legal/Regulatory Profile): In countries that require registration with local tax authorities for electronic invoicing, you must set up a country-specific configuration in SAP Business Network. During setup, your organization’s address and tax details are pulled from Additional Entities based on the selected country and company name. You must first create and maintain this information in Additional Entities before the country configuration can be created. Remittance and Bank Information Setup: You can link your Remit To address with specific remittance preferences and bank details. These are automatically included in invoices to ensure buyers receive accurate payment instructions. Invoice Creation: When creating invoices, you’ll select from a predefined list of addresses—Sold From, Remit To, Sold To, and Bill To— maintained under Additional Entities. This ensures that invoices use consistent and validated address data. When Acting as Buyers Document Routing Configuration: If you use multiple ERP systems, you can define routing rules that reference Bill To addresses maintained in Additional Entities. These rules determine which ERP system or business unit should receive and process documents like purchase orders or invoices. Managing Sold To Entities Prerequisites 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 9 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- You have the Company Information permission. If you're not an admin user, contact your account administrator to request access. Context Previously, the default Sold To address was created or set as default in: Account Settings Manage Profile Default Transaction Rules Now, all address creation, editing, and default assignment are centralized in: Company Profile Additional Entities You can still access legacy pages, but they now redirect or provide links back to the Additional Entities page to manage Sold To data. Procedure Create a Sold To Entity 1. In the Additional Entities section, click Create. 2. On the Create New Additional Entity page, provide the following information: Company and location information: Company (Legal) Name Contact Name Country/Region, City, State, Postal Code Address Lines 1-3 Network collaboration information: From the Functions dropdown, select Sold To. (Optional) Check Make this address default. Identification information Enter an Internal ID, which is used to recognize the entity within your organization, such as a company code, address ID, or other internal reference. Usage information: a. Select one or more categories. Categories define the context and purpose of the identifiers you are about to enter. Common categories include: GlobalUniqueID: For globally recognized identifiers like DUNS or Global Location Numbers (GLN). TaxID: For country-specific tax identification numbers (VAT ID, GST ID, for example). Peppol: For organizations using the Peppol e-invoicing network (Peppol ID, Leitweg ID, for example). The categories you select determine which sections and fields are shown below. b. Fill in the required identifiers for each category.  Note The first Sold To address you create is automatically set as the default. Its default status can’t be changed directly. To update the default, overwrite the existing default address with new values. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 10 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/BuyerAdminGuide for BTP.content: This permission… Enables a user to… Transaction Data Export for Deleted Data Download ZIP files of deleted transaction documents. Grants access to this area: Quick Links Deleted Transactions Transaction Monitoring Visibility Access the Transaction Document Report job type for Upload/Download without having the administrator role. Grants access to this area: Quick Links Upload/Download User Administration Create, delete, and manage users and roles. Grants access to this area: Manage Users Create and Publish Announcements Create and publish announcements. Grants access to this area: Account Settings Manage Announcements Quick Links Create Announcement Multifactor Authentication Multifactor authentication is a two-step verification process where you are required to authenticate yourself a second time using a time-based verification code. As compared to the single step authentication process, the multifactor authentication process provides enhanced security. If multifactor authentication is enabled for critical fields, you are required to perform the two-step verification process while attempting to update the values of critical fields such as email addresses, phone numbers, remittance information and so on. With multifactor authentication enabled for sign in, you are required to perform the two-step verification process to sign in to SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network administrators can now enable the following functionalities for users in their organization by selecting the desired users from a table: Require multi-factor authentication for critical fields Require multi-factor authentication for login Prerequisites  Note This permission is for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyer accounts only.  Note This permission is visible only to users assigned the Administrator role.  Note Only buyer administrators with the required permissions can disable multifactor authentication for sign ins. SAP Business Network does not prompt newly created users to complete the multifactor authentication setup immediately after a successful sign in. New users are recommended to set up multifactor authentication for sign in after they change their initial password. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 91 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- When multifactor authentication is enabled for your organization, you must install an authenticator application such as SAP Authenticator from iTunes (for iOS devices) or from Google Play (for Android devices) in your hand-held devices to generate a time-based verification code (also called time-based one-time password). The time-based verification code setup is also compatible with third-party authenticators such as Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator. Setting Up Multifactor Authentication (Buyer User) Context You can set up multifactor authentication after your SAP Business Network administrator has enabled the feature. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, click Personal Information. The Personal Information page appears. 3. Below the User Name text box, click the Set up multi-factor authentication link. The Set up Multi-factor Authentication page appears. 4. Download and install SAP Authenticator or any compatible authenticator application such as Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator on your hand-held device. 5. Open the authenticator application that you have installed on your mobile device and do either one of the following: a. Scan the QR code displayed on the page, and enter the code in the Time-based Verification Code input box, or b. Enter the secure key displayed on the page in the Time-based Verification Code input box. 6. Click Done. SAP Business Network Roles A user with the Administrator role can create a role with certain permissions and assign the role to a buyer user. A role defines a user function within SAP Business Network, such as Purchase Order Generator. Each role has a unique name and set of associated permissions that specify what users who are assigned to the role can see and do in SAP Business Network. A role can be assigned to any number of users. Using the Administrator Role After you complete registration, SAP Business Network creates a single default role named Administrator. The Administrator role is automatically linked to the user name and sign in that you entered during registration. The Administrator role should be assigned to the individual at your organization who is responsible for setting configuration options, managing supplier relationships and contacts, and maintaining the account over time. The account administrator serves as the primary point of contact for users with questions or problems. As the SAP Business Network account administrator, you control who can sign in to your organization’s SAP Business Network account and which areas of the service each user can access. To do this, you create roles and then add users. As a best practice, create roles that reflect the way your company does business to prevent confusion for your account users and maximize the efficiency of your team once roles are in place. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 92 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Only one SAP Business Network user can be assigned to the Administrator role. You cannot modify this role, but you can assign it to another user. The account administrator can assign user management capabilities to non-administrator buyer users, called user administrators. For more information, see the following topics: Transferring Administration Ownership Assigning User Management Capabilities to Users SAP Business Network Predefined Roles Predefined roles are visible only in accounts that were created before roles and permissions were introduced on SAP Business Network. If you registered with SAP Business Network after roles and permissions were implemented, Administrator is the only predefined role. To minimize disruption to these older users, SAP Business Network provides a small set of predefined roles to be used as templates for custom roles. SAP Business Network assigned the Full Access role to all preexisting users when it introduced roles and permissions. Administrators for these older supplier accounts should review the predefined roles and their permissions and consider using them as the basis for custom roles. The predefined roles are listed in the following table: This Role… Grants a User Access To… Administrator All areas of the account, including Settings Users and test account management Catalog Manager Catalogs Customer Catalogs Account Settings Manage Profile Notifications Catalog Service Full Access All areas of SAP Business Network, except areas that are reserved for administrators Purchasing Manager Give access to incoming and outgoing transaction documents and the following configuration pages: Account Settings Manage Profile Default Transaction Rules Account Settings Manage Profile cXML Setup Account Settings Manage Profile Notifications (transaction-related notifications only) Vendor Manager Supplier Enablement Current Relationships Supplier Enablement Contacts Account Settings Manage Profile Notifications Supplier Account Settings Company Profile Product Manager Catalogs Network Catalog Product Approver Catalogs Network Catalog The Administrator role includes all available permissions. These permissions grant the Administrator role access to all areas of your SAP Business Network account. Setting Up Multifactor Authentication Using a New Device (Buyer User) 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 93 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Context When you change your mobile device, you can reset the multifactor authentication that had been configured using your old device. Using the verification code from the old device, you can set up multifactor authentication on your new device. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, click Personal Information. The Personal Information page appears. 3. Below the User Name text box, click the Reset multi-factor authentication link. 4. Enter the verification code from your old mobile device. 5. Set up multifactor authentication again, using a new QR code on your new mobile device. 6. Click Done. Deleting a Role Buyer administrators and users assigned a role with the User Administration permission can delete roles that they no longer need. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. You have informed users about role changes that will affect them. SAP Business Network does not notify users of changes to roles. No users can be assigned the role you want to delete. To change a user to another role, see Reassigning Users to a Different Role. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. On the Manage Roles tab, you can perform a search for the role you want to delete, if necessary. Search for a Permission using the search filters. Or, scroll down and locate the role you want to delete. 3. In the Actions column of the roles results table, click the Delete  icon. Results SAP Business Network deletes the role and returns to the Users page. Changing a User’s Role and Resetting the Password You can select a different role for an existing user or reset the password. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 94 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Context Users can forget their sign in information if they do not sign in to SAP Business Network regularly. SAP Business Network provides a secure and relatively quick way for users to recover sign in information. However, even with this process in place, loss of user names and passwords can cause frustration and lost productivity for you and your users. If you do not want to reset a user’s password, instruct him or her to click Forgot Your Password? on the SAP Business Network Sign In page. After a user submits a user name, SAP Business Network Accounts Services sends the user an email containing steps to reset the password. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. Cick Edit for the user whose password you want to reset. 4. Do one of the following: To change a user’s role, select a different role in the Role Assignment section and click Save. To reset the user’s password, click Reset Password. 5. Click Save. SAP Business Network returns to the Users page. Results If you reset the user’s password, SAP Business Network sends an email to the user containing a new randomly-generated password. The password update takes effect immediately. Managing Multifactor Authentication for Users Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage User Authentication. 3. Select the desired multifactor authentication check boxes. 4. Select the users (from the table) for which you want to manage multifactor authentication. 5. Click the following buttons depending on what you wish to do: Enable: Enables multifactor authentication for the selected users. Disable: Disables multifactor authentication for the selected users. Reset: Resets multifactor authentication for the selected users. These users must either enter the secure key displayed on the user interface, or scan a new QR code during their next sign in session. Send Email Reminder: Sends a reminder email to the selected users. Unlock: Unlocks the selected users. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 95 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- 6. Click Save. Requesting Removal of Personal Data for a Buyer User SAP Business Network users can request the administrator for their account to remove their personal information from the system. If your request is approved, your personal information is removed, and you can't sign in to SAP Business Network. Prerequisites If you are currently assigned the Administrator role for your account, you can't perform this task until after you transfer the Administrator role to another user. See Transferring Administration Ownership. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose Manage Profile. 2. Click Personal Information. The Personal Information page opens. 3. In the Personal information usage section, check the Request to remove my personal information option. 4. Click Save. Results The administrator is notified of your request, and they can approve or reject it. Assigning User Management Capabilities to Users The current account administrator can create a role with the User Administration permission and assign it to non-administrator buyer users, called user administrators. User administrators can perform administrative functions, such as tasks relevant to user management and buyer user access to SAP Business Network. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. On the Manage Roles page, click the  icon. 3. Enter a distinctive name for the role. Enter a description to record your intentions for this role. 4. Go to the last page of permissions, and select the User Administration permission. 5. Click Save. 6. Click Manage Users. 7. On the Manage Users page, select the user you want to assign the user administrator role to. 8. Choose Actions Edit . 9. In the Role Assignment area of the Edit User page, select the user administrator role you created. 10. Click Save. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 96 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Transferring Administration Ownership The current account administrator can reassign ownership of the SAP Business Network account to another person. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Context Account administrators can quickly and easily transfer the Administrator role to another user. After the Administrator role is transferred to a new user, SAP Business Network sends a notification to the new account administrator, alerting them that they now have the Administrator role. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. Select the user you want to transfer the Administrator role to. 4. Choose Actions Make Administrator . The Assign a Role page opens. 5. Select a new role for your account, and click Assign. Updating Users Using an Excel Template Account and user administrators can update multiple users using an Excel template. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. Click the Upload Users button on the Manage Users page. 4. Click the Upload button on the Upload Users page. 5. Click the Download template link on the Upload File dialog box. Alternatively, if you already have an uploaded Excel template you can reuse it by selecting the download icon ( ) in the File column on the Upload Users page 6. Open the Excel template and fill out or update the required fields and click the Upload button on the Upload Users page. 7. Click the Browse button on the Upload Files dialog box, choose the Excel template from your computer and enter a descriptive name. 8. Click the Upload button.  Note If you do not know who the account administrator is, contact SAP Business Network Support. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 97 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- 9. Click the Refresh Status button on the Upload Users page and wait until it shows status Completed. If the status is Completed With Errors or Failed, select the download icon ( ) in the Log column to see the reasons for errors and to correct them. 10. Click the Done button. This opens the Manage Users page where you can see the updated users. SAP Business Network Users Access to a buyer account is secured with individual user identities and levels of permissions. A user is an SAP Business Network sign in (user name and password) that enables one individual in your organization to sign in to your account. The administrator adds users to the SAP Business Network account and assigns each user exactly one role, which typically corresponds to the user’s real-world job responsibilities. Best Practices in Managing User Accounts When the administrator of an SAP Business Network account creates users and assigns roles, it is mandatory that the administrator assigns a unique user name with an appropriate assigned role for each individual who needs to access the account. Users must not share their user name or password with other users. This is important for SAP Business Network and your company in managing data privacy and integrity on SAP Business Network. For security, account administrators and users who have PCard access but are not the PCard owner are required to update their password every 90 days. As a best practice, users should not share their secret question and secret answer. To ensure your organization and users have secure accounts on SAP Business Network, create individual user accounts for different roles in the organization. By default, add one role per user. Users can have multiple related roles, depending on the tasks assigned to the user. How Roles Control User Interface Access Every user can see the Configuration Personal Information area, which contains basic contact information and a preferred language setting for that specific user. Beyond that, the only areas that a user is permitted to see are those allowed by their role permissions. For example, if the administrator created a role that included the Contact Administration permission, a user assigned to that role could see only the Configuration Personal Information area and the Supplier Enablement Contacts area of your SAP Business Network account. While users can update their own personal information, the administrator is responsible for overall user maintenance, which includes deleting users or reassigning user sign ins when individuals leave the company, and resetting user passwords. Related Information SAP Business Network Roles Deleting a User If a user has left the company, you can delete the user to prevent its further use to access SAP Business Network. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 98 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Context When an employee leaves the company or changes jobs and no longer uses the SAP Business Network account, the administrator should either delete the user or reassign the user’s sign in to another individual. If you want to retain the user’s setup and data, reassign the sign in. See Reassigning a User Sign In. If you want to delete the user’s setup and data, perform this procedure. User deletion is permanent. There is no way for SAP Business Network or you to recover a deleted user. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. Search for the user you want to delete. See Creating a User for the steps to perform. 4. In the user results table, check the checkbox for the user you want to delete. 5. In the Actions column, click the Delete  icon in the row of the user you want to delete. Results SAP Business Network deletes the account and refreshes the page content. It does not maintain a record of deleted users. Prevention of Manual Sign In by SAP Business Network Buyer Users Buyers whose SAP Business Network accounts are configured for single sign-on (SSO) corporate authentication can prevent users from signing into the SAP Business Network manually, outside of the single sign-on (SSO) configuration. This SAP Business Network feature is applicable to all buyers who use single sign-on (SSO) corporate authentication for accessing the SAP Business Network. This feature does not affect SAP Business Network suppliers. Preventing users from signing in manually enhances the security of SAP Business Network accounts using single sign-on (SSO) authentication. When this feature is enabled, users cannot sign in to the SAP Business Network in any way other than through single sign-on (SSO). They cannot sign in by entering the URL buyer.ariba.com directly into a browser. Even users with the Administrator role cannot sign in manually. Users who try to sign in manually will receive an error message that says The user name and password pair you entered was not found. If this feature is not enabled, users can use their user name and password to manually sign in to the SAP Business Network. Enabling This Feature This feature is disabled by default. To enable this feature, ask your Designated Support Contact to log a case (formerly Service Request). An SAP Business Network Support representative will follow up to complete the request. Enabling the feature involves SAP Business Network setting an option in the single sign-on (SSO) configuration for the SAP Business Network account to disable manual sign in. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 99 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Enabling Multifactor Authentication for Sign In Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage User Authentication. The Multi-factor Authentication User Setup page is displayed. 3. Select the box Require multi-factor authentication for sign in. 4. Click Yes in the dialog box that appears. 5. Select the desired users by checking the boxes against their user names from the table, and click Enable. Configuring Retention Period for Revoked Users in Your Organization As an administrator, you can configure the retention period of user data for revoked users in your organization. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. Click Account Settings Settings Users . 3. Click Manage User Deletion. 4. Enter a retention period between 1 and 999 in the Retention period in months box. The data of all revoked users in your organization will be retained for a period that you configure here. 5. Click Save. After the retention period is over, user data will be deleted permanently from SAP Business Network. You cannot act upon a revocation request unless you configure the retention period first. Revoked users' data is available for you to view for purposes such as regulatory audits. All the data of an organization (including users' data - both revoked as well as deleted) is deleted when an organization is permanently deleted. Modifying a Role Buyer administrators and users assigned a role with the User Administration permission can edit a role's name, description, and assigned permissions.  Note Only the selected users are enabled for "multifactor authentication for sign in". If you do not select any user from the table, none of the users in your organization will be enabled for multifactor authentication. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 100 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/BuyerAdminGuide for BTP.content: Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. You have informed users about role changes that can affect them. SAP Business Network does not notify users of changes to roles. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. On the Manage Roles tab, search for a Permission using the search filters, or scroll down and locate the role you want to modify. 3. In the Role Name column of the search results table, select the role you want to modify. 4. Check Show me all the available permissions and select the permissions you want or uncheck the permissions you don't want for that role. 5. Choose Save. SAP Business Network applies your changes to all users assigned to the role. Changes take effect for each user at their next sign in. Reassigning Users to a Different Role Buyer administrators and users assigned a role with the User Administration permission can change the role assigned to users. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. SAP Ariba Buying Integration with SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass Description This section covers onboarding an SAP Fieldglass supplier on SAP Business Network and vice versa. Buyers can onboard the suppliers either in SAP Fieldglass or SAP Business Network ensuring unified user experience for suppliers across SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network. If SAP Ariba Buying that is part of SAP Ariba Procurement solutions uses SAP Fieldglass (restricted access) for service procurement, buyer cannot onboard a supplier on SAP Fieldglass. The buyer can leverage the SAP Business Network onboarding feature to onboard and manage suppliers. For more information on buyers and suppliers connection, see the How Buyers and Suppliers Connect section in the SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide. Onboarding SAP Business Network Supplier on SAP Fieldglass  Note Buyer can invite a supplier on SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass only if the buyer exists on both. Only the active supplier accounts can be integrated. Synchronization of supplier profile is not supported between SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass. After the supplier registers in SAP Fieldglass by approving the collaboration type as Service and establishes a connection with the buyer in SAP Fieldglass, a situation may arise wherein the buyer deletes the relationship or the supplier rejects the approved releationship in SAP Business Network. In that case, the relationship in SAP Fieldglass continues and it is not automatically deleted, you must manually deactivate the relationship. Only one remote external identity provider (IDP) is allowed to login to SAP Business Network. Therefore, while connecting to SAP Fieldglass, use only the SAP Fieldglass IDP. The Copy SES option on SAP Business Network is not supported in this integration scenario. Creation of service sheets from Orders tile is not supported for SAP Fieldglass suppliers. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 102 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Description This section explains onboarding a SAP Business Network supplier on SAP Fieldglass, which is mandatory in the following situations: If a buyer that uses SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass sends a purchase order containing serviceable items, to a supplier in SAP Business Network If a buyer uses SAP Ariba Buying to manage service orders, then the buyer can leverage the SAP Business Network onboarding feature to onboard and manage suppliers. The suppliers on SAP Business Network can create a new account or use the existing account and link that to a new or existing account on SAP Fieldglass. SAP Ariba Buying that is part of SAP Ariba Procurement solutions uses SAP Fieldglass (restricted access) for service procurement. After the supplier is registered on SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass, the supplier can use the SAP Business Network portal to view the service orders and navigate to SAP Fieldglass to manage the statement of work. If the buyer has a trading relationship with a supplier, then they can send a service collaboration request to the supplier to onboard them on SAP Fieldglass. The supplier can approve or reject the request. On approval, the supplier gets a notification to either create a new account or use an existing account on SAP Fieldglass. When the supplier creates a new account or uses an existing account, the supplier account in SAP Business Network is linked to the supplier account in SAP Fieldglass and single-sign-on is enabled. Prerequisites Ensure that the buyer exists on both SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass. Ensure that the buyer has a trading relationship with a supplier. Only then the buyer can send a service collaboration request to the supplier to onboard them on SAP Fieldglass. Ensure that the buyer Fieldglass ID (FGID) is included in SAP Business Network in the Fieldglass configuration section. In the buyer profile, ensure that the Enable Supplier Onboarding option is selected while configuring SAP Fieldglass. Restrictions Buyer can invite a supplier on SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass only if the buyer exists on both the applications. Synchronization of supplier profile is not supported between SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass. There is always one-to-one link between SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass account. The Active Relationships page under Supplier Management has a new option Services in the Add Collaboration pop up. The Enable Allow exchange of documents between Ariba Network, SAP Fieldglass, and SAP S/4HANA or SAP S/4HANA Cloud, for services procurement transaction rule is no longer available. Establishing Relationship Between SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass Buyer The buyer should establish a relationship between the SAP Business Network buyer account and the SAP Fieldglass buyer account, to onboard a SAP Business Network supplier on SAP Fieldglass. 1. Navigate to Configure Fieldglass Routing URL screen and enter the valid Fieldglass ID. 2. Select Enable Supplier Onboarding. 3. Click Save. 4. Navigate to Customer Relationships, click Advanced View, select the supplier, select Add Collaboration from More Actions, and then select Services to send an invite to the SAP Business Network supplier to onboard on SAP Fieldglass. Workflow of Onboarding a SAP Business Network Supplier on SAP Fieldglass This section explains the workflow of onboarding a SAP Business Network supplier on SAP Fieldglass. 1. If a supplier does not exist on SAP Business Network, then the SAP Business Network buyer admin invites a new supplier to onboard on SAP Business Network. 2. An invitation email is sent to the supplier contact to either create a SAP Business Network account or link an existing SAP Business Network. 3. On successful registration, the supplier gets onboarded on to SAP Business Network with a transactional relationship. 4. SAP Business Network buyer then sends the collaboration fulfillment request to establish a trading relationship with the supplier using the Customer Relationships page. 5. On acceptance from the supplier, the trading relationship with the buyer and the supplier is established. 6. If the trading relationship with the buyer and the supplier is already established on SAP Business Network, then the SAP Business Network buyer can send the collaboration service request inviting the supplier to register on SAP Fieldglass. Navigate to Customer Relationships, click Advanced view, select the supplier, select Add Collaboration from More Actions, and then select Services. 7. Supplier receives an email about the request, reviews it, and then approves or reject the request. Depending on whether the SAP Fieldglass user ID is same or not, SAP Business Network stores the SAP Fieldglass user ID as follows: If both SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network user ID are the same, then the SAP Business Network user ID is enabled for single-sign-on. If both SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network user ID are different, then SAP Fieldglass user ID is enabled for single-sign-on. Single-Sign-On Between SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass After the supplier accounts are integrated the supplier can use single-sign-on to work on both SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass. The supplier can use the SAP Business Network portal to view the service orders and navigate to SAP Fieldglass to manage the statement of work. Onboarding SAP Fieldglass Supplier on SAP Business Network Description This section covers onboarding an SAP Fieldglass supplier on SAP Business Network. If a supplier fulfilled both material and services, the supplier is required to log in to SAP Business Network as well as SAP Fieldglass separately for different processes. SAP Fieldglass now has the ability to initiate the onboarding of SAP Fieldglass suppliers on to SAP Business Network. The supplier can switch between the applications using single sign-on (SSO). Prerequisites Ensure that the buyer exists on both SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass. Ensure that you enable the Allow multiple private IDs per supplier buyer entitlement for the SAP Fieldglass buyer. Contact the Designated SAP Support contact to enable this feature. Ensure that the SAP Fieldglass supplier is subscribed to Fieldglass Onboarding Service permission to get the option to register with SAP Business Network. We recommend that you set the relationship acceptance type to auto-approved. Restrictions The supplier accounts on SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network must be present on US data centre. The supplier accounts on SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network must be active. SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network account integration does not support profile synchronization. Only one remote external identity provider (IDP) is allowed to login to SAP Business Network and in this flow it is SAP Fieldglass IDP. While using this flow, you cannot use any another IDP. Creation of service sheets from Orders tile is not supported for SAP Fieldglass suppliers. Supplier must create the custom role FIELDGLASS_REMOTE_USER_DEFAULT_ROLE with the following three permissions before registering with SAP Fieldglass: Invoice Generation Inbox Access Outbox Access Otherwise, the users that are created using the SCIM API are not granted the role. For more information on permissions, see Permissions You Can Assign to Users. How the Integration Benefits the Customer Supplier does not need to create an account of SAP Fieldglass user again on SAP Business Network. The supplier sub-users from SAP Fieldglass are automatically replicated in SAP Business Network. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 106 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- A user can perform actions on both SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network using single-sign-on. When a new supplier is onboarded on SAP Fieldglass by a buyer that exists on both SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network, the supplier is onboarded on to SAP Business Network too. User Interface Changes for Fieldglass Suppliers When a new supplier gets registered on SAP Fieldglass, the system displays an option as Complete SBN Registration. Clicking this option redirects the supplier to SAP Business Network to create a new account or integrate with an existing account on SAP Business Network. For existing suppliers, SAP Fieldglass displays the Complete SBN Registration option if the account is not already integrated with an account on SAP Business Network. When a service order is sent to SAP Fieldglass, SAP Business Network displays the statement of work number as a hyperlink. On clicking the hyperlink, the corresponding statement of work document gets displayed on SAP Fieldglass. SAP Fieldglass provides the option to return to SAP Business Network purchase order page. Workflow of Onboarding a SAP Fieldglass Supplier on SAP Business Network The following steps explain the workflow of onboarding a SAP Fieldglass supplier on SAP Business Network . 1. SAP Fieldglass buyer invites a supplier to onboard on SAP Fieldglass. 2. A new registration link is sent to the supplier via an email. 3. Supplier registers on SAP Fieldglass using the link. 4. The registration page displays a link to Complete SBN Registration. Suppliers on SAP Fieldglass that have the relationship with a buyer on both SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network, are displayed a link to Complete SBN Registration. The link is displayed until the supplier's account on both the applications are linked. 5. Complete SBN Registration provides the following two options: Create New Account Use Existing Account 6. Clicking the Create New Account opens the Registration page on SAP Business Network that pre-populates with the supplier's profile data from SAP Fieldglass. Modify the necessary fields on the SAP Business Network page, except the UserID field. 7. When a new supplier account is created on SAP Business Network, a relationship is created with the buyer ANID, account is enabled for single-sign-on, and a default role is assigned to that supplier. 8. When a supplier uses an existing account on SAP Business Network, the system does one of the following: If the supplier exists and relationship with SAP Business Network buyer does not exist, then the relationship is created, account is enabled for single-sign-on, and the default role is assigned to the user. If the supplier exists and relationship with SAP Business Network buyer is already established, then the account is enabled for single-sign-on and the default role is assigned to the user. If the supplier exists and the remote login and default role is assigned, but the relationship with the SAP Business Network buyer is not established, then only the relationship is created. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 107 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- 9. All the sub-users of the supplier on SAP Fieldglass are migrated to SAP Business Network.
