Related Information Setting Up SAP Ariba Buying Trading Partner Search The trading partner search on the SAP Business Network homepage helps buyers to discover and connect with trading partners and initiate transactions. You can search for trading partners by product and service category, product name or description, supplier or manufacturer name, part ID, ship-to or service location, or a combination of them. The search results prioritize relevant, reliable, and engaged trading partners based on several factors: Relevant catalogs: Trading partners offering the specific item in your search rank higher. Verified businesses: Trading partners with verified businesses rank higher. Trading relationships: Trading partners having established trading relationships with more buyers rank higher. Complete profiles: Trading partners with complete profiles that include accurate industry and capability-specific terms rank higher.  Note The sub-users are migrated only when the scheduled job is run.  Note For existing account, the Allow exchange of documents such as orders, service sheets, and invoices between SAP S/HANA Cloud, SAP Fieldglass, and Ariba Network for services procurement transaction rule is not visible when the buyer sends the collaboration service request inviting the supplier to register on SAP Fieldglass. For new account, the Allow exchange of documents such as orders, service sheets, and invoices between SAP S/HANA Cloud, SAP Fieldglass, and Ariba Network for services procurement transaction rule does not exist. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 108 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- In the search results, trading partners with verified businesses are marked with an (Verified Business) icon next to their names. Trading partners that have reported sustainability ratings in their profiles are marked with an  (Reported Sustainability Ratings) icon. You can also use search filters to narrow down the results. For example, you can apply a Trading Partner Status filter to locate trading partners with verified businesses or those having established trading relationships with you. Clicking a trading partner's name takes you to their public company profile. Searching for Trading Partners on SAP Business Network Use the search functionality on SAP Business Network to find trading partners and their catalog offerings. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. On the homepage, make sure Trading partners is selected in the search bar and enter your search terms. Your search terms can include product and service category, product name or description, supplier or manufacturer name, part ID, ship-to or service location, or a combination of them. As you type, SAP Business Network displays suggestions of what you intend to type below the search bar. You can accept a suggestion by selecting it or continue typing. 3. Click the  (Search) icon to start the search. The search results page opens, displaying top-ranking trading partners along with the thumbnails of their catalog offerings that are relevant to your search terms. 4. On the search results page, you can: Refine your results by selecting one or more filters from the Filters pane. Access a trading partner's company profile by clicking the trading partner name. Query information from a trading partner by clicking Request for Information. Save a trading partner by clicking the  (Save Supplier) icon. You can easily find saved trading partners by clicking the Account Settings user icon in the upper-right corner of the window and choosing Saved Suppliers. Search a trading partner's public catalog by clicking View Catalog, if available. If product thumbnails are displayed for a trading partner, click a thumbnail to view product details and request more information. View additional search results by clicking the page numbers (if any) at the bottom. SAP Business Network Documents You can use SAP Business Network object-oriented menus and the workbench to view incoming and outgoing documents. SAP Business Network acts as the intermediary for transactions between you and your suppliers. It allows you to manage many types of documents, including orders, releases, order confirmations, ship notices, invoices, credit memos, payment schedules, and remittance advice documents. SAP Business Network stores your account's electronic documents online for eacy access. View incoming and outgoing documents using the object-oriented menus. For a customized view of transaction documents, create tiles for the workbench. file://SBN/split/BuyerAdminGuide for BTP.content: Example of the Workbench Screen Tile Carousel The carousel adapts dynamically to your permissions so you only see tiles that are relevant to your role. Selecting a tile refreshes the list view below, showing the corresponding business documents. The active tile is marked with a blue bar. Each tile provides a compact summary that typically includes: Count or Amount – The number of documents, action items, or events. For payments-related tiles, the aggregated amount is shown in your local currency. Title – A predefined label describing what the tile represents (for example: New Orders, Changed Orders, Items to Confirm, Rejected Invoices). Titles are fixed and not user-editable. Subtitle – The name of the selected tile view. If no custom view is saved, the default view Standard is shown. You can use the Manage Tiles dialog to adjust the carousel by: Showing or hiding tiles. Changing the order of tiles (move up, down, top, or bottom). Tile Views The carousel adapts dynamically to your permissions so you only see tiles that are relevant to your role. Selecting a tile refreshes the list view below, showing the corresponding business documents. The active tile is marked with a blue bar. Each tile provides a compact summary that typically includes: Count or Amount – The number of documents, action items, or events. For payments-related tiles, the aggregated amount is shown in your local currency. Title – A predefined label describing what the tile represents (for example: New Orders, Changed Orders, Items to Confirm, Rejected Invoices). Titles are fixed and not user-editable. Subtitle – The name of the selected tile view. If no custom view is saved, the default view Standard is shown. You can use the Manage Tiles dialog to adjust the carousel by: Showing or hiding tiles. Changing the order of tiles (move up, down, top, or bottom). Workbench Filters Adapt Filters 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 111 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 9 -- You can choose which filters appear for each tile using the Adapt Filters dialog. Most filters can be customized, but some tiles include one or more fixed filters that cannot be removed. For instance, the New Orders tile always applies the Order Status = New filter, though you can still apply other filters on top of it. Save Filter Preferences as Tile Views The filters available vary by tile type. To work more efficiently, you can save your frequently used filter combinations as tile views and reuse them whenever needed. A single tile can have multiple views. For details, see and . Define Conditions for Filters Some filters allow you to refine results further by using Define Conditions. Clicking the  value help icon next to a filter opens the Define Conditions dialog, where you can set conditions for that filter. Once applied, the conditions are reflected in the filter results. Example Condition: Company Code Setting: equal to = 001 The following options are available when defining conditions: Section Condition Include contains equal to between starts with ends with less than less than or equal to greater than greater than or equal to empty Exclude does not contain not equal to not between does not start with does not end with not less than not less than or equal to not greater than 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 112 This is custom documentation. Accessing the Workbench Workbench Menu (Full Workbench Experience) Accessing the Workbench from the main menu provides full access to all tiles and the customizable tile carousel. From here, you can: View tiles across all document categories, including Orders, Invoices, Payments, Shipments, Leads, Postings, and more. Select which tiles to display and rearrange them on the carousel to suit your workflow. Apply filters to narrow down your search and save filter preferences as tile views. Homepage Shortcut From the homepage, you can open the Workbench by selecting a tile under Workbench Overview. This launches the full Workbench screen filtered to the selected category. Document-Specific Menus (Previously Topical Workbench → Now Workbench List Page) Previously, selecting a document category (for example, Orders, Invoices, or Payments) from a document-specific menu opened what was called a Topical Workbench. This concept has been retired. Now, these document-specific menus open a Workbench List Page, which: 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 113 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 9 -- Shows tiles relevant only to the selected category (for example, the Orders List Page only includes all order-related tiles such as New Orders, Changed Orders, Items to Ship, and Items to Confirm). Provides access to the filter bar, document list, and associated toolbar actions, just like the full Workbench. Does not include the Manage Tile option available in the full Workbench. Does not support available in the full Workbench. Customizing the Tiles Context The Workbench carousel displays tiles for different document types or categories, such as Orders, Invoices, or Leads. Managing tiles lets you prioritize frequently used documents, hide less relevant ones, and arrange them to match your workflow. Only tiles available to your account or role can be added. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Click Workbench to open the Workbench. 3. Click Manage Tiles at the top of the carousel. The Manage Tiles dialog opens, showing all available tiles. Selected tiles have a checkmark in the checkbox before the tile name. 4. Select tiles to display: Check the boxes for the tiles you want to appear on your carousel. 5. Rearrange tiles: Use the arrows to move a tile to the top, to the bottom, up, or down in the carousel order. 6. Confirm or cancel changes: Click OK to save your changes. Click Cancel to exit without saving. Results The Workbench carousel updates to display the tiles you selected, in the order you arranged them. Next, further customize your tiles by adding filters. For more information, see . Filtering Workbench Tiles Context  Note The Workbench tile carousel is dynamic and may expand over time as new tiles are introduced to meet evolving user needs. When new tiles are available, a red dot appears next to Manage Tiles. Hovering over it shows the message New tiles available. In the Manage Tiles dialog, new tiles are listed at the top in bold font until reviewed. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 114 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 9 -- When you open a Workbench tile, all documents associated with that tile are displayed. To focus on specific documents—such as orders in a certain status or from a particular trading partner—you can apply filters. Available filters vary by tile, and you can customize which filters are visible. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Click Workbench, and select a tile from the carousel. 3. Under the tile carousel, choose the filter values you want to apply. 4. Optional: Click Adapt Filters to adjust which filters appear: Use the drop-down to view All, Active, Visible, Visible and Active, or Mandatory filters. Enter a filter name in the search bar to quickly locate it. Select or deselect filters to control visibility. Rearrange filters (move up, down, top, or bottom) to set their order. Click Show Values (top right) to view or update filter values. Switch between List View (all filters in a list) and Group View (filters grouped, for example into Basic or Purchase Orders). 5. Click Go to apply the selected filter values. 6. (Optional) Click Clear to reset the filters. Results The tile updates to display only documents that match your filter criteria. You can save your filter setup as a tile view for future use. For details, see . Customizing Table Columns Context The documents associated with each tile are displayed in a table. You can customize the table by selecting which columns to display, sorting by a column, or grouping rows by a column. Procedure 1. Click the  icon at the top-right of the document list. The View Settings dialog opens. 2. Columns: Select which columns to show or hide. Rearrange column order using the move up/down or top/bottom buttons. 3. Sort: Select a column to sort by from the dropdown. Toggle between ascending and descending order. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 115 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 9 -- 4. Group: Select a column to group rows by its values. Rows with the same value appear under a collapsible header, making it easier to focus on related documents. Example: grouping by Order Status clusters all orders in the same status together. 5. Reset: Click the Reset button at the top-right of the dialog to clear all customizations and return to default settings. Results The table updates according to your selected columns, sorting, and grouping preferences, allowing you to better focus on the documents relevant to your workflow. Export Workbench Data Context The Workbench list view displays documents in a table, which you can customize with filters, columns, sorting, and grouping. If you need to work with this data outside SAP Business Network, you can export it directly to an Excel (.xlsx) file. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Click Workbench, and select a tile from the carousel. 3. Apply filters or adjust table columns as needed to refine the data. 4. Do one of the following: Click the  Export icon from the table toolbar. Click the  icon and choose one of the following: Export– Generates an export file with the current view, no customization. Export As– Lets you specify the export file name, format (currently only Excel), and additional options: Include filter settings in the export file. Split cells with multiple values (for example, a cell showing ID and Description will be split into two cells: ID and Description). Results If the filtered results contain 1,000 or fewer records, the system generates and downloads an Excel (.xlsx) file automatically.  Note Only visible rows and columns in the list view are exported. A maximum of 1,000 records can be exported at a time:: If the filtered results contain 1,000 or fewer records, the export runs automatically. If the filtered results contain more than 1,000 records, only the first 1,000 are included. A prompt informs you of this limit and directs you to the Reporting section to export the full data set. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 116 This is custom documentation. Purchase Order Invoices Through SAP Business Network, buyers and suppliers can seamlessly integrate their invoicing processes on a single network. By enabling the appropriate invoice rules, buyers can allow suppliers to: Create standard invoices against purchase orders. Create non-PO invoices and credit memos. Create invoices against contracts by accessing the customers’ contract collaboration sites. Invoice Routing Status Level Invoice routing status levels describe invoice validation against your invoicing rules. Status Level Definition Obsoleted The supplier canceled the invoice. Queued SAP Business Network received the invoice but has not processed it. Sent SAP Business Network sent the invoice to a queue. The invoice is awaiting pickup by you. Acknowledged Your application has acknowledged the receipt of the invoice. Unassigned Applies only to ICS invoices (invoices sent from an invoice conversion service provider). Indicates an unknown supplier. SAP Business Network either did not find an order matching the invoice or cannot verify the supplier ID. For information about invoice conversion, see the SAP Business Network Guide to Invoice Conversion. Invoice Details Page The Invoice Details page is redesigned to enhance usability and information clarity. The layout and label clarity are improved for easy navigation and understanding. Information is organized into various sections to improve visibility. You can navigate directly to the required sections of the details page by clicking on the respective tabs at the top of the Invoice Details page instead of scrolling through the page to search for the  Note If your supplier’s account is suspended, you cannot receive invoices or other incoming documents from this supplier. SAP Business Network displays a message at the top of the supplier’s basic profile if their account is suspended. SAP Business Network suspends your supplier’s account for failure to remit payment for network transaction service fees. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 117 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 9 -- required information. Clicking a line item on the Invoice Details place displays the selected line item details. All the existing functionalities like Resend invoice, Download attachment, Download cXML, and Print are now available on the new Details page. Types of Invoices Invoice type Description Material Also called purchase order-based, these are standard invoices routed through SAP Business Network that do not contain any service lines (lines that require a service sheet). Service Another type of standard invoice, these are based on service sheets that suppliers create from service lines in service purchase orders routed through SAP Business Network. Service sheets and service invoices can include both services and material goods. Lean Service These are invoices routed through SAP Business Network. A single invoice can be created for all the Lean Service line items in a purchase order. Limit Service These are invoices routed through SAP Business Network. A single invoice can be created for all the Limit Service line items in a purchase order. Limit Order A Limit Order line item is defined as the fulfillment of a service or material delivery at a price limited by a predetermined amount within a time period specified by the buyer. These are invoices routed through SAP Business Network. A single invoice can be created for all the Limit Order line items in a purchase order. Non-PO These invoices reference purchase orders that were not routed through SAP Business Network. Non-PO invoices also allow suppliers to invoice purchase orders that have expired and been deleted, or to generate an invoice that does not have a corresponding purchase order. Non-PO invoices can be issued to a buying organization even if the supplier doesn’t already have an active trading relationship with the buying organization. In that case, the buyer provides the supplier with buyer customer code to allow sending a non-PO invoice (quick enablement through invoice). Credit memo A credit memo represents an amount owed to a buyer by a supplier, typically from an earlier transaction such as a purchase order or a contract invoice. The amount due is a negative number. There are four types of credit memos: PO-based header level credit memos, PO-based line-level credit memos, non-PO credit memos, and dynamic discounting credit memos. Line-level credit memos can be based on a change in quantity or a price adjustment (price decrease). Line-level debit memo Line-level debit memos represent an amount owed to a supplier by a buyer from an earlier transaction. Line-level debit memos are always due to a price adjustment (price increase). 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 118 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 9 -- Invoice type Description Blanket purchase order based A blanket purchase order (BPO) is a type of contract that buyers create that forms an agreement to spend a specific amount with a supplier for critical items or services. If the blanket purchase order is used to purchase specific items (item level BPO), and the customer has not enabled their invoicing site or the BPO for collaborative invoicing, then suppliers can create an invoice directly from the BPO the same way as they can from a regular purchase order. If the BPO is a customer catalog, supplier level or commodity contract, and the buyers are either not using an SAP Ariba invoicing solution, or are using an SAP Ariba invoicing solutions for which collaborative invoicing has been disabled, then suppliers can view the BPO, but must create a non-PO invoice with the contract ID as reference to invoice against the BPO. Contract-based A buying organization using an SAP Ariba invoicing solution can allow collaborative invoicing for suppliers. In that case, suppliers punch in to the buyer’s invoicing solution to either create the entire invoice in the buyer’s invoicing site, or they punch in to retrieve the contract information and add items from the contract to the invoice, but finalize the invoice in and submit the invoice from the SAP Business Network - just as a standard invoice. If suppliers create the entire invoice in the buyer’s invoicing site, SAP Business Network compliance rules do not apply, since the supplier is subject to the invoicing processes and rules configured for the buyer’s invoicing solution. Self billing SAP Business Network can automatically transmit self-billing invoices to suppliers and buyers based on data in purchase orders, scheduling agreements, and goods receipts using an automated process. Invoicing - Buyer's Perspective  Note Service sheet is not supported for blanket purchase orders in SAP Business Network. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 119 This is custom documentation. Company Contacts By default, the main company contact is set to the account creator (administrator). However, you can update this information at any time to reflect your company’s most appropriate general contact. Click the Contacts tab in the Update Company Profile page. In the Individual Company Contacts section, you can create the contact details of a person with company-wide assignments. Here you can enter the contact name, business title, company assignment, address, email, phone number for the contact. The Inviter Contact checkbox when selected can be used as the Inviter Contact when adding a vendor. Show or Hide Company Profile When you create a public posting on SAP Business Network Discovery, your company profile information is, by default visible to suppliers. If you want to prevent suppliers from viewing your company profile information, then you can hide it. Showing your company profile in postings can help potential suppliers feel more comfortable with doing business with your organization, resulting in increased responses to your posting. Although you can choose to hide your company profile information, SAP recommends that you show it. To show or hide you company profile, select of deselect the Make my profile visible to supplier in postings option in the Settings tab. You can also replicate this settings to global regions by selecting the Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network. Upload Company Logo Prerequisites Before uploading your logo, ensure the following: You have the Company Information permission. If you're not an admin user, contact your account administrator to request access. Your logo file meets these requirements: Format: GIF (static only; no animation) Maximum size: 200 KB Dimensions: Up to 250 × 250 pixels Background: Remove any excess area surrounding your logo. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 14 This is custom documentation. Your test account and production account each use their own logo. You might want to create a logo for your test account that clearly indicates that the orders are test orders. Email Notifications Notifications are triggered by events that occur on SAP Business Network. For example, invoice received or updated, undelivered purchase orders, and so on. Buyers on SAP Business Network can specify which notifications to receive so that they are informed about events and activities related to their account. Notifications help monitor account activity and document updates related to transactions, such as purchase orders, order confirmations, ship notices, and invoices. Elements present in the classic SAP Business Network user interface have been added to the new user interface to maintain parity. Based on the notification type,SAP Business Network delivers these notifications in two places: on the SAP Business Network Portal (Online) and to a specified email address. Notifications related to transaction documents, such as purchase orders, order confirmations, ship notices, and invoices are delivered on SAP Business Network. To view these notifications, buyers can click the Quick Links icon and select Notifications. Changes to the User Interface The Notifications table displays the following: Field Name Description Document Type Displays the document type: Purchase Order Invoice Order Confirmation Ship Notice Status Displays the status of the notification as: Failed Rejected Received 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 15 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Field Name Description Updated From Displays the name of the sender who sent the notification. Subject Displays the subject line of the message. Order/Doc Number Displays the order number or document number. Date Displays the date and time when the notification was sent. Implementation Details Business End User Tasks To view notifications for your SAP Business Network account: 1. Go to Quick Links and select Notifications. The Notifications page appears. 2. Select a notification and click more details. 3. Select any notification to view the message details. A panel appears with the full details of the notification. Configure Email Notifications You can configure email notifications for various transactional documents or enablement tasks and select the events that trigger these notifications. You can also configure the email addresses where notifications are to be sent. You can specify up to 10 email addresses. To configure email notifications, follow these steps: 1. Click Configure email notifications under the Setup Actions section in the Home page of the SAP Buyer Portal. If this option is not visible on screen, click View All Tasks and then selectConfigure email notifications 2. Click Saved Version and select Draft to edit the configurations.. 3. The Notifications page displays all theavailable notification configurations under the Network Notifications tab. The events that trigger the notification are grouped as per the document type, such as purchase orders, order confirmations, ship notices, and invoices or as per the enablement tasks such as upload/download, relationship, or master data management notifications. The following table describes these groups and the various tasks that can be enabled for notifications under each group: Group Tasks Description Order Notifications Undeliverable Orders Send a notification when orders are undeliverable. Order Status Update Send a notification to the order requester on the order when the order status changes. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 16 This is custom documentation. Data Deletion Criteria for Buyers On the Configuration page, the administrator for your SAP Business Network account and other users with appropriate permission can specify the retention period for transaction documents. Additionally, SAP Business Network automatically deletes buyer master data after a period of inactivity following contract termination. You may need to delete old transaction documents to satisfy regulatory needs in your country/region or business requirements in your organization. If you request recurring deletion of transaction data, any transaction document sets older than the retention period are subject to deletion every month. Each document set includes transaction documents and any associated attachments. You can also request one-time deletion of transaction data. This operation is similar, but happens only once, not every month. For example, you can delete your transaction data older than January 1, 2018. Types of Transaction Documents That Can Be Deleted The following transaction documents can be deleted: Purchase orders (orders and blanket orders) Order confirmations Ship notices Receipts Service sheets Invoices, credit memos, and debit memos Payment documents SAP Business Network for Supply Chain transaction documents Notifications Quote requests and quote messages Associated attachments Workflow for Deleting Transaction Documents The following diagram shows the workflow for deleting transaction documents from SAP Business Network:  Note If a buyer account is deleted from the SAP Business Network, the posted RFx transactions get automatically deleted. Suppliers associated with the deleted RFx now can't view any of the deleted RFx transactions. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 18 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Workflow for Deleting Transaction Documents from SAP Business Network About Transaction Document Sets Each transaction document is part of a larger transaction document set, a sequence of related documents sent between the buyer and supplier (for example, purchase order, order confirmation, ship notice, receipt, invoice, and so on). Buyers and suppliers maintain their own data retention period. When all documents in a particular set are older than the specified data retention period, only then are they ready to be deleted. If any document in a set isn't older than the data retention period, the entire set is retained. Transaction Document Set For example, say that your company retains transaction documents for 36 months. A purchase order was created 60 months ago. However, an invoice associated with the purchase order was created only 30 months ago. Since the document set (the purchase order and invoice) isn't older than the retention period of 36 months, both the purchase order and the invoice are retained, not deleted. Documents are identified for deletion according to the data retention period that you specify (for example, 18 months). The age of a document is based on its creation date or the date of its last status update, whichever is later. On the first day of each month, the system finds any document sets older than the data retention period. If all documents in a particular set are older than the data retention period, that set is identified for deletion. The identified set is queued for deletion and deleted within 1 month after being identified.  Note SAP Ariba retains transaction data for a reasonable time after the 30-day grace period. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 19 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- When the system deletes a document, it’s deleted permanently; it can’t be restored. You can’t perform any operations against deleted documents (for example, searching). Data Deletion Restrictions This feature doesn't affect archived invoices, which are stored separately. Once a document has been identified for deletion, it’s deleted regardless if you later opt out of data deletion. Please carefully configure the retention period for transaction documents. Deletion of transaction documents is an irreversible process. You can’t retrieve any transaction documents after they're deleted by the system. If you're using long-term archiving services, we strongly recommend that you specify a retention period for transaction documents that is greater than or equal to the longest archiving retention period legally required by countries/regions where you operate. If the system deletes your invoices, you can't search for those invoices in SAP Business Network. Your archived invoices, however, continue to be retained by TrustWeaver or Sovos (third-party systems that SAP Business Network uses to archive invoices) for the full legal retention period. Data Deletion Notifications You can enable the following notifications for data deletion: Notification Type Notifications Data Identification and Deletion Send a notification when the transaction documents have been identified for deletion Send a notification after deletion of transactions Automatic Deletion of Master Data for Inactive Buyer Accounts Buyer accounts and their data are automatically deleted when their contract with SAP Ariba is terminated. When a buyer account's contract with SAP Ariba is terminated, the account status becomes Expired and SAP Business Network sends a notification to the buyer account administrator. The buyer account administrator can request reactivation of their account at this time. After 60 days of expiry, if the account has not been reactivated, the buyer account and all of its data is permanently deleted. Account deletion is irreversable.  Note Documents that have been identified for deletion can still be searched until they're deleted.  Note Accounts that have used archiving services at any time are not subject to the automatic deletion of master data due to inactivity; the account is expired but the master data is maintained.  Note Buyers who only use SAP Business Network Discovery are considered inactive after 3 years of inactivity.  Note When a buyer account is deleted, they're still visible to their suppliers with the identifier Deleted by SAP Ariba, and suppliers can still access transactions involving the deleted buyer. No company is able to perform new transactions with a deleted buyer. When the buyer and all its related suppliers are deleted, all remaining retained data is permanently deleted. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 20 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Company Data Deletion Configuration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. A transaction document is identified for deletion when all documents in its transaction document set, the sequence of related documents exchanged between the buyer and supplier, are older than the data retention period. The age of a document is based on its creation date or the date of its last status update, whichever is later. Buyers and suppliers maintain their own data retention period. Consequently, your suppliers can retain copies of documents that have been deleted from your account. To receive an email notification when transaction documents for your deletion request are available to download, the administrator needs to set up notifications. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, choose Data Deletion Criteria. Requesting a One-Time Deletion of Transaction Data for SAP Business Network Buyers You can request to delete transactions older than a certain date on a one-time basis for your SAP Business Network account. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Company Data Deletion Configuration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. A transaction document is identified for deletion when all documents in its transaction document set, the sequence of related documents exchanged between the buyer and supplier, are older than the specified date. The age of a document is based on its creation date or the date of its last status update, whichever is later. Buyers and suppliers maintain their own data retention period. Consequently, your suppliers can retain copies of documents that have been deleted from your account. All transactions created or last updated before that date are identified for deletion as soon as possible. 5. Click Done. Canceling a Request for Deletion of Transaction Data for SAP Business Network Buyers You can cancel a request to delete transaction data. After the request is canceled, you can request a new recurring or one-time deletion at any time. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Company Data Deletion Configuration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, click Data Deletion Criteria.  Tip You can click History log on the Data Deletion Criteria page to view deletion requests that already have run or been canceled.  Restriction Once a transaction document set has been identified for deletion, it’s deleted regardless if you later cancel the deletion request. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 23 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- The Data Deletion Criteria page appears. 3. Under Recurring Deletion or One Time Deletion, click Cancel. 4. Click Yes to confirm. 5. Click Done. Downloading ZIP Files for Deleted Transactions for SAP Business Network Buyers You can download transaction documents from your SAP Business Network account for 30 days after they were identified for deletion. SAP Business Network collects the transaction documents into ZIP files for download. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Transaction Data Export for Deleted Data permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. You have 30 days to download ZIP files for transaction documents identified for deletion. After that, the documents are permanently deleted. Procedure 1. Click Quick links, and choose Deleted Transactions in the Document Archive section. The Deleted Transactions page appears. If files are available for download, they appear in separate tables for recurring deletion and one-time deletion. Deleted Transactions Page 2. To download a ZIP file, go to the Action column and click the  Download icon.  Tip You can click History log on the Data Deletion Criteria page to view deletion requests that have been canceled.  Tip You can filter the table of ZIP files to show files for which download has not yet started. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 24 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Default Transaction Rules For documents entered on the SAP Business Network portal, the transaction rules are applied when the documents are created. If there are errors or incomplete information, the user cannot move to the next stage to submit the document to the buyer. For integrated documents, the rules are applied after the documents are received and processed. The network sends the relevant error messages as notifications on the SAP Business Network portal and the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network if the supplier investigates the document's status. The look and feel and the user experience of the Default Transaction Rules page is significantly improved in NextGen release. The rules are organized so that support, services, and buyers can easily search and identify specific rules they need to implement for their business needs. Each business rule is labeled with a unique rule ID for better identification. The default transaction rule page includes a new Production Status indicator to identify the rules that are out of sync between test and production accounts and to identify the rules that are candidates for migrating test accounts to production. In cases where the rules differ from the production environment, you can easily identify potential synchronization issues. Additionally, you can track rule modifications that require evaluation, testing, and eventual promotion to the production environment. Administrators can add comments providing the business rationale for the rule changes and share them with your team, services, or support for enhanced monitoring and traceability. The Default Transaction Rules page includes tabs for purchase orders, order confirmations, ship notices, invoices, planning, and attachment rules to categorize transaction rules into different groups as shown in the following image: These categories are further divided into smaller groups. The following table shows the detailed hierarchical structure: Category Group Order General Purchase Order Order Confirmation Order Confirmation Ship Notice Ship Notice Invoice General Invoice Planning Planning 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 25 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- When quantity tolerances are set, your suppliers can't enter quantities that are outside these tolerances when creating order confirmations. To determine whether a quantity is within tolerance, order confirmation quantities are compared with the required quantity on the purchase order line item or scheduling agreement release line item. While entering quantities on an order confirmation, if your supplier enters a quantity that is outside the permitted tolerance, a message displays to indicate the error. Tolerance checks are performed only when a quantity tolerance value is included for either underdelivery or overdelivery in the Apply line item quantity tolerance to order confirmations transaction rule or in control keys within the line item cXML. The underdelivery and overdelivery values are evaluated independently, so it's possible to have a value in one and not in the other. A value of 0 for either underdelivery or overdelivery means that it is not possible to create an order confirmation that exceeds the requested quantity in that direction. For example, say a purchase order line item requests a quantity of 10, and the transaction rule says that up to 10% underdelivery is allowed and 0% overdelivery is allowed. In this case, an order confirmation can be created with a quantity of either 9 or 10. Any other quantity is outside the allowed tolerances. If no tolerance value is included, the default system behavior applies – underdelivery is permitted, and overdelivery isn't permitted. (Having an empty value for overdelivery isn't permitted – instead, the system adds 0 as a default value.) The presence of tolerance values affects order statuses in the following ways: Orders for which there's underdelivery, but within tolerance, have a status of Partially Confirmed. Orders for which there's overdelivery, but within tolerance, have a status of Fully Confirmed. A tolerance value of 0% applies only to the upper end tolerance of the unit price. Country/Region-Based Invoice Rules SAP Ariba provides a set of default country/region-specific invoicing rule templates that you can use as a starting point when defining invoice rules. Country/region-based rule templates reflect the current knowledge of invoice requirements for those countries/regions. SAP Ariba strongly recommends buyers implementing country/region-based invoice rules to consult with their tax and legal advisors to determine the applicability of any business rule they implement. Enablement Process for Country/Region-Based Invoice Rules You can use the country/region-based invoicing rule templates to add countries/regions for which you want to implement specific invoice rules. By default, country/region-based invoice rules are disabled and no country/region-based invoice rules are activated. Follow these general steps to enable and activate country/region-based invoice rules: 1. Using the country/region-based invoicing rule templates, add the countries/regions for which you want to implement specific invoice rules and review the country/region's invoice rules set. 2. Based on legal requirements for a country/region, edit the invoicing rules set for the country/region. 3. View the final invoice rules that get applied based on the rules defined on the default transaction rule, supplier group rule, and country/region-based invoice rule levels. 4. You might want to discuss any changes to the invoicing rules with your suppliers to avoid unnecessary invoice rejections as a result of the new invoice rule enforcement. 5. If you are ready to put the rules in production, uncheck the rule Ignore country-based invoice rules: If you want to enable country/region-based invoice rules for all suppliers that do not belong to a supplier group, uncheck Ignore country-based invoice rules on the Default Transaction Rules page. If you want to enable country/region-based invoice rules by supplier group, uncheck Ignore country-based invoice rules on supplier group level. Suppliers can review the rules that are applied to their invoices by the country/region of origin after you have enabled country/region-based invoice rules for them. Related Information Country/Region-Based Invoice Rules Automatic Invoice Creation from Receipts SAP Business Network buyers in the United States, Australia, and South Africa can enable a country/region-based invoice rule to automatically create invoices from receipts. The Enable automatic invoice creation from receipts rule, effective only when Require suppliers to include only received quantities on invoices is checked, causes SAP Business Network to automatically create an invoice when you send a receipt for material goods. This rule ensures that invoices are based on goods that you have received. Before invoices can be automatically generated on behalf of a supplier, based on receipts sent from you, the supplier must agree to automatic invoicing by completing the Automatic Invoice Creation Acceptance page for each buyer that has enabled the country/region-based rule. When the supplier logs in to SAP Business Network, an alert notifies them of the need for confirmation of automatic invoicing against receipts. When you enable automatic invoice creation, SAP Business Network automatically generates a standard invoice or line-item credit memo when you send a receipt for received quantities. Partial invoicing is also supported. The date assigned to the invoice is the system date. Each automatically generated invoice has references to the related receipt and purchase order. When SAP Business Network generates an invoice automatically based on a receipt you submit, it gathers information for the invoice from the order, the receipt, and the supplier's company profile. Header-level information for the invoice comes from the order. If the tax information is not present on the order, the VAT information is obtained from the supplier's company profile. Item- level information for the invoice comes from the order with the exception of Order Line Number and Quantity, which come from the receipt. All taxes for invoices generated automatically from receipts must come from the purchase order. Taxes can be specified at the header-level of the order or at the line-item level, but not in both places. To ensure that line item level taxes for standard invoices are copied from the purchase order, check the Copy tax from purchase order to standard invoice rule. (Note that this rule does not apply to line item credit memos. For line item credit memos, taxes at line item level default from the invoice and not from the purchase order, even when this rule is enabled.) The rule Include allowances and charges in the unit price must be unchecked to ensure correct calculation of line item unit prices when the purchase orders have taxes and charges applied on the line items. All taxes should be specified as a percentage rate on the order. The percentage is applied to all invoices generated for the order. If the tax is specified as a flat amount on the order, it is also applied to all invoices generated for the order, which could result in higher taxes than intended. Allowances and charges for invoices generated automatically from receipts must come from the order. Allowances and charges can be specified at the header-level of the order and at the line-item level. Like taxes, all allowances and charges should be specified as a percentage rate on the order. The percentage is applied to all invoices generated for the order. If an allowance or charge is specified as a flat amount on the order, it is applied to every invoice generated from a receipt, which could result in cumulatively higher allowances or charges than intended. Invoice Number for Automatically-Generated Invoices There are two methods SAP Business Network uses to assign invoice numbers to invoices created automatically from receipts:  Note You can view the invoice rules for countries/regions that are in an “Active” status. The rules belonging to countries/regions that are in an inactive status are not available in the downloaded CSV file. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 51 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Receipts with Delivery Note Information: If the buyer uses the SAP ERP to create a receipt from a ship notice coming from SAP Ariba, the Delivery Note field on the receipt is auto-populated with the packing slip ID from SAP Business Network. In that case, the invoice number for an automatically-generated invoice or line-item credit memo is based on the delivery note information, with a four-digit number appended to it. Receipts without Delivery Note Information: If a receipt does not include delivery note information, the invoice number is a system-generated unique number that starts with "A" (for example, "AI7VCKN40"). Restrictions The following receipts do not result in an automatically-generated invoice: Receipts for items from multiple orders. Receipts for items from a purchase order that contains both services and material goods. Buyers and cXML-enabled suppliers must upgrade to cXML 1.2.030 or later to support the ShipNoticeIDInfo child element in the ReceiptRequestHeader element. All items in a receipt must have either positive or negative quantities and must be either of type "received" or "returned". Otherwise, the receipt will be rejected. All taxes, allowances, and charges must be specified on the order as a percent rate, not as a flat amount. The Enable automatic invoice creation from receipts country/region-based invoice rule is supported only for United States, Australia, and South Africa. The rule only applies to suppliers that invoice through the SAP Business Network and not through an integrated ERP system. In addition to required business rules that the buyer must select to enable automatic invoice creation from receipts, there are other rules that affect the fulfillment flow. The following default transaction rules, if checked, affect the workflow for automatic invoicing from receipts: Allow suppliers to increase item quantities Allow suppliers to increase line item subtotals Require suppliers to fully confirm line items before fulfillment Require suppliers to create an order confirmation for the PO before creating an invoice Require suppliers to create a ship notice for the PO before creating an invoice For example, if the first two rules are unchecked, the invoice quantities and subtotals cannot be increased from the order. If the last three rules are checked, an order confirmation, ship notice, and receipt must be created in sequence for an order before SAP Business Network can automatically create an invoice on behalf of the supplier. Related Information Country/Region-Based Invoice Rules Catalog Validation Preferences SAP Business Network enables suppliers to check their customer catalogs against your catalog validation preferences before publishing the customer catalog to you. The supplier’s ability to qualify their customer catalog for your organization increases the likelihood that you can upload their customer catalogs without encountering errors. You can set the following validation preferences: Specify the UNSPSC (United Nations Standard Products and Services Code) code version that you support. If the supplier’s UNSPSC version is different, SAP Business Network automatically converts the commodity codes in the customer catalog to your supported version. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 52 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Set an option to allow 0 price values. SAP Business Network’s standard customer catalog checking produces an error for 0 price values. Set an option to disable Unit of Measure (UOM) checking. This enables you to upload suppliers' customer catalogs without encountering an error if the customer catalog UOM codes differ from those you support. If you customize your UOM maps, you should disable UOM checking. Set an option to disable commodity code checking. This enables you to download suppliers' customer catalogs without encountering an error if the customer catalog commodity codes differ from those you support. If you customize your commodity code maps, you should disable commodity code checking. Click Save. Audit Logs for Buyers You can access classic and standard audit logs. To view audit logs, click the Account Settings icon, and choose Settings. Under Audit Log, choose Classic for the legacy audit log or Standard for the Intelligent Configuration Manager audit log. These are the available classic audit logs: Transaction Rule Changes – This log tracks changes to default transaction rules. Supplier Group Membership Changes – This log tracks changes to supplier groups. Profile Changes – This log tracks changes to user profiles. User Access – This log tracks user access activity, which includes the number of failed access attempts since the last successful sign in and their reasons. Currency Preference Changes – This log tracks changes to currency preferences. For more information about the standard audit log, see Managing SAP Ariba Audit Information. Unit of Measure Data for Your Account You can use the unit of measure CSV template to define the unit of measure codes that you use in your business, as well as provide additional information such as the symbol, name, and description for each code. Unit of measure codes can be based on ISO or UN/CEFACT standards, or they can be any arbitrary codes defined by your company. If unit of measure codes are company-specific, it's important to provide additional information about the codes to suppliers so they can understand what the codes mean in purchase orders and other SAP Business Network documents. The unit of measure CSV template has the following four header rows at the top of the template: Row 1: Character encoding (for example, 8859_1). Row 2: Field names (Code, Name, Symbol, and Description). Row 3: Whether the field is required or optional. Row 4: Data type and maximum length (for example, "String 100"). The first three fields in the template, Code, Name, and Symbol, are required. The Description field is optional. The fields can be rearranged in any order as long as the field names are not changed.  Note If there is no symbol for a code, we recommend that you repeat the Code value in the Symbol field. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 55 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- The following table shows an example of unit of measure information that you can add to the CSV template: Code Name Symbol Description 2N dB decibel decibel 2P kbyte kilobyte kilobyte 2Q kBq kilobecquerel kilobecquerel 2R kCi kilocurie kilocurie DZN dozen DOZ dozen PK pack PK pack TP ten pack TP ten pack Language Support The unit of measure master list supports multiple languages. Fill in the template in a separate CSV file for each locale. To activate a master list, upload strings for at least the English locale. Enabling or Disabling Unit of Measure Codes You can disable and enable unit of measure codes that you uploaded to your account. If you disable a unit of measure code, suppliers can't find it anymore in the application, although they can still enter it. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Before you can enable or disable unit of measure codes, you must first upload them to your account. When you upload unit of measure codes, they are enabled by default. Procedure 1. Choose Settings Master List . 2. For the Unit of Measure master list, click Enable or disable codes. The Enable or disable unit of measure codes page appears. 3. Select Code or Name from the list. 4. Type the start of a code or name, and then click Search. 5. Select one or more codes. 6. Click Enable to enable the selected codes, or click Disable to disable them. 7. Click Done.  Restriction Once you upload a unit of measure code to your account, you cannot delete it. However, you can update the Name, Symbol, and Description fields for a unit of measure code. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 56 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Uploading Unit of Measure Data You can use the unit of measure CSV template to upload additional unit of measure information to your account for use in SAP Business Network documents. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Fill in the CSV template with information about unit of measure information codes for one or more locales. To activate the list in your account, upload strings for at least the English locale. Procedure 1. Choose Settings Master List . 2. For the Unit of Measure master list, click Upload or download master list. 3. For the locale of the CSV file you are uploading, click Upload. 4. Click Browse to select a CSV file, and then click Upload. 5. Repeat steps and for other locales, as needed. 6. Click Done. To support different locales, save a different version of the file for each locale. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Procedure 1. Choose Settings Master List . For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- 2. For the Unit of Measure master list, click Download template, and save the file to your computer. Activating the Analytics Functionality in Your SAP Business Network Buyer Account You activate the analytics functionality in your SAP Business Network buyer account from the Configuration page. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, click Analytics Configuration. 3. Click Submit to configure and activate the analytics functionality. If the operation fails, click Retry. You can retry the operation for a maximum of 4 times. Contact SAP Ariba Customer Suppor for help if the operation fails after the maximum number of tries. UI Customization This feature allows buyers to create custom attributes that display additional data that is relevant for their business but not available as part of SAP Business Network in a self-service manner and add them to a customization project. The buyers can edit or create standard and custom attributes and display them in the specific section of the transactional documents, such as invoice, purchase order, advance ship notice, and order confirmation. Customization helps the buyers to collect additional information, that are not captured as part of standard default fields. For example, if the orders include the fixed bin location for items, you can customize ship notices to include that field, too. The data from the fields that you add are sent as extrinsics in cXML documents. Depending on the country or industry specific rules, customers may require additional fields in transactional documents. The buyers can determine if the customizations are applicable for a supplier group or a multiple supplier groups. You can also control the behavior of fields, such as adding notes, warnings or page hints or hide field lables and values for the amount and subtotal fields. When you customize the user interface, the following conditions are applicable: SAP Business Network creates an audit log for all the customizations done and user who performed it. The audit log stores information about the projects created and also the fields customized to have a control. The buyer can assign the customization project to a supplier group or multiple supplier groups. The buyer can create a copy of the customization projects and assign that to a different supplier. The buyer can add, edit, or remove customization projects. Implementation Details General Prerequisites 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 58 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Ensure that the admin has the following permissions to customize a project and add custom attributes:: ADMIN_TS_CUSTOMIZATION ADMIN_CUSTOMIZATION ADMIN_TS ADMIN_CUSTOM_ATTRIBUTES CUSTOMIZATION ATTRIBUTE EDITOR CUSTOMIZATION EDITOR CUSTOMIZATION PUBLISHER Restrictions The following restrictions are applicable for creating custom attributes: Custom attributes can be created in a centralized library and added to the customization project. Custom attributes can also be created while creating the customization project. These attributes are automatically saved to the library and can be added to other customization projects. Each customer must have their own custom field library. Custom fields created by the customer in their own library are accessible only by them (not by other customers). Attributes can be deleted from the library, only if they are not yet included in a published project. User can select the area of the chosen document to be customized with additional attributes. The custom fields that are added must not override system-required fields. The transactional document types have their own transaction rules that limit the types of values a supplier is allowed to enter UI Customization must not override a Transaction Rule. Different versions of the projects are available that the buyer can track and restore. Buyer can edit field level and section level of a document type in a project. Configuration Business End User Tasks Follow these steps to customize the user interface: 1. Login to the SAP Business Network as an editor. 2. Navigate to Users Settings to open the Settings page. 3. Scroll down to the Integration section and select Customization Self-service to open the Customization Self-service page. 4. Click Create to create a new project. 5. Enter a name for the project, select the supplier account and then select the document type for which you want to add additional fields or customize the attributes.  Note 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 59 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- 6. Select one of the document customization areas from the following options: Document display CSV Excel PDF Workbench 7. Click Create. When you create a project for a document type, all the fields available in the document template for that document are included to the project. Click View details to list the different sections and fields available for that project. To customize a document refer to . Add Attributes After you create a project, you can view the different sections of the document by clicking the View details link. Expand the section to view the fields and select a field to view the attributes. Adding an Attribute To add an attribute, follow these steps: 1. Click View details for a project you created for a document type. 2. Expand a section and select a field to list the attributes of the field. 3. Click Create Create Attribute to open the Create Attribute page. 4. Enter a attribute name and then enter the description. You can select mutiple suppliers. For example, if you select Ship Notice as document type, then the customization area displays CSV, PDF, Excel, and Items to Ship, whereas, if you select Order Confirmation, the customization area displays Excel and Items to Confirm.  Note The Create Add Existing Attribute option allows you to add or edit an existing attribute to a field. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 60 This is custom documentation.
