Click Save to create the new attribute either to the customization project and to the library. The system validates the field name within the project and within the centralized library if it is unique and displays the newly created attribute in the subsection, which you can edit. Customizing a Field You can customize an existing field or a newly created filed to control the behavior and appearance in documents. You can do any of the following customizations for a field: Default values: Set a default value. Default value can be dynamic (based on extrinsic from the PO, in the INV case). Flippable Values: Set this field if you want to select a field from a document and map it to a field in another document (example Purchase Order), so that the data is automatically populated. Required: Make a field required with or without a condition. Required fields display with an asterisk. Some fields are already set as required.  Note The system does not allow duplicate field names within the library.  Note Static type only is available within Project. This type of attribute is created only in the project and is not added to attribute library. Examples for Static type are Section heading, Page hint, Warning, Note, Hyperlink, and Mail to. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 61 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Hidden: Hide a field with or without a condition. Read only: Make a field read-onlywith or without a condition. For example, make field Currency read-only if the purchase order status is Submitted or Approved. Edit field label. Set a validation expression. For example, GST ID should have alphanumeric characters and cannot exceed 20 characters. Set minimum and maximum length for a field. Provide a tooltip message. Make a field visible through a rule. For example, the supplier GST ID is visible only when Bill to Address country is India. Set a custom attribute as a filter. A maximum of three filters can be added. Select Rules and then define the rule action as hide, read-only or required based on the conditions. Click Save to save the customization. You can export these customization by clicking Export For information on customization, publishing a project and audit logs, refer to Central Extensibility Portal Guide. Customization for Order Confirmation SAP Business Network allows the buyer to customize Order Confirmation page based on the country or industry specific rules. To customize the Order Confirmation page, first create a project by selecting the document type as Order Confirmation. When you create a project for a document type, all the fields available in the document template for that document are included to the project. Click View details to list the different sections and fields available for that project. The buyer can make the following customizations for Order confirmation header level and limited fields at item level: Copy extrinsics from purchase order to order confirmation. Define a format that can be used to validate some standard or extrinsic fields. Make fields mandatory or optional, visible or hidden, or as read-only. Limit the length of the field, validate a specific format, and allow or disallow a set of characters. Use different type of controls, such as Text, Text box, drop down list, radio button, and so on. To customize a document refer to . Master Data Management SAP Business Network now offers you the ability to centrally manage all types of master data codes, including Unit of Measure (UOM). The new Manage Code Lists page allows you to view all code lists available to your organization. When viewing a specific type of master data code, you can Create, Import, Enable, and Disable individual codes of that type. The Import from CSV tab keeps a history of import events.  Note Required fields cannot be hidden. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 62 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Unit of Measure codes are based on ISO or UN/CEFACT standards, or they can be any arbitrary codes defined by your company. If unit of measure codes are company-specific, it's important to provide additional information about the codes to suppliers so they can understand what the codes mean in purchase orders and other SAP Business Network documents. SAP Business Network Trading Partner Buyer can use Master List in the Settings page to manage the unit of measure codes by downloading the code list template, upload the code list values, view code list, and enable and disable codes. Additional types of master data codes are available depending on your permissions and entitlements, including: Quality Notification Codes Quality Review Codes Carrier Codes Priority Codes Reason Codes Change Request Rejected Reason Codes Confirmation Rejected Reason Codes Example of User Interface Implementation Details Business End User Tasks Follow these steps to open Unit of Measurement master list: 1. Login to SAP Business Network buyer portal. 2. Click username and then choose Settings. 3. Click the Transactions tab and then select Master List to open Manage Code Lists page. 4. Click Unit of Measure to open the Unit of Measure master list. Enabling or Disabling Unit of Measure Codes Prerequisites Ensure that the following prerequisites are met: Ensure that you have been assigned Administrator role. Before you can enable or disable unit of measure codes, you must first upload them to your account. When you upload unit of measure codes, they are enabled by default.  Restriction Once you upload a unit of measure code to your account, you cannot delete it. However, you can update the Name, Symbol, and Description fields for a unit of measure code. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 63 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Enable and Disable Unit of Measure Codes Follow these steps to enable or disable unit of measure codes. 1. Choose Settings Transactions Master List to open the Manage Code Lists page. 2. Select Unit of Measure. This opens the Unit of Measure page that lists all the unit of measure that are added by default. 3. To enable the codes, select the disabled codes and to disable the codes select the enabled codes. Alternatively, click Disabled that displays the list of disabled codes from which you can select the codes to enable. On the other hand, click Enabled to display the list of enabled codes. 4. Select the code that you want to enable or disable.. You can select one or more codes. 5. Click Enable to enable the selected codes, or click Disable to disable them. Creating New Unit of Measure You can create multiple unit of measure codes by using the CSV file or create a new unit of measure code by using the Create button. Create a New Unit of Measure To create a new unit of measure, follow these steps: 1. In the Unit of Measure page, click Create. The following table shows the list of fields that you need to enter to create a new unit of measure code: Field Description Code Unit of measure code. Name Name of the code. Status By default, the status is Enabled. you can disable the code after you create it. Symbol Symbol that represents the unit of measure. Description Description for the unit of measure code. All the fields except the Description field is mandatory to create a new unit of measure code. 2. Click Create in the Additional Information section to add locale, name and description for the code that you added. 3. Click Create to save the unit of measure. Creating Unit of Measure Using the CSV Template You can download a CSV template to populate it with unit of measure codes to upload to your SAP Business Network account. To support different locales, save a different version of the file for each locale. For the Unit of Measure master list, click Export, and save the file to your computer. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 64 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- The unit of measure CSV template has the following four header rows at the top of the template: Row 1: Character encoding, for example,UTF-8. Row 2: Field names (Code, Name, Symbol, Description, and Code Language). Row 3: Whether the field is required or optional. All fields except the Description field is optional Row 4: Data type and maximum length (for example, "String 100"). The following table shows an example of unit of measure information that you can add to the CSV template: Code Name Symbol Description 2N dB decibel decibel 2P kbyte kilobyte kilobyte 2Q kBq kilobecquerel kilobecquerel 2R kCi kilocurie kilocurie DZN dozen DOZ dozen PK pack PK pack TP ten pack TP ten pack To activate the list in your account, upload strings for at least the English locale. To upload the CSV file, follow these steps: 1. Click Import from CSV. You can work with CSV file in three ways: download a template and start fresh. start working with the master list that you downloaded by clicking the Export button. download any of the existing CSV file and work on that. 2. Click Download Template to download a new template. 3. Click Open File to download an existing CSV file. 4. Fill in the CSV template with information about unit of measure information codes for one or more locales. 5. Save the file and click Upload. 6. Browse to the file and click Upload to upload the CSV file with the new entries. SAP Business Network treats the unit of measure code uploaded as follows: If a new file is uploaded using the template, all the entries are appended to the master list. However, the status of the code is disabled and you need to enable them after they are added.  Note If there is no symbol for a code, we recommend that you repeat the Code value in the Symbol field. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 65 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- If the master list is exported and changes are made to the master list and uploaded, then the entries are handled in the following way: if there are any codes that are deleted in the CSV and are not referred anywhere, then they are deleted. if there are any codes that are deleted in the CSV file and are referred, then the status is changed to disabled. any new entries added to the master list are appended to the existing list and the status is disabled.You need to enabled them after they are added. If an existing file is opened and modified, then the new entries are appended to the master list. Enable the code after they are added. Update Personal Information The Personal Information page includes the user name, password, name, and other information about the current user. Only the account administrator’s name and email address are included in the company profile. Context All users have access to the User Account page, which contains basic contact information, preferred language setting, time zone and address for that specific user. The only other areas that a user can see are those allowed by their role permissions. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Settings . 2. Click User Account under under User Preferences. 3. On the User Account page, choose Account Information tab. 4. Click Edit. 5. Update values on the Account Information section as necessary, noting the following constraints and guidelines: User Name is a value you enter when you sign in to SAP Business Network. A user name must be in the format of an email address (name @ domain .com); however, SAP Business Network does not send messages to the address. User names are case-sensitive, can contain any English character, and cannot contain any punctuation except the ampersand and period required by the name @ domain .com format. Email Address is where SAP Business Network sends account notifications. By default, SAP Business Network sends all notifications to the account administrator. If you change your email address, SAP Business Network sends an email to the newly updated email address requesting you to confirm the email address. You must use the link in the email to activate and sign in to the account. First Name is the first name of the user. Last Name is the last name of the user. 6. Update the values in the Preferences section, as necessary: Preferred Language is the language of notifications that SAP Business Network sends you. This is different than your web browser’s language setting, which controls the user interface and actions you initiate there. Preferred Time Zone controls how SAP Business Network displays dates and times on purchase orders routed by fax or email. Date and time stamps are displayed as GMT.. 7. Update the phone number along with the region, area code and extension if applicable in the Contact Information section. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 66 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- 8. Click Change Address if you want change your address. 9. Click Save. Account Administration Account Adminstration section of User Settings Settings page allows you to create a user, create a role, assign permissions, add user to role, set preferred timezone and currency and configure multifactor authentication settings. Creating a User You can set up sign in credentials and assign permissions to access an SAP Business Network account. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. Before you create a user, you can use the Filter function in the Manage Users page that you can open by clicking Account Settings Settings Manage Users . 1. Use th search attribute as you wish: User Name, Email Address, or First or Last Name. 2. Enter a search attribute value in the text box. 3. Enter additional search values for the same search attribute as desired, up to 10. 4. Click Serch icon. Context Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings . 2. Click Manage Users. The Manage Users page appears. 3. Click Create. The Create User page appears. 4. Enter a user name, email address, first and last name, and optionally a phone number for this user. 5. Select a role in the Roles section.  Note You can search with only one attribute type at a time.  Restriction You can create no more than 6,000 users. When an account has more than 1,000 users, SAP Business Network displays a simplified view of the Manage Users page. You can create only one user for each employee who performs tasks on SAP Business Network. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 67 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- 6. Click Create. Creating a Role Buyer administrators and users assigned a role with the User Administration permission can define new roles with a specific set of user permissions that determine what the assigned users can see or do in SAP Business Network. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. Before creating your first role, you might want to review the list of permissions. This list is useful for planning your approach to roles. Some companies create broadly defined roles that include all or most of the available permissions, while others create specialized roles that include narrow sets of permissions. By planning your approach to roles, you can prevent confusion for your account users and maximize the efficiency of your team after roles are in place. Before creating new roles, use the Permission dropdown menu to filter the Roles table for existing roles that already include that permission. Context A role defines a user function within SAP Business Network. You assign roles when you create users. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings . The Settings page appears. 2. Click Manage Roles 3. Click Create. 4. Enter a distinctive name for the role. 5. Enter a description to record your intentions for this role. Descriptions can be useful later, if you want to review or revise the structure of your roles. 6. Select one or more permissions for the new role. Each role must have at least one permission. 7. Select one or more users to assign the role to those selected users. 8. Click Create. Results  Restriction You can create no more than 25 custom roles. SAP Business Network does not notify users of changes to roles. Before you make changes, you might want to inform users who will be affected.  Note You can also select all permissions by clicking on the checkbox at the top left of the list of permissions. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 68 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- SAP Business Network creates the role and returns you to the Manage Roles page. Configuring Multifactor Authentication Settings Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings . 2. Click Account Security. 3. Click Multi-Factor Authentication Login. 4. Click Multi-Factor Authentication for Critical Fields. 5. Enter a value in the Time allowed to skip multi-factor authentication setup box. This field specifies the maximum number of days the user can skip the multifactor authentication setup when an administrator has enabled it for that user. The default value is 5 days. 6. The Maximum multi-factor authentication attempts before user lockout field displays the maximum number of invalid multifactor authentication attempts that the user can make. The default value is 5 attempts. After the number of invalid attempts specified in this field, the user account is locked. It can be unlocked only by an administrator. 7. The Grace period to skip activating multi-factor authentication field displays 24 hours, which is the grace period that is skipped before activating multi-factor authentication. 8. The Multi-factor authentication lockout duration displays the default value of 1 hour after which the user account is automatically unlocked and can be re-used. If the user gets locked a second time, the default value becomes 2 hours minutes, and the user is unlocked only after 2 hours. If the user gets locked a third time, the user account is locked for good, and can be unlocked only by an administrator. 9. Click Save. Timezone and Currency Settings In the Timezone and Currency settings, you can set the following options: Preferred Timezone controls how SAP Business Network displays dates and times on purchase orders routed by fax or email. Date and time stamps are displayed as GMT (Greenwich Mean Time) +/-. Preferred Currency is the currency that SAP Business Network uses for all entered and displayed monetary amounts in your account. These settings affect how SAP Business Network displays date/time stamps and currency to all account users. Supplier Management  Note Users can contact their administrator at any time during this period to get their account unlocked. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 69 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Configuring Supplier Group Rules Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions. Context You can use supplier groups for the following purposes: Customization projects—With the help of an SAP representative, you can customize the SAP Business Network supplier user interface by creating a customization project. You can then assign the customization project to specific supplier groups. A customization project can be used to do several things, such as customize supplier profile requirements, add invoice or ship notice fields, control the behavior of order confirmation fields, or enable CSV invoices. Transaction rules—You can use supplier groups to organize your suppliers according to different order confirmation and ship notice rules, service sheet rules, and invoicing rules, including country-based rules. If you subscribe to an SAP Ariba invoice conversion services (ICS) solution, you can create supplier groups for the suppliers who send paper invoices to the ICS provider. Typically, buying organizations want the invoice rules for ICS invoices to be less stringent than the rules for non-ICS invoices, to prevent some of the automatic validation that occurs with the default rules. For more information about invoice conversion, see the SAP Business Network Guide to Invoice Conversion. Discount management—If your organization uses SAP Ariba Invoice Management or SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing with an SAP Ariba payment module, and discount management is enabled for these solutions, you can define multiple discount offers and then assign them to supplier groups. Custom PDF layouts—With the help of an SAP representative, you can define custom PDF layouts for purchase orders and ship notices and then assign them to supplier groups. Procedure 1. Choose UserSettings Settings . 2. Choose Supplier Group Rules in the Transaction section. The Supplier Group Rules page appears. 3. Click Create. The Supplier Group page appears. 4. Enter a meaningful group name and description and click OK. Suppliers do not see your group names or descriptions. 5. To change transaction rules for the group, click Supplier Group Transaction Rules. The Supplier Group Transaction Rules page appears. The settings you make here affect only this group of suppliers. 6. When you are finished configuring transaction rules, click OK to save your settings and close the Supplier Group Transaction Rules page. 7. Click OK to save the supplier group. SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network allows easy integration of SAP ERP and the backend systems with SAP Business Network and other solutions. This feature helps you to configure SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network from SAP Business Network. General Prerequisites SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network must be installed and configured to integrate with the customer ERP system. The user must have access to the Managed Gateway for Spend&Network interface. The buyer must have SSO enabled to authenticate into Managed Gateway for Spend&Network interface. Multi ERP setup and endpoint must have been configured correctly. Configuring the Integration To configure the integration between SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network and SAP Business Network, follow these steps: 1. Login as a buyer or supplier and navigate to User Settings Settings Manage Gateway for Spend & Network Setup . This option is available in the Integration section. Click the Integration tab and select this option. 2. Select Enable Manage Gateway for Spend & Network. 3. Select the data center from the list. 4. Click Save. 5. If there are any changes to the setup or change in the endpoint configuration, uncheck the Enable Manage Gateway for Spend & Network and then select again. 6. If there are changes in the data center click Edit and then select the data center. For change of data centre a revalidation is needed. 7. Click Reset in the dialog to reset the cofiguration. 8. Click Sign in to Manage Gateway for Spend & Network to use the SSO to login to SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. System ID, Endpoint Integration and Document Type Routing Configurations for Buyer Business Details Buyer administrators can configure end points in SAP Business Network to manage and control the flow of data from an SAP Ariba account to each of the various systems connected to it. An end point in SAP Business Network acts as a document routing placeholder that ensures documents from SAP Business Network are sent to the required destinations (systems). 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 71 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- These destinations could be external ERP systems and the SAP Ariba procurement solution. When the SAP Ariba end point is configured, SAP Business Network automatically configures a default routing of all documents. End points functionality in SAP Business Network focuses on applying logic to determine the destination system route for all inbound transactions from a supplier to the SAP Ariba procurement solution or external ERP. The legacy SAP Business Network includes multiple routing configurations, which makes it difficult for the buyer to do the configuration and also switching the routing when needed. SAP Business Network on BTP introduces a haromonized way of routing configuration that enables buyer to configure: Single and Multi-ERP System End Points End Point for SAP Business Network On Demand Solution like P2P and Invoice Management by the buyer user Examples of the User Interface The following image shows a sample System ID page: figure to be included Implementation Details General Prerequisites To configure end points, you must have been assigned an Administrator role. Authorizations End Points Integration If your organization has more than one business application, you can create an ID for each of them in SAP Business Network. This allows you to easily manage all transactions with suppliers using a single SAP Business Network account. To use multiple business applications with a single SAP Business Network account, you must create a System ID for each business application. To create a system ID, follow these steps: 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Settings page, go to Integration and Document Routing section, and then choose System IDs and Enpoints (Document Routing). 3. Click Create to create a new system ID. 4. Enter the system ID. 5. Select any one of the business application from the available options given below: Ariba Procurement Solution Other cXML Compatible Appications 6. Click Create. SAP Business Network returns to the Create System ID screen. 7. Select the data center from the drop-down list. 8. Click Create. The system displays the Bill to Addresses tab.  Note Refer to <link to SAP note> for further boundary conditions of <name of the innovation, for example, name of app or API>. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 72 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Assigning Bill To Address 1. Click Assign to display the Assign Bill to Addresses screen. You can either search for an address or select from the list of addresses that are available for that buyer. The addresses are listed from the Global Address Book. You can select multiple address for a system ID. You either create or new address or edit an existing address by clicking the Create or Edit Bill To Addresses button. 2. Select the Bill to Addresses and then click Assign. The selected company and the details are listed. 3. Click Save to assing the bill to addresses to the system ID. Configuring End Points To configure the end points, follow these steps 1. Click the Endpoints tab and click Create to create a new end point. 2. Enter the end point ID. 3. Select the integration type from the list. You can select from cXML, OData or cXML and OData 4. Click Create. cXML Setup Several SAP Ariba applications, communicate with SAP Business Network using cXML (commerce eXtensible Markup Language). To enable this communication, you need to configure the authentication method and endpoint integration of your application. In the Authentication Method section, click Edit and choose the authentication method from the dropdown: Shared Secret. (Default) Enter a confidential text string as your shared secret. The shared secret is used to authenticate all cXML transactions between your organization and SAP Business Network. If you change your shared secret, you must also make the same change in your cXML-enabled application. If the values do not match, your documents cannot be delivered. To change your shared secret, you must enter the current value in the Current Shared Secret text box. If you forget your shared secret, SAP Business Network Customer Support must reset it. Choose Contact Support from the Help menu, and in the Support page set Category of Issue to “Reset Shared Secret” and click Submit. Certificate. Purchase and maintain a digital certificate signed by a trusted certificate authority. Paste the signed client certificate into the Certificate text box. Your website and SAP Business Network use this certificate for cXML authentication. You can also use the backup certificate if your primary certificate becomes invalid. Backup certificates are useful when your primary certificate expires or when you need to perform certificate maintenance. Digital certificates require more setup steps, they cost money, and they expire over time. However, they might be more compatible with your organization’s security strategy.You can also use a backup digital certificate. For a list of SAP Business Network’s trusted certificate authorities, see the cXML Solutions Guide. Configuring Endpoint Integration In the Endpoint Integration section, click edit and select one of the options listed below: If you select Profile URL, do the following: 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 73 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- If you use Ariba Buyer with contract collaboration, SAP Ariba Sourcing to create SAP Business Network Discovery postings, or SAP Business Network Adapter, enter the externally accessible URL of your SAP Ariba application or SAP Business Network Adapter application in the Profile URL text box. Specify a URL with an https prefix so communication is encrypted. For example: If you use both Ariba Buyer with contract collaboration and SAP Ariba Sourcing with the Public RFX feature, enter your Ariba Buyer cXML channel URL or your SAP Ariba Sourcing cXML channel URL in the Profile URL text box. Specify a URL with an https prefix so communication is encrypted. For example: Click Clear Profile Cache to clear the cXML profile cached on SAP Business Network. The next time SAP Business Network needs to send you a cXML document, it gets your cXML profile instead of using the cached profile, which can be up to 24 hours old. This function is helpful when developing support for the Profile transaction. Select POST URL if you want to receive documents through POST method and enter the URL in the POST URL text box. Select cXML Pending Queue if you want store documents that are addressed to you to a temporary queue before the application downloads them regularly from SAP Business Network. Click Save to save the endpoint integration method. Document Routing The following table lists the default document routing for various document types: Group/Category Actions Ordering Purchase Order Send a copy of a purchase order originating in the external system to the Ariba on demand solution: Routes all purchase orders (POs) to the destination (SAP Business Network solution or an external ERP). Configuring Content Management System (CMS) Settomg If you use the content management system (CMS) to manage customer catalogs in your procurement application, then you must configure the end point URL of your data center to enable the flow of customer catalog data from SAP Business Network to your procurement application. Click Save to save your changes. Compliance Audit Log Management on SAP Business Network on BTP Business Details 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 77 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- The SAP Business Network audit service, logs selected user and administration actions performed in SAP Business Network applications. It also logs user interface audit actions like create, download, purge, or delete audit reports. The audit actions are divided into the following categories: Generic audit actions - purge, delete and download audit reports Inegrated audit actions - create audit reports For more information about audit logs for buyers, see Audit Logs for Buyers. For more information about audit logs for suppliers, see Audit Logs for Suppliers. The SAP Business Network on BTP audit service enables administrators and security personnel to take a detailed look at what occurs in their SAP Business Network site, reproduce potential malicious activities of users and administrators, monitor administrative activities, like configuration changes, and retrieve forensic evidence if a security breach occurs. The SAP Business Network audit service records activities and events relevant for security auditing. You can access audit service records for evaluation in the form of security audit reports. In legacy SAP Business Network Audit Classic is where you can view the audit logs. In SAP Business Network on BTP, all audit logs are now written to BTP and retrieved from BTP. The main difference of audit between SAP Business Network on BTP and legacy SAP Business Network is that in legacy SAP Business Network the audit events were generated in a synchronous manner, providing a real-time view of the audit trail. Whereas in SAP Business Network on BTP you first need to create an audit repor, download it to view them. To view audit logs, click Account Settings Settings and then choose Audit Log Standard from the Compliance section. Implementation Details General Prerequisites Ensure that the user have the following permissions to access audit logs: User Administration Audit Log Administration Business End User Tasks The SAP Business Network audit service log entries contain identifying information, such as user, event type, date, and time. When users change data, the SAP Business Network audit service records both the old and new value. The SAP Business Network audit service creates a log entry when a user, integration tool, or scheduled event performs the following actions: Changes a user's authorization Exports or downloads data Creates, edits, or deletes data Authenticates a user Changes system configuration Accesses or changes sensitive information The SAP Business Network audit service also records user consent to privacy policies, including the version number of the policy and whether the policy was a custom privacy policy or the SAP Business Network SAP Business Network Privacy Statement. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 78 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- For information about the types of actions recorded by the SAP Business Network audit service, refer to Audit Log Criteria for SAP Business Network. Audit Events and Reports The Audit events and reports page is where you view the list of audit reports that are created. The audit log report has filters for filtering the reports. Creating an Audit Report Follow these steps to create an audit report: 1. Click Create. 2. The Create Audit Report page displays the following fields: Fields Description Name This is a mandatory field. Enter a name for the report. Event type This is a mandatory field. Choose the type of logged audit events for which you want to create a report. For example, choose Security to view security critical events. Choose Data access to view data access related activities. The available event types are: Security Data access Data modification Configuration modification Generic action Integration From This is a mandatory field. Choose the start date for the events. You can choose a valid date (within the last 3 months) using the calendar tool. To Choose the end date for the events. You can choose a valid date (within the last 3 months) using the calendar tool. 3. Click Create to create an audit report with the specified name. Viewing the List of Audit Reports The Audit Events and reports page displays the list of reports that have been generated. In this page, you can use the search filters to look for a particular report, download a report, or delete a report. Search a report User the search filters to search for a report. The available fields are: Name Event Type 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 79 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Status After entering the required search criteria, click Apply to search for audit reports based on the search filters. Click Clear to clear the search filter fields. The Audit Reports Log section shows all generated reports. Each row in the table displays information for the generated report such as name of the report, who created it, when it was created, type of the event, and the status. The following table explains the statuses that appear on the Status column. Status Description PROCESSING Indicates that the report creation is in progress. COMPLETED Indicates that the report is successfully generated and can be downloaded. An email is sent to the user when the report is generated. FAILED Indicates that the report generation has failed. An email notification is sent to the user when the report generation fails. PURGE SCHEDULED Indicates that the report will be purged. An email notification is sent to the user one day before the report is automatically purged. From the day the notification is sent to the user and till the report is purged, the report will be in purged scheduled status. There is no retention period for the purged report. PURGED Indicates that the report has been purged. SAP Business Network purges the generated report after 30 days. A reminder email is sent to the user one day before the actual purge. If the user wishes to download the report can do so. The status of the report is changed to Purged scheduled. The purged reports are permanently deleted and there is no retention period. Audit Reports The Audit Report Logs section lists all generated reports. Click Download to download the generated report in XLS format. Click Delete to delete a generated report. Click Create to create a new audit report. SAP Business Network Users and Roles By creating roles and then adding users to them, the SAP Business Network administrator controls who can sign in to your organization’s account and which areas of the service each user can access. Mass Uploading Users Using an Excel Template Account and user administrators can create and update users through mass upload using an Excel template. Using an Excel template, user administrators can perform the following actions: create or update users, assign roles, assign business units, authorization profile assignments. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. For the mass upload capability using an Excel template, all required fields must be filled out in the Excel template before uploading it. List of the required fields in the Excel template: Action User Name Corporate User Name (if SSO is enabled) Email Address First Name Last Name Has Limited Access; if this value is set to "No", at least one role must be assigned Only Excel files in the .XLSX format can be uploaded Only five roles, business units, and authorization profiles can be assigned using an Excel template. These roles, business units, and authorization profiles must exist already, and cannot be created using Excel upload. If additional ones are needed, they can be added from the user interface. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 81 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Change of first name, last name, or email address fields is not allowed when updating user details using Excel upload, consistent with the handling in the user interface. The number of users entered in the Excel file must not exceed 500. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. Click the Upload Users button on the Manage Users page. 4. Click the Upload button on the Upload Users page. 5. Click the Download template link on the Upload File dialog box. 6. Open the Excel template and fill out the required fields. 7. Click the Browse button on the Upload Files dialog box, choose the filled out Excel template from your computer and enter a descriptive name. 8. Click the Upload button. 9. Click the Refresh Status button on the Upload Users page and wait until it shows status Completed. If the status is Completed With Errors or Failed, select the download icon ( ) in the Log column to see the reasons for errors and to correct them. 10. Click the Done button. This opens the Manage Users page where you can see the uploaded users. Revoke User Access and Remove a User's Personal Information SAP Business Network users can request the administrator for their account to remove their personal information from the system. If approved, the user can’t sign in to SAP Business Network any longer, and their personal information is no longer visible to users, including in transaction documents shared and exchanged with business partners. Restrictions Comments or attachment files associated with transaction documents aren’t affected when users remove personal information. Therefore, avoid entering personal information in comments or attached files. After a user’s revocation of user access request is approved, their personal information is pseudonymized in SAP Business Network transaction documents. However, transaction documents that were integrated with other systems (such as an ERP) or downloaded before the request was approved may still have the user’s personal information. The customer needs to take additional action, including informing impacted business partners, to remove it. If a customer needs to re-identify a user that has been pseudonymized for legal purposes, the administrator of the account can provide that information. Reassigning a User Sign In If a user has left the company, you can reassign that user’s sign-in to another individual, to retain the user setup and data. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions.  Note For audit and compliance purposes, the user's personal information is still visible to the user who is the administrator for your SAP Business Network account. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 82 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Context When an employee leaves the company or changes jobs and no longer uses the SAP Business Network account in their name, the administrator should either delete the user or reassign the user’s sign-in to another individual. If you want to retain the user’s setup and data, reassign the sign-in. If you want to delete the user’s setup and data, delete the user. Procedure 1. Sign in using the user’s user name and password. If you do not know the password, click Help Support to contact SAP Business Network Support. 2. Choose Account Settings Manage Profile . 3. On the Configuration page, choose Personal Information. 4. Change the user name and password and optionally other information. 5. Click OK. 6. On the Configuration page, choose Notifications. 7. Make any modifications to notification emails based on the user sign in reassignment. 8. Click OK. Viewing and Exporting Revoked Buyer Users As an administrator, you can view the list of revoked users and export the table to an XLS file. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Revoked Users. 3. The Revoked Users table lists all users whose access to SAP Business Network has been revoked. 4. To export the table, click the  Table Options Menu icon, and choose Export All Rows. Results An XLS file containing the list of revoked users downloads to your computer. Workflow for Removing Personal Information for a User from SAP Business Network This procedure describes the workflow for removing personal information for an SAP Business Network user:  Tip You can filter the table by User Name, Email Address, or First or Last Name. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 83 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Workflow for Removing Personal Information for a User 1. A user signs in to the SAP Business Network portal to request the removal of their personal information. 2. The administrator for the account receives an email notifying them of the user's request. 3. The administrator signs in to the SAP Business Network portal and approves or rejects the user's request. 4. If the administrator approved the request, the user's personal information is removed. 5. If the administrator approved the request, the user can't sign in to SAP Business Network. Configure Retention Period and Manage Deletion of Revoked Users in SAP Business Network As a buyer administrator, configure a retention period for revoked users. SAP Business Network users can request the administrator of their account to remove their personal information from the system. This is called a revocation request. If the request is approved, users cannot sign in to SAP Business Network any longer, and their personal information is no longer visible to other users. As an administrator, you can configure a retention period for the user data of all the revoked users in your organization. The data of revoked users is automatically removed from SAP Business Network after this retention period is reached. In the meantime, you can view the list of revoked users in the Revoked Users tab. You must have configured the retention period before accepting or rejecting any revocation request. If the retention period for an organization is not configured, SAP Business Network prompts you to configure the retention period before you can act on a revocation request. You can change the retention period at any time before the previously configured retention period is reached. The newly configured retention period takes effect immediately. The retention period must be configured in months, and must be between 1 and 999 months. SAP Business Network Permissions A permission grants access to a certain area of the SAP Business Network user interface. Each role includes one or more permissions. For example, the Archive Access permission grants access to the Archived Invoices tab and the functionality of the Invoices area. Any user who is assigned a role that includes the Archive Access permission can access the Archived Invoices tab. You can view the list of available permissions while creating a role. See Creating a Role.  Note Only users with non-administrator roles can request revocation of their access from SAP Business Network. Administrators cannot raise a revocation request. If administrators want to request revocation of their access from SAP Business Network, they must transfer their administrator role to another user. For more information, see Transferring Administration Ownership. For this reason, it is not for production use. For more information, please visit https://help.sap.com/docs/disclaimer. 5/6/26, 7:27 AM 1 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Change in the Names of SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway and Ariba Network SAP has renamed SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway and Ariba Network to SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network and SAP Business Network respectively. This document uses the revised names. This change is effective from the SAP Ariba 2302 release and it does not affect the functionality of SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway and Ariba Network. The UI components of SPRO nodes contain the short name, Managed Gateway for Spend&Network. The content on the Performance Assistant pages associated with the SPRO nodes displays the name as SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. Also, the name Ariba Network is renamed as SAP Business Network throughout the SPRO menu components. Exceptions The product name Ariba Network adapter for SAP NetWeaver is not updated in this document. The names of the integration scenarios that contain the name Ariba Network are not updated in this document. The technical names of the ABAP objects in the SPRO nodes associated with the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network, addons for SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA and SAP Business Network are not renamed. SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide This guide is for SAP Ariba administrators or business users responsible for setting up SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA with SAP Ariba solutions and SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA buyers can integrate SAP Ariba solutions with SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network and use the functionalities integrated across SAP Ariba solutions. Buyers can find information about the system requirements, data flows, and prerequisites that they require before sending master data and transaction data through the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. SAP Ariba recommends that you read this guide first and then the following guides to know more about the supported functionalities. This guide applies to: SAP Ariba Buying SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing SAP Ariba Invoice Management SAP Ariba Catalog SAP Business Network Commerce Automation  Caution SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network is not audited for compliance with the Payment Card Industry Standard (PCI). You should not submit Purchasing Card (PCard) data in transactions sent to the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. SAP Ariba may reject transactions that include data in the field designated for PCard use. 5/6/26, 7:27 AM 2 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- SAP Ariba Contracts SAP Ariba Collaborative Sourcing SAP Ariba Discount Management SAP Ariba Invoice Management SAP Business Network SAP Ariba Payables SAP Ariba Spot Buy Catalog SAP Ariba strategic sourcing solutions SAP Ariba Sourcing SAP Ariba Supplier Information and Performance Management SAP Ariba Supplier Lifecycle and Performance SAP Ariba Supplier Risk Related Guides SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Installation Guide SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Configuration Guide SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Migration Guide Introduction You've decided to integrate your SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA system with SAP Business Network and SAP Ariba solutions to efficiently manage supplier interactions across the spend management lifecycle. The SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network simplifies and accelerates the integration. This document is intended for business users and administrators and provides an overview of the supported functionalities. In addition, it includes information about software components, access rights, and system requirements on SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA side before you can begin the integration process. Please note that this guide does not provide process descriptions on how to carry out the integration. Refer to the following documents for information about: Installation and configuration of SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA add-on Integration steps on the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network Configuration requirements on the SAP Business Network and SAP Ariba solutions. SAP Help Portal Overview of the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network Solution for Buyers SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network provides a simple and efficient Integration-as-a-Service (IaaS) solution. SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network facilitates the integration of buyers' SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA systems with SAP Business Network and SAP Ariba solutions. By leveraging the SAP Cloud Platform integration, SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network: Supports the configuration on the basis of the core ERP capabilities Supports certificate-based or basic user name and password based authentication for connectivity Offers tools such as: Document Validator tool to validate documents for schema, content and transformation Supplier Reporting to view the integration status of their suppliers Transaction Tracker to search and track transaction status Test Central to help users perform self-test before moving to a production environment In addition, SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network: Simplifies integration by using a guidance-based setup Reduces the integration deployment time 5/6/26, 7:27 AM 4 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Provides an integrated test framework to verify various scenarios configured in the system Facilitates smoother upgrade of the solution Aligns with SAP standard software delivery processes by supporting download through the SAP Service Marketplace and by addressing issues with standard SAP Notes and correction instructions Uses the single sign-on functionality to enable buyers to access their SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network account from their SAP Business Network, SAP Ariba Procurement solutions, or SAP Ariba strategic sourcing solutions account. The following section describes the behavior in SAP ERP for requisitions with taxes, charges, and discounts received from the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions: The following examples describe the behavior of SAP ERP when requisitions received from SAP Ariba Procurement solutions contain a: Line item with a charge From SAP Ariba Procurement solutions: A line item of USD 100 has a shipping charge of USD 10. Result in SAP ERP: Single line with amount = USD 110. Line item with charges From SAP Ariba Procurement solutions: A line item of USD 100 has a shipping charge of USD 10 and a handling charge of USD 5. Result in SAP ERP: Single line with amount = USD 115. Line item with a charge and tax on charge From SAP Ariba Procurement solutions: A line item of USD 100 has a shipping charge of USD 10 along with a tax amount of USD 5. Result in SAP ERP: Two lines: First line contains the actual line item amount = USD 100. Second line contains the total amount of shipping charge and tax on the shipping charge = USD 15. Line item with a non-deductible tax amount From SAP Ariba Procurement solutions: A line item of USD 100 has a non-deductible tax of USD 5. Result in SAP ERP: Single line with amount = USD 105. Line item with a deductible tax amount From SAP Ariba Procurement solutions: A line item of USD 100 has a deductible tax of USD 5. Result in SAP ERP: Single line with amount = USD 100. Line item with a discount From SAP Ariba Procurement solutions: A line item of USD 100 has a discount of USD 10. Result in SAP ERP: Single line with amount = USD 90. Prerequisites Restrictions Prerequisites  Note The budget reserved amount is equal to the final requisition amount derived in SAP ERP after calculating all applicable taxes, charges, and discounts. 5/6/26, 7:27 AM 91 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Maintain the following configurations on SAP Ariba Procurement solutions before sending purchase requisitions to the SAP ERP system: Enable the following parameters: Application.Budget.StartDateToEnableRealTimeBudgetChecksInExternalSystem Application.Budget.RealTimeBudgetSynchronousSubmit Application.Budget.EnableFundsManagement Application.Budget.SendEarlierVersionRequisitionToExternalSystemForBudgetReversal Application.Procure.EnableTaxesChargesAndDiscount Application.Procure.EnableServiceItemFieldInRequisition . Configure the following integration events: Export Requisitions for User-Initiated External Budget Check Export Requisitions to External System to Revert Funds Export Requisitions to Get the Accounting Information for Funds Management Export Submitted Requisitions for External Budget Check Export Modified Requisitions To Revert Funds Before creating requisitions, if not already applied, apply the following SAP Notes in your SAP ERP: SAP Note 1279915 - Purchase requisition BAPI: Release date is not transferred. SAP Note 970686 - Item category change deletes source of supply. SAP Note 962638 - Valuation price is not output. SAP Note 1510700 - BAPI_PR_CHANGE: account assignment failure. Ensure that the Business Function, LOG_MM_CI2 switch MM_SFWS_SC2 is active, if you want to include the budget information in purchase requisitions containing service line items. To display an error message in the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions when you exceed the budget, perform the following in SAP ERP: Set appropriate tolerance limits for the General Budget Profile and the Budget Profile Investment using the Define Tolerance Limits for Availability Control. Set the parameter Availability control action to 3 (Error message). To avoid calculation errors in SAP ERP, you must not exceed the configured decimal limit in the parameter Application.Procure.ERPAmountPrecision when entering values in the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions. Restrictions SAP Ariba supports only web services to integrate corresponding transactional documents associated with a requisition containing the budget information. The integration does not support percentage-based condition. Only amount-based conditions are supported. Purchase Order Buyers create a purchase order to request for product or services from suppliers. A purchase order is sent from SAP Ariba Procurement solutions to SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA and upon approval the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions would send it to SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network then routes the purchase order to the appropriate supplier using the supplier's preferred order routing method. The following types of purchase orders are supported: Standard purchase orders Service purchase orders 5/6/26, 7:27 AM 93 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Prerequisites Restrictions Integrating Amount-Based Purchase Orders The SAP Ariba Procurement solutions allow you to export amount-based purchase orders to SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. For amount- based purchase orders, the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions map the amount to the quantity in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, and sets the unit price to 1. For example, if the amount of the purchase order in the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions is $95, it is exported to SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA as a receipt with a quantity of 95 and with a price of $1. Integrating Changed and Canceled Purchase Orders The SAP Ariba Procurement solutions can export changed and canceled purchase orders to SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. The following are important notes on exporting changed and canceled purchase orders to SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA: If you enable the change/cancel purchase order feature, users must change or cancel orders through the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions and not through SAP ERP. Therefore, apply the appropriate authorization concept in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to prevent users from changing purchase orders directly in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. Plant data is not editable in the following situations: Purchase Order Line Item is partially or fully received in the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions or SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. Purchase Order Line Item is partially or fully invoiced in the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions or SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. Importing Header Status of Purchase Orders When changed orders are in a Received, Receiving, Invoiced, or Invoicing state, the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions cannot cancel them. Similarly, when purchase orders have been received or invoiced in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, the cancel export to SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA fails. If an order reaches SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA successfully, its status can still change in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. For example, if you receive against an order in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, a subsequent cancel order from SAP Ariba Procurement solutions is certain to be rejected. To reduce the occurrence of such situations, the scheduled task ProcessERPHeaderStatusPull, imports header status information from SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. This task sets the ERPAllowCancel field, which specifies whether or not the order can be canceled.  Note Use ProcessERPHeaderStatusPull only if you have enabled change and cancel order exports to SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, and you are doing a lot of receiving in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. The ProcessERPHeaderStatusPull scheduled task does not eliminate all the cancel export failure errors. SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA uses many factors to determine if it is possible to cancel an order. However, the status import is based on the invoicing and receiving status. This is applicable for the web services channel. For file channel, this is a batch data import and pulled as part of status import. 5/6/26, 7:27 AM 94 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- ProcessERPHeaderStatusPull imports the status for all orders that are in the Ordered state for the time period (days before the current date) you specify in the QueryPeriod parameter. Integrating Closed Purchase Orders SAP Ariba Procurement solutions Cloud integration enables buyers using SAP Ariba Procurement solutions integrated with SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to integrate purchase order closure information from SAP Ariba Procurement solutions with SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. The integration supports header level and line level close. Integration of purchase order closure information between SAP Ariba Procurement solutions and SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA ensures that the purchase order information in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions and SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA is in sync, and improves the fund allocation and utilization. SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA receives the status when a purchase order is closed in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions. SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA releases any unused fund that was allocated for the purchase order and sets any open quantity to zero. However, note that the integration also updates the status of corresponding purchase orders in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA when buyers reopen purchase orders in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions. If a buyer reopens a closed purchase order in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions, SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA restores any fund that was released as unused when the purchase order was closed. In Cloud integrations, SAP Ariba Procurement solutions sends the purchase order closure information to SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA in real time. In SAP Ariba Procurement solutions, buyers can specify a status while they close a purchase order. The following table lists the status messages that buyers can set in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions and the corresponding status update in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA: Status in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions Status in SAP ERP Order Closed for Receiving Delivery Complete Order Closed for Invoicing Final Invoice Order Closed for All Actions Delivery Complete and Final Invoice When buyers reopen purchase orders that were previously closed in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions, the status checkboxes, such as Delivery Complete or Final Invoice or both, in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA for the corresponding purchase orders are also cleared. Integrating Taxes and Charges This section describes the behavior in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA for purchase orders with taxes, charges, and discounts received from the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions: The following examples describe the behavior of SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA when purchase orders received from SAP Ariba Procurement solutions contain a: Line item with a charge From SAP Ariba Procurement solutions: A line item of USD 100 has a shipping charge of USD 10. Result in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA: Single line with amount = USD 110. Shipping charge = USD 10 is maintained as a condition in the Conditions tab of the purchase order transaction. Line item with charges From SAP Ariba Procurement solutions: A line item of USD 100 has a shipping charge of USD 10 and a handling charge of USD 5. Result in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA: Single line with amount = USD 115. Shipping charge = USD 10 and Handling charge = USD 5 are maintained as separate conditions in the Conditions tab of the purchase order transaction. 5/6/26, 7:27 AM 95 This is custom documentation. Tax code I1 is maintained in the Invoice tab of the purchase order transaction. Line item with a tax amount From SAP Ariba Procurement solutions: A line item of USD 100 has a tax code, for example, I1. Result in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA: Single line with amount = USD 100. Result in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA: Single line with amount = USD 90. Discount = USD 10 is maintained as a condition in the Conditions tab of the purchase order transaction. Using this feature, buyers can use attachments and comments with purchase orders in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA-integrated documents. In SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, the attachments and comments are processed as follows: Attachments Header level using the SAP Generic Object Services (GOS) for purchase orders. Line level using the SAP Document Management System (DMS) for purchase orders. Along with the attachments on the header and line level, the following additional information is sent from the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions to SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA: File name: Specifies file name. If this field is left blank in the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions, the file displays as unknown in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. File type: Specifies file extension. File size Comments on header and line level. For more information on defining lookup values, see Defining Values in the Lookup Table.  Note SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA truncates file name of attachments exceeding 50 characters (inclusive of extension). 5/6/26, 7:27 AM 96 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- If you modify a purchase order in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions by adding an attachment, the buyer’s SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA sends a corresponding purchase order with an attachment to SAP Business Network. Buyers can also include URL-based links to external information sources in line items of purchase orders. External information sources can include anything that a buyer wants to add to support an order item. Examples of such sources are supporting memos, technical drawings, or a link to a website containing item specifications. Buyers can choose to decide if they want to send the external information sources (attachments) as a copy or provide references to attachments as URL-based links. To provide the reference to an attachment, in the OrderRequestcXML, buyers can include the URL in the AttachmentReference element in the item's ItemDetails element. Suppliers can use the links to securely access external information sources using single sign-on (SSO). Comments Comments are supported for purchase orders at both the header and the line level. The comments field allows you to enter free form text that can be associated with a purchase order. You use the comments field to enter any additional information about a purchase order. Integrating Evaluated Receipt Settlement (ERS) for Purchase Orders The feature is supported in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions integrated with SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA using SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. The feature allows buyers to use Evaluated Receipt Settlement (ERS) to automatically settle confirmed material and service purchase orders. The flag for ERS is set in the vendor’s master record. The ERS flag must be enabled in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA and the vendor master data must be synchronized with the SAP Ariba solution so that the buyers can create a purchase order with ERS enabled line item and process it. Prerequisites Install the latest SAP Ariba Procurement solutions components. Configure the purchase order integration, change purchase order integration, and close purchase order integration between SAP Ariba Procurement solutions and SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. Enable the following asynchronous integration events in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions: Purchase Orders Export Purchase Orders Asynchronously  Note If all the attachments associated with a purchase order line item in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions are removed, the change PO triggered to the buyer's SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA subsequently does not contain an indicator for this deletion. Because of this problem, the attachments associated with the purchase order line item in the buyer’s SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA are not removed.  Note If the ERS flag is disabled in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA and if the vendor master data is not synchronized with the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions after this, a change purchase order processed from the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions with the ERS flag enabled for a line item will fail in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. 5/6/26, 7:27 AM 97 This is custom documentation. Restrictions The SAP Ariba Procurement solutions do not support exporting zero value amount for line items in amount-based purchase orders. The integration does not support percentage-based condition. Only amount-based conditions are supported. Purchase orders with a combination of charges with and without taxes are not supported. For a purchase order line item, only a summation of taxes is allowed. Multiple or nested tax lines are not supported. If the Account Assignment category is modified in the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions, the Account Assignment category is changed in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA does not support the Order Closed and Adjusted for Receiving and Closed for Change status for purchase orders. Purchase orders closed with either of these status flags in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions are not updated in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. Buyers cannot add or change the price-based quantity on a purchase order line item with charge. Purchase orders containing line items with a Price of 0 are not supported. For amount-based purchase orders: Split accounting is not supported and discounts cannot be applied. Input for Net Amount or Net Price Amount can support up to 28 characters. Input for Quantity can support up to 13 characters. SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA supports maximum 40 characters in line item text for create and change purchase orders. If the length of line item text imported from SAP Ariba Procurement solutions exceeds 40 characters, SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA would truncate the text. Deleting a comment on SAP Ariba Procurement solutions will not delete the corresponding comment in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. Attachments for service line items in purchase orders are supported only at the parent line level and not at the child line level. The attachment size cannot exceed 74 MB either at the header or line level (purchase orders). The attachment is associated with the latest IDoc. For the Japanese Yen (JPY), South Korean Won (KRW), and Vietnamese Dong (VND) currencies, you can enter upto 11 digits for amount. For purchase order and follow-on documents, SAP Ariba Procurement solutions support only the manual receipt – received by quantity (Commodity code, 1411) and manual receipt – received by amount (Commodity code, 44112002) receiving type fields. Service Requisitions and Service Purchase Orders Buyers create service requisitions in the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions to request for services performed by supplier organizations. While creating service requisitions, buyers can validate the requisitions for the availability of budgets in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. If budget is available in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, buyers would get a successful response. If the response is successful, the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions sends a request to SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to create a service requisition to reserve the fund. Buyers can delete or cancel a service requisition. In that case, the funds reserved for the requisition is released to the budget in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. When a service requisition is fully approved, the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions creates a service purchase order corresponding to the requisition. The service purchase order is then sent to SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA assigns a unique number to the service purchase order and sends it to the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions. SAP Ariba Procurement solutions then sends the purchase order to the supplier on the SAP Business Network. The Expected Amount field for service purchase orders in the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions is mapped to the Expected value under the tab Limits of the service order in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. The Expected Amount is added to the Net Price condition for the main line item. The create and change interfaces of service requisitions and service purchase orders support all scenarios related to the addition, modification, and deletion of the account assignments of child services and their splits. There is a limitation on SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA on the precision value for percentage and amount. You can configure the following parameters on SAP Ariba Procurement solutions to ensure the rounded-off value matches on SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA: Application.Procure.PercentagePrecisionForSplits - Set the precision for percentage. SAP ERP supports precision up to one decimal place.  Note When a split line item is deleted in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions, the line would reflect in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA with the value 0. 5/6/26, 7:27 AM 100 This is custom documentation. Service purchase orders created with the simplified procurement of services capability Buyers integrated with SAP Business Network, SAP Ariba Procurement solutions, and SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network can enable simplified procurement of services. This capability enables buyers to create service requisitions and service purchase orders without adding child items, and enables suppliers to invoice these orders without submitting service sheets. This capability simplifies and expedites the invoicing process for service orders. When a service purchase order created in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions is sent to SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, the purchase order is created with the GR-Bsd IV and S.-Based IV fields deselected in the Invoice tab, and the Goods Receipt Indicator field deselected in the Delivery tab. Based on the buyer configuration, either SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA or SAP Ariba Procurement solutions send the purchase order to SAP Business Network. Spend Limits for Unplanned Items In service purchase requisitions, buyers can specify the following limits for the amounts that can be spent on unplanned items: Contract limit - the maximum amount that can be spent on unplanned contract items. A contract must be selected before this amount can be specified. Other limit - the maximum amount that can be spent on unplanned non-contract items. When service sheets and invoices are submitted, the value of the unplanned contract and non-contract items are validated against these limits. SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network supports these fields when importing service requisitions from SAP Ariba Procurement solutions to SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. These fields in the associated service sheets and invoices are also supported. Account Assignment Category U (Unknown) Starting SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network, Release 2105 (Q2 2021), buyers on SAP Ariba Procurement solutions can export account assignment category U (Unknown) for service line items to SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA using the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. You can use account assignment category U (Unknown) when you are not certain of the appropriate account assignment category to which a service line item’s expenditure is to be assigned. When you assign account assignment category U (Unknown) to a service line item, you are not required to provide accounting information. When an SOW or a work order is updated in SAP Fieldglass, the corresponding service requisition is also updated in SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing through SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. However, the service purchase order reference is updated in SAP Fieldglass directly and not routed through SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. Similarly, when an SOW or a work order is closed in SAP Fieldglass, the corresponding service purchase order is closed in SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing directly. Prerequisites This section describes the prerequisites for this feature. SAP Ariba Procurement solutions must support the plant information master data and incorporate it in all relevant transactions. The plant information master data must be imported to SAP Ariba Procurement solutions. Goods Receipt A receipt is an acknowledgment of the goods that have arrived. The receiving process starts when an order has been sent to a supplier and the supplier ships goods in exchange. When the shipment arrives, the person who receives those items, submits a receipt to acknowledge that the items have indeed arrived. SAP Ariba provided integration code integrates receipts as goods receipts with Movement Type as 101. Create a negative receipt in the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions to reverse some received quantity as a result of incorrect shipment or manual errors. SAP Ariba provided integration code integrates negative receipts as goods receipts with Movement Type as 102. Exporting Amount-Based Receipts The SAP Ariba Procurement solutions allow you to receive based on quantity or amount. For amount-based receipts, the SAP Ariba integration code maps the amount to the quantity in SAP, and sets the price to 1. For example, if the amount of the receipt in the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions system is $95, it is exported to SAP as a receipt with a quantity of 95 and with a price of $1. Prerequisite Maintain the parameters for goods receipt. For more information, see SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Configuration Guide. To create receipts on the SAP ERP system and send them to SAP Ariba Procurement solutions, enable the task, Import Receipts from an External Application Asynchronously. To stop receipts from being sent from the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions to the SAP ERP system, disable the following tasks in the section, Integration Manager > Managed Gateway for Spend&Network on the Manage Managed Gateway for Spend&Network tasks page: Export Receipts Asynchronously Import Receipt Status Asynchronously When you disable these tasks, SAP Ariba Procurement solutions creates the receipt but does not send it to the SAP ERP system.  Note By default, when you run the integration event tasks to create receipts on the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions system, the receipt that is created on the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions system is also created again on the SAP ERP system. This leads to the duplication of the same receipt on both the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions and SAP ERP systems. 5/6/26, 7:27 AM 106 This is custom documentation.
