Data Deletion Criteria Page and Deleted Transactions Page The Data Deletion Criteria page (which is now renamed Deletion Settings for Transaction Data) and the Deleted Transactions page of SAP Business Network have a new, streamlined user interface. By adapting to SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP) and SAPUI5 technology, the two pages now enable you to manage deletion settings and deleted transactions more efficiently. Changes to the User Interface The following changes are made: The Data Deletion Criteria page is renamed Deletion Settings for Transaction Data. For the Deletion Settings for Transaction Data page: It shows two distinctive tabs for better organization and context: Recurring Deletion and One-Time Deletion. For each table in the two tabs, a search bar is added at the top right. You can enter text related to any attribute of the table to refine your search. For each table in the two tabs, the  Settings icon is added at the top right. You can use it to adjust the columns or sort the items.  Note Supplier users with administrator privileges have the API Development Access permission by default. The supplier administrator must first sign in to the SAP Ariba Developer Portal. The supplier organization is created in the SAP Ariba Developer Portal only after the supplier administrator signs in to the portal. Subsequently, supplier administrators can create users and selectively assign roles with the API Development Access permission. For more information, see Users and Roles. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 134 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- For each table in the two tabs, an  Export icon is added at the top right. You can use it to export the table to a spreadsheet. For the Deleted Transactions page: This page now has a direct entry point in the Compliance section of the Account Settings Settings page. It shows a Deleted Results table with a search bar, a  Settings icon, and an  Export icon. A detail page is available for each deleted result. You can download the deleted transactions from here. Implementation Details General Prerequisites You access these pages, you need the following user permissions: To access the Deletion Settings for Transaction Data page, you must have the Company Data Deletion Configuration user permission. To access the Deleted Transactions page, you must have the Transaction Data Export for Deleted Data user permission. Deletion Settings for Transaction Data (Suppliers) The administrator for your SAP Business Network account and other users with appropriate permission can specify the retention period for transaction documents. Additionally, SAP Business Network automatically deletes supplier master data after an extended period of inactivity. You may need to delete old transaction documents to meet regulatory needs in your country/region or business requirements in your organization. If you request recurring deletion of transaction data, the system deletes any transaction document sets older than the retention period every month. Each document set includes transaction documents and any associated attachments. You can also request a one-time deletion of transaction data. This operation is similar, but it happens only once, not every month. For example, you can delete your transaction data older than January 1, 2018. Types of Transaction Documents That Can Be Deleted The following transaction documents can be deleted: Purchase orders (orders and blanket orders) Order confirmations Ship notices Receipts  Note If a supplier account is deleted from the SAP Business Network, the RFx transactions responded by the supplier are not deleted immediately. The RFx transactions get deleted only after the buyers' and the suppliers' accounts associated with that RFx are deleted. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 135 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Service sheets Invoices, credit memos, and debit memos Payment documents SAP Business Network for Supply Chain transaction documents Quote requests and quote messages Associated attachments Workflow for Deleting Transaction Documents The following diagram shows the workflow for deleting transaction documents from SAP Business Network: Workflow for Deleting Transaction Documents from SAP Business Network Data Deletion Restrictions This feature doesn't affect archived invoices, which are stored separately. Once a document has been identified for deletion, it’s deleted even if you later opt out of data deletion. Please carefully configure the retention period for transaction documents. Deletion of transaction documents is an irreversible process. You can’t retrieve any transaction documents after they're deleted by the system. If you're using long-term archiving services, we strongly recommend that you specify a retention period for transaction documents that is greater than or equal to the longest archiving retention period legally required by countries/regions where you operate. If the system deletes your invoices, you can't search for those invoices in SAP Business Network. Your archived invoices, however, continue to be retained by TrustWeaver or Sovos (third-party systems that SAP Business Network uses to archive invoices) for the full legal retention period. Data Deletion Notifications You can enable the following notifications for data deletion:  Note SAP Business Network retains transaction data for a reasonable time after the 30-day grace period. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 136 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Notification Type Notifications Data Identification and Deletion Send a notification when the transaction documents have been identified for deletion Send a notification after deletion of transactions Requesting Recurring Deletion of Transaction Data for SAP Business Network Suppliers You can request to delete transactions older than a certain age in months on a recurring basis every month for your SAP Business Network account. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Company Data Deletion Configuration permission. See Permissions You Can Assign to Users. A transaction document is identified for deletion when all documents in its transaction document set are older than the data retention period. The transaction document set is the sequence of related documents exchanged between the buyer and supplier. The age of a document is based on its creation date or the date of its last status update, whichever is later. Buyers and suppliers maintain their own data retention period. Consequently, your buyers may keep copies of documents that you have deleted from your account. To receive an email notification when transaction documents for your deletion request are available to download, the administrator needs to set up notifications. Procedure 1. Go to Account settings Settings Compliance . 2. Select Deletion Settings for Transaction Data. The Deletion Settings for Transaction Data page appears. 3. In the Recurring Deletion tab, click the Set Up Now button in the Recurring Deletion Setting section. 4. In the popup, for Delete Transactions Older Than ___ Months, enter a number equal to or greater than 18. 5. Click Save.  Caution Once a transaction document set has been identified for deletion, it’s deleted even if you later opt out of data deletion.  Tip You can go to the Setting Change Log table in the Recurring Deletion tab to view changes to the recurring deletion settings.  Note 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 137 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Requesting a One-Time Deletion of Transaction Data for SAP Business Network Suppliers You can request to delete transactions older than a certain date on a one-time basis for your SAP Business Network account. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Company Data Deletion Configuration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. A transaction document is identified for deletion when all documents in its transaction document set are older than the data retention period. The transaction document set is the sequence of related documents exchanged between the buyer and supplier. The age of a document is based on its creation date or the date of its last status update, whichever is later. Buyers and suppliers maintain their own data retention period. Consequently, your suppliers may keep copies of documents that you have deleted from your account. To receive an email notification when transaction documents for your deletion request are available to download, the administrator needs to set up notifications. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Settings Compliance . 2. Select Deletion Settings for Transaction Data. The Deletion Settings for Transaction Data page appears. 3. In the One-Time Deletion tab, click the Set Up button. 4. In the popup, for Delete Transactions Before, select a date older than 18 months. All transactions created or last updated before that date are identified for deletion as soon as possible. 5. Click Save. Canceling a Request for Deletion of Transaction Data for SAP Business Network Suppliers You can cancel a request to delete transaction data. After the request is canceled, you can request a new recurring or one-time deletion at any time. SAP Business Network uses your data to help you analyze your business activities in the analytics dashboard. When a recurring deletion request deletes transactions, the data used in analytics are also deleted.  Caution Once you identify a transaction document set for deletion, it’s deleted even if you later opt out of data deletion.  Tip You can go to the History Log table in the One-Time Deletion tab to view one-time deletion requests that already have run, been removed, or completed. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 138 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Company Data Deletion Configuration permission. See Permissions You Can Assign to Users. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Settings Compliance . 2. Select Deletion Settings for Transaction Data. The Deletion Settings for Transaction Data page appears. 3. In the Recurring Deletion or One-Time Deletion tab, click Cancel. 4. Click Cancel to confirm. Downloading ZIP Files for Deleted Transactions for SAP Business Network Suppliers You can download transaction documents from your SAP Business Network account for 30 days after they were identified for deletion. SAP Business Network collects the transaction documents into ZIP files for download. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Transaction Data Export for Deleted Data permission. See Permissions You Can Assign to Users. You have 30 days to download ZIP files containing transaction documents that were identified for deletion. After that, the documents are permanently deleted. Procedure 1. Click , and choose Deleted Transactions. The Deleted Transactions page appears. 2. Click the line for a deletion result in the Deleted Results table. The detail page appears. 3. In the Deleted Transactions table, choose one or more ZIP files that you want to download. 4. Click the Download button. The system downloads and saves the files to your local drive. Transaction Data Download The administrator for your SAP Business Network account and other users with appropriate permission can request to download your account's transaction data at any time for any period up to 90 days. If you would like to be notified by email when ZIP files are available to download, ask your administrator to set up notifications. The following transaction documents can be downloaded:  Caution Once you identify a transaction document set for deletion, it’s deleted even if you later cancel the deletion request. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 139 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Purchase orders (orders and blanket orders) Order confirmations Ship notices Receipts Service sheets Invoices, credit memos, and debit memos Payment documents SAP Business Network for Supply Chain transaction documents Notifications Quote requests and quote messages SAP Business Network maintains transaction documents in cXML (Commerce eXtensible Markup Language) format, and you can download them in ZIP files. For more information about cXML, see the cXML Reference Guide at cXML.org . Downloading Transaction Data for SAP Business Network Suppliers You can download transaction documents from your SAP Business Network account at any time. Prerequisites You need the Download Current Transactions permission to perform this task. The age of a document is based on its creation date or the date of its last status update, whichever is later. To receive an email notification when requested documents are ready for download, the administrator needs to set up notifications. After your download request is processed, you have 7 days to download ZIP files for the requested transaction documents. After that, the ZIP files are deleted. The original transaction documents are unaffected and remain on SAP Business Network. Procedure 1. Choose ... Current Transactions . The Current Transactions page appears. 2. Select a start date and an end date for transaction documents. The date range can be up to 90 days. 3. Click Request. 4. After your request is processed, you should receive an email notification informing you whether ZIP files are available for download. 5. If ZIP files are available, choose ... Current Transactions again. 6. To download a ZIP file, go to the Action column and click the  Download icon.  Tip You can filter the table of ZIP files to show files for which download hasn't started yet. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 140 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SBN BTP Supplier Admin.content: Analytics Data Export The administrator for your SAP Business Network account can request to export the analytics data from your account. Analytics data refer to your master data and transaction data (purchase orders, invoices, credit memos, and debit memos) used by SAP Business Network to provide analytics features such as the analytics dashboard. SAP Business Network exports analytics data in separate CSV (Comma-Separated Values) files, and you can download them. The data export and download won't affect the original data on SAP Business Network. Requesting Analytics Data Export for SAP Business Network Suppliers You can request to export your analytics data from your SAP Business Network account. Prerequisites You are the administrator of your SAP Business Network account. You know the ANID of your SAP Business Network account. You have a secured email box for receiving encrypted email notifications when the requested data is ready for download. Context SAP Business Network uses part of your master data and transaction data (purchase orders, invoices, credit memos, and debit memos) to help you analyze your business activities in the analytics dashboard. If you want to export the data used in analytics, you can make a request. Procedure Create a case on component SBN-AN-ANL to request the analytics data export from your SAP Business Network account. Ensure to provide the ANID of your SAP Business Network account and a secured email box for receiving encrypted email notifications. For information on how to create a case, see Get Support Application Online Help . Results An SAP support representative verifies that you are the account administrator, then sends an encrypted email including a URL and a shared access key for downloading the requested data. You have 7 days to download the data. After that, the download package is deleted. The original data are unaffected and remain on SAP Business Network. Editing Your Company Information Prerequisites You have the Company Information permission. If you're not an admin user, contact your account administrator to request access. Context The About Us section on your company profile displays key company details, such as company name, address, employee count, revenue, founding year, and business type. Follow the steps below to update your company information: Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Click your user initials at the top right of the home page and choose Company Profile from the menu. 3. In the Overview tab, locate the About Us section and click Edit. 4. On the Edit About Your Company page, edit the following as needed: Basic Information: Company Name: The name of your company. DUNS Number: A nine-digit number from Dun & Bradstreet. If you don’t know your DUNS number, click  to open the Find Your DUNS Number page and search by company name and address. See Synchronizing Company Information from Dun & Bradstreet for more details. GIRO: A standardized economic activity code that identifies the primary business activity a supplier is legally registered to perform in Chile, such as manufacturing, retail, or professional services. These codes are issued and maintained by the Chilean Internal Revenue Service (SII). This field is mandatory for Chilean suppliers. Click the  icon to select from the applicable code list. For a complete list of official economic activity codes and their descriptions, see https://www.sii.cl/ayudas/ayudas_por_servicios/1956-codigos-1959.html . Short Description: A brief summary of your company. Long Description: A more detailed overview of your company. Business Type: Select one or more types that represent your business. Buyers can search suppliers by Business Type. Legal Form: Choose your company’s legal structure. Other Business Type: Shown only if Other is selected for Business Type. Stock Symbol: Your stock ticker symbol (if publicly traded). Number of Employees: Approximate number of employees in your organization. Founded: Year your company was established (yyyy format). Company Alias 1 & 2: Alternative company names, if any. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 11 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Revenue: Select an annual revenue range. If you prefer not to disclose, select Contact company for information at the bottom of the list. Website URL: Your company’s official website. Address Information: Country/Region State City Address Line 1 Address Line 2 (optional) Address Line 3 (optional) Postal Code 5. Click Save to apply your changes. Adding Products, Services, Ship-to Locations, and Served Industries to Your Profile Prerequisites You have the Company Information permission. If you're not an admin user, contact your account administrator to request access. Context The Products and Services section on your company profile helps buyers discover what your business offers—including product categories, service areas, and the industries you serve. Buyers can search for suppliers using this information. Keeping this section accurate and complete improves your visibility in search results and helps match your business with relevant buyer opportunities and postings. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Click your user initials at the top right of the home page and choose Company Profile from the menu. 3. In the Overview tab, locate the Products and Services section and click Edit. 4. On the Edit Products and Services page, update the following as needed: Product and Service Categories Enter a product/service category or keyword in the text box, then select from the dropdown suggestions. Or click the  icon to explore all categories. To remove a selection, click the  (delete) icon next to it.  Note SAP Business Network will validate your address for completeness and accuracy. If any issues are found, suggestions will be provided. You can accept a suggested correction or keep your original input. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 12 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Ship-to or Service Locations Enter a location or keyword in the text box, then select from the dropdown suggestions. Or click the  icon to explore all options. To indicate global coverage, toggle on Serve globally. After adding a location, click the  icon to mark locations where you have a physical presence. Editing Your Business Information Prerequisites You have the Company Information permission. If you're not an admin user, contact your account administrator to request access. Context Your company’s business information - including financial, tax, shareholder, executive board, and banking details - is essential for transaction processing, business verification, and ensuring tax and financial compliance. SAP Business Network applies country-specific field requirements and validation rules to help suppliers meet local legal and tax regulations. Depending on your selected country, additional fields and validation logic may appear automatically. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Click your user initials at the top right of the home page and choose Company Profile from the menu. 3. Click the Business Information tab. 4. To update your financial and tax information: a. In the Financial & Tax Information section, click Edit. b. Update the necessary fields: Field Description Penalty Information Indicates whether the company is subject to any financial penalties or penalty-related conditions that may affect transactions or settlements. Discount Information Specifies any discount-related terms or conditions associated with the company’s financial arrangements. Legal Name The officially registered legal name of the company as recognized by government or regulatory authorities. State of Incorporation The state, province, or region in which the company is legally incorporated or registered. Exempt from Backup Withholding Indicates whether the company is exempt from backup withholding requirements under applicable tax regulations.  Note Ensure that your social media links are accurate and active to maintain a professional online presence. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 14 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Field Description Global Location Number A 13-digit globally unique identifier for any location, physical, operational, or legal, that needs to be identified for use in the supply chain. Tax Classification Select your company’s applicable tax classification. Taxation Type Choose the relevant taxation type. Tax ID Allowed characters: 0–9, A–Z, a–z, dash (-), period (.), space ( ), and ampersand (&). Max length: 20 characters. Tax ID is visible to and searchable by buyers you have a relationship with. State Tax ID Do not enter dashes. Regional Tax ID Do not enter dashes. VAT ID Same character rules as Tax ID. VAT Registered Select the checkbox if your company is VAT registered. VAT Registration Document Upload documentation if your company is VAT registered. Tax Clearance Enter clearance details. Tax Clearance Number Provide the official clearance number. Tax Clearance Document Upload supporting documents if required. Tax Clearance Expiry Date Enter the expiration date. c. Click Save. 5. To add a shareholder: a. In the Shareholders table, click Create. b. In the dialog box appeared, enter the following details: Field Description Shareholder Name Name of the shareholder. Ownership Percentage Percentage of shares owned by the shareholder. Shareholder Type Select from: Company, External, Individual, Others, or Registered. c. Click Create.  Note Your tax information is critical for billing. Failure to provide valid tax details may lead to account suspension. Your Tax ID or VAT ID is usually issued by your country’s tax authority. You can typically find it on your business registration documents, tax returns, or official invoices. If you’re unsure, contact your local tax office or your accounting department for assistance. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 15 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- 6. To add an executive board member: a. In the Executive Boards table, click Create. b. In the dialog box appeared, enter the following details: Field Description Member Name Board member’s full name. Company Name Organization the member is affiliated with. Business Title Official title of the member. End of Term Date when the board member's tenure officially ends. c. Click Create. 7. To add bank information: a. In the Bank Information table, click Create. b. On the Create Bank Information page, enter the following details: General Information Field Description Account Alias Unique name for the bank account. Additional Entities Understanding Additional Entities How Additional Entities Are Used Managing Sold From Entities Managing Remit To Entities Understanding Additional Entities Additional entities represent your company’s organizational units such as branches, affiliates, or subsidiaries that operate under your main organization. They allow you to present a transparent view of your company structure on SAP Business Network so trading partners can better understand how your organization is set up. When adding an additional entity, you provide key details such as the legal name, address, and tax information, and define its network collaboration function. By entering and maintaining address information here, you can manage all business addresses centrally instead of keeping them in separate locations. This centralized approach is built on the Global Address Book (GAB) framework, which provides a unified model for managing address data across SAP Business Network. Through this shared framework, Additional Entities ensure consistency and accuracy of address information across invoicing, payments, and shipments.  Note Currently, each certification is limited to a maximum of two versions. If you have reached the limit and want to add a new one, you have to delete an older one first. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 25 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Each additional entity includes an address and a collaboration function that defines how this address is used in business transactions. The function specifies the business role of the entity within the network, ensuring each address serves its correct purpose in transactional processes Collaboration functions include: Sold From: Supplier entity selling goods to buyers. Remit To: Supplier entity where buyers remit payments after receiving an invoice. Bill To: Buyer entity to whom suppliers issue invoices. Sold To: Buyer entity that receives goods from suppliers. Assigning the appropriate function helps ensure address information is applied correctly across transactions and supports consistent, efficient operations. Related Information How Additional Entities Are Used How Additional Entities Are Used The information managed in Additional Entities supports a range of configurations and transactional processes. Depending on your role on SAP Business Network, these use cases may apply: When Acting as Suppliers Country Configuration (formerly Legal/Regulatory Profile): In countries that require registration with local tax authorities for electronic invoicing, you must set up a country-specific configuration in SAP Business Network. During setup, your organization’s address and tax details are pulled from Additional Entities based on the selected country and company name. You must first create and maintain this information in Additional Entities before the country configuration can be created. Remittance and Bank Information Setup: You can link your Remit To address with specific remittance preferences and bank details. These are automatically included in invoices to ensure buyers receive accurate payment instructions. Invoice Creation: When creating invoices, you’ll select from a predefined list of addresses maintained under Additional Entities. This ensures that invoices use consistent and validated address data. When Acting as Buyers Document Routing Configuration: If you use multiple ERP systems, you can define routing rules that reference Bill To addresses maintained in Additional Entities. These rules determine which ERP system or business unit should receive and process documents like purchase orders or invoices. It is only then you can select the company name during the country configuration. You can also edit and delete the country configuration. Contacts Efficient communication is a cornerstone of successful business interactions, and maintaining accurate contact information is paramount to achieving this goal. Within SAP Business Network, the contact management feature empowers organizations to effectively manage both the main company contact and individual contacts. Main Company Contact: The Main Company Contact includes essential contact information for the company, specifically the general email, phone, and fax numbers. Each account has one main contact, defaulted to the information of the account creator (administrator), and you have the flexibility to edit and update this information as needed. Individual Company Contacts: In addition to the main company contact, you can create multiple individual contacts and assign them one or more roles, such as Sales Representative, Marketing Manager, or Technical Contact. Allow buyers to contact my company using Trading Partner Search Lets buyers send messages directly via search. Your email address remains private, and you'll be notified of new messages. Allow other suppliers to contact my account administrator During supplier registration, SAP Business Network checks existing profiles for potential matches (based on company name, aliases, DUNS number, or tax ID). If your company is identified as a match and this setting is enabled, the registrant can email your administrator to request account access credentials. Public Profile Your public profile on SAP Business Network is the version of your company profile that is visible to anyone with your public profile URL. Always Visible Sections These sections are always visible to anyone who accesses your public profile: About Us – Key company details, such as company name, location, founding year, revenue, employee count, and legal form. Products & Services – Your offerings, industries served, and shipping/service locations. Company Showcase – Content that showcase your strengths and advantages. Social Media – Links to your company’s social media platforms. Configurable Sections You can control the visibility of the following sections using your profile settings. Assessments – Business-related evaluations, such as human rights assessments. Certifications– Your company’s official accreditations and compliance with recognized standards.  Note Pending customers mean trading partners who have sent you a relationship request. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 36 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Sustainability Ratings – Your company’s performance on environmental, social, and governance (ESG) criteria as assessed by third-party rating providers. Organization Structure – Overview of your company’s organizational hierarchy. You can show these sections to all trading partners with or without an existing relationship, or only to those with an existing relationship, or just hide them from all trading partners. Always Hidden Sections The following items are never visible on your public profile: Company Keywords Contacts How to View or Share Your Public Profile To view your public profile, go to the Company Profile page and click View My Public Profile in the upper-right corner. To share your profile, click the More options () menu and copy your public profile URL. Profile Data Federation This feature enables your company profile data to be replicated across SAP Business Network's global data centers, making your profile visible to trading partners in different regions. For more information, refer to How Profile Data Federation Works and Enabling Profile Data Federation. How Profile Data Federation Works Profile data federation replicates your company profile data across all global data centers of SAP Business Network, enabling trading partners in different regions to find and view your company profile, thereby facilitating potential business opportunities. To understand how profile data federation works, consider two trading partners located in different regions: Trading Partner A is based in the United States (US) data center. Trading Partner B is based in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) data center. For Trading Partner B to view Trading Partner A’s profile, Trading Partner A’s profile data must be replicated from the US data center to the KSA data center. To make this happen, Trading Partner A must enable profile data federation. For details about how to enable profile data federation, refer to Enabling Profile Data Federation. Once enabled, an initial replication synchronizes your company profile data across all global data centers of SAP Business Network. Future updates are automatically synchronized to ensure your profile remains consistent and up to date across all data centers.  Note Profile data federation is only available to companies that are not sole proprietors. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 37 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Enabling Profile Data Federation Profile data federation allows your company profile to be visible across all global data centers of SAP Business Network. This makes it possible for trading partners in different regions to find and view your company profile, facilitating potential business opportunities. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Company Information permission. See Permissions You Can Assign to Users. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Click the Account Settings icon and choose Company Profile. This opens the Company Profile page. 3. Click the Options menu in the upper-right corner of your profile and select Profile settings. 4. On the Profile Settings page, locate the section labeled Search Results Visibility: a. Optional: Toggle Show my profile in search results to allow your profile appear in search results. This setting determines whether your company profile is visible to trading partners in their search results. To enable global searchability, turn on this setting along with Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network. Currently, this setting is unavailable to buyers. b. Toggle Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network to enable profile data federation. This setting determines whether your profile data will be replicated to other data centers of SAP Business Network. For suppliers, this setting is enabled by default. Buyers need to enable it manually. Once enabled, this setting cannot be reversed. 5. Click Save to confirm your settings. Results Your company profile will be replicated and visible across all data centers of SAP Business Network. Future updates to your profile will be automatically synchronized globally. If Show my profile in search results is enabled, your profile will also become searchable across all global regions. Company Profile Experience for Promote Suppliers with a promote subscription on SAP Business Network enjoy exclusive features that enhance their company profiles and foster trust with potential buyers. Active Supplier Status Showcase your active platform engagement and readiness for new business opportunities. For more information, refer to Active Supplier Status. Verified Business Badge Confirm your company’s authenticity and legitimacy with trusted third-party partners. By becoming a verified supplier, you gain a competitive advantage over unverified businesses. For more information, refer to Business Verification. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 38 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Company Showcase Promote your company by adding marketing materials such as customer presentations, case studies, and website links. For more information, refer to Company Showcase. Related Information Buying the Promote Subscription Business Verification Trust is the foundation of successful business relationships. SAP Business Network is dedicated to creating a secure and reliable platform for suppliers and buyers. To mitigate risks associated with unverified businesses, we’ve introduced the Business Verification feature, designed to foster trustworthy, long-lasting partnerships within the network. Understanding Business Verification Business verification is a crucial process that confirms the authenticity and legitimacy of a supplier company. This process is typically carried out in collaboration with reputable third-party organizations, CDQ and Dun & Bradstreet , which specialize in validating business information. The Verification Process Once you submit the verification request: 1. We first verify your business details with CDQ. If your information matches their record, your business is verified. 2. If there is no match or discrepancies are found with CDQ, we check if you have provided a DUNS number. If available, we use it to verify your business details with Dun & Bradstreet. 3. Once your business is successfully verified through either CDQ or Dun & Bradstreet, a verification badge ( ) will be added to your profile. The business details verified include: Company Name Primary Address (Country, State, City, Address Line 1, and Postal Code) Tax ID or VAT ID DUNS Number (if Dun & Bradstreet is the verifier) Benefits of Verifying Your Business Enhanced Credibility The verification badge demonstrates to prospective buyers that you are who you say you are on the world’s largest B2B network. This can give you a competitive edge over businesses that have not undergone the verification process. Increased Visibility 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 39 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Verified businesses enjoy increased visibility in search results. Stronger Trust Verification confirms the accuracy of your business details, reducing fraud risks and building trust with potential customers. Qualifying for Business Verification To qualify for business verification, ensure the following: You have bought the promote subscription for your SAP Business Network supplier account. If your organization has a parent-child hierarchy, you must be part of the parent organization, as only parent organizations can initiate business verification. The verification badge is granted exclusively to the parent organization. You have the Company Information permission to edit your company profile. Only users with this permission can start the verification process. If you don't have this permission, contact your organization’s administrator to assign it to you. Verifying Your Business Maintaining an accurate, up-to-date, and verified profile can significantly enhance your credibility with potential buyers. Here’s a step-by-step guide to help you through the verification process: Prerequisites Ensure you've bought the promote subscription for your SAP Business Network supplier account. Ensure you're part of the parent organization if your organization has a parent-child hierarchy. Ensure you have the Company Information permission to edit the company profile. Only users with this permission can initiate the verification process. Contact your organization’s administrator to assign the necessary permission if needed. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network supplier account. 2. Click the Account Settings icon and choose Company Profile. This opens the Company Profile page. 3. Click Verify your business under the Promote suggestions section at the top of the Overview page. The system will check for any missing required or recommended information. If any details are missing, a popup will guide you to add the necessary information. 4. Add required and recommended information: Required information: Number of Employees Year Founded Revenue Legal Form 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 40 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SBN BTP Supplier Admin.content: Business Type Recommended information: DUNS Number Adding a DUNS number can increase your chances of successful verification. If your business cannot be verified through CDQ, the system will use the DUNS number for verification with Dun & Bradstreet. Without a DUNS number, Dun & Bradstreet verification will not be attempted. If you don't know your DUNS number, click Find my DUNS number and use the Lookup DUNS Number service to search based on your company name and address. If your existing company name and address don't match the records in the D&B database for the DUNS number you’re adding, you need to accept the updates from D&B. Upon acceptance, your company name and address will automatically update to match the D&B records and will become non-editable unless you clear your DUNS number. In addition to the mandatory updates, you can also import other optional updates such as Website URL and Short Description from D&B to enrich your profile data. 5. Confirm your business details: Company Name Primary Address DUNS Number (if available) 6. Add and confirm your tax information. If you already have a tax ID or VAT ID, double-check to confirm it's correct. Your tax information is used solely for verification and will not be publicly displayed or shared. 7. Click Verify to submit your verification request. Verification Process 1. SAP Business Network verifies your details with CDQ. 2. If CDQ cannot verify, and you’ve provided a DUNS number, verification proceeds with Dun & Bradstreet. Verification Result Success A blue checkmark badge ( ) is displayed against your company name on your profile. This badge will also appear in search results and SAP applications, like Guided Sourcing. Buyers can search for trading partners by verified status. Failure Handling Click View Verification Summary on the result page to check the failure cause. To reinitiate the verification process, follow steps in Reverifying Your Business After Verification Failure. Notifications: You'll receive an in-app notification regarding your verification result. Click the bell icon in the top-right corner of the SAP Business Network portal to view it. Disclaimer 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 41 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- SAP does not verify the accuracy of Third-Party Verification Information and is not responsible for any losses, direct or indirect, that may arise from it. Reverifying Your Business After Verification Failure If your business fails third-party verification, you can reinitiate the process to ensure successful verification. The verification badge boosts your visibility in search rankings, builds trust with buyers, and helps you stand out among competitors. Procedure 1. On the verification result page, click View Verification Summary to access the summary page of your verification. If the result page is closed, go to your Company Profile and click Verify your business under the Promote suggestions section at the top of the Overview page. This will also open the summary page of your last verification. 2. On the Verification Summary page, review the failure cause and click Edit and Resubmit to return to the business information review page. 3. On the business information review page: a. Update your tax information. b. Click Company Profile in the error message strip to update your company name, address, or DUNS number. 4. After resolving all inconsistencies, click Verify to resubmit your verification request. Business Verification Troubleshooting Business verification issues can occur for various reasons. Below are common scenarios and guidance to resolve them: What Should I Do Upon Verification Failure? Verification through third-party services may fail for various reasons. Below are common causes and the steps you can take to address them: Common Reasons for Verification Failure: Incomplete or Incorrect Data: The data you provided is incomplete or incorrect, or the reference data has discrepancies due to outdated or incorrect official records. Data Not Found: The provided identifier is invalid, does not match the business, or is from a country or type not yet supported by the verification service. Network or Server Error: Temporary technical issues may prevent the verification process from completing. Actions to Take: 1. Review and correct your submitted data. Ensure that the following fields are correct:  Note If you have a DUNS number, we recommend adding it to your profile. This will enable verification with Dun & Bradstreet (D&B) if verification with CDQ is unsuccessful. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 42 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Company Name: Make sure it matches the official name on your business registration. Primary Address: Verify that all address fields are accurate and complete. VAT or Tax ID: Double-check that your VAT or tax identifiers are valid and match the format required by the system. 2. Cross-check your data with official records. The official data sources that CDQ replies on include: Business Registers: for example, Companies House (UK), Handelsregister (Germany) VAT Databases: for example, VIES (EU VAT Information Exchange System) Tax Authorities: for example, IRS (USA), CRA (Canada) Before resubmitting, refer to your local business register, VAT database, or tax authorities. Make sure the details on your SAP Business Network profile exactly match those found in these official sources. This can include checking any identifiers, registration numbers, or business names that are critical to the verification process. 3. Contact your local authority. If there are any errors in the official records, reach out to your local business registry or tax authority for help. 4. Submit a new verification request. Once you’ve reviewed and corrected any discrepancies, you can resubmit your verification request. Make sure that all the information is up to date and accurate to increase the chances of success. For detailed instructions on resubmitting your verification request, refer to Reverifying Your Business After Verification Failure. 5. Escalate the issue. If your verification continues to fail despite your efforts to correct the data, or if you believe the failure is due to an issue with the verification process, you can escalate the issue to SAP Support. We'll work with the verification partner to investigate and improve the service if needed. Please provide: The submitted (correct) data (Company Name, Address, and Identifier). Any official reference sources (for example, business registry extracts) to assist in the investigation. A brief explanation of the issue. Synthetic Examples for Escalation Cases to CDQ Example 1 Abbreviation Not Recognized Submitted: Name: ABC Corp, Address: 123 Main St, London, WC2N 5DU, UK. Reference: Name: ABC Corporation, Address: 123 Main Street, London, WC2N 5DU, UK. Issue: The abbreviation “Corp” was not recognized as equivalent to “Corporation.” Resolution: Escalate the case to CDQ to review the fuzzy comparison logic. Example 2 Missing or Incomplete Reference Data Submitted: Name: XYZ GmbH, VAT Number: DE123456789, Address: Musterstr. 12, 10115, Berlin, Germany. Reference: The business is not found in the current data source. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 43 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Issue: The reference source may not have up-to-date or complete records. Resolution: Escalate the issue with the input data for analysis and, if needed, review the reference source’s coverage. Example 3 Regional Variations Submitted: Name: ABC Ltd, Address: Flat 2, 10 Downing Street, London, UK. Reference: Name: ABC Limited, Address: Flat 2, 10 Downing St, London, UK. Issue: The matching algorithm fails to reconcile regional address formatting differences. Resolution: Escalate the case for review and possible algorithm refinement. Example 4 Identifier Not Recognized Submitted: Name: Tech Innovations Inc., Identifier: US TIN 123456789. Reference: Name: ABC Limited, Address: Flat 2, 10 Downing St, London, UK. Issue: The system does not support U.S. Taxpayer Identification Numbers (TIN). Resolution: Escalate the case to assess expanding identifier support. Detailed Cases of Intended Verification Failure with CDQ 1. VAT Number Issues Reason: Invalid VAT number format or structure (for example, missing check digits). VAT number not found in the database. Example: A supplier submits VAT Number ESX12345678, which does not follow the correct format for Spain (2 letters + 8 digits). Resolution: Confirm the VAT number with the local tax authority. 2. Address Inconsistencies Reason: Missing critical address fields (for example, postal code, street name). Significant mismatches in address details between the input and reference. Example: Input address is “Main Road, Berlin, Germany”, but the reference requires the house number and postal code (for example, “123 Main Road, 10115, Berlin, Germany”). Resolution: Provide a complete address, including postal code and house number. 3. Business Name Discrepancies Reason: Placeholder or dummy names (for example, “Unknown Supplier”). Major differences between the submitted name and reference data. Example: Submitted: Tech INNVOITASNO, Reference: Tech Innovators GmbH. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 44 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Resolution: Ensure that the official name match the business register. 4. Identifier Does Not Match Business Reason: The identifier belongs to a different business. Example: VAT Number DE987654321 is submitted for “XYZ GmbH”, but the reference shows it belongs to “ABC GmbH”. Resolution: Provide the correct identifier for your business. 5. Data Source Limitations Reason: The identifier is from a country or type not yet supported by the verification service. Example: A supplier provides a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) from the USA, which is not yet supported. Resolution: Escalate to CDQ if necessary. Why Do I Lose My Verification Badge? Your verification badge can be removed for the following reasons: Updating Verified Business Information If you update any of the following verified business details, your badge will be removed: Company name Primary address (Country, State, City, Address Line 1, and Postal Code) Tax ID or VAT ID For businesses verified with Dun & Bradstreet, changing or removing your DUNS number will also result in the loss of the verification badge. However, if your business is verified with CDQ, altering your DUNS number will not affect your badge. After making any updates to these details, you must go through the verification process again to regain your badge. Expired Promote Subscription If your promote subscription expires and is not set to auto-renew, your badge will be removed. To restore it, you need to renew your subscription and reinitiate the verification process. To regain your verification badge, follow the steps outlined in Verifying Your Business to reinitate the verification process. Active Supplier Status Suppliers who actively engage on SAP Business Network are awarded an icon on their company profile. This status boosts credibility with potential buyers and demonstrates readiness for new business opportunities.  Note If your promote subscription is set to auto-renew, you will not lose your badge. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 45 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Eligibility Criteria To qualify for Active Supplier status, you must have the promote subscription for your SAP Business Network supplier account and meet at least one of the following requirements: Complete at least one successful transaction (invoice or order) within the last three years. Only transactions within this timeframe are considered. Maintain at least one active trading relationship. Status Activation and Maintenance Activation The Active Supplier status is automatically activated when the eligibility criteria are met. The Active Supplier icon is prominently displayed under your company name on your profile, visible to the public. Maintenance If you no longer meet the criteria, your status will change to Inactive Supplier. The Inactive Supplier icon is not visible to the public. To regain Active Supplier status, you must once again fulfill the eligibility requirements. Notifications You receive both an in-app and email notifications once the Active Supplier status is activated. Company Showcase You can add company showcase materials, including customer presentations, company website, best practices, case studies, and more, in the form of attachments or external links, to your profile to promote your company and attract new business opportunities. This feature is now exclusive to SAP Business Network, promote subscribers. For promote subscribers, you can add and manage company showcase materials on your company profile to enhance visibility and showcase your expertise. For non-promote users, you can only view or delete existing company showcase materials. To continue using the full functionality, you will need to buy the SAP Business Network, promote subscription. Users and Roles The account administrator can create users, roles and assign specific roles to users so they can perform different activities. An SAP Business Network user’s role typically corresponds to their functional role in your company. Administrators also maintain user list, assign user roles and permissions, delete users, and transfer administrative rights. The Manage Users and Manage Roles pages are redesigned to help administrators and users with the User Administration permission. Administrators can perform the following: View, create, manage, revoke, and deactivate or activate sub-users  Note Existing company showcase materials will remain visible to buyers, even without a promote subscription. However, you’ll need to subscribe to the promote package in order to upload new assets or make changes to your current showcase. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 46 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Manage revocation period Manage and assign roles Supplier Administrators and users with User Administration permission: Upgrading to a supplier Enterprise account will list additional enterprise-only permissions. If you downgrade to a supplier Standard account, you can't activate the additional supplier enterprise-only permissions. In addition, a supplier can have a paid premium subscription such as bronze. Each of the subscription level may have different premium permissions. Removing the premium subscription will remove the premium permissions. Managing Users and Roles Administrators can create, edit and revoke users by navigating to Account Settings Settings Manage Users . The Manage Users contains the Active (N), Deactivated (N), and Revoked (N) tables where N represents the number of users. The Active (N) table is displayed by default. 1. On the Active (N) table, you can choose the following options: Create a new user. Select an existing user to Revoke their access to SAP Business Network. Import Users using an Excel file. The following table is an example of an active user: Active User User Name Email Address First Name Last Name Created On username@example.com emailaddress@example.com John Doe Aug 14, 2024, 12:00:05 PM 2. The Deactivated (N) table contains a list of users whose accounts were deactivated on SAP Business Network. Deactivated users temporarily do not have access to SAP Business Network. If required, you can select a user name and choose Reactivate to reactive the user account. The reactivated user is moved to the Active (N). The following table is an example of a deactivated user: Deactivated User User Name Email Address First Name Last Name Deactivated On username@example.com emailaddress@example.com John Doe Aug 14, 2024, 12:00:05 PM  Note If an enterprise-only permission is added to a role for a user who has downgraded to a Standard account, the permission is removed from the role. Re-upgrading to an Enterprise account does not restore the permission that was removed. If necessary, the removed permission must be reassigned to the role.  Note You can download a template to add a list of users with their contact information. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 47 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- 3. The Revoked (N) table contains a list of users whose accounts were revoked and no longer have access to SAP Business Network. The following table is an example of a revoked user: Revoked User User Name Email Address First Name Last Name Suspended On Revocation Status username@example.com emailaddress@example.com John Doe Aug 14, 2024, 12:00:05 PM Approved Revoking and Deleting Users: Users can be revoked from their roles and be placed for account deletion. A retention period is available for administrators if they want to revoke users from accessing SAP Business Network. By default, the retention period has no value. A user cannot be revoked if there is no retention period set. If the retention period is set, a user can be revoked, and after the retention period has passed, the user will be deleted from the system. To create and assign roles to a user, go to Account Settings Settings Manage Roles . The Manage Roles page contains the Custom Roles (N) and Pre-defined Roles (N) tables where N represents the total number of roles. 1. On the Custom Roles (N) table, you can Create a new role with permissions, or Delete an existing role. Created roles are considered custom roles and can be edited or deleted. 2. The Pre-defined Roles (N) table contains a list of roles that are managed by SAP Business Network. If you have users assigned to a default role, the list of role will appear in the Default Roles (N). You cannot delete or edit the default roles that are managed by SAP Business Network. Mass User Upload: Option to upload an .xlsx file containing a list of users for creating or updating users on SAP Business Network. You can upload an .xlsx file of up to 100 users for each upload.  Caution Choosing Revoke will remove the selected user’s access to SAP Business Network. You can retrieve the user data within the configured retention period, but you can’t retrieve it once the confirmed retention period has passed. This action cannot be reversed.  Note If you are deleting a role, ensure that there are no users assigned to the selected role.  Note Your upload may fail if the spreadsheet file exceeds the maximum number of users, has any file errors, or the buyer and supplier have different templates. When updating users on SAP Business Network, ensure that the list of users on the spreadsheet file matches the same email address, same user name, same first name, and same last name. However, the phone number cannot be updated. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 48 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Transferring Administrator Roles to Another User: A sub-user with User Administrator and Transfer Administrator Ownership permissions can make any user and themselves an administrator by checking the Make Admin of the user detail page. Customer Assignment (Supplier Administrators Only): If a sub-user with assigned customers becomes an administrator, the assigned customers are removed from the sub-user, and all customers are moved to the parent user account. If the administrator user is changed back to a sub-user account, the parent user retains all assigned customers as the default. Updated email notifications for requests to reset account passwords or if there are changes in administrator roles. Implementation Details General Prerequisites You meet any of the following requirements: You are an administrator for your company's organization or are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. Have the User Administration/Transfer Ownership permission to transfer authorization roles to another user. Managing Roles Use this procedure to create or update roles to assign to users so they can perform different activities. An SAP Business Network user’s role typically corresponds to their functional role in your company. Prerequisites Only the account administrator can manage users and roles. Context You can assign a role to any number of users. Each role has a unique name and a set of associated permissions that specify what the assigned users can see and do in SAP Business Network. For example, you might create an Invoice Generator role for people who handle incoming purchase orders and create invoices. You can assign multiple roles to a single user. When users have multiple roles, the Roles section in the Manage Users lists the multiple assigned roles. Procedure 1. Click Account Settings, and choose Settings Manage Roles . 2. Perform one of the following actions in the Manage Roles page. Click Create to create a new role.  Restriction You can create a maximum of 10 custom roles. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 49 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Select a the right-arrow against the role and click Edit that you want to update. Select a role and click Delete to delete a role. 3. Enter a distinctive name for the role. 4. (Optional) Enter a description to record your intentions for this role. Descriptions can be very useful later, if you want to review or revise the structure of your roles. 5. In the Permissions section, click Add and select one or more permissions for the role. Each role must have at least one permission. SAP Business Network does not display the administrator-specific permissions in the list. 6. In the Users section, click Add and select one or more users for the created role. 7. Click Save to create or update the role. Next Steps You assign roles to people when you create users in your account. Duplicate Account Check Process for Administrators SAP Business Network automatically performs a duplicate check when users attempt to create new accounts. When SAP Business Network determines that your account matches the details provided by a user attempting to create a new account, they are given the option to contact you to request access. As the account administrator, you receive an email notification that includes the contact information of the requester and a message from them. In an offline process, you should contact this user by email or phone to determine if they should be granted access to your account. If the result of the offline process is to NOT grant the user access, no further action is required by you, the administrator. If the result of the offline process is to grant access to the user, you must add the user to your account and ensure appropriate permissions are granted. The new supplier user receives two email notifications - one containing their user name, the other including a temporary password for their first time signing in. If the new supplier has issues accessing the account, you can assist them by resetting the password or by logging a service request with SAP Product Support. Managing Users  Note If you modify a role that is already assigned to users, those users will notice the permission changes the next time they sign in to SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network doesn't notify users when you change a role. Therefore, we recommend telling users before you make changes.  Remember Before you can delete a role, you need to reassign associated users to a different role. You cannot delete roles that are currently assigned to users. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 50 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SBN BTP Supplier Admin.content: A user is a user name and password combination that a single individual in your company enters when signing into SAP Business Network. You assign roles to each user to give them access to different areas of your SAP Business Network account. Prerequisites Only the account administrator can manage users and roles. Context Create a unique user name for each user who needs to access the account. Users should not share their user name or password with other users. This is important for SAP Business Network and your company in managing data privacy and integrity on SAP Business Network. To ensure your company and users have secure accounts on SAP Business Network: Users can have multiple roles, depending on the tasks they need to perform. All users should store their user name and password (sign in information) in a safe place. Users can forget their sign in information if they do not sign in to SAP Business Network regularly. SAP Business Network provides a secure and quick way for users to recover sign in information and reset passwords. When an employee leaves the company or changes jobs, and no longer uses the SAP Business Network account in their name, we recommend either deleting the user or reassigning the user’s sign in to another individual. If you reassign the sign in, you retain the user’s setup and data. Procedure 1. Click Account Settings and choose Settings Manage Users . 2. Perform one of the following actions: On the Manage Users page, click the Create User button to create a new user. Select the right-arrow next to the user details that you want to edit, and then click Edit. 3. Enter a user name, email address, first and last name, and optionally an office phone number for the user. 4. In the Roles section, click Add and choose one or more roles for the user.  Recommendation Create roles before you begin to create users.  Restriction You can create a maximum of 6000 users. When an account has more than 1000 users, SAP Business Network displays a simplified version of the Manage Users page.  Note Because SAP Business Network doesn't notify users when you change their assigned roles, we recommend telling users before you make changes.  Note When users create transaction audit reports or submit documents such as invoices, order confirmations, and ship notices, SAP Business Network captures the user’s first and last name, so ensure that these values are correct. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 51 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- 5. In the Customer Assignment section, click Add and select customer assignment. 6. Click Save. Users can start conversations within the portal and continue participating offline through email, ensuring timely and uninterrupted collaboration. Overview of the Messaging Feature The Messaging feature enables buyers and suppliers on SAP Business Network on BTP to communicate directly with each other using online messaging and email messaging. It supports structured, auditable communication related to procurement and invoicing activities by ensuring that all message exchanges are centrally stored, traceable, and accessible in one place. The feature is available to all buyer users and all supplier users. Buyers and suppliers can use Messaging to clarify purchase order details, follow up on order status, and resolve invoicing or payment issues. By moving these conversations from offline channels into SAP Business Network, the feature improves visibility, accountability, and collaboration efficiency. Online Messaging Online messaging allows buyers and suppliers to communicate directly within SAP Business Network using the Message Center. It provides a centralized, real-time workspace for all conversations, ensuring full message history and visibility for all participants. There are two types of online conversations: In-Context Conversations: Linked to a specific business document (including purchase orders and invoices) and initiated from the document's Details page. These conversations allow users to discuss and resolve document-related issues while maintaining a clear audit trail. Context-Free Conversations: General, document-independent conversations initiated directly from the Message Center, allowing users to communicate more broadly with trading partners. All online conversations, regardless of type, are stored and managed in the Message Center for easy tracking, access, and follow- up. Email Messaging 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 64 This is custom documentation. By default, SAP Business Network includes the latest two messages of a conversation in the email. Recipients can reply directly from email, and their responses are processed by SAP Business Network and added to the corresponding conversation thread. For more information, see Email Messaging. On the SAP Business Network portal, click the  Message icon in the top-right corner of the screen. The Message Center is displayed. 2. From the left panel of the Message Center, select the conversation you want to view. The conversation thread appears on the right. 3. Enter your reply in the text box and click the  Send icon to send it. 4. Optional: To attach files, click the  Attachment icon and select the files you want to upload. Unsubscribing from Email Notifications for Online Messages As a supplier, you can unsubscribe from email notifications that are sent when new conversation messages are posted.  Note Files attached to messages cannot be deleted or recalled once sent.  Note You can upload up to 5 files, and each file can be up to 10 MB in size. Files attached to messages cannot be deleted or recalled once sent. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 69 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Context By default, when buyers and suppliers communicate using the Message Center, the Messaging feature sends an email notification for each message. If you do not want to receive an email for every message, you can unsubscribe using the steps below. Procedure 1. Open the notification email. 2. Click the Unsubscribe link for email message notification. Results After unsubscribing, you will no longer receive email notifications for new conversation messages. To resume receiving email notifications, contact your SAP Business Network account administrator and ask them to add your email address back to the notification list. Supplier Administrator Tasks Closing a Conversation To prevent accidental replies, the conversation initiator or an administrator from the initiator’s organization can close a conversation, making it read-only. Prerequisites You are either the conversation initiator or an administrator from the initiator’s organization. Procedure 1. On the SAP Business Network portal, click the  Message icon in the top-right corner of the screen. The Message Center is displayed. 2. In the left panel of the Message Center, select the conversation that you can close. 3. Click Close Conversation in the top-right corner of the screen. 4. In the confirmation dialog, click Close to confirm. Results The conversation becomes inactive and you’re not able to send new messages until reopened. Related Information Reopening a Conversation Reopening a Conversation 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 70 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SBN BTP Supplier Admin.content: You can reopen a closed conversation if you need to continue communicating with the recipient. Prerequisites You are either the conversation initiator or an administrator from the initiator organization. Procedure 1. On the SAP Business Network portal, click the  Message icon in the top-right corner of the screen. The Message Center is displayed. 2. From the left panel of the Message Center, click the closed conversation you want to reopen. 3. Click Reopen Conversation at the top-right corner of the conversation details screen. 4. In the confirmation dialog, click OK to confirm. Results The conversation is active again, and you can continue exchanging messages with the recipient. Deleting a Conversation If a conversation is no longer needed, an administrator from the initiator organization can delete it. Once deleted, the conversation cannot be resumed and will be permanently removed from the system in accordance with the system’s data retention policy. Prerequisites You are an administrator from the initiator organization. Procedure 1. On the SAP Business Network portal, click the  Message icon in the top-right corner of the screen. The Message Center is displayed. 2. From the left panel of the Message Center, select a conversation that you want to delete. 3. Click Delete at the top right of the panel. Results The conversation is removed from the conversation list and cannot be resumed. Deleting a Message from a Conversation An administrator from the initiator organization can delete individual messages from a conversation.  Note Checkboxes are disabled for conversations that were not initiated by your organization. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 71 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Prerequisites You must be an administrator from the initiator organization. Procedure 1. On the SAP Business Network portal, click the  Message icon in the top-right corner of the screen. The Message Center is displayed. 2. From the left panel of the Message Center, open a conversation that was initiated by a user from your organization. 3. Under the message you want to remove, click Delete. Results The selected message is deleted from the conversation. The recipient can no longer view the message. Configuring a Supplier Account to Receive Email Notifications As a supplier administrator, use this procedure to configure email addresses for a supplier account to receive certain kinds of email notifications. Context Supplier accounts can receive email notifications for the following types of messages: Document-specific messages Purchase order-related messages. Invoice-related messages Default email notifications for all messages You can specify a maximum of three comma-separated email addresses to receive the notifications. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose Settings Account Administration Notifications . 2. On the Notifications page, click the Messaging tab. 3. Choose your next step. Send notifications when purchase order messages are received. In the Global document-specific settings section, check the Send notifications to these addresses checkbox, and enter the required email addresses in the textbox next to it. Send notifications when invoice messages are received. Check the Send notifications when invoice messages are received checkbox, and enter the required email addresses in the textbox next to it. Send notifications for all types of buyer messages received. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 72 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- In the Global default settings section, check the Send notifications when customer messages are received checkbox and enter the required email addresses in the textbox next to it. If global document-specific settings aren't defined, or if those email addresses are unsubscribed from receiving notifications, the Messaging feature sends the notifications to the specified email addresses. Send all notifications to the SAP Business Network administrator. Check theSend all notifications to the SAP Business Network administrator checkbox. If you enable both global default settings, the Messaging feature sends notifications to the SAP Business Network Supplier Administrator only when the email addresses in Global document-specific messages are unsubscribed. Send notifications when context-free messages are sent or received. In the Context-free settings section, check the Send context-free message notifications to these addresses checkbox and enter the required email addresses in the textbox next to it. 4. Click Save. 5. Click Close. Quality Notifications Improvements have been made for the Notification list page, search, permissions, settings, email notifications, and authorizations for buyers and suppliers on SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain has adapted the SAPUI5 technology to improve user experience intuitiveness, navigation, content organization, and visual consistency. Elements present in the classic SAP Business Network for Supply Chain user interface have been added to the new user interface to maintain parity. Buyers and suppliers can access the redesigned Notification list page by navigating to Quality Notification from the shellbar.
