file://SBN/split/SBN Supplier Account _.content: 2 Get your results This calculator will help you determine your: Subscription level We offer five subscription levels: Premium, Bronze, Silver, Gold, and Platinum. Estimated annual fee The data you provide will help you estimate your annual fee. This calculator provides an estimate of subscription and transaction fees for SAP Business Network based on the information you provide and the current, generally applicable fees schedule for SAP Business Network enterprise accounts. This calculator applies to the usual global fee model (exceptions exist in Brazil, Chile, Peru, and southern Africa - see specific fee schedules). Please note that fees are billed only in the following currencies: USD, CAD, AUD, SGD, JPY, EUR, GBP, CHF, and ZAR. The calculator automatically switches to the relevant currency once you choose your country. Frequently asked questions Why would some suppliers need to pay fees to use SAP Business Network? SAP invests significantly in SAP Business Network to ensure it offers suppliers and other trading partners more value and support than any other collaboration product in the industry. This includes providing suppliers with onboarding services and support in multiple languages and locations worldwide, which requires investment from our customers as well. In addition, SAP bundles value-added functionality, services, and support into subscriptions tailored to suppliers’ level of participation How do suppliers obtain access to specific features or services available at their subscription level? We offer five subscription levels: Premium, Bronze, Silver, Gold, and Platinum. The subscription level each supplier receives is aligned with the financial volume and number of documents they transact on SAP Business Network as well as their technology usage. Many of the subscription features and services are available directly on SAP Business Network, so suppliers can access them by simply logging / / Overview Features Promote subscription Pricing Customer stories Support Log in All products SAP Business Network Suppliers Pricing -- 1 of 2 -- in to their accounts. For answers to more specific questions regarding subscription services or billing, suppliers may sign into their SAP Business Network account to contact support through the help center. How are supplier fees calculated? To understand how fees are calculated, please download the subscription overview and fee schedule above. You can also try the fee calculator that can help you estimate fees based on your expected SAP Business Network activity. How are “transaction volume” and “document counts” calculated? Transaction volume is calculated as the total financial value in the applicable currency, including any taxes such as value-added taxes (VAT), of all non-PO invoices plus the total financial value of all POs, excluding canceled orders, or all invoices generated from a PO, whichever is greater, sent over SAP Business Network for the preceding 12 months. To avoid double counting, PO-based invoices sent through SAP Business Network are not included in the transaction volume. Which documents are included in these annual counts? Only purchase order and invoice, both PO- and non-PO-based, documents are included in the annual counts. / / Overview Features Promote subscription Pricing Customer stories Support Log in All products SAP Business Network Suppliers Pricing -- 2 of 2 --

Configuration Guide This guide is for an SAP Business Network buyer user or buyer administrator who is enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. You configure and use SAP Business Network for Supply Chain functionality for additional ways to collaborate with your suppliers. This guide applies to: • SAP Business Network for Supply Chain • SAP Business Network Related Guides: SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide cXML Solutions Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide PUBLIC 7 -- 7 of 10 -- SAP Business Network for Supply Chain SAP Business Network for Supply Chain is an extension of SAP Business Network that enhances the ability of buyers to collaborate with suppliers in supply-chain tasks such as ordering, invoicing, and shipping. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Overview This extension of SAP Business Network provides additional capabiities for buyers and suppliers. With SAP Business Network for Supply Chain enabled, an array of features become available to buyers and suppliers on SAP Business Network. These features facilitate collaboration between buyers and suppliers, for example on transactions pertinent to direct material supply chains. As a buyer, the SAP Business Network for Supply Chain solution allows you to do the following: • Collaborate efociently with all supply chain partners through a single global solution. • Improve visibility into supply with continuous monitoring, benchmarking, and enhancement of supplier performance • Easily manage all direct materials procurement and typical retail and manufacturing collaborative processes - including consigned inventory, rolling delivery schedules, and contract manufacturing - all in one place • Respond intelligently to changes in supply and demand with real-time visibility into supply chain metrics • Rapidly connect to thousands of suppliers with minimal IT costs • Instantly identify errors through configurable business rules with automated validation and reconciliation  Note SAP Ariba Supply Chain Collaboration features entail enhancements to the SAP Business Network user interface. Fields and tabs that do not appear in the regular SAP Business Network interface may appear in the SAP Ariba Supply Chain Collaboration user interface. Also, the same tab may be labeled with one name in the regular SAP Business Network user interface, and with another in the SAP Ariba Supply Chain Collaboration user interface. Users should take note of these differences, especially when they first switch from the regular SAP Business Network user interface to the SAP Ariba Supply Chain Collaboration user interface. Alternate cXML Document Routing You might need alternate cXML document routing enabled for you and your suppliers to use certain features. Many SAP Business Network for Supply Chain features require enablement of alternate cXML document routing, which allows cXML documents to be routed to alternate paths specified in the cXML. If you haven’t already enabled alternate cXML document routing, ask your Designated Support Contact to log a case (formerly Service Request). An SAP Business Network Support representative follows up to enable alternate cXML document routing for each supplier-buyer relationship that you request. 8 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain -- 8 of 10 -- SAP Business Network Overview SAP Business Network is a cloud-based business network where buyers and suppliers establish business relationships and run their business transactions. SAP Business Network has a number of advantages for customers. On the technical level, customers only have to connect to a single service in the cloud, instead of having to set up and operate technical integration to all their business partners, using different protocols and technologies. On the business level, customers not only save costs with automated procurement processes, but they can also use the network to find new business partners and opportunities. For more information about SAP Business Network, see SAP Business Network - Supplier Help Roadmap. Deployment Process for SAP Business Network and SAP Business Network for Supply Chain [page 10] Buyer System Integration with SAP Business Network [page 11] Buyer System Entitlement for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain [page 12] Deployment Process for SAP Business Network and SAP Business Network for Supply Chain You need to plan, configure, and test your system to prepare it for deployment. The SAP Business Network for Supply Chain solution sits within SAP Business Network, so, as a buyer, you can set it up as part your initial SAP Business Network setup, or you can set it up after the initial SAP Business Network setup. Guide for Suppliers Content -- 4 of 10 -- Change in the Names of SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway and Ariba Network SAP has renamed SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway and Ariba Network to SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network and SAP Business Network respectively. This document uses the revised names. This change is effective from the SAP Ariba 2302 release and it does not affect the functionality of SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway and Ariba Network. The UI components of SPRO nodes contain the short name, Managed Gateway for Spend&Network. The content on the Performance Assistant pages associated with the SPRO nodes displays the name as SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. Also, the name Ariba Network is renamed as SAP Business Network throughout the SPRO menu components. Exceptions • The product name Ariba Network adapter for SAP NetWeaver is not updated in this document. • The names of the integration scenarios that contain the name Ariba Network are not updated in this document. • The technical names of the ABAP objects in the SPRO nodes associated with the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network, addons for SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA and SAP Business Network are not renamed. SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network How to Guide for Suppliers Change in the Names of SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway and Ariba Network PUBLIC 5 -- 5 of 10 -- SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network How to Guide for Suppliers This guide helps SAP Ariba supplier administrators perform the configurations required for integrating SAP Business Network and the supplier ERP application using SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. This guide applies to: • SAP Business Network Related Guides SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network overview guide for ERP integration for suppliers SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network installation guide for ERP integration for suppliers SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network configuration guide for ERP integration for suppliers 6 PUBLIC SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network How to Guide for Suppliers SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network How to Guide for Suppliers -- 6 of 10 -- About the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network The SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network is a self-service gateway that allows suppliers to configure and integrate to SAP Business Network and transact with buyers seamlessly. Using the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network, you can: • Configure your integration between SAP Business Network and your ERP application to manage one or more buyer-supplier trading relationships. • Specify the mapping configuration. • Validate and self test transaction documents. • Monitor and track the integration lifecycle overall.  Note SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network supports only Unicode systems. There are different types of documents. UN-EDIFACT, ASC-X12, OAGIS, and PIDX follow different naming conventions for the document types. The file size is limited to 100 MB. You can send multiple document types within an EDI envelope; however, the combined payload must be less than 100 MB. Individual transactions (after splitting the envelope) must be less than 40 MB. Audience and Prerequisites [page 6] Typography [page 6] 1.1 Audience and Prerequisites This document is intended for application developers who design cXML-enabled applications. cXML is an open versatile language for the transaction requirements of: • E-commerce network hubs • Electronic product catalogs • PunchOut catalogs • Procurement applications • Buyers • Suppliers • E-commerce service providers Readers should have a working knowledge of e-commerce concepts, the HTTP Internet communication standard, and XML format. This document does not describe how to use specific procurement applications or network hubs. 1.2 Typography cXML elements and attributes are denoted with a monotype font. cXML element and attribute names are case-sensitive. Both are a combination of lower and uppercase, with elements beginning with an uppercase letter, and attributes beginning with a lowercase letter. For example, MyElement is a cXML element, and myAttribute is a cXML attribute. The following table describes the typographic conventions used in this book: Typeface or Symbol Meaning Example AaBbCc123 Text you need to change is italicized. http://server:port/inspector AaBbCc123 The names of user interface controls, me- nus, and menu items Choose Edit from the File menu. 6 Getting Started with cXML Preface -- 6 of 10 -- Typeface or Symbol Meaning Example AaBbCc123 Files and directory names, parameters, fields in CSV files, command lines, and code examples A ProfileRequest document is sent from a buyer to the network. AaBbCc123 Book titles For more information, see Acme Con- figuration Overview. Getting Started with cXML Preface 7 -- 7 of 10 -- 2 Introduction to cXML This section introduces cXML (commerce eXtensible Markup Language) for electronic-commerce transactions. cXML, an XML Implementation [page 8] cXML Capabilities [page 8] Types of Applications that Use cXML [page 12] Content Delivery Strategy [page 13] cXML DTDs [page 14] Profile Transaction [page 15] Service Status Response [page 16] XML Utilities [page 16] 2.1 cXML, an XML Implementation XML (eXtensible Markup Language) is a meta-markup language used to create syntaxes for languages. It is also a standard for passing data between applications, particularly those that communicate across the Internet. XML documents contain data in the form of tag/value pairs, for example: <DeliverTo>Joe Smith</DeliverTo> XML has a structure similar to HTML (HyperText Markup Language), which is an implementation of SGML, XML’s parent meta language. Applications can extract and use data from XML documents more easily than from HTML documents, however, because XML data is tagged according to its purpose. XML contains only data, while HTML contains both data and presentation information. Each cXML document is constructed based on XML Document Type Definitions (DTDs). Acting as templates, DTDs define the content model of a cXML document, for example, the valid order and nesting of elements, and the data types of attributes. The DTDs for cXML are files available on the www.cXML.org website. 2.2 cXML Capabilities cXML allows buying organizations, suppliers, service providers, and intermediaries to communicate using a single, standard, open language. 8 Getting Started with cXML Introduction to cXML -- 8 of 10 -- Successful business-to-business electronic commerce (B2B e-commerce) portals depend upon a flexible, widely adopted protocol. cXML is a well-defined, robust language designed specifically for B2B e-commerce, and it is the choice of high volume buying organizations and suppliers. cXML transactions consist of documents, which are simple text files containing values enclosed by predefined tags. Most types of cXML documents are analogous to hardcopy documents traditionally used in business. The most commonly used types of cXML documents are: • Catalogs [page 9] • PunchOut [page 10] • Purchase Orders [page 11] The following subsections describe these cXML documents. 2.2.1 Catalogs Catalogs are files that convey product and service content to buying organizations. They describe the products and services offered by a supplier and their prices, and they are the main communication channel from suppliers to their buyers. Suppliers create catalogs so that organizations that use procurement applications can see their product and service offerings and buy from them. Procurement applications read catalogs and store them internally in their databases. After a buying organization approves a catalog, that content is visible to users, who can choose items and add them to purchase requisitions. Figure 1: Sending Product and Service Content to a Buying Organization Suppliers can create catalogs for any product or service, regardless of how it is measured, priced, or delivered. For each item in a catalog, basic information is required, and optional information enables advanced catalog features, such as multi-language descriptions. Getting Started with cXML Introduction to cXML 9 -- 9 of 10 -- 2.2.2 PunchOut PunchOut is an easy-to-implement protocol for interactive sessions managed across the Internet. Using real-time, synchronous cXML messages, PunchOut enables communication between applications, providing seamless user interaction at remote sites. There are three types of PunchOut: • Procurement PunchOut [page 10] • PunchOut Chaining [page 11] • Provider PunchOut [page 11] Procurement PunchOut Procurement PunchOut gives suppliers an alternative to static catalog files. PunchOut sites are live, interactive catalogs running on a website. Suppliers that have e-commerce websites can modify them to support PunchOut. PunchOut sites communicate with procurement systems over the Internet by using cXML. For PunchOut sites, procurement applications display a button instead of product or pricing details. When users click this button, their Web browsers display pages from the supplier’s local website. Depending on how the supplier implements these pages, users can browse product options, specify configurations, and select delivery methods. When users are done selecting items, they click a button that returns the order information to the procurement application. The fully configured products and their prices appear within users’ purchase requisitions. The following diagram shows an interactive PunchOut session between a user and a supplier web site. Figure 2: Interactive PunchOut Session Between a User and a Supplier Website 10 Getting Started with cXML Introduction to cXML -- 10 of 10 --

Page 1 of 21 Ariba Network UOM Mapping for ANSI X12 This document describes Unit of Measure (UOM) mappings between cXML documents and American National Standards Institute (ANSI) X12 documents sent through Ariba Network. It discusses the following topics: • How Mapping Codes Work • Mapping Inconsistencies Between the Mapping Codes • Unsupported Mapping Codes • Valid Codes How Mapping Codes Work cXML documents use United Nations Units of Measure (UNUOM) codes while EDI X12 documents use ANSI UOM codes. The UNUOM standard is also known as the United Nations Center for the Facilitation of Procedure and Practices for Administration, Commerce, and Transport (UN/CEFACT) codes, and as United Nations Trade Data Elements Directory (UNTDED) common codes. You can configure your Ariba Network account and your EDI application to route ANSI X12 and EDIFACT business documents, such as purchase orders and invoices. The following figure shows the flow of a purchase order from a buying organization to you: 1. The buying organization sends a cXML OrderRequest to Ariba Network. 2. Ariba Network converts your document to an ANSI ASC X12 EDI 850 document. It maps two-and three-character UNUOM codes in the cXML document to two-character ANSI UOM codes. However, if the UNUOM code has no direct translation to the ANSI code table used by cXML, it does not get converted and remains the same in the EDI 850 document. 3. Ariba Network sends the EDI 850 document containing the converted ANSI UOM to the VAN or to AS2 as configured by you and then routes it to you. 4. When you send the corresponding ANSI X12 810 Invoice through VAN or AS2, Ariba Network converts ANSI UOM codes to two-and three-character UNUOM codes. On mapping the 810 Invoice gets converted to a cXML InvoiceDetailRequest and is sent to Ariba Network. Ariba Network then sends it to the buying organization. cXML Order Request from buying organization AS2 Supplier VAN Ariba Network -- 1 of 10 -- Copyright © 1996–2014 Ariba, Inc. All rights reserved. Page 2 of 21 If the document contains errors, it fails. While converting the ANSI X12 810 Invoice, there are two reasons for the document to fail: 1. If the UOM code present in the ANSI X12 Invoice does not have a direct translation to UNUOM code, the document fails and is rejected. Ariba Network sends you an error notification. For example, the cXML purchase order has an invalid UNOUM code of ‘Q5’. When Ariba Network converts the cXML purchase order to an ANSI X12 850 document, this code remains the same. Because ‘Q5’ is an invalid UNUOM code and does not have a direct translation to an ANSI code. While converting the corresponding ANSI X12 810 invoice containing “Q5” to a cXML InvoiceDetailRequest, the document fails and is rejected. This happens because ‘Q5’ is an unsupported ANSI code. This error occurs for all invalid ANSI UOM codes. See Unsupported Mapping Codes. 2. If the UOM code present in the ANSI X12 Invoice has a direct translation to UNUOM code, Ariba Network maps it to a corresponding code. If there are differences in the UOM code present in the ANSI X12 Invoice and the PO cXML documents, the document fails. For example, the PO cXML has ‘PC’ as the UNUOM code. On converting the PO cXML to an ANSI X12 850 document, this code remains the same. This is because the ‘PC” UNUOM code is an invalid UNUOM code and does not have a direct translation to an ANSI code present. But, on converting the corresponding ANSI X12 810 invoice to a cXML InvoiceDetailRequest, it maps the UOM code ‘PC’ in your EDI 810 document to the corresponding UNUOM code ‘C62’ in the cXML InvoiceDetailRequest document. This happens because ‘PC’ is a valid ANSI UOM code and has a mapping to ‘C62’ which is an ANSI UOM code. However, the document fails due to the difference in the code present in the PO and the invoice. If documents fail, Ariba Network sends a notification to you with the error description. To avoid any mapping errors, ensure that your buying organization uses valid UOM codes in their documents. For more information on EDI, see Getting Started with EDI. file://SBN/split/Buyer Objections and Re.title: Buyer Objections and Responses_Part1
file://SBN/split/Buyer Objections and Re.content: Common Buyer Objections and Responses Key Message to Reinforce with Buyers Test Central allows suppliers to complete majority of integration testing independently using test-only purchase orders that do not touch your ERP. Buyers remain in control of scope, visibility, and final validation, but are removed from the day-to-day burden of generating test POs and coordinating testing schedules while SAP manages the setup and supports troubleshooting. The result is shorter testing timelines and less manual effort for buyer teams. Objection: I am not the one who can approve using Test Central. Solution: I can send you an email that outlines test central and its benefits, along with documents for your internal team to review. I’m also happy to schedule a separate call to demo Test Central and discuss more in depth as well! Objection: We don’t want suppliers sending POs are on our behalf or junk data in our system. Solution: All Test Central activity is limited to the test environment and will also not make it to your ERP because they are not generated in your ERP. Suppliers generate their own test POs and OC/ASN/Invoice testing independently, which significantly reduces your time away from your job. Objection: We’ve been onboarding suppliers without this. Solution: Test Central simply enhances what already works by removing the need for back-and-forth coordination and buyer-generated test documents. It’s about making a good process even more efficient and reducing testing timelines. Objection: I’m worried suppliers won’t use it correctly or it will confuse them.” Solution: Your SAP Integration Resource guides the supplier through the process directly, and Test Central provides clear automated feedback to them so they can troubleshoot without involving the buyer. In practice, it simplifies their experience. Instead of waiting for your team to issue test POs or schedule testing, suppliers can run tests on their own timeline with clearer validation steps. Objection: We need visibility into what’s being tested. Solution: We review and confirm with all teams what scenarios on the Test Plan will have Test Central generated POs. These POs will able be available in your SAP Business Network Test Account as well as the supplier’s documents. You can be as hands off or as involved as you’d like while the supplier is utilizing Test Central for testing. -- 1 of 2 -- Objection: Will this create more work for us? Solution: Absolutely not! The point of Test Central is to give buyers more time back. All I need from you is to enable Managed Gateway in your SBN Test & Prod environments (if applicable), confirm what PO types are in scope, and provide me with the cXML of each PO type or PO #s that I can pull the cXML from to set up Test Scenarios on the backend. -- 2 of 2 --

file://SBN/split/Buyer Test Central FAQ_.title: Buyer Test Central FAQ_Part1
file://SBN/split/Buyer Test Central FAQ_.content: Buyer FAQ – Test Central & Your Integration Process 1. What is Test Central? Test Central is a safe, test‑only environment in the SAP Business Network where suppliers can generate test Purchase Orders (POs) on your behalf and send back their documents (OC/ASN/INV/Credit Memos) to validate their integration before you need to get involved. 2. Why are suppliers sending POs instead of us? This approach helps reduce the natural delays that can occur when testing depends on buyer generated POs, which often require coordination across multiple systems and teams. With Test Central, suppliers can test independently, resolve issues more quickly, and complete most of the Test Plan without needing frequent involvement from your team. 3. Does enabling Test Central change my connection or systems? No. Enabling Managed Gateway simply gives SAP permission to set up Test Central scenarios on the backend. Your existing connection and ERP integrations remain unchanged. 4. Will Test Central send anything to our ERP system? If your ERP is configured to accept only ERP‑generated POs (which is the case for most buyers), Test Central POs will not enter your system. Only if your ERP is set to allow non‑PO documents (POs created outside your ERP/Business Network) could a test PO try to route into your ERP—and in that case, it would simply fail validation. Most buyers do not allow non‑ERP‑generated POs, so Test Central POs remain contained within the network. 5. How much of the testing does Test Central cover? Test Central typically covers about 85% of testing. This allows suppliers to generate the Purchase Orders needed for most—or all—of the scenarios in the agreed‑upon Test Plan on their own. You’re only needed for final end‑to‑end testing once their documents already pass your SAP Business Network transaction rules. 6. What is the benefit to us as the buyer? • Long‑term efficiency — your Test Central setup is done once and can be used by all of your suppliers. Updates are only needed if your organization begins sending new PO types that require additional scenarios. • Reduced buyer workload — suppliers drive most of the testing • Faster overall delivery — testing often goes from ~6 weeks down to ~3 • Cleaner results — suppliers identify and fix mapping issues early in the process • Smoother experience — fewer issues reach your team because they’re resolved upfront -- 1 of 2 -- 7. What is expected from us? Only three simple tasks: 1. Enable Managed Gateway in your Test & Production SAP Business Network accounts 2. Confirm which PO types you use (e.g., material, service, non‑catalog, multi‑Ship‑To, etc.) 3. Provide a PO example for each type so SAP can create the correct Test Central scenarios After that, SAP handles all setup, supplier guidance, testing support, and troubleshooting. 8. What if we’re not familiar with Test Central? Your SAP Integration Resource is here to support you every step of the way. They will: • Walk you through how Test Central works • Provide a demo of the tool • Answer any questions you may have • Support both you and your supplier throughout the process There’s no need for you to learn anything new or take on any additional technical tasks—we’ll guide and handle the details for you. 9. Why do we still need an end‑to‑end test at the end? After suppliers complete all testing with Test Central, we’ll ask your team to send at least one PO for each PO type in scope. This quick end‑to‑end check confirms everything flows exactly as it should and verifies readiness for go‑live. Since suppliers resolve their document validation and transaction rule issues using POs from Test Central before you’re involved, you reach this step much faster with a smoother path to go‑live. 10. What if we prefer our old testing process? The goal of Test Central is to reduce your workload, not add to it. Your team becomes involved only at the very end, once most issues have already been identified and fixed — leading to faster timelines and smoother projects. 11. How long does the supplier take to complete Test Central? It depends on their availability, but most suppliers complete testing much faster – about half of the time it normally takes – than the traditional approach because they can test without waiting on buyer POs. 12. Who should we contact if we have questions? Your SAP Integration Resource will manage the project from start to finish, coordinating setup, guiding the supplier, and keeping the process moving. We’ll continue to meet regularly if you’d like, but your active involvement during testing will be minimal — we’ll only pull you in when your input is needed. -- 2 of 2 --

file://SBN/split/How to Prep PO Examples.content: How to Prep PO Examples for Test Central Templates The goal when editing cXML to use in a Test Case is a reusable template that shows structure, not real data. 1. Save PO example as [Buyer] [Region] [PO Type] in a central location on your computer as you will need to be able to copy & paste the edited cXML to multiple locations 2. Open the file an editor like Notepad++ or Oxygen What to Remove vs What to Keep Remove or Replace 1. Change the following fields so they are all variables in all outbound documents: • payloadID • Header Credentials: From, To, Sender • Verify deploymentMode = “test” • OrderRequestHeader: orderDate, orderID You can even just copy and paste the cXML below into to ensure it’s the same <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <!DOCTYPE cXML SYSTEM "http://xml.cxml.org/schemas/cXML/1.2.044/cXML.dtd"> <cXML payloadID="#PAYLOADID#" timestamp="2020-10-13T14:53:00-07:00" version="1.2.044" xml:lang="en-US"> <Header> <From> <Credential domain="NetworkId"> <Identity>#SENDERID#</Identity> </Credential> </From> <To> <Credential domain="NetworkId"> <Identity>#RECEIVERID#</Identity> </Credential> </To> <Sender> <Credential domain="NetworkID"> <Identity>#PROVIDERID#</Identity> </Credential> <UserAgent>Ariba SN</UserAgent> </Sender> </Header> <Request deploymentMode="test"> <OrderRequest> <OrderRequestHeader orderDate="#DATETIME#" orderID="#DOCUMENTID#" orderType="regular" orderVersion="1" type="new"> -- 1 of 4 -- Supplier-specific information • Supplier name • Supplier address • Supplier product details (e.g., “Argos Water Filter” should become a generic name like “Water Filter”) Document-specific values • PO numbers • Document IDs • Order IDs • Agreement IDs • Effective dates • Expiration dates • Requested delivery dates • Period start/end dates Production indicators • deploymentMode="production" → replace with test Real identifiers • Payload IDs • Sender / Receiver / Provider IDs • Document Identifiers → replace with placeholders (e.g., #PAYLOADID#, #SENDERID#,#RECEIVERID#, #PROVIDERID#,#DOCUMENTID#, #DATETIME#)) For Change and Cancel PO – make sure you delete any document reference line! KEEP Buyer-specific information • Buyer identifiers can remain since the PO represents the buyer’s sample PO structure -- 2 of 4 -- • Line-item structure • Required fields and hierarchy • Order type logic (standard vs release) Standardized test values • Unit price → 1.00 • Quantity → 100 • Ship From / Remit To → Sample name, supplier address, PA, US 15212 Reusable placeholders • Use placeholders instead of real values (e.g., #DOCUMENTID#, #DATETIME#) Key Rule of Thumb If the value identifies a real supplier or changes every PO, remove it. If the value defines structure or behavior, keep it. Element(s) Description Replacement Value <payloadID> Payload ID of PO #PAYLOADID# <From><Identity> Identity of who document is from #SENDERID# <To><Identity> Identity of who document is to #RECEIVERID# <Sender><Identity> Identity of who is sending document #PROVIDERID# deploymentMode="" Replace with “production” “test” <orderDate> Date and time of PO #DATETIME# <orderID> PO # #DOCUMENTID# requestedDeliveryDate Make year +100 of current year <ShipFrom> All lines in the Ship From Supplier Name, Supplier Address, PA, US 15212 -- 3 of 4 -- <RemitTo> All lines in the Remit To Supplier Name, Supplier Address, PA, US 15212 <effectiveDate> Blanket PO or Service only Make date prior to current day <expirationDate> Blanket or service PO only Make year +100 of current year <Extrinsic name="ServicePeriod"> <Period endDate="2013-09- 01T23:59:59-00:00" startDate="2012-07- 12T00:00:00-00:00"> </Period> Make year +100 of current year -- 4 of 4 --

file://SBN/split/How to use the BUYER_TC.content: How to use the BUYER_TC_Scenario_Tracker Template Key Takeaways  Always check if buyer has a file already created in CPR  Allows you to confirm what has already been loaded so you do not duplicate scenarios  No duplicating the buyer’s scenario tracker since it’s already been created  Consolidate scenarios whenever possible  Do not make test scenarios mandatory within Test Central. Test Scenarios will be made “mandatory” through enforcement of test plan.  Ensure Test Scenario Name/Description match the Test Case name/Description/Expected Result & Test Scenario Name/Description in Test Central setup  Ensure PO Modifiable Fields tab is accurate when Doc Characteristics are selected during Test Scenario creation  Add notes in Notes field to advise which are modifiable in which scenario  Ensure PO Modifiable Fields are present in the cXML payload or the Test Scenario will not work correctly 1. Access the Test Central section of the TPS Warehouse: Test Central a. Click on Internal Guides and Documents -> Functional Documents -> TC Set Up Tracking folder b. Open BUYER_TC_Scenario_Tracker_template and SAVE A COPY i. If you do not save a copy, changes will be made to the original document -- 1 of 4 -- • You need somewhere on your computer to save files for Test Central however that makes the most sense for you • Replace BUYER with the buyer’s name and remove template so it says as *Buyers Name*_TC_Scenario_Tracker 2. Populate the buyer’s scenario tracker according to the instrcutions below for each tab Tabs 1. Instructions and Examples: an example of how to use the Test Scenarios tab -- 2 of 4 -- 2. Test Scenarios tab: Populate this tab with the sample PO data you are putting into Test Central for your Buyer. Template Columns  Test Scenario Name – Descriptive Name of Test Scenario, this appears in Test Central. You must follow this format: [BUYER] [REGION] [PO TYPE]  Sample Document - Transaction order for scenario with samples to reference (included on PO's Loaded to TC Tab)  Description – Description of Purchase Order, this appears in Test Central  Notes – Notes for Admin  Active – TRUE for active scenarios [TRUE]  Mandatory – Indicate if scenario is required by the system [FALSE] 3.PO – Modifiable Fields tab: Fields that are editable on a Test Scenario for the supplier when creating test POs in Test Central Template Columns  Field Name – Name of field/cXML tag  Level – Indicate if field is header or detail (line)  Notes – Instructions on who and how the field may be modified -- 3 of 4 -- 4.POs Loaded to TC: Sample cXML payloads that have been edited and used in corresponding test cases • Template Columns  The number of columns will vary depending on the scenarios and samples provided  Each column will contain the first row with a heading that ties back to the Test Scenarios tab  Key Takeaways  Update samples with variables prior to pasting in template  Update column names with corresponding Test Scenario Names & Test Scenario #  Ensure you delete all cXML samples and replace them with your buyer’s corresponding cXML payloads -- 4 of 4 --

file://SBN/split/Internal Test Central I.title: Internal Test Central Instructions_Part1
file://SBN/split/Internal Test Central I.content: INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Managed Gateway for Spend & Network- Test Central Setting up Test Central and adding buyer specific scenarios for Test Central SAP June, 2025 -- 1 of 10 -- 2 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Agenda • Overall Process, Roles and Responsibility for setting up Test Central • Standard Buyer-Initiated Project utilizing Test Central • Supplier-Initiated Project utilizing Test Central • Determine if the Buyer has Test Central enabled and if Test Scenarios have been previously configured • Setting up Buyer and Supplier Accounts to utilize Test Central with your Admin Access • Determining Relevant PO Types via Buyer Integration Kit for Accurate cXML Configuration in Test Central • Exporting, Editing and Saving cXML for POs to use for Test Central Scenarios • Demo of editing cXML • BUYER_TC_Scenario_Tracker_Template & PO samples • Tracking Scenarios with JIRA and CPR • Accessing Admin Area in Managed Gateway for Spend&Network • Creating Test Cases • Creating Test Scenarios • Confirming Set up was successful • Troubleshooting -- 2 of 10 -- 3 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Roles and Responsibilities Involved in the Test Central Set Up Process Task IS Buyer Supplier Discuss Test Central Process and Caveat R/A C I Agreement to use Test Central C R/A I Enable Managed Gateway in Production and Test Manage Profile >> Managed Gateway >> Enable Managed Gateway A/C R I Create Test Plan with Buyer based on type of POs in scope C R/A I Work with Buyer to create/select specific PO examples for each PO type to be used in Test Central R A I Prep the Purchase Orders for Test Central R/A I I Load the Purchase Orders in Test Central R/A I I Submit JIRA ticket for tracking Test Central Setup R/A I I Confirm Test Central Ready for Supplier Use R/A I C R = Responsible -The person or people who actually do the work to complete the task. They are responsible for action/implementation. Responsibility can be shared. A = Accountable (or Approver) -The one ultimately answerable for the correct and thorough completion of the task. Whoever is Accountable must sign off or approve work that Responsible provides. There must be exactly one Accountable person per task. C = Consulted-Those whose opinions are sought before a decision or action is taken. Typically, they are subject-matter experts, and there is two-way communication. I = Informed -Those who are kept up to date on progress or decisions. They receive information but are not necessarily consulted or responsible for the work. Communication is usually one-way. -- 3 of 10 -- Standard Buyer-Initiated Project utilizing Test Central Following today’s current process, majority of assigned projects are initiated by the buyer. Not much changes aside from advising the use of TC for majority of testing, and set up on the backend for TC if needed -- 4 of 10 -- 5 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Pre-Kickoff Activities •Project assigned to IS via Atlas. •Along with your normal pre-work activities, confirm if the Buyer is enabled for Test Central. •Check system settings, Check Test Central and/or the Buyer’s CPR folder for the Buyer_TC_Scenario_Tracker to view any existing Test Scenarios previously created by another IS. Initial Kickoff Call •IS schedules a kickoff call with Buyer and Supplier to review blueprints/ guidelines as usual •Communicate that Test Central will be used for testing—it is not optional. •If Buyer pushes back, notify Shannon and consider a separate call with the Buyer to present the Value Prop Slide Deck. Follow-Up Call: Test Plan Alignment •Include Buyer and Supplier to align on: •Connectivity setup (if applicable) •Test Plan and Test Central •Focus discussion on: o Identify which production Purchase Orders can be leveraged by the IS to configure Test Central o Confirm Test Plan and that all tests outlined in the Test Plan can be supported using these selected POs Configuration & Setup •Once Transaction Numbers for Test Case Payloads are confirmed, follow the Engineering PowerPoint to: •Set up Test Central •Create test cases and scenarios •Save and upload the Buyer TC Scenario Tracker to their CPR folder and attach to the JIRA ticket for tracking (engineering slide deck) Testing Preparation & Execution •Continue with project as normal until testing phase. •Before testing begins: •Review Test Central with Supplier (if not already done) to ensure they are prepared to complete testing independently. •Share the Supplier-Facing Test Central Instruction Guide when appropriate •It’s recommended to introduce the guide in a dedicated call ahead of testing. Alternatively, share the guide and offer to sch edule a follow-up call for questions and clarification, depending on the IS’s preference Final Testing & Go-Live •After Supplier completes testing in Test Central, reengage Buyer to send at least on end -to-end test. •Proceed to Production deployment as usual. •Project complete! Buyer Initiated Project - Sequence of Events -- 5 of 10 -- Supplier-Initiated Project utilizing Test Central -- 6 of 10 -- 7 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Project Kickoff • Project is assigned to the IS • IS initiates a call with the supplier to discuss project, introduce Test Central, discuss connection setup, and share relevant buyer documentation • IS confirms the PO types currently in Prod between both (if any are there) and begins to develop the Buyer’s TC Scenarios Tracker and export cXML from the Production POs to configure Test Central according to Buyer documentation • Work with supplier to configure Managed Gateway and Connection (if needed) Buyer Engagement • IS should involve Buyer before Supplier’s Testing begins to confirm all necessary PO Types are set up in Test Central • i.e. There is SAP Rush PO and B&I PO (according to buyer documentation) in Production, you want to confirm with Buyer if ther e are any other PO types they will be sending to supplier, change orders, cancel orders, etc. • Review and confirm Buyer’s Test plan with both parties if there is one in the buyer’s CPR folder • If not, use a generic test plan • Advise buyer they will be needed for end-to-end testing once TC Testing is complete Testing Execution • Check if the Buyer is enabled for Test Central by checking system settings and/or the Buyer’s CPR folder for the Buyer_TC_Scenario_Tracker to view any existing Test Scenarios previously created by another IS. • If the Buyer is not set up for TC, follow along with the Engineering Slide Deck to set up Test Central • IS finalizes Test Central setup and gives the go-ahead for supplier testing. • Supplier utilizes Test Central to send Test POs per the test plan • IS assists supplier with testing/troubleshooting if needed • IS does NOT send test POs for supplier – they need to do this on their own Final Validation • Upon supplier confirmation of testing completion, IS reconnects with Buyer to execute at least one end-to-end test from their system (exact details at Buyer/Supplier discretion). • Once Buyer and Supplier validate successful testing, IS assists with Production deployment as needed. Supplier Initiated Project - Sequence of Events -- 7 of 10 -- 8 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only • Current PO (types) in Prod between buyer and supplier (if any) • If not – what PO types are going to be used • If there are no POs currently in Prod, then the Buyer will need to send at least 1 PO for each PO type in Test • Confirm what documents supplier should be sending back • These are not in any way related in Test Central and there is no set up in Test Central needed • These documents will flow through the connection supplier has set up as normal testing without TC • Review Buyer’s Test Plan with buyer and supplier and confirm what PO types/scenarios should be included. • Adjust as needed and provide copy to both parties as you normally do • Advise Buyer they will need to send at least 1 PO from their test system to ensure success in end-to-end process • Timeline/Go Live Date • Discussion should be similar to what you currently have around timeline/go live date • Confirm any hard go live dates with Buyer • Ideally, TC Testing should cut testing in half (6 weeks down to 3 weeks) – Of course this Depends on how many Test scenarios in scope, supplier’s availability to complete testing on their own , any is sues etc. Supplier Initiated - Discussion with Buyer and Supplier regarding PO Samples for TC -- 8 of 10 -- 9 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Hi Buyer Team, I’ve been assigned as the SAP Integration Resource to support your supplier, [Supplier Name] (Supplier ANID), to facilitate [Supplier Name]’s migration from manual invoice handling to automated electronic invoice. This initiative stems from a recent supplier consultation, and we're leveraging the Managed Gateway for Spend and Network’s Test Central feature to conduct testing—allowing us to proceed without requiring a direct Target resource to generate Purchase Orders. To ensure comprehensive test coverage, it would be extremely valuable to have someone from [Buyer Name] confirm which Purchase Orders [Supplier Name] should use during testing. This will help us account for all relevant scenarios and reduce any gaps in validation. Would someone from your team be available to join a brief call with me and [Supplier Name]’s technical resource to align on this? Below is my availability for next week: Thanks, Your Name Supplier initiated project - Email Templates for reaching out to Buyer for TC Discussion -- 9 of 10 -- Determine if the Buyer has Test Central enabled and if Test Scenarios have been previously configured Do not miss this step!!! -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/Internal Test Central I.content: 11 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only • As time goes this will naturally be built up from those adding their scenarios and eventually no new test scenarios will need to be added to TC by an IS. • We do not want multiple scenarios of the same PO type which is why it is very important to check what is already there before adding any new Test Scenarios in TC • Confirm PO Types that have already been loaded for the Buyer • Check Buyer’s CPR folder – There should be a Buyer_TC_Scenario_Tracker with the Buyer’s Name in their CPR folder • Check Test Central for previously configured POs – Check on the Admin side by searching in Test Scenarios for the Buyer’s name – If the buyer and supplier have an established trading relationship and supplier has managed Gateway enabled, you can go to their Test Central, click on the Buyer’s Name and OrderRequest in Document Type to confirm what is already added Confirm PO Scenarios have already been loaded for Buyer in TC -- 1 of 10 -- Setting up Buyer and Supplier Accounts to utilize Test Central with your Admin Access If Managed Gateway/Test Central is not configured for the Buyer & Supplier, you’ll need to follow these steps -- 2 of 10 -- 13 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Once Buyer confirms the use of Test Central, make sure they Enable Managed Gateway for Spend & Network in buyer’s Test account. This does not mean that Buyer must use Managed Gateway, it is just confirmation that Buyer allows Suppliers to use Test Central for testing purposes. The buyer can turn this on by logging into their SAP Business Network Test account, going to the Settings menu, clicking on Manage Profile, SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network Setup and enabling Managed Gateway for Spend & Network. If this is already enabled, you can go straight to Managed Gateway Admin and check “TC Send to AN” (slide 16). If Managed Gateway is not already enabled, you need to follow the above steps to have Buyer enabled Managed Gateway in their Test Account. Instruct Buyer to Enable Managed Gateway in their SAP Business Network -- 3 of 10 -- 14 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Supplier will need to enable Managed Gateway in both Test and Production prior to utilizing Test Central. G o to the Settings menu on the top right. Select Electronic Order Routing -> Configure SAP Integration, Managed Gateway -> check the box to Enable Managed Gateway for Spend&Network and click Save. They need to repeat the same process in their Production Account Instruct Supplier to Enable Managed Gateway in their SAP Business Network -- 4 of 10 -- 15 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Prior to the supplier utilizing Test Central to send Purchase Orders, they will need to confirm their Electronic Order Routing for POs is set up according to how they’d like to receive POs. Using Test Central to send Test POs does not necessarily mean they have to receive the POs via the Managed Gateway. They can elect to receive POs via Online, Email or cXML set in the Business Network. Test Central will check the supplier’s Electronic Order Routing settings and send the PO to them however they have set. Instruct Supplier to change Order Routing if needed -- 5 of 10 -- 16 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only • Be sure to enable the "TC Send transactions to AN" option located under Trading Partner Properties in Managed Gateway Admin. • This critical step ensures that Purchase Orders sent from Test Central are properly routed through the buyer’s SAP Business Network account. • if you do not have this access, reach out to Shannon or Sumedha • Outbound document flow if “TC Send to AN” is enabled: – Managed Gateway Test Central -> Buyer’s SAP Business Network Account -> Supplier’s SAP Business Network Account (to check routing method) -> Managed Gateway Transaction Tracker -> Supplier • Outbound document flow if “TC Send to AN” is not enabled: – Managed Gateway Test Central -> Managed Gateway Transaction Tracker -> Supplier via project/connection set up in Managed Gateway Enable Buyer’s TC POs to flow through their SAP Business Network -- 6 of 10 -- Determining Relevant PO Types via Buyer Integration Kit for Accurate cXML Configuration in Test Central -- 7 of 10 -- 18 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Check Production to confirm there are current POs flowing between buyer and supplier Log into the supplier’s production account to check any POs between the supplier and buyer for the last year -- 8 of 10 -- 19 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only You’ll want to simultaneously be looking at the buyer’s Transaction Guidelines/Integration Blueprints and their EDI/cXML Deltas/Transaction Samples to see what types of Purchase Orders they could potentially send to suppliers. Knowing this information will help you to know exactly what you’re looking for when searching in the SAP Business Network. For this example, My Buyer is Target. I checked the project record in Atlas to confirm the CPR link. I checked Target’s CPR to find their Integration Blueprint and Transaction Samples for EDI since my supplier is using EDI. 1. I see that their transaction sample tabs showing B&I PO, SAP Rush PO, and SAP Direct PO so I am going to want to be aware of that when checking the business network for POs between the two. -- 9 of 10 -- 20 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only I logged into Admin and went to the Supplier’s Production Account 2. I clicked ‘Show More’ of the filter to be able to filter on additional values. • Enter the Buyer you are working with in Customers • Change Creation date to at least the last 365 days • Click Apply and view results -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/Internal Test Central I.content: 21 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only I sorted on the Order Number and changed the Items shown to 100 to be able to see more POs. I went through the pages until I saw a change in the PO # format based on the transaction samples i.e. 700 vs 97 • I saw noted in the blueprint that their B&I POs start with 7 • I checked the other types of POs and it seems the SAP Rush POs start with the 97 • Therefore, I am going to start off with these two types of POs for Target and my supplier • **You can also export the search results to an excel file if it’s easier for you to review that way -- 1 of 10 -- Exporting, Editing and Saving cXML for POs to use for Test Central Scenarios -- 2 of 10 -- 23 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only 1. Export the cXML for each type of PO we need -- 3 of 10 -- 24 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only 2. Save it as an .xml file with the Name format: [BUYER] [REGION] [PO TYPE] PO so you can edit it in a cXML editor such as Notepad++, or Oxygen • Notepad works as well, but it’s easier to confirm you’re not missing anything in an editor • Save somewhere you’ll remember because you’ll need to add it to the Buyer’s TC Scenario Tracker file and the JIRA ticket for tracking as well as loading the cleaned up version of the cXML to Test Cases setup part of Test Central • Suggest creating a folder in your OneDrive for Test Central Buyers -> and then subfolders for each buyer so you can save all of the documents in the corresponding folder • You will need to replace certain elements within the file with standard values which can be seen on the next slide – If there are any questions regarding what needs to be replaced that either this slide deck or the Engineering slide deck does not answer, reach out to Jessica, Lisa, Sumedha or Shannon -- 4 of 10 -- 25 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only List of common cXML tags/elements that will need to be replaced and the value that should replace them • Any supplier identifying information such as supplier name, supplier location, etc. needs to be removed • i.e. “Airgas Water Filter” remove Airgas so that the Product Name is just “Water Filter” • Buyer specific information can be left in the cXML because it is the buyer’s PO sample • Modify Instructions and Examples 2. Test Scenarios 3. PO – Modifiable Fields 4. POs Loaded to TC BUYER_TC_Scenario_Tracker_Template : Instructions and Examples & Test Scenarios Template Columns • Test Scenario Name – Descriptive Name of Test Scenario, this appears in Test Central. You must follow this format: [BUYER] [REGION] [PO TYPE] Purchase Order • Sample Document - Transaction order for scenario with samples to reference (included on PO's Loaded to TC Tab) • Description – Description of Purchase Order, this appears in Test Central • Notes – Notes for Admin • Active – TRUE for active scenarios [TRUE] • Mandatory – Indicate if scenario is required by the system [FALSE] Key Takeaways • Consolidate scenarios whenever possible • Test Scenarios will be made “mandatory” through enforcement of test plan. Do not make test scenarios mandatory within Test Central. Test Scenarios tab: Populate this tab with the sample PO data you are putting into Test Central for your Buyer. -- 9 of 10 -- 30 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Tabs 1. Instructions and Examples 2. Test Scenarios 3. PO – Modifiable Fields 4. POs Loaded to TC BUYER_TC_Scenario_Tracker_Template : PO – Modifiable Fields Template Columns • Field Name – Name of field • Level – Indicate if field is header or detail (line) • Notes – Instructions on who and how the field may be modified Key Takeaways • Modifiable fields are fields that the supplier is allowed to change when sending PO • List of common modifiable fields will be present in the template • When creating Test Scenarios, if you make any additional fields modifiable, be sure to add the fields to this tab to keep track of what the supplier can modify on the PO they create in Test Central -- 10 of 10 --

Accessing Test Central Set up through the Managed Gateway Admin Area -- 9 of 10 -- 40 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Test Scenario • Test Scenarios are constructed from the Test Cases you've created • You can associate multiple Test Cases with a single Test Scenario to simulate a purchase order document flow. – For example, a typical Test Scenario can with an original Purchase Order and include a subsequent Change or Cancel Purchase Order Test Case Repository • A Test Case is a sample document that suppliers use to develop their Test Purchase Orders when working with Test Central. • It serves as a blank PO template containing key attributes—such as those indicating a material or service PO type. • Suppliers can edit these details when utilizing Test Central, like part ID or quantity, to resemble the actual purchase orders they receive from buyers. • SAP will load a cXML payload of a Purchase Order to create the Test Cases • The only document types we will set up are Purchase Orders, Change Orders and Cancel Orders Test Central Setup: Test Cases and Scenarios for Suppliers -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/Internal Test Central I.title: Internal Test Central Instructions_Part5
file://SBN/split/Internal Test Central I.content: Creating Test Cases -- 1 of 10 -- 42 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only This is the main screen of the Test Case Repository that shows a list of Test Cases that have been created previously by anyone with the ability to do so. Choose the Add Test Case button to add a new Test Case or if you want to edit an existing test case, select the pencil icon under the Actions tab on the right. Creating Test Cases in Test Case Repository -- 2 of 10 -- 43 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Once you have entered the Details on the Purchase Order, ensure you check Active then click on the pencil next to Payload to add the scrubbed cXML. It is VERY important to confirm: • Document has Generic header • From ID, To ID, Sender ID, PrivateID, SystemID,VendorID, etc. should be removed from the header and replaced with #SENDERID#, #FROMID#, etc. • Remove any supplier identifying information • Supplier Name, Supplier Identifying Product Information, supplier specific locations, etc. • Remove any document Numbers and replace with #DOCUMENTID# • such as OrderID,MasterAgreement, etc. • Dates should be changed because these will be autogenerated by Test Central • Order ID and Order Date – Example: OrderRequestHeader orderDate="#DATETIME#" orderID="#DOCUMENTID#“ • For Service PO, if there is a Service End Date in the cXML of PO, please change that to 10 years after today's date so that Service PO does not expire. – Example: <Period startDate="2021-02-01T00:00:00- 00:00"endDate="2031-02-28T00:00:00-00:00"/> Click Save! The test case added will show up at the end of the list. You can click on the pencil on right side next to the Test Case if you need to edit. file://SBN/split/Quick Guide for Trouble.content: Quick Guide for Troubleshooting Test Scenarios not appearing in a supplier’s Test Central If a buyer‘s Test Scenarios aren’t displaying in the supplier’s Test Central, return to the Admin Area and verify the following: • Your Test Cases and/or Test Scenarios are marked as Active • Each Test Scenario is associated with the correct Buyer • ANID is the most accurate way to confirm the Buyer is correct • The Test Case/Scenario has been deployed to the Data Center corresponding to your supplier's location If all those are correct and you are still not seeing the Test Scenarios in supplier’s Test Central, act as supplier in Managed Gateway/Test Central: • Ensure a project is created in Managed Gateway • If a project exists, but it is set to All – recreate a project with the same connection and set customer to the specific buyer • Ensure you’re selecting OrderRequest, ChangeOrderRequest, CancelOrderRequest in Document Type when creating a Test Script If you’re still unable to see the buyer’s Test Scenarios in the supplier’s Test Central, reach out to an SME NAMER/LAC: • Jessica Roth – jessica.roth@sap.com • Sumedha Gupta – sumedha.gupta@sap.com APAC/EMEA: • Dean Worth – dean.worth@sap.com -- 1 of 1 --

It enables efficient transaction processing with buyers while providing enhanced visibility and control over connectivity and data exchange. Positioned between the supplier’s ERP system and their SAP Business Network account, the Managed Gateway offers advanced tool s and functionality beyond the standard legacy integration available within SAP BN. It delivers a more transparent view of integrat ion status and transactional flows Below is a general overview of the system architecture, although specific configurations may vary based on each buyer –supplier relationship. With Managed Gateway for Spend & Network, you can: - Streamline integration between your ERP system and the SAP Business Network, enabling seamless management of one or multiple buyer relationships. - Validate and test transaction documents independently against buyer transaction rules and validations to ensure accuracy befo re transmitting. - Track and monitor the entire integration lifecycle, providing real-time visibility into document flow and connection status -- 3 of 10 -- 4 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Configure your Managed Gateway For Spend & Network account Log into your SAP Business Network Test account, and go to the Settings menu on the top right. Select Electronic Order Routing -> Configure SAP Integration, Managed Gateway -> check the box to Enable Managed Gateway for Spend&Network and click Save. You’ll need to repeat the same process in your Production Account. You can now log in to the Managed Gateway by clicking on the Log in to Managed Gateway for Spend&Network link shown here. -- 4 of 10 -- 5 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Change Document Routing in SAP Business Network to Managed Gateway Navigate to Electronic Order Routing from the Settings menu and verify that Document Routing is configured to use Managed Gateway for Spend and Network.* This setting can be applied at the default level, impacting all buyer relationships, or at the buyer level, allowing configuration for individual buyer connections. -- 5 of 10 -- 6 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Create your project in Managed Gateway For Spend & Network Select "Create a New Integration Project“ and enter a Project Name and select which customer you’re integrating with. -- 6 of 10 -- 7 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Choose an existing connection or add a new connection Choose an existing connection by selecting the down arrow to the left of the connection Name in the Reusable Connections section and click Save or click Add New Connection on the right to set up a new connection. -- 7 of 10 -- 8 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Choose an existing connection or add a new connection If you choose to Add New Connection, you’ll be prompted to enter your connection details. -- 8 of 10 -- 9 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Configure Document Mapping The Mapping step shows what documents are mapped, the format/version of the document, and in which direction the documents are set up. Things to consider: • Send direction is From the Supplier to the Buyer • Receive direction is From the Buyer to the Supplier • Be sure to add 824 and 997 to receive status updates • cXML connections do not require document mapping and will skip this section -- 9 of 10 -- 10 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Confirm you are ready to use Test Central Once your project status is updated to ‘In Testing’, go to Test Central to start submitting test Purchase Orders on behalf of your buyer. -- 10 of 10 --

Please make sure you do not test with StandardOrderRequest. This Document Type is not specific to a buyer and will therefore not have buyer specific information. Select the test scenario that includes the Name of the Buyer that you are testing with. -- 2 of 10 -- 13 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Test Scripts with multiple Purchase Order Scenarios You can include multiple Purchase Order types within a single Test Script. This allows all associated documents to be submitted simultaneously and treated as part of one unified test. For the Script to be marked as Completed, each scenario within the Test Script must successfully run to completion. To modify a specific scenario, simply click the pencil icon to edit its details -- 3 of 10 -- 14 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Modifying Line Items on a Test Central Purchase Order Once you click into the specific test scenario, you can edit each line item and/or Add more lines to the Test Purchase Order. Select Close and your line items will be saved. For address-related fields, simply enter the relevant Address ID to display on the PO. The full address does not need to be manually entered. Best Practice Tip: To ensure a meaningful and successful integration test, it's important for suppliers to update the buyer’s test Purchase Order with their actual product data, including item names, SKUs, pricing, and quantities. Here's why: •Realistic Simulation: Updating the PO reflects the actual products and formats used in production, allowing us to closely mimic live transaction behavior. •Accurate Validation: It helps confirm that product data flows correctly between systems— ensuring everything from unit of measure to tax and pricing logic is configured as expected. •Fewer Surprises: Testing • with real data helps identify potential mapping or formatting issues before go-live, reducing the risk of failed transactions later. •Streamlined Onboarding: If the test is successful, transitioning to production will be smoother and faster, with fewer adjustments needed. -- 4 of 10 -- 15 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Complete and Send your Test PO via the Test Script Click Save to send your Test Purchase Orders listed in the Test Scenarios -- 5 of 10 -- 16 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Test Central Dashboard The Test Central Dashboard will show you the list of Test Scripts you have submitted and their Status. file://SBN/split/Supplier Objections and.title: Supplier Objections and Responses_Part1
file://SBN/split/Supplier Objections and.content: Common Supplier Objections and Responses Key Message to Reinforce with Suppliers Test Central gives suppliers more control, not more responsibility. It removes delays, reduces rework, and lets you test thoroughly—without risking buyer systems or production data. Objection: This sounds like extra work for our technical team. Response: In practice, it’s less work. Test Central provides ready-made PO templates and automated validation feedback, so your team spends less time troubleshooting and re-submitting documents. You also avoid repeated coordination with buyers just to get test POs issued. Objection: What if we do something wrong and it impacts the buyer? Response: That risk is removed by design. Test Central validates documents automatically and provides immediate feedback before anything reaches production. SAP resources remain involved throughout testing, and nothing you send through Test Central affects live transactions or buyer systems. Objection: We’ve successfully onboarded without Test Central before. Why do we have to use it now? Response: That’s true—and Test Central builds on that success. It removes bottlenecks like waiting for buyer availability and manual PO creation. The goal isn’t to change what works, but to make testing faster, more predictable, and less dependent on external coordination. Objection: We don’t have time to learn a new tool Response: Test Central is designed to be lightweight. Suppliers use it only to generate test POs; the interface is simple, and SAP provides clear instructions and support. Most suppliers become productive quickly, and the time saved during testing far outweighs the short learning curve. Objection: What if Test Central doesn’t reflect real buyer POs? Response: All Test Central scenarios are built using actual buyer PO samples provided by the buyer. These are scrubbed only to remove sensitive or supplier-specific data. Structurally and functionally, the POs you test with mirror real production documents. You also are able to add/remove/edit line items specific to your actual product data to ensure real life test scenarios. -- 1 of 2 -- Objection: We prefer buyers to control testing. Response: Buyers still control the scope and final validation. Test Central simply lets you handle the early and middle stages independently. Buyers still perform end-to-end testing from their ERP before go-live, ensuring nothing changes from a governance perspective. Objection: What if our team needs help during testing? Response: You’re not on your own. SAP Integration Resources remain engaged throughout testing and troubleshooting. In addition, Test Central’s automated validations help you identify issues immediately, often without needing buyer or SAP intervention. We also have a guide for sending test POs with Test Central and troubleshooting if needed. Objection: Does this mean we must use Managed Gateway for everything? Response: No. Managed Gateway must be enabled and you must create a connection for at least one document to flow through to allow Test Central usage, but you can still receive POs via your preferred routing method—cXML, email, or online—based on your SAP Business Network configuration. Test Central reads what routing you have configured for the particular buyer and sends documents via that route. Objection: Will this slow down our go-live? Response: Actually, it usually accelerates it. Because you can complete most testing independently, overall timelines are shorter. Many projects see testing duration reduced significantly because dependencies on buyer availability are minimized. Objection: I don’t see how this benefits us since it’s giving us more work. What’s in it for us as a supplier? Response: • Faster testing cycles • Fewer rejections late in testing • Clear validation feedback • Less back-and-forth with buyers • Greater confidence before go-live Ultimately, Test Central helps you get to production faster with fewer surprises. -- 2 of 2 --

file://SBN/split/Supplier TC Cheat Sheet.title: Supplier TC Cheat Sheet_Part1
file://SBN/split/Supplier TC Cheat Sheet.content: Supplier Cheat Sheet: Testing With Test Central A quick guide for suppliers connecting to SAP Business Network via SAP Managed Gateway What Is Test Central? A safe test-only environment where you can send test POs on behalf of the buyer and send back your documents (OC/ASN/INV/Credit Memos) to make sure everything works before real testing begins. Why We’re Using Test Central 1. Make sure everything works before involving the buyer • Confirm you can receive the buyer’s PO through your Managed Gateway connection • Check your documents are well-formed, valid, and meet cXML/EDI standards • Verify your documents pass the buyer’s transaction rules in the SAP Business Network 2. Fix issues faster • You can send as many test POs as needed until everything passes—no waiting on the buyer 3. Faster onboarding, fewer escalations • You test on your own schedule, which speeds up the entire project What Does Change? • The only thing really changing for you is that you will be completing a portion of the testing by generating POs on behalf on the buyer without having to wait for them to send from their system What Does NOT Change? • SAP still runs the kickoff call and reviews all requirements • SAP can demo how to use Test Central • SAP supports you through testing, troubleshooting, and getting to go‑live • The buyer will send at least 1 test from their systems to confirm end-to-end testing is successful -- 1 of 3 -- What You Need To Do Follow this simple 5-step workflow for each Test Scenario: 1. Generate and send the Test PO in Test Central The Test PO will flow to you as it is defined in the Default Order Routing or if the buyer has a Custom Order Routing • You can edit line items of the different Test POs generated in Test Central 2. Process the PO in your system Receive and process the PO into your system exactly as you would if the buyer was sending the test PO • Confirm your connection can receive buyer POs through Managed Gateway • Check that all fields map correctly 3. Send back the required documents Respond to the Test PO with the documents that were confirmed during the kickoff call, such as: • Order Confirmation (OC) • Advance Ship Notice (ASN) • Invoice • Credit Memo These documents help verify that your transactions are: • Well-formed and valid (cXML/EDI) • Aligned with the buyer’s business rules in the SAP Business Network 4. Track progress for each Test Scenario Use the agreed-upon Test Plan to track which documents you have submitted. This makes it easy for SAP and the buyer to review results and identify anything that needs adjustment. -- 2 of 3 -- 5. Repeat if needed — this is normal If a document doesn’t pass validation the first time, don’t worry. Test Central is designed for multiple test cycles, so you can correct issues and resend until everything passes. If anything is unclear at any step, please ask — SAP is here to support you through testing and help you reach a successful go-live. -- 3 of 3 --

file://SBN/split/Supplier Test Central F.title: Supplier Test Central FAQ_Part1
file://SBN/split/Supplier Test Central F.content: Supplier Test Central FAQ 1. What if we already tested our connection with another customer? Each buyer sends different requirements based on their business practices. Testing with buyer specific scenarios in Test Central ensures your integration works for this specific buyer. 2. What is Test Central? A safe, test‑only environment in the SAP Business Network where you can receive test POs and send back your documents (OC, ASN, Invoice, Credit Memo) to confirm everything works before involving the buyer, helping shorten the overall testing timeline. 3. Why am I sending POs on behalf of the buyer? This lets you test faster. You don’t need to wait for the buyer to generate POs — you can create and send as many test POs as needed on your own schedule. 4. Will Test Central affect my production setup? No. Everything you do in Test Central stays in the test environment. 5. What documents do I need to send? Your SAP Integration Resource will confirm the documents in scope during the kickoff (e.g., OC, ASN, Invoice, Credit Memo). 6. Are Test Central POs real? They look and behave like real POs but are non‑ERP, test‑only documents and do not post to the buyer’s ERP. 7. How do I know if my documents passed validation? Test Central provides automated status updates. Your documents must be: • Well-formed (technically correct) • Valid against cXML/EDI standards • Aligned with the buyer’s SAP Business Network transaction rules If anything fails, Test Central provides an error message so you can correct and resend -- 1 of 3 -- 8. What if my documents fail? This is normal and would happen if the buyer was sending the test POs as well. Fix the issue in your system and send another test PO or test document. Test Central allows unlimited retries with no down time since you’re the one sending the Test PO. 9. How many test cycles can I complete? As many as necessary. You can create multiple Test POs to adjust mapping, routing, or formatting on your documents. 10. Do I need Managed Gateway enabled to use Test Central? Yes. You must have a connection in the Managed Gateway to use Test Central. 11. How do I know which scenarios to test? Your SAP Integration Resource will review and confirm the Test Plan with you and the buyer, outlining all required scenarios and documents. You can mark progress directly in the plan. 12. Do I still need to do end-to-end testing after Test Central? Yes — but only at the very end. After testing with Test Central is complete, the buyer sends at least one PO from their ERP to confirm your documents are accepted by their ERP. 13. How long does Test Central testing take? It depends on your availability and how quickly you address errors, but most suppliers complete the majority of testing in about two weeks or less, since they can test independently. 14. Do I need to change my mapping for Test Central? No special mapping is needed for Test Central. The POs you test with come directly from the buyer’s real Production samples, so they match what you’ll receive in both Test and Production when the buyer sends a PO themselves. -- 2 of 3 -- You may make small fixes if validations fail, but the mapping you build in Test Central is the same mapping used for end-to-end testing and Production. Nothing is temporary — you are building your final live integration. 15. What if I use EDI instead of cXML? Test Central supports both. 16. Who supports me during Test Central testing? Your SAP Integration Resource will: • Demo how Test Central works • Guide you through setup • Help troubleshoot errors • Support you through all test cycles • Confirm you're ready for end-to-end testing and go-live You are not testing alone. 17. What happens after I finish Test Central testing? The buyer sends at least one PO from their ERP to verify your documents flow correctly and pass their ERP validations. After this confirmation, the process continues exactly as it always has: • Move the connection to Production (if applicable) • Update your Order Routing settings in your SAP Business Network Production account • Make any necessary updates in your internal systems • Proceed to go-live on the agreed-upon date 18. What if I still have questions? Just ask your SAP Integration Resource. We’re here to support you, clarify expectations, and make the testing process as smooth and quick as possible. -- 3 of 3 --
