file://SBN/split/BuyerAdminGuide includi.content: Sales Order Rule You can configure this transaction rule for sales orders, which are confirmation documents sent to the customers before delivery of goods or services. Allow sales orders. Check this rule to allow suppliers to submit sales orders. Default setting: No D-U-N-S Number Rule A D-U-N-S (Data Universal Numbering System) number is a nine-digit number issued by Dun & Bradstreet, Inc. to identify each corporate location of an organization. By default, suppliers do not require a D-U-N-S number to register with SAP Business Network. If you prefer, you can make a D-U-N-S number required for suppliers you invite to register. Do not require suppliers to enter their D-U-N-S number. Uncheck this rule to make a D-U-N-S number mandatory for suppliers that you invite to register with SAP Business Network. If you require D-U-N-S numbers and request a relationship with a supplier that has registered without entering one, after they accept the invitation (either by default or manually), SAP Business Network prompts the supplier to enter a valid D-U-N-S number at the next sign in. Your suppliers can contact Dun & Bradstreet directly with questions about the requirements for acquiring a valid D-U-N-S number. Default setting: Yes Work Order Information Purchase orders received by SAP Business Network suppliers contain work order-related information. Documents transacted in SAP Business Network display workorder information at the line level. The WorkOrder ID and Equipment ID fields are included at the line level of documents, in a new section named Work Order Information. These fields are auto populated in documents that are displayed on SAP Business Network. The work order information is derived from purchase orders received into SAP Business Network. These fields provide important information to suppliers and enables them to offer accurate and timely services. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 101 -- 1 of 10 -- Workflow for adding work order information 1. A work order is created in the Plant Maintenance component of SAP S/4HANA or SAP ERP. 2. A purchase order is created if one or more items in the work order are not available in the inventory. 3. SAP Business Network receives the purchase order. The purchase order contains the following information at the line level, under a new section named Work Order Information: • WorkOrder ID • Equipment ID 4. A supplier hosted on SAP Business Network logs in to SAP Business Network and creates one or more of the following documents from the purchase order: • invoice • credit memo • debit memo • line item credit memo • line item debit memo • service entry sheet • order confirmation • advance ship notice 5. SAP Business Network displays work order information fields on the document that is created from the purchase order. The work order information fields are displayed only if buyers have enabled the Allow supplier to view work order information rule in their SAP Business Network accounts. Prerequisites • To enable suppliers hosted on SAP Business Network and buyer users to view work order information fields, buyers need to enable the Allow supplier to view work order information rule in Account settings Manage Profile Default Transaction Rules . • To send purchase orders with work order information to your suppliers, your organization must use one of the following: • Your organization must use either of the following SAP Ariba procurement solutions and enable Management of Work Order-Based Requisitions: • SAP Ariba Buying using procurement operations desk • SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing using procurement operations desk • SAP Business Network must be integrated with the buyer’s SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to send purchase orders to suppliers. In this case, buyers need to enable the Integration to support sending work order- based purchase orders to SAP Business Network feature on SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway. List of transaction documents in SAP Business Network that display the Work Order ID field The purchase order cXML document contains work order-related information. The following is a list of transaction documents for suppliers hosted on SAP Business Network and buyer users that displays the work order information: • purchase order • invoice • credit memo • debit memo • line item credit memo 102 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration -- 2 of 10 -- • line item debit memo • service entry sheet • order confirmation • advance ship notice • goods receipt note Changes to existing functionality Documents transacted in SAP Business Network display two new fields at the line level. These fields provide work order-related information and are auto-populated by deriving their values from the purchase order. These fields provide important information to suppliers and enable them to offer accurate and timely services. • The purchase order cXML document contains the WorkOrder ID at the line level.  Note This feature supports multiple WorkOrder IDs as well. Multiple WorkOrder IDs are displayed as comma- separated IDs at the line level. • The WorkOrder ID and Equipment ID fields are included at the line level of documents, in a new section named Work Order Information. These work order information fields are displayed only if buyers have enabled the rule Allow supplier to view work order information in their SAP Business Network accounts. Related Information Allowing Suppliers to View Work Order Information [page 103] Allowing Suppliers to View Work Order Information You can allow your suppliers on SAP Business Network to view the Work Order Information in documents transacted with them. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Transaction Configuration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. Context Documents transacted in SAP Business Network display work order-related information at the line level. The two new work order information fields are auto populated in documents that are displayed on SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 103 -- 3 of 10 -- Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, choose Default Transaction Rules. 3. Check the box Allow suppliers to view work order information. This box is unchecked by default. The WorkOrder ID and Equipment ID fields are included at the line level of documents, in a new section named Work Order Information. Related Information Work Order Information [page 101] Quality Collaboration Rules Buyers enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain can configure transaction rules for quality collaboration. To use quality collaboration, buyers must be entitled for the quality collaboration component, and suppliers must have a trading relationship with a buyer entitled for the quality collaboration component. The following quality collaboration rules are available for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyers on the Administration Configuration Default Transaction Rules page in the Quality Collaboration section. For additional transaction rules available to all SAP Business Network buyers, see Default Transaction Rules [page 53] in the SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide. Rule Default Setting Description Allow suppliers to create non-PO quality notifications in a multi-ERP environment No If this rule is checked, suppliers can create non-PO quality notifications and select which system they apply to when there are multiple routing end points. Otherwise, quality notifications are always sent to the default routing end point.  Note The buyer's account must be configured for multi-ERP support. Allow suppliers to send quality notifications for indirect orders without part numbers No If this rule is checked, suppliers can send quality notifications for line items without specifying a customer part number or customer location. This rule makes those two quality notification fields optional. 104 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration -- 4 of 10 -- Rule Default Setting Description Do not allow suppliers to send non- PO quality notifications No If this rule is checked, suppliers can only create quality notifications that reference an order. Otherwise, suppliers can create non-PO quality notifi- cations from the Quality tab. Activate DocuSign for quality inspection documents No If this rule is checked, suppliers must electronically sign quality inspec- tion results before submitting them. Currently DocuSign is the only sup- ported electronic signature provider. Managing Default Transaction Rules The buyer administrators can manage default transaction rules and supplier group transaction rules that are configured in the SAP Business Network buyer account. You can download or upload the transaction rules in a spreadsheet format. This feature is useful when you want to export the transaction rules from one environment to another or to store the transaction rules for future reference. For example, when you test the transaction rules setup in a test enviroment and want the same set of transaction rules in the production environment, then you can first download these rules in the test environment, which can then be uploaded in the production environment. When you download the default transaction rules, all the default trasaction rules are imported in a spreadsheet format. To import the supplier group rules, you need to select the individual supplier groups configured in your environment. You can also translate the transaction rules while downloading to the desired language. All languages within the SBN product capabilities are supported. When you download the default transaction rules or supplier group transaction rules, they are available under the Downloads tab of the Manage Transaction Rules Details page. Similarly, the uploaded files are available under the Uploads tab. Restrictions The following restrictions are applicable: • You cannot upload a file with a duplicate rule in it. • You cannot upload a file that has a country specific rule that is not allowed for the organization's country. If you do, upload fails. • You cannot update the default address using business rule. Default addresses should be updated manually. • You cannot upload a file that has any other extension other than XLS. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 105 -- 5 of 10 -- Manage Transaction Rules The Manage Transaction Rules Details screen helps you view the list of downloaded and uploaded files. Click Dowloads or Uploads tab to view the list of files that have been downloaded or uploaded. The Downloads and the Uploads tab displays the following fields: • Name: Displays the name of the generated or uploaded file. • Rule TypeYou can search for a particular transaction rule that is downloaded or uploaded and: Displays if the file is a default transaction rule or a supplier group transaction rule file. • Supplier Group: If the Rule Type is Supplier Group Transaction Rules, this field displays the supplier group name. For default transaction rule type, this field is left blank. • Language: Displays the language in which the file is downloaded or uploaded. • Create Time: Displays the date and time at which the trasaction rule file is generated or uploaded. • Create By: Displays the name of the user who downloaded or uploaded the file. • File Status: Displays the generation or the upload status of the transaction rule file. The available statuses are: Completed, Failed, or In progress. • Action: You can use the Action buttons to view the log file for the failed operations, perform the upload or the download operation again, or delete the file. The Search Filter in the Manage Transaction Rules Details screen helps you to search for a particular transaction rule that is downloaded or uploaded. You can further filter your search by using the following search filters: • Name: Enter the name of the transaction rule that you want to search. • Creation Date Range: Specify the date range within which you want to search for the transaction rules. • Language: Specify the language by which you want to filter your search. • Rule Type: Select the transaction rule that want to search for, Default Transaction Rule or Supplier Group Rule. • Supplier Group Name: Specify the supplier group name to search the rules for a particular supplier group. If you select Supplier Group Rule in the Rule Type filter, you can further filter the search for a particular supplier group by specifying the supplier group name. If you do not select any supplier group, then the search result displays the transaction rules of those supplier groups for whom the transaction rules have been downloaded or uploaded. • Creating a Supplier Group • Configuring Default Transaction Rules • SAP Ariba Product Language Capabilities Download Default Transaction Rules Follow these steps to download the transaction rules: 1. Log in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Navigate to the Default Transaction Rules screen. 3. Click Manage Transaction Rules to view the Manage Transaction Rules Details screen. 4. Click the Downloads tab and then click New Download to open Download Transaction Rules screen. 5. Enter the name for the download file, select the rule type, and then select the language. 1. Rule Type can be either Default Transaction Rules or Supplier Group Transaction Rules. 106 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration -- 6 of 10 -- 2. If you select Supplier Group Transaction Rules, you must select a supplier group. The Supplier Group field lists all the supplier groups created for the logged in buyer account. 3. By default, the language is English. Select the language to which you want to translate the downloaded transaction rules. 6. Click Downloads to view the status of the downloaded file. • Creating a Supplier Group • Configuring Default Transaction Rules Upload Default Transaction Rules Follow these steps to upload the transaction rules: 1. Log in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Navigate to the Default Transaction Rules screen. 3. Click Manage Transaction Rules to view the Manage Transaction Rules Details screen. 4. Click Uploads, and then the New Upload button to open the Upload Transaction Rules screen. 5. Browse for the downloaded file and click Upload. The system displays a message that the transaction rules has been updated. 6. Click the Uploads tab view the status of the uploaded file. • Creating a Supplier Group • Configuring Default Transaction Rules Currency Precision and Rounding SAP Business Network Commerce Automation customers can configure currency precision and rounding rules for service entry sheets. Currency fields in SAP Business Network are, by default, rounded to the precision defined in the ISO standard currency codes using common rounding rules (commercial rounding). However, to eliminate potential mismatches between the invoice and your system that could delay payments to suppliers, you can configure currency precision and specify rounding rules by overriding default settings. The currency precision and rounding feature enables you to: • Configure currency precision values for different systems. • Enforce the number of decimal places that suppliers can include in the unit price field of service entry sheets. • Enforce precision per currency, and override precision set at the default system level. • Override rounding rules for the following service entry sheet components: • Taxes • Allowances • Charges Therefore, the values entered by suppliers in service entry sheets get rounded off according to the currency precision and rounding rules defined by you. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 107 -- 7 of 10 --  Note The currency precision and rounding configuration in SAP Business Network must match the configuration in your system exactly. Any mismatch will result in transmission failures of documents (service entry sheets). Rounding Rules in SAP Business Network The following currency rounding rules are available in SAP Business Network: • Round half up (also called commercial rounding) - rounds off the numerical value to the previous lower number or the next higher number based on the value to be rounded. Example If the value is 82.x, and if x > 4, the value gets rounded to 83 If the value is 82.x, and if x <= 4, the value gets rounded to 82 • Round up - increases the value to be rounded to the immediate higher whole number Example If the value is 82.x, it gets rounded to 83 • Round down - decreases the value to be rounded to the immediate lower whole number Example If the value is 82.x, it gets rounded to 82 Restrictions • This feature can be used to configure currency precision and rounding rules for service entry sheets and to configure how many decimals places are allowed for Unit Price based on the currency or all currencies. • Currency precision validation applies only to invoices in electronic format. It does not apply to paper based invoices - these include paper invoices and paper invoices received via ICS. • The currency settings that you configure are not visible to suppliers. You must ensure that you share the currency settings with suppliers, so suppliers can evaluate if the currency precision and rounding rules affect their invoice or credit memo submittals. 108 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration -- 8 of 10 -- • Currency precision and rounding will be applied to service entry sheets for purchase orders that are created after the feature is enabled. If there are any pending purchase orders, you must enable the rule to let suppliers change the unit price on invoices and credit memos until the pending purchase orders have been closed. • This feature provides an ability to configure how many decimals places are allowed for Unit Price based on the currency. If the buyer enables the option to provide pricing details then the validation of the decimal precision will be applied to the Pricing Details (Price Unit and Price Unit Quantity). • All calculated fields like Subtotal are rounded based on buyer configuration settings. If not, commercial rounding (default) would happen based on system defined precision. • Decimal precision validation is applied for hosted suppliers, integrated suppliers, and external documents (channels that are supported like cXML and CSV) to the Database level. • If the buyer does not configure a rounding mechanism for a currency, it will follow the existing rounding mechanism (commercial rounding) and ISO standards for that currency. • This feature provides a validation check if the entered price, amount (in any of the price, amount field) is not adhering to the allowed precision based on the currency code configuration. Overriding Standard Currency Precision and Rounding for Invoices and Credit Memos Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Transaction Configuration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, choose Currency Precision and Rounding. The Configure currency precision and rounding rules page appears. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 109 -- 9 of 10 -- Figure 12: Configure Currency Precision and Rounding Rules Page 3. Check the Enable currency precision and rounding overrides box in the Configure currency precision and rounding rules page. When the Enable currency precision and rounding overrides box is checked, users are shown options to exclude the following invoices from currency precision and rounding configurations. • Paper invoices received via ICS • Paper invoices 4. Choose a specific system (or Default (All Systems)) for which you wish to configure currency precision. 5. Choose the decimal places for unit price for your system from the dropdown. 6. Click Add currency and select the currency for which you want to add precision and rounding overrides. 7. Choose the decimal place and rounding rule for the currency selected in the previous step. The rounding rule selected here applies by default to all the amount fields for this currency. 8. Choose the override rounding rules for Tax, Allowances, and Charges. The rounding rules selected here override the defaults set in the previous step. 9. Click Save. Country/Region-Based Invoice Rules SAP Ariba provides a set of default country/region-specific invoicing rule templates that you can use as a starting point when defining invoice rules. Country/region-based rule templates reflect the current knowledge of invoice requirements for those countries/ regions. SAP Ariba strongly recommends buyers implementing country/region-based invoice rules to consult with their tax and legal advisors to determine the applicability of any business rule they implement.  Note See the SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing for a detailed list of country/region-based invoice rules. 110 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/BuyerAdminGuide includi.content: Enablement Process for Country/Region-Based Invoice Rules [page 111] Configuring Invoice Rules for a Country/Region [page 112] Editing Invoice Rules for a Country/Region [page 113] Activating or Deactivating Invoice Rules for a Country/Region [page 114] Preventing Suppliers from Sending Invoices to Selected Countries/Regions [page 115] Viewing Invoice Rule Results [page 116] Downloading Country/Region-Based Invoice Rules [page 117] Automatic Invoice Creation from Receipts [page 118] Enablement Process for Country/Region-Based Invoice Rules You can use the country/region-based invoicing rule templates to add countries/regions for which you want to implement specific invoice rules. By default, country/region-based invoice rules are disabled and no country/region-based invoice rules are activated. Follow these general steps to enable and activate country/region-based invoice rules: 1. Using the country/region-based invoicing rule templates, add the countries/regions for which you want to implement specific invoice rules and review the country/region's invoice rules set. 2. Based on legal requirements for a country/region, edit the invoicing rules set for the country/region. 3. View the final invoice rules that get applied based on the rules defined on the default transaction rule, supplier group rule, and country/region-based invoice rule levels. 4. You might want to discuss any changes to the invoicing rules with your suppliers to avoid unnecessary invoice rejections as a result of the new invoice rule enforcement. 5. If you are ready to put the rules in production, uncheck the rule Ignore country-based invoice rules: • If you want to enable country/region-based invoice rules for all suppliers that do not belong to a supplier group, uncheck Ignore country-based invoice rules on the Default Transaction Rules page. • If you want to enable country/region-based invoice rules by supplier group, uncheck Ignore country-based invoice rules on supplier group level. Suppliers can review the rules that are applied to their invoices by the country/region of origin after you have enabled country/region-based invoice rules for them. Related Information Country/Region-Based Invoice Rules [page 110] SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 111 -- 1 of 10 -- Configuring Invoice Rules for a Country/Region You can define country/region-based invoice rules that are different from the invoice rules defined in the Default Transaction Rules for your SAP Business Network account. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Transaction Configuration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, choose Country-based Invoice Rules. The Country-based Invoice Rules page appears. Figure 13: Country-Based Invoice Rules Page 3. Click the Select Country dropdown and choose a country/region. 4. Click Add Country Rules. A list of invoicing rules for the country/region appears. 5. View the list of invoice rules for the country/region, and edit them if necessary. SAP Ariba recommends that you consult your tax and legal advisors to determine the applicability of any business rule you implement. 6. Click View Invoice Rules Results to review the rules [page 116] that apply to supplier invoices. 7. Click Done to return to the Country-based Invoice Rules page. 8. Click OK to save rules. 112 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration -- 2 of 10 -- Related Information Country/Region-Based Invoice Rules [page 110] Editing Invoice Rules for a Country/Region For each country/region that you have defined country/region-based invoice rules for your SAP Business Network account, you can view and edit the rules. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 117 -- 7 of 10 -- Related Information Country/Region-Based Invoice Rules [page 110] Automatic Invoice Creation from Receipts SAP Business Network buyers in the United States, Australia, and South Africa can enable a country/region-based invoice rule to automatically create invoices from receipts. The Enable automatic invoice creation from receipts rule, effective only when Require suppliers to include only received quantities on invoices is checked, causes SAP Business Network to automatically create an invoice when you send a receipt for material goods. This rule ensures that invoices are based on goods that you have received. Before invoices can be automatically generated on behalf of a supplier, based on receipts sent from you, the supplier must agree to automatic invoicing by completing the Automatic Invoice Creation Acceptance page for each buyer that has enabled the country/region-based rule. When the supplier logs in to SAP Business Network, an alert notifies them of the need for confirmation of automatic invoicing against receipts. When you enable automatic invoice creation, SAP Business Network automatically generates a standard invoice or line-item credit memo when you send a receipt for received quantities. Partial invoicing is also supported. The date assigned to the invoice is the system date. Each automatically generated invoice has references to the related receipt and purchase order. When SAP Business Network generates an invoice automatically based on a receipt you submit, it gathers information for the invoice from the order, the receipt, and the supplier's company profile. Header-level information for the invoice comes from the order. If the tax information is not present on the order, the VAT information is obtained from the supplier's company profile. Item-level information for the invoice comes from the order with the exception of Order Line Number and Quantity, which come from the receipt. All taxes for invoices generated automatically from receipts must come from the purchase order. Taxes can be specified at the header-level of the order or at the line-item level, but not in both places. To ensure that line item level taxes for standard invoices are copied from the purchase order, check the Copy tax from purchase order to standard invoice rule. (Note that this rule does not apply to line item credit memos. For line item credit memos, taxes at line item level default from the invoice and not from the purchase order, even when this rule is enabled.) The rule Include allowances and charges in the unit price must be unchecked to ensure correct calculation of line item unit prices when the purchase orders have taxes and charges applied on the line items. All taxes should be specified as a percentage rate on the order. The percentage is applied to all invoices generated for the order. If the tax is specified as a flat amount on the order, it is also applied to all invoices generated for the order, which could result in higher taxes than intended. Allowances and charges for invoices generated automatically from receipts must come from the order. Allowances and charges can be specified at the header-level of the order and at the line-item level. Like taxes, all allowances and charges should be specified as a percentage rate on the order. The percentage is applied to all invoices generated for the order. If an allowance or charge is specified as a flat amount on the order, it is applied to every invoice generated from a receipt, which could result in cumulatively higher allowances or charges than intended. 118 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration -- 8 of 10 -- Invoice Number for Automatically-Generated Invoices There are two methods SAP Business Network uses to assign invoice numbers to invoices created automatically from receipts: • Receipts with Delivery Note Information: If the buyer uses the SAP ERP to create a receipt from a ship notice coming from SAP Ariba, the Delivery Note field on the receipt is auto-populated with the packing slip ID from SAP Business Network. In that case, the invoice number for an automatically-generated invoice or line-item credit memo is based on the delivery note information, with a four-digit number appended to it. • Receipts without Delivery Note Information: If a receipt does not include delivery note information, the invoice number is a system-generated unique number that starts with "A" (for example, "AI7VCKN40"). Restrictions The following receipts do not result in an automatically-generated invoice: • Receipts for items from multiple orders. • Receipts for items from a purchase order that contains both services and material goods. Buyers and cXML-enabled suppliers must upgrade to cXML 1.2.030 or later to support the ShipNoticeIDInfo child element in the ReceiptRequestHeader element. All items in a receipt must have either positive or negative quantities and must be either of type "received" or "returned". Otherwise, the receipt will be rejected. All taxes, allowances, and charges must be specified on the order as a percent rate, not as a flat amount. The Enable automatic invoice creation from receipts country/ region-based invoice rule is supported only for United States, Australia, and South Africa. The rule only applies to suppliers that invoice through the SAP Business Network and not through an integrated ERP system. In addition to required business rules that the buyer must select to enable automatic invoice creation from receipts, there are other rules that affect the fulfillment flow. The following default transaction rules, if checked, affect the workflow for automatic invoicing from receipts: • Allow suppliers to increase item quantities • Allow suppliers to increase line item subtotals • Require suppliers to fully confirm line items before fulfillment • Require suppliers to create an order confirmation for the PO before creating an invoice • Require suppliers to create a ship notice for the PO before creating an invoice For example, if the first two rules are unchecked, the invoice quantities and subtotals cannot be increased from the order. If the last three rules are checked, an order confirmation, ship notice, and receipt must be created in sequence for an order before SAP Business Network can automatically create an invoice on behalf of the supplier. Related Information Country/Region-Based Invoice Rules [page 110] SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 119 -- 9 of 10 -- External Tax Invoice Rules An external tax invoice is any tax invoice in electronic format that is not created online in SAP Business Network. External tax invoice handling allows buyers to apply a specific set of SAP Business Network transaction rules to all external tax invoices irrespective of the supplier that is referenced in the invoice. This set of configurable transaction rules is called External Tax Invoice Rules. The configured external tax invoice rules are applied only to external electronic tax invoices. To prevent automatic invoice field validations, buyers typically would like to have less stringent rules for external tax invoices than for regular invoices. • Buyers are given the option to configure a set of invoice rules to be applied to all external tax invoices. • Buyers can configure transaction rules for external tax invoices by creating supplier groups and configuring appropriate rules for such groups. The following table summarizes what SAP Business Network does with external tax invoices and regular invoices when a buyer account has external tax invoice rules configured. Invoice Scenario Supplier Is in a Supplier Group SAP Business Network Action Any external tax invoice Does not matter Applies external tax invoice rules Regular invoice created in SAP Business Network Yes Applies group-specific transaction rules No Applies default transaction rules Workflow for External Tax Invoice Handling When a buyer's account in SAP Business Network is configured to use external tax invoice rules: 1. Buyer administrators configure external tax invoice rules. These rules are a subset of default transaction rules. 2. Suppliers send an external tax invoice to SAP Business Network from their ERP systems or through their service provider. 3. SAP Business Network receives the external tax invoice invoice and applies external tax invoice rules. Configuring Transaction Rules for External Tax Invoices You can create a general set of transaction rules that apply to all external tax invoices regardless of other custom transaction rules (for example, country/region-specific rules). Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. 120 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration -- 10 of 10 --

Request to have your SAP Business Network account enabled for EFT. 3. Enabling Your Account for EFT Payment You must perform several steps to enable EFT payment. Procedure 1. Go to www.verisign.com and obtain a VeriSign account. 2. Send a request to SAP Business Network Support to enable your SAP Business Network account for EFT payment. Catalog Validation Preferences SAP Business Network enables suppliers to check their customer catalogs against your catalog validation preferences before publishing the customer catalog to you. The supplier’s ability to qualify their customer catalog for your organization increases the likelihood that you can upload their customer catalogs without encountering errors. You can set the following validation preferences: • Specify the UNSPSC (United Nations Standard Products and Services Code) code version that you support. If the supplier’s UNSPSC version is different, SAP Business Network automatically converts the commodity codes in the customer catalog to your supported version. • Set an option to allow 0 price values. SAP Business Network’s standard customer catalog checking produces an error for 0 price values. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 123 -- 3 of 10 -- • Set an option to disable Unit of Measure (UOM) checking. This enables you to upload suppliers' customer catalogs without encountering an error if the customer catalog UOM codes differ from those you support. If you customize your UOM maps, you should disable UOM checking. • Set an option to disable commodity code checking. This enables you to download suppliers' customer catalogs without encountering an error if the customer catalog commodity codes differ from those you support. If you customize your commodity code maps, you should disable commodity code checking. Related Information Setting Catalog Validation Preferences [page 124] About Overriding Your Rules and Preferences for a Supplier [page 201] Setting Catalog Validation Preferences You can configure catalog validation preferences for your SAP Business Network account. Suppliers can check their customer catalogs against your catalog validation preferences before publishing their customer catalogs to you. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, choose Catalog Validation Preferences. The Catalog Validation Preferences page appears. 124 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration -- 4 of 10 -- Figure 14: Catalog Validation Preferences Page 3. To convert UNSPSC codes in the supplier's customer catalogs to the version supported in your Ariba Buyer configuration, choose Change and select the version number. 4. To disable some validation checking, choose one or more of the following: • Disable commodity code (UNSPSC) checking to ignore differences between the commodity codes specified in customer catalogs and commodity codes you support • Disable Unit of Measure (UOM) checking to ignore differences between the UOM specified in customer catalogs and UOM you support • Ignore zero (0) price values to ignore items with a price of 0 If you do not select a UNSPSC version, SAP Business Network validates against its “pinned” version, which is 13.5. 5. Click Save. Document Number Preferences for Invoices and Service Sheets The Document Number Preferences page allows you to configure document number preferences for service sheets, invoices, credit memos, debit memos, line item credit memos, non-PO invoices, and contract invoices in addition to standard invoices and service entry sheets. SAP Business Network allows buyer administrators to configure the numbering of documents for all or specific suppliers using the following rules: • Include a prefix which is limited to three characters • Include a sufox which is limited to three characters • Specify the maximum length of a document number • Whether to implement the rule for all suppliers or specific suppliers or specific supplier groups • Whether a document number can include digits (numbers) SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 125 -- 5 of 10 -- • Whether a document number can include upper case letters • Whether a document number can include lower case letters • Whether a document number can include special characters. SAP Business Network supports only the following special characters in document numbers: `, ~, !, @, #, $, %, ^, &, *, (, ), -, _, =, +, \, |, ', ", ;, :, /, and ?. However, we recommend that you use these special characters only if necessary. • Currently, SAP Business Network supports only the English alphabet to be used in the document number.  Note • Suppliers cannot view the preferences set by the buyer administrators. However, if the supplier enters a document number outside the premise of the buyer’s configuration, specific error messages will be displayed. • If a buyer has a customization project that customized the document number fields, the options specified on the Document Number Preferences screen override those settings. • Specific preferences configured for a supplier takes precedence over general preferences set for all suppliers. • Autogenerated service entry sheets have do not follow configured document numbering preferences and the service entry sheet number is the same as the invoice number. On the Configuration page, the Document Number Preferences link opens a page which contains the Configure Document Number Preferences section where you can configure document numbering preferences. The document subsections display the following fields: • Suppliers • Prefix • Sufox • Maximum length • Include numbers • Include uppercase letters • Include lowercase letters • Include special characters The field Maximum length refers to the maximum number of characters in the document number. This is a mandatory field. You can specify the preferences for the document number using the following options: Rule Description Remove sufox for auto-generated Service Sheet. Check this rule to remove the sufox appended to the document number for auto-generated service sheets. Otherwise, SAP Business Network auto-gen- erates the service sheet number. 126 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration -- 6 of 10 -- Rule Description Maximum number of characters Set the maximum number of characters, up to 35 for service sheets and up to 16 for invoices.  Note Buyers that enable auto-generation of service sheets should apply the same maximum number of characters to service sheet and invoice numbers to avoid problems. Whenever the SES ID exceeds the maximum number of characters preference value set for the service sheet, the SES ID is auto-generated. This behavior is also applicable for scenarios when the Remove sufox for auto- generated Service Sheet rule is checked. As a result, the service sheet document number auto-generated with or without the sufox does not fail, and the invoices are processed successfully. • If the Remove sufox for auto-generated Service Sheet rule is checked, the following scenarios occur based on the preference value set for Maximum number of characters for Invoice and Service Sheet: For invoice For Service Sheet Behavior No preference value set. No preference value set. The SES ID will be the same as the invoice ID with- out a sufox. No preference value set. Preference value set. If the invoice ID exceeds the service sheet docu- ment number preference, the SES ID will be auto- generated without a sufox. Preference value set. Preference value set. If the invoice ID preference value exceeds the serv- ice sheet document number preference, the SES ID will be auto-generated without a sufox. If the invoice ID is lesser than the service sheet document number preference, the invoice ID is re- tained as SES ID. Preference value set. Preference value set. If the service sheet document number preference is greater than the invoice document number pref- erence, the SES ID will be the same as the invoice ID without a sufox. • If the Remove sufox for auto-generated Service Sheet rule is not checked, the following scenarios occur based on the preference value set for Maximum number of characters for Invoice and Service Sheet: For invoice For Service Sheet Behavior No preference value set. No preference value set. The SES ID will be the same as the invoice ID with the _SS_1 sufox appended. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 127 -- 7 of 10 -- For invoice For Service Sheet Behavior No preference value set. Preference value set. If the invoice ID exceeds the service sheet docu- ment number preference, the SES ID will be auto- generated without a sufox. Preference value set. Preference value set. If the service sheet document number preference is less than the invoice document number preference: • And, if the invoice ID appended by _SS_1 equals less than the service sheet document number preference, the SES ID is set to invoice ID appended with _SS_1. • And, if the invoice ID is greater than the service sheet document number preference, the SES ID is auto-generated.  Note The _SS_1 sufox will not be appended to auto- generated SES ID if the SES ID does not adhere to service sheet document number preference after appending _SS_1. Preference value set. Preference value set. If the service sheet document number preference is greater than the invoice document number pref- erence, after appending _SS_1, if the SES ID is less than the service sheet document number pref- erence, invoice ID is retained and appended with _SS_1, otherwise SES ID will be auto-generated.  Note The _SS_1 sufox will not be appended to auto- generated SES ID if the SES ID does not adhere to service sheet document number preference after appending _SS_1. Supplier Profiles and Other Supplier Customizations You can customize the SAP Business Network supplier user interface with the help of an SAP representative. Customization enables you to change the presentation and behavior of SAP Business Network for your specific business. You can: • Create customized profile pages and require your suppliers to complete them. This feature enables you to collect additional information about your suppliers that is not captured in the default SAP Business Network company profile. • Add fields to invoices and ship notices. You can add specialized fields that support your procedures. For example, if your orders include the fixed bin location for items, you can customize ship notices to include that field, too. The data from the fields you add will be sent to you as extrinsics in cXML documents. • Control the behavior of fields in order confirmations, and add notes, warnings, page hints, and other text to order confirmation pop-up messages. • Hide amount-related fields in blanket purchase orders. You can hide the field labels and values for amount and subtotal fields. You can also just mask the values of certain fields, so the field label is displayed but the value shows as Undisclosed. • Enable your suppliers to upload invoices in CSV (comma-separated value) format. You can specify CSV-to- cXML conversion parameters and provide your suppliers with a CSV template for smooth integration with your procurement system. After the CSV template is finalized and available in your SAP Business Network buyer account, you can create a supplier group for CSV invoicing and assign all suppliers who should have access to the CSV template to this group.  Note Contact your SAP Ariba account manager to begin the CSV invoicing customization process. Working with an SAP representative, you create customization projects. Each time you and the Ariba representative create or modify a customization project, it must pass through the required stages described as follows. Stages 1-3 and 6 occur outside of SAP Business Network: 1. Create or edit pages. The SAP representative creates or modifies a customization project according to your specifications, or to convert CSV invoices to cXML format. 2. Unit test. The SAP representative unit tests each new or modified page in the customization project. 130 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/BuyerAdminGuide includi.title: BuyerAdminGuide including Rules_Part14
file://SBN/split/BuyerAdminGuide includi.content: 3. System test. You work together with the SAP representative to test the new or modified pages in the customization project. Testing occurs in your buyer test account and all associated supplier test accounts. At this stage in the process, you review the user interface as it will appear to suppliers and work with the SAP representative directly to request changes. In addition, through your buyer test account, you can integrate all installed SAP Ariba products to verify that the customization meets your specification. 4. Review. If the customization project involves adding fields, you sign in to SAP Business Network to review the cXML fragments for a customization project by entering values, submitting the forms, and viewing the response. This confirms that your ERP system (or other backend system that will receive the response) can recognize the new extrinsics. 5. Approve. You approve the customization project for publication. 6. Publish. The SAP representative publishes the new or modified pages from a customization project so that your suppliers can access them. You can assign customization projects to specific supplier groups. To review and approve customization projects, you must have the Customized Content Administration permission. To find out more about customization, contact your Customer Success Manager or Account Manager for more information on SAP Ariba Services. Reviewing and Approving Customization Projects [page 131] Validating Custom Fields in Invoices [page 132] Adding Custom Fields for Validation [page 133] Related Information Creating a Supplier Group [page 204] SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306] Reviewing and Approving Customization Projects If you work with an SAP representative to add custom fields to the SAP Business Network supplier interface, you can review the changes and approve the project for publication. Context The purpose of reviewing a customization project is to check the cXML fragment, not how the customized user interface appears to suppliers. At the review and approval stage, SAP Business Network does not display the customized user interface as it appears to suppliers. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 131 -- 1 of 10 -- Procedure 1. Choose Customization from the menu bar. This link appears only after you and the SAP representative have begun system testing. SAP Business Network displays a list of all customization projects that the SAP representative has created for your organization. 2. Click Review for one of the projects. SAP Business Network displays all of the custom fields from that project on a single Review Customization page. 3. Enter values in the custom fields. 4. Click Submit Forms. SAP Business Network displays the cXML fragment at the bottom of the Review Customization page with a field key and its associated value for each extrinsic. 5. When you are finished reviewing the output, click Done Reviewing. 6. To approve the project for publication, click Approve. The SAP representative then publishes the new or customized forms for access by your suppliers. Related Information Supplier Profiles and Other Supplier Customizations [page 130] Validating Custom Fields in Invoices You specify rules for your suppliers when you want the value in these custom fields to be carried forward or validated against the order. You can allow or restrict suppliers to change the value in these custom fields when they create invoices. To do this, you request your SAP Ariba representative to add extrinsic fields for the order and invoice. Once these fields are added and published in a customized project, SAP Business Network automatically generates the corresponding invoicing rule for each custom field added. These rules are available in the Invoice Custom Field Rules section in the Default Transaction Rules and Supplier Group Transaction Rules pages. If the rule is checked, suppliers can edit the values in the custom fields while creating an invoice. SAP Business Network does not match the value in the invoice against the order. If this rule is unchecked, suppliers cannot edit the values in the custom fields while creating invoices. SAP Business Network copies the custom field value from the order to the invoice. The values in the invoice must match the values specified in the order, else the invoice fails. Related Information Supplier Profiles and Other Supplier Customizations [page 130] 132 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration -- 2 of 10 -- Adding Custom Fields for Validation You can validate custom fields in invoices against the values on the order. Procedure 1. Request your SAP Ariba representative to create a project and add custom fields to an order and invoice. For example, you request to add the CustomerPartID to an order and invoice. 2. You review and publish the project. 3. The following rules are available in the Invoice Custom Field Rules section in the Default Transactions Rules page. These rules are also available in the Supplier Group Transaction Rules page for supplier groups. By default, both these rules are checked. • Allow suppliers to change the line item field customerPartID on PO-based invoices • Allow suppliers to change the line item field customerPartID on BPO-based invoices  Note • If you request to add multiple custom fields, then a rule is added for each custom field. • If you have subscribed to the ICS Service, then the above rules are also available in the ICS Invoice Rules section. • The rules are available in the Invoice Custom Field Rules section until they are a part of the customized project. For example, if you request a change and remove the customerPartID for blanket purchase orders in the customized project, then the rule Allow suppliers to change the line item field customerPartID on BPO-based invoices is removed from the Invoice Custom Field Rules section. However, if the customerPartID field is removed from both order and blanket purchase order in the customized project, then the Invoice Custom Field Rules section itself is not available on the from Default Transaction Rules and Supplier Group Transaction Rules. End Points Integration Buyer administrators can configure end points in SAP Business Network to manage and control the flow of data from an SAP Ariba account to each of the various systems connected to it. An end point in SAP Business Network SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 135 -- 5 of 10 -- acts as a document routing placeholder that ensures documents from SAP Business Network are sent to the required destinations (systems). These destinations could be external ERP systems and the SAP Ariba procurement solution. When the SAP Ariba end point is configured, SAP Business Network automatically configures a default routing of all documents. This configuration provides the following benefits: • End point configuration can be used to define the destination for each inbound transaction from a supplier. • An end point may be an SAP Ariba solution (for example, SAP Ariba Buying) or your external enterprise resource planning system (ERP). • Buyers may configure multiple end points for each System ID/ERP account. Each end point has its own set of authentication (shared secret or certificate) criteria and profile URL. • For each transaction/document type, buyers may configure the destination as an SAP Ariba end point, an external ERP end point, or originating end point on an order. Figure 16: End Points Integration End points functionality in SAP Business Network focuses on applying logic to determine the destination system route for all inbound transactions from a supplier to your SAP Ariba procurement solution or external ERP. Enabling End Points Integration To use end points integration in SAP Business Network, contact your SAP Ariba Support Representative for assistance in enabling your account. End Points Integration Steps Configuring an end point and associating it with a specific document type entails the following steps: • Creating an end point with a unique identifier. • If necessary, creating or applying the settings from your current cXML configuration. • Assigning an end point destination for each document type (that is, order confirmation, invoice, order). • If your organization uses multiple external ERPs, you will need to create a SystemID before creating and assigning an end point. 136 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration -- 6 of 10 --  Note The first workflow assumes a first-time (out-of-the-box) setup in which your account has been enabled for end point support (multiple ERP not required), and that you are familiar with your organization’s cXML configuration. If your organization utilizes more than one external ERP, refer to the second workflow. Things to Remember When Configuring Document Routing • SAP Business Network creates the “Default” end point when end points integration is enabled for the buyer account. This default end point refers to the external ERP system with which SAP Business Network communicates. • If the buyer account is not configured for “Multi-ERP”, then the Default end point is automatically considered to be the ERP end point. • SAP Business Network creates the SAP Ariba Cloud Solution End Point (default name “Ariba”) as soon as the buyer account has been configured as an “SAP Ariba Invoice Management user” and/or an “SAP Ariba procurement solution user”. This means that the SAP Ariba end point becomes the gateway for all documents to flow between SAP Business Network and the SAP Ariba procurement solution. • Typically, in a multi-ERP environment, multiple end points are created (for each ERP system). These end points are available for selection in the drop down list. • Select the check box corresponding the documents that require copies to be delivered to certain end points based on customer requirements. • Keep in mind that each System ID you create will need to have its own document routing configuration. Example End Points Integration Scenarios 1. Your system landscape may encompass both an SAP Ariba procurement solution and an ERP system that integrates with SAP Business Network. In this case, orders and releases can originate from both SAP Ariba procurement system and the ERP system. You can create two end points, one for the SAP Ariba procurement solution and the other for the ERP system. This allows SAP Business Network to send the corresponding invoices to the respective systems. 2. If you want your non-PO invoices to be sent to an SAP Ariba procurement solution (for example, SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing), you can create and configure one end point accordingly. Click Save to save your changes. Quote Automation Rules You can configure rules for Request for Quote (RFQ) postings in SAP Business Network Discovery. You can configure rules to specify which suppliers are invited to RFQ postings based on the product and service categories in those events. For example, you can configure a rule to specify that if commodities in the Chemicals category are specified in the RFQ posting, only vendors in your approved vendor database are invited, and if commodities in the Ofoce Suppliers and Printing category are specified, all public SAP Business Network suppliers are invited. You can also configure a default supplier matching rule for any category that might not have a rule. By default, SAP Business Network Discovery matches commodities with approved vendors. SAP Business Network applies these rules to an RFQ posting if the SupplierSelector element in the QuoteRequest document does not include the matchingType attribute. Therefore, you can choose to do one of the following: • Include the matchingType element in the QuoteRequest document that is sent to SAP Business Network; SAP Business Network uses the specified matching type for the RFQ posting as a whole. Any configured quote automation rules are ignored. • Remove the matchingType attribute before the QuoteRequest document is sent to SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network applies the quote automation rules to the commodities in the RFQ postings and selects an appropriate matching type for the event as a whole. Configure quote automation rules from the Quote Automation page by choosing Account settings Manage Profile Quote Automation . Purging Audit Logs Customer administrators can use the Intelligent Configuration Manager workspace to purge audit log data older than a specified date or configure recurring data purges based on the retention policy in your site. For more information, see Data Purge Capabilities in Intelligent Configuration Manager in the Intelligent Configuration Manager Administration guide. Audit Logs for Buyers You can access classic and standard audit logs. To view audit logs, click the Account Settings icon, and choose Settings. Under Audit Log, choose Classic for the legacy audit log or Standard for the Intelligent Configuration Manager audit log. These are the available classic audit logs: • Transaction Rule Changes – This log tracks changes to default transaction rules. • Supplier Group Membership Changes – This log tracks changes to supplier groups. • Profile Changes – This log tracks changes to user profiles. • User Access – This log tracks user access activity, which includes the number of failed access attempts since the last successful sign in and their reasons.  Note This log can be exported to a PDF file with a maximum of 500 records. If you need additional records, change the search criteria to filter for a specific time period, user, or other field. • Currency Preference Changes – This log tracks changes to currency preferences. For more information about the standard audit log, see Managing SAP Ariba Audit Information. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 151 -- 1 of 10 -- Audit Log Management on SAP Business Network on BTP Business Details The SAP Business Network audit service, logs selected user and administration actions performed in SAP Business Network applications. It also logs user interface audit actions like create, download, purge, or delete audit reports. The audit actions are divided into the following categories: • Generic audit actions - purge, delete and download audit reports • Inegrated audit actions - create audit reports For more information about audit logs for buyers, see Audit Logs for Buyers [page 151]. For more information about audit logs for suppliers, see Audit Logs for Suppliers. The SAP Business Network on BTP audit service enables administrators and security personnel to take a detailed look at what occurs in their SAP Business Network site, reproduce potential malicious activities of users and administrators, monitor administrative activities, like configuration changes, and retrieve forensic evidence if a security breach occurs. The SAP Business Network audit service records activities and events relevant for security auditing. You can access audit service records for evaluation in the form of security audit reports. In legacy SAP Business Network Audit Classic is where you can view the audit logs. In SAP Business Network on BTP, all audit logs are now written to BTP and retrieved from BTP. The main difference of audit between SAP Business Network on BTP and legacy SAP Business Network is that in legacy SAP Business Network the audit events were generated in a synchronous manner, providing a real-time view of the audit trail. Whereas in SAP Business Network on BTP you first need to create an audit repor, download it to view them. To view audit logs, click Account Settings Settings and then choose Audit Log Standard from the Compliance section. Implementation Details General Prerequisites Ensure that the user have the following permissions to access audit logs: • User Administration • Audit Log Administration Business End User Tasks The SAP Business Network audit service log entries contain identifying information, such as user, event type, date, and time. When users change data, the SAP Business Network audit service records both the old and new value. The SAP Business Network audit service creates a log entry when a user, integration tool, or scheduled event performs the following actions: 152 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration -- 2 of 10 -- • Changes a user's authorization • Exports or downloads data • Creates, edits, or deletes data • Authenticates a user • Changes system configuration • Accesses or changes sensitive information The SAP Business Network audit service also records user consent to privacy policies, including the version number of the policy and whether the policy was a custom privacy policy or the SAP Business Network SAP Business Network Privacy Statement. For information about the types of actions recorded by the SAP Business Network audit service, refer to Audit Log Criteria for SAP Business Network. Audit Events and Reports The Audit events and reports page is where you view the list of audit reports that are created. The audit log report has filters for filtering the reports. Creating an Audit Report Follow these steps to create an audit report: 1. Click Create. 2. The Create Audit Report page displays the following fields: Fields Description Name This is a mandatory field. Enter a name for the report. Event type This is a mandatory field. Choose the type of logged audit events for which you want to create a report. For example, choose Security to view security critical events. Choose Data access to view data access related activities. The available event types are: • Security • Data access • Data modification • Configuration modification • Generic action • Integration From This is a mandatory field. Choose the start date for the events. You can choose a valid date (within the last 3 months) using the calendar tool. To Choose the end date for the events. You can choose a valid date (within the last 3 months) using the calendar tool. 3. Click Create to create an audit report with the specified name. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 153 -- 3 of 10 -- Viewing the List of Audit Reports The Audit Events and reports page displays the list of reports that have been generated. In this page, you can use the search filters to look for a particular report, download a report, or delete a report. Search a report User the search filters to search for a report. The available fields are: • Name • Event Type • Status After entering the required search criteria, click Apply to search for audit reports based on the search filters. Click Clear to clear the search filter fields. The Audit Reports Log section shows all generated reports. Each row in the table displays information for the generated report such as name of the report, who created it, when it was created, type of the event, and the status. The following table explains the statuses that appear on the Status column. Status Description PROCESSING Indicates that the report creation is in progress. COMPLETED Indicates that the report is successfully generated and can be downloaded. An email is sent to the user when the report is generated. FAILED Indicates that the report generation has failed. An email notification is sent to the user when the report generation fails. PURGE SCHEDULED Indicates that the report will be purged. An email notification is sent to the user one day before the report is automatically purged. From the day the notification is sent to the user and till the report is purged, the report will be in purged scheduled status. There is no retention period for the purged report. PURGED Indicates that the report has been purged. SAP Business Network purges the generated report after 30 days. A reminder email is sent to the user one day before the actual purge. If the user wishes to download the report can do so. The status of the report is changed to Purged scheduled. The purged reports are permanently deleted and there is no retention period. Audit Reports The Audit Report Logs section lists all generated reports. • Click Download to download the generated report in XLS format. • Click Delete to delete a generated report.  Note If a user offboards from SAP Business Network, all the associated audit reports are deleted automatically. • Click Create to create a new audit report. 154 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration -- 4 of 10 -- Audit Event Types The following table describes the types of events: Event Type Description Security Security-related events for discovery and analysis of security critical incidents. For example, server start or stop, failed sign-in attempts, failed authorization checks, critical system pa- rameter changes, and so on. Data access Data access-related events, such as successful and unsuccessful attempts to access personal identifiable data and confidential data, access to different services or applications, read ac- cess of confidential data, and so on. Data modification Personal data modification events and auditing reasons. This includes personal and confiden- tial data updates, changes to group membership, or contact information. Configuration modification Administrative actions and events in your site and all configuration modifications. Generic action Actions generated or occurring in the system, such as: • Actions that transfer data to or from the system. For example, file uploads or downloads. • Scheduled integration tasks. Integration Actions related to integration events such as data import and export, inbound or outbound API calls, and events related to configuration files. Unit of Measure Data for Your Account You can use the unit of measure CSV template to define the unit of measure codes that you use in your business, as well as provide additional information such as the symbol, name, and description for each code. Unit of measure codes can be based on ISO or UN/CEFACT standards, or they can be any arbitrary codes defined by your company. If unit of measure codes are company-specific, it's important to provide additional information about the codes to suppliers so they can understand what the codes mean in purchase orders and other SAP Business Network documents. The unit of measure CSV template has the following four header rows at the top of the template: • Row 1: Character encoding (for example, 8859_1). • Row 2: Field names (Code, Name, Symbol, and Description). • Row 3: Whether the field is required or optional. • Row 4: Data type and maximum length (for example, "String 100"). The first three fields in the template, Code, Name, and Symbol, are required. The Description field is optional. The fields can be rearranged in any order as long as the field names are not changed.  Note If there is no symbol for a code, we recommend that you repeat the Code value in the Symbol field. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 155 -- 5 of 10 -- The following table shows an example of unit of measure information that you can add to the CSV template: Code Name Symbol Description 2N dB decibel decibel 2P kbyte kilobyte kilobyte 2Q kBq kilobecquerel kilobecquerel 2R kCi kilocurie kilocurie DZN dozen DOZ dozen PK pack PK pack TP ten pack TP ten pack Language Support The unit of measure master list supports multiple languages. Fill in the template in a separate CSV file for each locale. To activate a master list, upload strings for at least the English locale. Downloading the Unit of Measure Template You can download a CSV template to populate it with unit of measure codes to upload to your SAP Business Network account. To support different locales, save a different version of the file for each locale. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Procedure 1. Choose Settings Master List . The Master List page appears. 156 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration -- 6 of 10 -- Figure 17: Master List Page 2. For the Unit of Measure master list, click Download template, and save the file to your computer. Uploading Unit of Measure Data You can use the unit of measure CSV template to upload additional unit of measure information to your account for use in SAP Business Network documents. Prerequisites • You are assigned the Administrator role. • Fill in the CSV template with information about unit of measure information codes for one or more locales. To activate the list in your account, upload strings for at least the English locale. Procedure 1. Choose Settings Master List . 2. For the Unit of Measure master list, click Upload or download master list. 3. For the locale of the CSV file you are uploading, click Upload. 4. Click Browse to select a CSV file, and then click Upload. 5. Repeat steps 3 [page 157] and 4 [page 157] for other locales, as needed.  Note To verify the data you uploaded, click Download. 6. Click Done. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 157 -- 7 of 10 -- Enabling or Disabling Unit of Measure Codes You can disable and enable unit of measure codes that you uploaded to your account. If you disable a unit of measure code, suppliers can't find it anymore in the application, although they can still enter it. Prerequisites • You are assigned the Administrator role. • Before you can enable or disable unit of measure codes, you must first upload them to your account. When you upload unit of measure codes, they are enabled by default.  Restriction Once you upload a unit of measure code to your account, you cannot delete it. However, you can update the Name, Symbol, and Description fields for a unit of measure code. Procedure 1. Choose Settings Master List . 2. For the Unit of Measure master list, click Enable or disable codes. The Enable or disable unit of measure codes page appears. 3. Select Code or Name from the list. 4. Type the start of a code or name, and then click Search. 5. Select one or more codes. 6. Click Enable to enable the selected codes, or click Disable to disable them. 7. Click Done. Activating the Analytics Functionality in Your SAP Business Network Buyer Account You activate the analytics functionality in your SAP Business Network buyer account from the Configuration page. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. 158 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration -- 8 of 10 -- Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, click Analytics Configuration. 3. Click Submit to configure and activate the analytics functionality. If the operation fails, click Retry. You can retry the operation for a maximum of 4 times. Contact SAP Ariba Customer Suppor for help if the operation fails after the maximum number of tries. Setting Default Decimal and Digit Group Separators for Peru SAP Business Network buyers whose addresses are set to Peru can set default decimal and digit group separators. For some locales, including Spanish-Peru, the default Web browser setting is to use the comma (,) as a decimal separator and the dot (.) as a digit grouping separator. This can lead to errors on SAP Business Network in locales that actually use the dot as a decimal separator and the comma as a digit group separator. As a buyer, you can set default decimal and digit group separators in SAP Business Network that override the defaults that apply to your preferred browser in your locale. These defaults can be set by administrators to be applied at organization level or at individual user level. Preferences set at individual user level override those set at the organization level. Separator preferences are reflected in all fields that use separators in SAP Business Network reports. Enabling This Feature This feature is disabled by default. To enable this feature, please have your Designated Support Contact log a service request. An SAP Ariba Support representative will follow up to complete the request. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 159 -- 9 of 10 -- Setting Default Decimal and Digit Group Separators at Organization Level You can set default decimal and digit group separators at the organization level. These settings override the defaults that apply to your preferred browser in your locale. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the Company Information permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. • The default decimal and digit group separators feature must be enabled for your account. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, choose Company Profile. 3. Add the required defaults for the Decimal Separator and Digit Grouping Separator fields in the Separator Preference area. 4. Click Save. Results Your changes take effect at the next sign in. Setting Default Decimal and Digit Group Separators at Individual User Level You can set default decimal and digit group separators at the individual user level, which override settings at the organization level. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the Company Information permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. 160 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration -- 10 of 10 --
