However, we recommend that you manually convert the vendor IDs that were not automatically converted through transaction documents from SAP Ariba Procurement solutions. When all vendors use the new vendor compound keys, SAP Business Network does not create duplicate accounts and supplier relationships during quick enablement.  Note If buying organizations using Oracle Fusion Middleware with SAP Business Network document automation features (and without SAP Ariba Procurement solutions) want to use the vendor compound key, they must convert their SAP Business Network vendor IDs. There are two ways to convert vendor IDs manually: • Mass conversion using the vendor CSV file • Converting vendor IDs from the active relationships page  Tip To find out which SAP Business Network vendors have not been converted, run the Vendor Data Export report. If the Site ID column or the Legacy Vendor ID column has no value, then the vendor ID has not been converted. Related Information Converting Vendor IDs in the SAP Business Network User Interface [page 192] Mass-Converting Vendor IDs Using the Vendor CSV File [page 192] Converting Supplier Identifiers Used by SAP Ariba Procurement solutions [page 193] SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 191 -- 1 of 10 -- Mass-Converting Vendor IDs Using the Vendor CSV File To convert existing vendor IDs to the vendor compound key manually, you edit and upload the vendor CSV file. The Legacy Vendor ID column is used to look up the old vendor ID. You can add the vendor compound key values in the appropriate columns as needed. Context You can edit the CSV output from a full vendor data export report to move values in the Vendor ID column to the Legacy Vendor ID column. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. Download a full vendor data export report from the Reports tab, and open the resulting CSV file. 3. For the vendors you want to convert, move the values in the Vendor ID column to the Legacy Vendor ID column in the vendor CSV file. 4. Enter values in the Vendor ID column. If applicable for your ERP system, enter values in the Site ID and Site Auxiliary ID columns, too. 5. Save and upload the file. (Choose Supplier Enablement Manage Vendors , click Upload, provide a name for the upload operation, and specify the file.) Related Information Converting Vendor IDs in the SAP Business Network User Interface [page 192] Converting Supplier Identifiers Used by SAP Ariba Procurement solutions [page 193] Converting Vendor IDs in the SAP Business Network User Interface You can convert vendor IDs in the user interface by editing the supplier identifiers for suppliers on the Active Relationships page. These IDs were formerly called supplier private IDs and are the IDs used by SAP Ariba Procurement solutions. Related Information Mass-Converting Vendor IDs Using the Vendor CSV File [page 192] 192 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management -- 2 of 10 -- Converting Supplier Identifiers Used by SAP Ariba Procurement solutions [page 193] Converting Supplier Identifiers Used by SAP Ariba Procurement solutions You can convert vendor IDs from the Active Relationships page. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . 3. For the vendor whose supplier identifier you want to convert, choose More Actions Edit . 4. In the Edit Preferences for Supplier page, scroll down to the Unique Supplier ID Configuration section. 5. Click Convert for an ID that you want to convert. The Convert Supplier Private ID dialog box opens. The value you are converting is in the Legacy Supplier Private ID field. 6. Enter a value in the Vendor ID field. If applicable, enter values in the Site ID and Site Auxiliary ID fields, too. 7. Click Save. Related Information Mass-Converting Vendor IDs Using the Vendor CSV File [page 192] Converting Vendor IDs in the SAP Business Network User Interface [page 192] Integration of Supplier ID Normalization with ERP Systems Buyers can integrate supplier ID normalization with their existing SAP or Oracle ERP systems. No action is required for buyers that use a PeopleSoft ERP system. With PeopleSoft, there is no integration with the ERP system through SAP Business Network. Integrating with SAP ERP [page 194] Integrating with Oracle [page 194] SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 193 -- 3 of 10 -- Integrating with SAP ERP For buyers using SAP ERP, integration is easy because SAP ERP uses only one field to identify suppliers. If your organization uses SAP ERP, consider the following: • Buyers that use SAP ERP do not need to do anything to integrate the new vendor compound key with their ERP system, because SAP ERP uses only one field, Vendor ID, to identify supplier sites. • The SAP Business Network entitlement option Send VendorID, SiteID and SiteAuxID in outgoing documents is not turned on for buying organizations using SAP ERP, because the SAP ERP adapter has not been updated to consume values sent using the VendorID domain. • New SAP Business Network buyers do not need to fill in the Legacy Vendor ID column when uploading vendors to SAP Business Network using the vendor upload CSV file. • When vendor IDs are converted, the vendor ID and legacy vendor ID values are identical. Related Information Vendor Compound Keys Mapping to Vendor IDs in External Systems [page 180] Integrating with Oracle Buyers using the Oracle Fusion Middleware adapter must use a version of the adapter that supports the supplier ID normalization feature (adapter version 12s2 and later). For Buyers Using SAP Ariba Invoice Management Buyers using Oracle Fusion Middleware with SAP Ariba Invoice Management must decide which credentials to use, Vendor ID only, or Vendor ID and Site ID. If you chose to use Vendor ID only, then you must configure the private IDs at the supplier organization level in SAP Ariba Invoice Management. If you chose to use Vendor ID and Site ID, you are not required to configure the private IDs in SAP Ariba Invoice Management, but you must manually convert existing supplier IDs configured on SAP Business Network. For Buyers Using the SAP Business Network Document Automation Feature for Invoices or Purchase Orders If buying organizations using Oracle Fusion Middleware with Ariba Invoice Automation or Ariba Purchase Order Automation (and without SAP Ariba Procurement solutions) want to use the vendor compound key, they must convert their SAP Business Network vendor IDs. 194 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management -- 4 of 10 -- Related Information Vendor Compound Keys Mapping to Vendor IDs in External Systems [page 180] Configuring the Oracle Fusion Middleware Adapter to Send the Vendor Site ID [page 195] Configuring the Oracle Fusion Middleware Adapter to Send the Vendor Site ID By default, the 12s2 Oracle Fusion Middleware adapter only sends the vendor ID, not the vendor site ID to the ERP system. Therefore, existing buyers get time to learn about supplier ID normalization details, and to convert their SAP Business Network vendor IDs to use the vendor compound key. If you want the adapter to send the vendor site ID to the ERP system, you must: • Configure the adapter to send the vendor site ID. To configure the adapter to send the vendor site ID, you must populate the MAP_TYPE, MAP_KEY, and MAP_VALUE columns in the VALUE_MAP table using Insert/Update SQL commands. To send the vendor site ID, run the following insert command: insert into value_map values ('COMP_VENDOR_KEY','VENDOR_SITE_ID','YES') The following table explains the values in the preceding command: Field Value MAP_TYPE COMP_VENDOR_KEY MAP_KEY VENDOR_SITE_ID MAP_VALUE YES  Note This value tells the adapter to send the vendor site ID. If you do not insert the record in VALUE_MAP, or if you set MAP_VALUE to NO, the adapter sends only the vendor ID and not the vendor site ID. • Manually convert existing SAP Business Network vendors to use the vendor compound key (Vendor ID and Site ID). • Contact SAP Ariba Customer Support to enable the SAP Business Network option Send VendorID, SiteID and SiteAuxID in outgoing documents. Correcting Legacy Vendor IDs You can correct the legacy vendor ID in three ways: by editing preferences for the supplier, by editing vendor details, and by uploading corrected legacy vendor ID. • Edit preferences for the supplier from the Active Relationships page. In the Unique Supplier ID Configuration section of the Edit Preferences for Supplier page, the Legacy Supplier Private ID field is always editable. • Edit the vendor details from the Manage Vendors page. On the Vendor Details page, the Legacy Vendor ID field is always editable. • Upload corrected legacy vendor IDs in the CSV vendor upload file. Supplier Relationships After you establish a relationship with a supplier, you can manage and view details of suppliers. On the Supplier Enablement Active Relationships page, you can perform the following supplier management tasks: • Use filters to group suppliers and view status and details for them. • Resend email invitations to private suppliers. • Override default transaction rules and catalog validation preferences for suppliers. • Remove a vendor from the list of active suppliers. Viewing Supplier Relationships [page 199] Overriding Your Rules and Preferences for a Supplier [page 201] Terminating Active Supplier Relationships [page 203] Viewing Supplier Relationships You can view your organization’s supplier relationships on the Supplier Enablement tab. You can view your invited and current suppliers, as well as pending and declined relationships. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 199 -- 9 of 10 -- Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . 2. Click Supplier Selector and select a category of suppliers [page 200] to view. Supplier Status Information The Alerts and Messages section displays the status information about your suppliers. You can use this section to quickly view detailed information about the suppliers you have a relationship with. The next section on the page displays the different status information you can view by clicking these corresponding links in the Alerts and Messages section: • The Chargeable Suppliers link displays the number of suppliers you have a chargeable relationship with. • The Declined Private Suppliers in the last 30 days link displays the number of your private suppliers who declined to take ownership of their account in the last 30 days. • The Failed Private Suppliers in the last 30 days link displays the number of your private suppliers that SAP Business Network could not enable. • The New Suppliers added in the last 30 days link displays the number of your suppliers that have been added in the last 30 days. • The Suspended Suppliers link displays the number of your suppliers that are currently suspended. • The Declined Relationships link displays the number of suppliers that have declined to establish a trading relationship with you. Supplier Selector Categories The Supplier Selector button on the Active Relationships page displays the different supplier categories. Click this button and select a category to view the supplier information. SAP Business Network has the following supplier categories: • Private Suppliers displays suppliers with SAP Business Network accounts that were created on your behalf and of which the supplier has not taken ownership. You can resend the sign in information to private suppliers so that they can register and take ownership of their account. You can use the supplier enablement process on SAP Business Network to manage and track enablement activities for private suppliers. See Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network for more information. • Current-Former Private Suppliers displays private suppliers that have taken ownership of their account. • Declined Private Suppliers displays the private suppliers that have declined to establish a trading relationship with you. • Failed Private Suppliers displays the private suppliers for which SAP Business Network cannot create a private account. You can resend the sign in information to private suppliers so that they can register and take ownership of their account. 200 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/BuyerAdminGuide includi.title: BuyerAdminGuide including Rules_Part21
file://SBN/split/BuyerAdminGuide includi.content: • Invited Registered Suppliers displays registered suppliers that have not responded to relationship requests you have sent. You cannot yet transact with these suppliers. After SAP Business Network enables these suppliers, they are classified as Current Suppliers. If you invite a registered supplier and their account is set up to accept relationship invitations automatically, the supplier appears as a Current Supplier. If a registered supplier’s account is set up so that a user must review and respond to relationship requests manually, the relationship appears as a Pending Relationship until the supplier approves your request. • Invited Unregistered Suppliers displays unregistered suppliers to which you have sent relationship requests. You cannot yet transact with these suppliers. Suppliers might delay accepting requests so they can configure their order receiving systems before receiving purchase orders from new buying organizations. This process helps ensure that a supplier can receive your orders effectively. • Current Suppliers displays suppliers with which you have active relationships. Unless a current supplier’s account has been suspended, you can transact with these suppliers. • Suspended Suppliers displays suppliers with suspended accounts, which means you cannot transact with them. • Declined Relationships displays the suppliers that have declined your relationship requests. When a supplier declines your relationship request, SAP Business Network sends email notifications to you and the supplier. Suppliers might temporarily reject your relationship request if they are having trouble with your orders or to configure their order receiving systems to handle orders in a different manner. If you feel the supplier has declined the relationship in error, contact them directly. If you decide to establish a relationship, you can send them another relationship request. • Pending Relationships displays the suppliers you have invited and that have configured their accounts to review relationship requests manually. You cannot yet transact with these suppliers. Related Information Suspended Supplier Accounts [page 19] Supplier Membership Status Reports [page 270] Supplier Subscriptions [page 18] Private Suppliers [page 170] Supplier Relationships [page 199] Overriding Your Rules and Preferences for a Supplier You can edit the supplier relationship to override your default transaction rules and catalog validation settings. These overrides affect only the selected supplier. The Edit Preferences for Supplier page has the following categories of supplier preferences that you can override: • Purchase order rules • Scheduling agreement release setup rules • Contracts, invoices, time and expense sheets site setup • Invoice rules SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 201 -- 1 of 10 -- • Unique supplier ID configuration • Catalog validation preferences • Sales order rules • Forecast collaboration Figure 25: Edit Preferences for Supplier Page Invoice Rules By default, the invoicing rules you set in Configuration govern all your suppliers. You can choose not to apply your customized invoice rules to individual suppliers. For example, if you allow some suppliers to change the unit price during invoicing, but want to block other suppliers from changing the unit price, you can override the invoicing rules for suppliers who should not be allowed to change the unit price during invoicing. If you click Enable invoice rules, SAP Business Network uses your invoicing rules [page 91] from this supplier.  Note If you clear Enable invoice rules, SAP Business Network does not use any invoicing rules except the following (these rules cannot be turned off and are set to Yes or whatever is appropriate): • Allow suppliers to reuse invoice numbers. • Allow suppliers to send invoices with service information. You can also override invoice rules for supplier groups [page 204]. 202 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management -- 2 of 10 -- Overriding Rules and Preferences for Suppliers SAP Business Network enables you to set catalog validation preferences so that suppliers can qualify their customer catalogs for your organization before publishing them to you. You can override these settings on a per-supplier basis to enforce or unenforce certain rules. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . 2. Click More Actions Edit for a supplier. 3. Select a check box for each rule you want to override. 4. Click Save. Results Your updates take effect the next time the supplier logs in to their account on SAP Business Network. Related Information Catalog Validation Preferences [page 123] Terminating Active Supplier Relationships If you have already enabled a supplier’s account and are no longer buying from their organization, you can remove them from your list of current suppliers. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 203 -- 3 of 10 -- Context When you delete an active supplier, you • Remove your company from the list of companies to which that supplier can publish private customer catalogs • Cancel any customer catalog subscriptions you have with that supplier Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . 2. Click Supplier Selector and select Current Suppliers. 3. Click More Actions and then Delete in the Supplier column. SAP Business Network removes that supplier from your list of current suppliers. 4. Click Continue. Results SAP Business Network sends an email notification to suppliers you delete from your list of current suppliers. Creating a Supplier Group You can group suppliers in specific supplier groups to associate them with a customization project, define invoice rules, assign discount offers, or assign custom PDF layouts. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. Context You can use supplier groups for the following purposes: • Customization projects—With the help of an SAP representative, you can customize the SAP Business Network supplier user interface by creating a customization project [page 130]. You can then assign the customization project to specific supplier groups. A customization project can be used to do several things, such as customize supplier profile requirements, add invoice or ship notice fields, control the behavior of order confirmation fields, or enable CSV invoices. 204 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management -- 4 of 10 -- • Transaction rules—You can use supplier groups to organize your suppliers according to different order confirmation and ship notice rules [page 65], service sheet rules [page 84], and invoicing rules [page 91], including country-based rules [page 110]. If you subscribe to an SAP Ariba invoice conversion services (ICS) solution, you can create supplier groups for the suppliers who send paper invoices to the ICS provider. Typically, buying organizations want the invoice rules for ICS invoices to be less stringent than the rules for non-ICS invoices, to prevent some of the automatic validation that occurs with the default rules. For more information about invoice conversion, see the SAP Business Network Guide to Invoice Conversion. • Discount management—If your organization uses SAP Ariba Invoice Management or SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing with an SAP Ariba payment module, and discount management is enabled for these solutions, you can define multiple discount offers and then assign them to supplier groups. • Custom PDF layouts—With the help of an SAP representative, you can define custom PDF layouts for purchase orders [page 218] and ship notices [page 219] and then assign them to supplier groups. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Supplier Groups . The Supplier Groups page appears. Figure 26: Supplier Groups Page 2. Click Create. The Supplier Group page appears. 3. Enter a meaningful group name and description and click OK. Suppliers do not see your group names or descriptions. 4. To change transaction rules for the group, click Supplier Group Transaction Rules. The Supplier Group Transaction Rules page appears. The settings you make here affect only this group of suppliers. 5. When you are finished configuring transaction rules, click OK to save your settings and close the Supplier Group Transaction Rules page. 6. Click OK to save the supplier group. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 205 -- 5 of 10 -- Related Information Custom PDF Layouts [page 217] Modifying Supplier Groups You can modify a supplier group by adding or removing suppliers from them. You can also search for suppliers within a group. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. • If you defined a custom PDF layout for purchase orders or ship notices, an SAP Ariba Support representative must upload the PDF layout file (an XSLT file) to your account and configure the layout before you can assign it to supplier groups.  Restriction You cannot delete supplier groups after creating them, but they can be disabled and hidden. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Supplier Groups . SAP Business Network lists your supplier groups. 2. Click the name of the group you want to modify. 3. To add suppliers to this group: a. Click Add Members. b. Search for suppliers to add to the group. You can search only for your current suppliers. You can search for the supplier’s company name or ANID. c. When you find the supplier you want to add, select it and click OK. SAP Business Network adds the supplier to the group. 4. Locate suppliers to remove from this group or assign group members to another group: a. Enter the name of a supplier at the top right of the Group Members table and click Search. SAP Business Network performs a match based on exactly the value you specify. For example, entering “acme” returns all suppliers listed as “acme” or “ACME.” This field is not case-sensitive. you can search only for your current suppliers. b. Scroll down through the list of displayed group members. The list includes only the first 200 suppliers in the group. If you do not see the supplier you are looking for, use the Search feature. 206 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management -- 6 of 10 -- 5. Select the suppliers you want to remove or assign to another group. 6. Do one of the following: • To remove suppliers, click Remove Members. • To assign suppliers to another group, click Assign Group. Assign the suppliers to another group and click OK. 7. To change invoice rules for the group, click Supplier Group Transaction Rules. The settings you make here affect only this group of suppliers. If you subscribe to an ICS solution, you can configure one supplier group as the group to which SAP Business Network adds new suppliers created through ICS quick enablement. The check box Use this group for suppliers created through the Invoice Conversion service can be selected for one supplier group only. For details, see the SAP Business Network Guide to Invoice Conversion. If you want to change invoice rules for suppliers that belong to a country/region that requires specific invoice rule, specify them. Click View Invoice Rule Results to view invoice rules based on a supplier group level, default transaction group level, or country/region level. 8. In the Custom PDF Layouts section, find Purchase Order Layouts or Ship Notice Layouts and click Assign Layouts. a. Select one or more layouts to assign to the group.  Note If the Assignment List is empty, there are no custom PDF layouts configured for your account. b. Click Save. c. Click Done to close the Supplier Group Layout Assignment page. 9. Click OK. Related Information Invoice Rules [page 91] Overriding Your Rules and Preferences for a Supplier [page 201] Custom PDF Layouts [page 217] Assigning Suppliers to a Supplier Group For easier configuration, you can assign suppliers to a supplier group. The group's transaction rules apply to all its members. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 207 -- 7 of 10 -- Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . SAP Business Network lists your supplier groups. 2. Select suppliers you want to assign to a group. 3. Click Actions and choose Assign Supplier Group. 4. Click the supplier group to assign the selected supplier and click OK. Assigning Multiple Vendors to a Supplier Group On the Manage Vendors page, you can assign multiple vendors to a supplier group. The vendors can include active suppliers. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Manage Vendors . SAP Business Network displays the Manage Vendors page. 2. Select the vendors you want to assign to a supplier group. 3. Click Actions Assign to Supplier Group . SAP Business Network displays the Assign to Supplier Group dialog box. 4. Choose the supplier group to which you want to assign the selected vendors. 5. Click Assign. 6. Click Done. The vendors are now members of the assigned supplier group. You must refresh the Manage Vendors page to view the updated information. 208 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management -- 8 of 10 -- Assigning Suppliers and Vendors to a Supplier Group Using Vendor CSV Upload You can assign suppliers and vendors to a supplier group by uploading a vendor CSV file. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306].  Restriction If multiple vendors are uploaded with different supplier groups specified, and each vendor corresponds to the same supplier account, the supplier account is assigned to the last-specified supplier group. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Manage Vendors . SAP Business Network displays the Manage Vendors page. 2. Click Upload. SAP Business Network displays the Upload Vendors page. 3. Complete the following steps if you do not have a completed vendor CSV file: a. Click Download Template on the Upload Vendors page to download the vendor CSV file template. b. Enter supplier details, including supplier group information in the AN Supplier Group column, in the vendor CSV file template. c. Save the vendor CSV file. 4. Enter a name of the vendor CSV file you are uploading in the Name field. 5. Click Choose File and browse for your saved vendor CSV file, then click Open. SAP Business Network displays the warning, “Existing supplier groups might get replaced with the newly uploaded supplier group if present in the Vendor row” if values have been entered in the Group column of the CSV file. 6. Click Upload. SAP Business Network validates the uploaded vendor CSV file and displays its name, status and other information in the Upload Details table. You must click Refresh Status to view any updated changes. If the vendor CSV file is valid and does not create any errors, suppliers without a supplier group are assigned to the supplier group in the vendor CSV file, and suppliers that are members of a different supplier group are reassigned to the supplier group in the vendor CSV file. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 209 -- 9 of 10 -- Configuring Invoice Rules by Supplier Group Supplier groups can have different invoice rules than those defined in the Default Transaction Rules for your SAP Business Network account. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Supplier Groups . 2. Click a supplier group link or click Create to create a new supplier group. 3. On the Edit Supplier Group page, click Supplier Group Transaction Rules. 4. The default rule settings are displayed. Select Enter supplier group specific transaction rules and override the default rules. 5. Click Done. 6. Click OK to save the supplier group. Removing a Supplier from a Supplier Group You can remove a supplier from a supplier group at any time. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . 2. Select the supplier you want to remove from the group. 3. Click Actions and choose Remove From Supplier Group. 210 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/BuyerAdminGuide includi.title: BuyerAdminGuide including Rules_Part22
file://SBN/split/BuyerAdminGuide includi.content: Deactivating Unused Supplier Groups If a supplier group isn’t used anymore, you can deactivate it. You can’t delete a supplier group after creating it.  Restriction Before they can be deactivated, supplier groups must not contain any supplier or vendor members and they must not be used for suppliers created through Invoice Conversion Services (ICS). Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Supplier Groups . 2. Click Deactivate in the row of the supplier group you want to deactivate. 3. Click Yes to confirm the deactivation. Hiding Supplier Groups To simplify the Supplier Groups page, you can hide supplier groups that have been deactivated. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306].  Restriction Supplier groups must be deactivated before they can be hidden. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Supplier Groups . 2. Click Hide Deactivated Supplier Groups. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 211 -- 1 of 10 -- Reactivating Supplier Groups If you deactivated a supplier group temporarily, you can reactivate it and assign suppliers to it again. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Supplier Groups . 2. Click Show Deactivated Supplier Groups if the Deactivated Supplier Groups table is hidden. 3. Click Activate in the row of the deactivated supplier group you want to activate. 4. Click Yes to confirm the activation. Custom Routing Method for Suppliers You might have suppliers that have invested in a non-SAP Business Network business-to-business integration data format system and protocol to support their existing customer integrations. You can continue to standardize your business processes using SAP Business Network while allowing these suppliers to retain their existing infrastructure and processes to transact with you on SAP Business Network. Using an intermediary between SAP Business Network and the supplier, you can map cXML documents from SAP Business Network to the format required by the supplier and route documents between the supplier and SAP Business Network. To route your documents to the intermediary, you configure a custom routing method. The following overview describes the process to set up custom routing: 1. Identify the suppliers that require a custom routing method. 2. Contact SAP Ariba Support and request enablement for custom routing. 3. SAP Ariba Support obtains the list of your suppliers that require custom routing and set up these suppliers on SAP Business Network. SAP Ariba Support then configures your account to use the custom routing method. 4. Choose the suppliers that require the custom routing method in your SAP Business Network account. 5. Your suppliers are contacted and provided instructions on setting up their account. Once the supplier's account is configured, they receive a confirmation notification. 6. The supplier configures their SAP Business Network accounts to send and receive documents from their business application to you over SAP Business Network using the custom routing method. You can view details on the custom routing methods when you generate a Supplier Profile report. 212 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management -- 2 of 10 -- Configuring Your Account to Use a Custom Routing Method You can enable a custom routing method to support suppliers that require it. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. Procedure 1. Contact SAP Ariba Customer Support and request enablement for custom routing. Once your account is configured, sign in to SAP Business Network. 2. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . SAP Business Network lists your current suppliers. 3. Select the suppliers that require a custom routing method. 4. Click Actions and choose Activate Custom Routing. Commodity and Sales Territory Mappings You can bulk upload commodity and sales territory information to Vendor profiles in your SAP Business Network Vendor Master. After the supplier takes ownership of their account, further commodity and sales territory uploads do not impact the supplier’s profile. Uploaded commodities should be in UNSPSC version 14 format. To upload non-UNSPSC taxonomy commodities to SAP Business Network, corresponding mappings must exist in your sourcing realm. Uploading Commodity and Sales Territory Mappings You can map the custom commodity, currency, and unit of measurement values in your ERP system to values in SAP Business Network. A commodity code map translates custom commodity codes in one domain to another domain, such as UNSPSC. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 213 -- 3 of 10 --  Restriction If a vendor’s profile has missing commodity and sales territories information, then the vendor may not be matched to the RFQ posting in the Matched Vendor case. Context This mapping ensures that the custom taxonomy in your ERP system is mapped to values in SAP Business Network when you upload your suppliers from your ERP system. During vendor matched supplier enablement, the mapping allows existing suppliers in your vendor master to be matched to RFQ postings based on commodity and sales territories. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Manage Vendors . 2. Choose Upload Supplier Commodity Codes and Sales Territories . The Upload Supplier Commodity Codes and Sales Territories page appears. 3. Click Download Template to download the supplier commodity codes and sales territories template. 4. Upload a CSV file with the supplier commodity codes and sales territories you want to add to your SAP Business Network profile. Details uploaded will be added incrementally to your existing commodities and sales territories.  Note The maximum recommended upload file size is 10MB. Your browser might time out for larger files.You can use a zip utility to compress CSV File before uploading it. Zipped files must have a .ZIP file extension. 5. Click Done. Supplier Contacts Individuals within your company can serve as contacts for current and potential trading partners. Before you can assign individuals in your company as specific contact types, you must create a pool of contact personnel. Suppliers need to know whom to contact within your company with various inquiries, ranging from initial contacts to technical questions related to your SAP Business Network account. Managing Contact Assignments [page 215] Managing Supplier Contact Types [page 216] 214 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management -- 4 of 10 -- Managing Contact Assignments You can assign individuals in your company to serve as contacts for current and potential trading partners. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the Contact Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. • For each individual, you must provide a first and last name, and either a valid email address or a phone number. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Contacts . The Contacts page appears. Figure 27: Contacts Page 2. To create a new contact person, do the following: a. Click Create. The Create New Contact page appears. b. Enter the first and last names of the contact. The Business Title field is optional. c. Enter a valid email address or a phone number, or both, and click Save. SAP Business Network returns to the Contact Personnel page. Your new contact is displayed.  Note When specifying an email address or telephone number, you might want to ask employees which contact method they prefer, to ensure they are prepared to handle inquiries effectively. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 215 -- 5 of 10 -- 3. To edit a person’s contact information, do the following: a. Select the person and click Edit. b. Update the person’s name, contact information, or select a different contact type. To create new contact types, see Managing Supplier Contact Types [page 216]. c. Click Save. 4. To delete a person from your contact personnel pool, select the person and click Delete. Managing Supplier Contact Types You can create custom contact types that suit the way your organization does business. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the Contact Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. • You must add personnel to your list of contact personnel before you make contact assignments. See Managing Contact Assignments [page 215]. Context SAP Business Network provides one standard contact type—Business Contact. You cannot rename or delete this standard contact type. However, you can create custom contact types. Your companywide contact types are visible to all suppliers on SAP Business Network. The individuals who are assigned to these contact types should be prepared to respond to high-level inquiries. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Contacts . 2. Click Companywide Assignments. SAP Business Network displays a list of standard and custom companywide assignments. 3. To create a new type, do the following: a. Click Create. The Create Companywide Assignment page appears. b. Enter a name for the new contact type. This contact type is visible to supplier organizations on SAP Business Network and to others within your company. c. Select an individual from the Contact Person list. d. Click Save. SAP Business Network returns to the Companywide Assignments page and displays the new assignment. 216 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management -- 6 of 10 -- 4. To edit a contact type, do the following: a. Click the contact type. b. Select a different individual to assign to this contact type. If this is a custom contact type, you can also modify the contact type name. c. Click Save. 5. To delete a custom contact type, click Delete in the Actions column.  Note If you click the Delete link for a standard contact type, SAP Business Network removes the individual who is assigned. You cannot delete standard contact types. Custom PDF Layouts With the help of an SAP Ariba representative, you can define custom PDF layouts for purchase orders and ship notices and then assign them to supplier groups. Enabling This Feature This feature is disabled by default. To enable this feature, please have your Designated Support Contact log a service request. An SAP Ariba Support representative will follow up to complete the request. This feature requires custom XSL-FO stylesheets to be developed before the feature is turned on. You must engage SAP Ariba Services for help with this. Contact your Customer Success Partner (CSP) or Account Manager for more information about SAP Ariba Services. After a custom PDF layout has been configured by SAP Ariba Support for your account, an administrator for your account can assign the layout to supplier groups. See Modifying Supplier Groups [page 206]. Prerequisites • SAP Business Network buyers must request help from SAP Ariba Services to develop XSL-FO stylesheets for custom PDF layouts.  Note If you engage with SAP Ariba Services to develop custom XSL-FO stylesheets for custom PDF layouts, you will incur additional fees. • When XSL-FO stylesheets for custom PDF layouts are ready to be deployed, an SAP Ariba Support representative must upload them to your account. • Suppliers must belong to a supplier group that has been assigned a custom PDF layout to download and print it. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 217 -- 7 of 10 -- Custom PDF Layouts for Orders [page 218] Ship Notice Barcode Labels [page 219] Custom PDF Layouts for Quality Inspections [page 222] Custom PDF Layouts for Orders You can define custom PDF layouts for purchase orders to • Make them consistent with orders that originate from your ERP systems • Provide a familiar PDF layout for suppliers • Include only required information on the PDF, thus saving paper when printing  Note A custom PDF layout for orders can also include barcode labels. See Supported barcode types [page 220]. Workflow for Custom PDF Layouts for Orders The following describes the workflow for custom PDF layouts for orders: 1. An SAP Business Network customer contacts SAP Ariba Support to engage with SAP Ariba Services to define one or more custom PDF layout templates for orders. The templates are XSL-FO stylesheets. 2. An SAP Ariba Support representative uploads the custom XSL-FO stylesheets to the customer's account. Each custom PDF layout configuration should have a name that clearly identifies its intended purpose (for instance, an intended supplier, industry, or order format). 3. An administrator for the SAP Business Network customer assigns the custom PDF layout to a supplier group. Members of the supplier group can now print an order using the assigned PDF layout. 4. A supplier that belongs to the supplier group opens an order, and clicks Download PDF > LayoutName in the header to download the custom PDF format.  Note LayoutName is a placeholder for the name assigned to the custom PDF layout configuration for orders. There could be multiple PDF layout configurations for different types of orders. 218 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management -- 8 of 10 -- Figure 28: Custom PDF Layout for Orders Workflow Ship Notice Barcode Labels Buyers can provide suppliers with barcode labels to use for shipments. To facilitate the shipping of goods, SAP Business Network allows suppliers to print barcode labels directly from a ship notice in PDF format. The barcode label is generated from a custom PDF layout that customers can implement for their suppliers with the assistance of SAP Ariba Services. Ship notice barcode labels help buyers and suppliers to accelerate their logistics processes. They can use barcode scanners to quickly scan the barcodes for shipment information for their systems. Barcode label layouts can be applied at the header and the item level of the ship notice, giving suppliers the ability to print a single set of labels containing all the items of a ship notice or a label containing the information for a single line item. The specific fields needed on ship notice barcode labels can vary per customer. The ship notice barcode label layout can gather needed information at runtime from the ship notice cXML, related documents (such as a purchase order), and the buyer's and supplier’s SAP Business Network profile. For information about cXML data you can access from a ship notice or other related SAP Ariba documents, see the cXML reference guide at http:// www.cxml.org . Barcode Label Scenarios for Different Industries This feature flexibly supports different industry scenarios for ship notice barcode labels. For instance, suppliers in the automotive industry may need to generate one barcode label per item, a master barcode label for a grouping of items in a pallet, or a mixed barcode label for a grouping of a set of mixed items in a pallet. At the same time, suppliers in the food industry may require a single barcode label per shipping container. All of these scenarios can be supported by designing and configuring multiple barcode label layouts. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 219 -- 9 of 10 -- Figure 29: Barcode Label Scenarios: Automotive Industry Figure 30: Barcode Label Scenario: Food Industry Supported Barcode Types SAP Business Network uses Barcode4J 2.1 to generate barcodes. The Barcode4J library supports the following 1D and 2D barcode types: • Interleaved 2 of 5 • ITF-14 • Code 39 • Code 128 • EAN-128, GS1-128 (based on Code 128) • Codabar 220 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/BuyerAdminGuide includi.title: BuyerAdminGuide including Rules_Part23
file://SBN/split/BuyerAdminGuide includi.content: • UPC-A and UPC-E (with supplementals) • EAN-13 and EAN-8 (with supplementals) • POSTNET • Royal Mail Customer Barcode (Four State) • USPS Intelligent Mail (4-State Customer Barcode) • PDF 417 (ISO/IEC 15438:2001(E)) • DataMatrix (ISO/IEC 16022:2000(E)) For more information about Barcode4J, go to http://barcode4j.sourceforge.net/ . Workflow for Ship Notice Barcode Labels The following describes the workflow for ship notice barcode label printing: 1. An SAP Business Network customer contacts SAP Ariba Support to engage with SAP Ariba Services to define one or more custom layout templates for ship notice barcode labels. The templates are Extensible Stylesheet Language Transformations, or XSLT, files. 2. SAP Ariba Services uploads the custom PDF layout templates to the customer's account. Each custom PDF layout configuration should have a name that clearly identifies its intended purpose (for instance, an intended supplier, industry, or label format). 3. An administrator for the SAP Business Network customer assigns the custom PDF layout to a supplier group. Members of the supplier group can now print a ship notice using the assigned PDF layout. 4. A supplier that belongs to the supplier group opens a ship notice, and clicks Download PDF > BarcodeLabelLayoutName in the header or in a line item to print a barcode label in PDF format.  Note BarcodeLabelLayoutName is a placeholder for the name assigned to the custom PDF layout configuration for Ship Notice barcode labels. There could be multiple PDF layout configurations for different types of barcode labels. Figure 31: Ship Notice Barcode Label Workflow SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 221 -- 1 of 10 -- Custom PDF Layouts for Quality Inspections You can customize the PDF layout for quality inspections. These are some possible customizations: • Add a company logo. • Remove one or more of the standard quality inspection fields. • Add one or more of the quality inspection fields not shown by default. Workflow for Custom PDF Layouts for Quality Inspections The following describes the workflow for custom PDF layouts for quality inspections: 1. An SAP Business Network customer contacts SAP Ariba Support to engage with SAP Ariba Services to define one or more custom PDF layout templates for quality inspections. The templates are XSL-FO stylesheets. 2. A SAP Ariba Support representative uploads the custom XSL-FO stylesheets to the customer's account. Each custom PDF layout configuration should have a name that clearly identifies its intended purpose (for example, an intended supplier or industry). 3. An administrator for the SAP Business Network customer assigns the custom PDF layout to a supplier. 4. The supplier opens the quality inspection and downloads the custom PDF layout. Figure 32: Custom PDF Layout for Quality Inspections Workflow Application Gateway for Supplier Access to Non-SAP Ariba Applications SAP Business Network can be configured as an Application Gateway providing suppliers with access to a buyer's non-SAP Ariba applications through Single Sign-On (SSO). A buying organization can use this tool to provide any of its suppliers (with an active trading relationship) access to one or more of its third-party party applications. Buyers can request SAP Ariba to configure an Application Gateway on the supplier home page. This gateway shows links to customer applications that supplier users can access through SAP Business Network SSO. Buyers can then assign suppliers to access the third-party applications SAP Ariba has set up on the buyer's behalf. Buyers 222 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management -- 2 of 10 -- can configure access for suppliers by uploading a CSV file with the required information. SAP Business Network uses the uploaded information to enable or disable access. This also allows bulk configuration when there are large numbers of suppliers. For more information, see Workflow for Single-Sign-On (SSO) Access to Customer Applications [page 223]. Prerequisites • To have this feature enabled, please have your Designated Support Contact (DSC) contact your SAP Ariba Customer Success Partner (CSP) or Services Account Executive (Services AE), who can provide information about enabling the feature. • Buying organizations must provide access to their non-SAP Ariba cloud applications to their suppliers. • To use this feature, buyer third-party applications must be set up for single sign-on access. This is done by SAP Ariba Services. • Supplier administrators of authorized suppliers must assign roles that have the required permissions to access SSO. This authorizes users to access the buying organization's non-SAP Ariba cloud applications. • The buying organization's non-SAP Ariba cloud applications must support the configuration of SAP Business Network as the identity provider (IDP) using SAML 2.0. • Suppliers must have active trading relationships with buying organizations. Workflow for Single-Sign-On (SSO) Access to Customer Applications The workflows for single-sign-on (SSO) access to customer applications cover access using the Application Gateway widget and direct access. Workflow for SSO Access to Non-SAP Ariba Customer Applications from the Application Gateway 1. A supplier user signs in with their default SAP Business Network sign in credentials. 2. If the supplier is SSO-enabled for one or more customer applications, the Gateway icon is shown on the home page. 3. The supplier user clicks the Gateway icon to display the Application Gateway widget. 4. The Application Gateway widget will show links to all SSO-enabled applications from all buyers. 5. The supplier user clicks a link to access a customer application. 6. After successful authentication via SSO, the supplier user is redirected to a pre-configured landing page in the buying organization’s non-SAP Ariba application. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 223 -- 3 of 10 -- Workflow for Direct Access to Non-SAP Ariba Customer Applications Using SSO. 1. A supplier user signs in directly to the non-SAP Ariba customer application for which the supplier is enabled for SSO. 2. This sends a SAML request to SAP Business Network identity provider (IDP). 3. The SAP Business Network sign in page is shown. 4. The supplier user signs in with their default SAP Business Network credentials. 5. SAP Business Network IDP authenticates the supplier user. 6. After successful authentication, the supplier user is redirected to a pre-configured landing page in the buying organization’s non-SAP Ariba application. Configuring Third-Party SSO Service Subscriptions Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Context You can configure SSO access for suppliers by uploading a completed SSO service subscription CSV file. The Upload_Third_Party_SSO_Service_Subscriptions_Template.csv has the following structure: UTF-8,,,,,, Service Id,Supplier ANID,Operation Required,Required,Required String 150,AN0xxxxxxxxxx,String (must match pre-configured value) sample.service.com,AN01111111111,Enabled Column Description Required? Value Service Id Unique identifier of the third- party service Yes String of length 150 characters Supplier ANID The ANID of the supplier for whom access is to be enabled or disabled Yes Valid ANID Operation The operation to be performed for the supplier Yes Enabled or Disabled Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 224 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management -- 4 of 10 -- 2. On the Configuration page, choose Third Party SSO Service Subscriptions Configuration. 3. On the Third Party SSO Service Subscriptions Configuration page, complete the following steps if you do not have a completed SSO service subscription CSV file: a. Click Download latest template version in the Upload File section to download the SSO service subscription CSV file template. b. Enter the Service Id, supplier ANID, and the operation (Enabled or Disabled) in the CSV file template. c. Save the CSV file. 4. Enter a name for the upload event. 5. Browse to select the SSO service subscription CSV file. 6. Click Upload. Results SAP Business Network validates the uploaded CSV file and displays the upload event name, status and other information in the Upload Details table. You must click Refresh Status to view any updated changes. If there are no errors, the status shows Successfully updated Third Party SSO Service Subscriptions. If there are any errors, it shows Errors Found. You can correct the errors and upload the corrected CSV file for an upload event in the Reload File section of the Upload Details page of that event. If the uploaded CSV file is valid and does not create any errors, suppliers that are enabled for SSO access will see the corresponding application in their Customer Application Center, while suppliers whose SSO access is disabled will stop seeing the corresponding application. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 225 -- 5 of 10 -- Reports for SAP Business Network Buyers Use reports to collect information about activities related to your organization’s SAP Business Network account, such as transaction activity and the suppliers you transact with. A report is a snapshot of data generated at a particular point in time. With manual reports, you specify the data to include and then you generate the report. When you generate a scheduled report, SAP Business Network creates a report file in CSV (comma separated value) format, with UTF-8 encoding, and overwrites the last report you ran from that template. You can view and download reports to your local drive to save a record of your account activity over time. Your organization can generate a total of 100 reports. The maximum number of scheduled reports is 20. Your report templates and report files are visible to all account users.  Note You can generate up to six months of data in Order and Invoice reports, and up to seven days of data in Failed Invoice reports. Report Management [page 226] Report Templates [page 227] Generate and Download Reports [page 284] Report Management The Reports area of your account enables you to carry out all reporting tasks, including creating, editing, and deleting report templates, as well as running and downloading reports. To access the Reports area of your account, choose Reports Reports . The Reports page allows you to do the following: Button Description Run Puts a report into the report queue. SAP Business Network generates reports in the order in which they enter the queue. Regardless of the actual start time, the report will collect information for the date range and time zone you specified in the report template. The exact timing of a report run might differ from one run to the next, but the coverage period is always determined by the criteria in the report template Download Downloads a report file to view the contents. You can download any report that has run successfully. Save the file to your computer hard disk if you want to keep a record. The next time you run the same report, the new report file will overwrite the current report file on SAP Business Network. Edit Modifies reporting criteria in an existing template. The updated template replaces the previous version. Copy Copies a report template, edits any criteria, and saves it with a new name. When you save a new report template, SAP Business Network automatically puts your new report into the queue. 226 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Reports for SAP Business Network Buyers -- 6 of 10 -- Button Description Delete Deletes a report template and its corresponding report file. You might delete a report template if your organization has reached the maximum of 20, and you want to create an entirely new report rather than use Edit to modify an existing one. Create Creates a new report template. When you save a new report template, SAP Business Network automatically puts your new report into the queue. Refresh Status Refreshes the onscreen display of report status. You might refresh status when a report has been in Queued or Processing status for some time. To maximize the benefits of report templates, you can create scheduled reports.  Note If your organization has reached the 20 template maximum, or generated 80 manual and 20 scheduled reports, the Copy and Create buttons are grayed. Before you can create another template or report, you must delete unneeded reporting files. If multiple individuals in your organization have reporting permission, you might want to coordinate your approach to reporting. Changes made by one user affect reporting for all other users. Related Information Creating a Report Template [page 228] Report Templates With scheduled reports, the data included is specified from a report template. The report template defines what information is included in reports that are generated from it. For example, a purchase order report template defines which customers you want to include in the report, specifies that you want to report on purchase orders with amounts in a particular range, and so on. Your report templates are visible to all account users. Users see only those report types for which they have permissions. Users with permission can perform all tasks for a particular report type, including creating new reports, running, downloading, and deleting reports. You can run a manual report at any time by selecting the report on the Reports page and clicking Run. SAP Business Network collects information for the time and date ranges you set for the report. The exact timing of a report run might vary depending on the queue, but the coverage period will always be the same. Creating a Report Template [page 228] Canceled Payment Transactions Reports [page 230] Collaboration Type Status Reports [page 230] Daily Payment Summary Reports [page 234] Discount Metrics Reports [page 235] Discount Acceptance Reports [page 236] Early Payment Limit Reports [page 237] SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Reports for SAP Business Network Buyers PUBLIC 227 -- 7 of 10 -- Failed Dynamic Discounting Credit Memo Creation Reports [page 238] Failed Invoice Reports [page 240] Failed External Invoice Reports [page 240] Failed Order Reports [page 241] Goods Receipt Reports [page 243] Invoice Reports [page 244] Open Orders Report [page 246] Order Reports [page 252] Order Summary Reports [page 253] Organization Profile Reports [page 254] Payment Transactions Reports [page 255] SCF Trade Details Reports [page 256] Service Sheet Reports [page 257] Service Sheet Activity Log Reports [page 261] Ship Notice Reports [page 263] Supplier Enablement Status Reports [page 265] Supplier Enablement Task Status Reports [page 268] Supplier Membership Status Reports [page 270] Supplier Profile Reports [page 273] Supplier Legal Profile Status Reports [page 280] Supplier Remittance Information Reports [page 281] Tax Book Reports [page 282] Vendor Data Export Reports [page 283] Messaging Reports [page 284] Creating a Report Template You can create report templates that define what information is included in reports and whether they are scheduled or run manually. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with one or more report administration permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. 228 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Reports for SAP Business Network Buyers -- 8 of 10 -- Procedure 1. Choose Reports Reports . The Reports page appears. Figure 33: Reports Page 2. Click Create. 3. Enter a unique title that will help you and other users easily identify this report from a list. For example, “Monthly Rejected Order Report.” 4. Enter a description. The description is useful for identifying the scope and target of the report for all account users. For example, “Monthly report of all rejected purchase orders.” 5. Choose a value from the Time zone list. Date and times in your report file use the time zone you select here, expressed as GMT +/-. In addition, SAP Business Network uses the time zone to determine the range of information collected for the report. 6. Choose a language. SAP Business Network uses this language for labels in the resulting report file. It displays report data in the language in which the information was entered into the system. 7. Choose a report type. 8. Click Next. SAP Business Network displays the Schedule page with details for the report type you selected. 9. Click either Manual Report or Scheduled Report. To generate a manual report, go to the Reports page and click Run. SAP Business Network automatically generates scheduled reports using the frequency that you specify. 10. If you choose Scheduled Report, SAP Business Network refreshes the page and displays the Scheduling section. Do the following: a. Select a date range. By default, a scheduled report includes three months beginning with tomorrow’s date.  Note The maximum date range you can include in Order and Invoice reports is six months. You can include up to seven days of data in Failed Invoice reports. b. Choose a value from the Automatically Run list to set the report generation frequency. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Reports for SAP Business Network Buyers PUBLIC 229 -- 9 of 10 -- c. Enter up to three email addresses, each separated by single comma. SAP Business Network sends a notification to these addresses when the report status is Processed. 11. Click Next. 12. On the Criteria page, choose the parameters for the report. 13. Click Submit. SAP Business Network puts your report into the queue. You can view and download it when its status is Processed. 14. To view and download the report, select the report template and click Download. Click one of the following: • Open to view the report. Your browser starts Microsoft Excel and displays the report. • Save to save the report to your hard disk. Canceled Payment Transactions Reports SAP Business Network emails the Canceled Payment Transactions report as a CSV file attachment at the end of each day to the email address specified during the report setup. The Canceled Payment Transactions report contains information about all payment canceled that day, in the following columns: • Payment Number • Payment Date • Cancelled Date • Supplier ANID • Supplier Name • Private ID • Amount • Reason for Status • Cancelled By Collaboration Type Status Reports Collaboration Type Status reports contain detailed information about suppliers on SAP Business Network, assigned to their collaboration activities. The report includes information on the collaboration status, collaboration type, collaboration role, purchase order activity, and supplier contact details. The report also shows information on suppliers with the On Hold status and the reason provided for this status change. To run this report, you need the Supplier Enablement Report Administrator permission.  Note Suppliers can't generate this report. 230 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Reports for SAP Business Network Buyers -- 10 of 10 --
