file://SBN/split/BuyerAdminGuide includi.content: Related Information SAP Business Network Guide to Invoice Conversion Supply Chain Finance Capability You can unlock working capital by using supply chain finance, a tool that enables you to extend the payment terms and Days Payable Outstanding (DPO). The goal of supply chain finance is to optimize your accounts payable metrics, cash management, working capital, transaction costs, administration, and risk. On SAP Business Network, supply chain finance involves a third party financing organization connected to SAP Business Network that pays your supplier early at a discounted rate. The third party executes two separate agreements, one with you and one with your supplier. The agreement with you is a guarantee that you will pay the third party the full amount of the approved invoice at the term due date. The agreement with the supplier is a purchase agreement that transfers ownership of the supplier’s receivables to the third party when the early payment is settled. When the agreements are in place, the process works as follows: 1. You approve the invoices to pay and post them through SAP Business Network, which sends a copy to the third party provider. 2. The third party provider pays the supplier at the agreed upon discount rate. 3. You pay the third party provider the full amount of the invoice at the full term due date of the invoice. Related Information Ariba Working Capital Management Services datasheet Account Administrator Responsibilities One person in your organization acts as the account administrator. The administrator is responsible for: • Setting configuration options. See SAP Business Network Configuration [page 33]. • (Optional) Adding additional users to the account. See SAP Business Network Users and Roles [page 291]. • (Optional) Creating a test account for testing document flow with suppliers. See Using Test Accounts on SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network for Buyers PUBLIC 21 -- 1 of 10 -- Getting Started with the SAP Business Network User Interface for Buyers The SAP Business Network application user interface for buyers has the following key components: 1. Home page [page 22]—The default page you see when you sign in to SAP Business Network. Click Home to access your home page from anywhere in the application. 2. Menu bar—Provides access to the various pages in the application. Some menus go directly to a page, while others provide a dropdown list of commands. The menu bar that you see may vary depending on your account’s entitlements. 3. Header bar—Provides helpful menus, commands, and information about you and your company. • Use the dropdown on the top-left corner of the header bar to switch between different SAP Ariba web applications. • Click the Account Settings icon to choose one of the following commands from the dropdown: • ANID (Ariba Network ID)—A number that uniquely identifies your company on SAP Business Network. You might need this number to contact some support services. • Switch to Test Account—Change from production to test account modes. • Company Profile—Review and manage your company profile on SAP Business Network. • Manage Services—Manage your SAP Business Network services. • Manage Profile—Configure company settings such as locale settings, cXML settings, document routing preferences, system notifications, default transaction rules, country/region-based invoice rules, payment settings, application end points, and quote automation rules. • Settings—Access configurations for users and roles, self-service customization, the unit of measure master list, and your audit log. Also manage purge requests. • Logout—Exit SAP Business Network when you’re done with your session. • Click the Help  icon to activate SAP Companion in-app help. 4. Search bar—Provides capabilities to search for trading partners and network catalog products on SAP Business Network. • Trading partners search. See Searching for Trading Partners on SAP Business Network [page 333]. • Discovery search. See Searching for Products in Network Catalog from Various Suppliers [page 336]. Figure 2: SAP Business Network User Interface for Buyers Home Page You can navigate back to the SAP Business Network home page by clicking Home on the menu bar. Depending on your permissions, the Home dashboard can display the following content items. Only the Alerts and Messages content item is not permission-based. 22 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network for Buyers -- 2 of 10 -- • Alerts and Messages. This content item displays important information about SAP Business Network, and reminders about your account. A yellow icon is shown for alerts that require your attention soon, and a red icon is shown for alerts that require your immediate attention. You can permanently delete any item that does not have an icon by clicking the trash can icon. • Shipment Tracking. See Tracking Shipments from the Home Dashboard [page 427]. Be sure to respond promptly to alerts in the Alerts and Messages content item. Overview Tile Bar The Overview tile bar displays the default tiles for your business role, or tiles that you have configured. On the SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Home page, up to five tiles are displayed in the Overview tile bar by default. You can reveal an additional five tiles with the More button. You can also configure which tiles are displayed from the Workbench. For more information, see The Workbench [page 395] The Overview tiles are displayed intelligently: if one or more Pinned documents exist, that tile is displayed first. Otherwise, it is moved to the end of the order. Getting Started Tile Bar The Getting started tile bar offers you recommended tasks and information resources for first time users. The Getting started tile bar directs you to complete important configuration tasks for your account. For example, Update company profile, Upload company logo, or Upload vendors.  Note The tasks available to you depend on your permissions. Each Getting started tile includes an info icon that you can click to learn more about the task. You can mark Getting started tiles as complete to remove them from the tile bar. Marking a task complete increments the count on the Completed task tile. Click the Completed task tile to view tasks that were previously marked as complete, when, and by whom. Home Page Widgets Your Home page provides widgets to show at a glance current information for your business activities. The SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Home page displays role-based widgets. These widgets help you focus on important tasks, insights, key performance indicators, and benchmarks for your business. To customize the contents of your Home page, see Customizing Your Home Page Widgets. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network for Buyers PUBLIC 23 -- 3 of 10 -- Shipment Tracking Widget The Shipment tracking widget allows you to quickly track the status of shipments. Enter a purchase order number and click Track to view shipment status information. Purchase Orders Widget The Purchase Orders widget shows you the total value of purchase orders you have created in each month of the selected year. Data is displayed in your preferred currency. Click View all to view additional details on the Analytics dashboard. You must have the Analytics dashboard access permission and the analytics functionality must be activated to access the Analytics dashboard.  Note Purchase order and invoice amounts specified in non-USD currencies are converted to USD for the purpose of aggregation using the currency exchange rate at the time the transaction document is created. The aggregated amount is further converted to your user-specified currency for display in widgets. Therefore, you may see a difference between the original amounts displayed in the workbench and the aggregated amount displayed in widgets. Invoices Widget The Invoices widget shows you the total value of invoices you have received in each month of the selected year. Data is displayed in your preferred currency. Click View all to view additional details on the Analytics dashboard. You must have the Analytics dashboard access permission and the analytics functionality must be activated to access the Analytics dashboard. Delivery Execution Widget The Delivery execution widget displays the Perfect delivery, On time delivery, and In full delivery key performance indicators (KPIs) for your entire supply chain in the previous month. The KPIs are calculated by the underlying Delivery execution analytics story. You can click View all to view the full story in the Analytics dashboard. The KPIs are defined as follows: • Perfect delivery: The percent of items delivered on time and in full, calculated by dividing the total count of line items delivered on time and in full by the total count of line items evaluated. 24 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network for Buyers -- 4 of 10 -- • On time delivery: The percent of items delivered on time, calculated by dividing the total count of line items delivered on time by the total count of line items evaluated. • In full delivery: The percent of items delivered in full, calculated by dividing the total count of line items delivered in full by the total count of line items evaluated. To view the widget, you must be enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. You must have the Analytics dashboard access permission and the analytics functionality must be activated to access the Analytics dashboard. Supplier Enablement Widgets The Enablement summary, Full enablement progress, and Light enablement progress widgets enable you to quickly check the real-time enablement progress for your potential suppliers that are planning to use either an enterprise account or a standard account. To view the widgets, you must have at least one of the following permissions assigned to your account: Supplier Enablement Configuration, Supplier Enablement Program Administrator, Supplier Enablement Report Administration, or Supplier Enablement Task Management For more information, see Supplier Enablement Widgets. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network for Buyers PUBLIC 25 -- 5 of 10 -- Your Company Profile The buyer company profile on SAP Business Network provides information about your company and its business. You can review and manage information in the Company Profile to help suppliers learn about your company. Your Company Profile page consists of the following sections: Section Description Quick navigation pane Use the navigation pane on the left side of the Company Profile page to upload your company logo, jump to Contacts, or return to the Overview. Company Information An overview of your company information is displayed at the top of your profile. You can edit details such as the company name, website, DUNS number, number of employees, year founded, annual revenue, legal form, address, and business type. Categories, Locations, and Industries The data for Product and Service Categories and Receiving Locations are retrieved from your SAP Business Network Discovery activities and cannot be edited. You can specify Industries for your company. Marketing Collateral You can enhance your profile by adding marketing collateral in the form of attachments or external links. This helps suppliers learn more about your company. Activity Data Your activity data is displayed to provide transparency into your SAP Business Network Discovery posting history and build trust. Buyers with the Company Information permission can click the edit icon  beside each editable section to edit the information contained in the section. The  Options menu in the upper-right corner includes commands for viewing your public profile, obtaining a public profile URL, and setting profile visibility. Editing Your Company Profile [page 27] Uploading Your Logo [page 28] Editing the Main Contact [page 29] Showing or Hiding Your Company Profile in Discovery Postings [page 30] Profile Data Federation [page 30] 26 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Your Company Profile -- 6 of 10 -- Editing Your Company Profile You can enter or revise information about your company so that suppliers can identify the company and contact you. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Company Information permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Company Profile . This opens the Company Profile page. 2. Click the edit icon  for the section that you want to edit information, enter or revise values as needed, and save your changes. Note the following constraints and guidelines: • DUNS Number—A nine-digit number issued by Dun & Bradstreet, Inc. to identify each corporate location of an organization. You can obtain a DUNS number or look up your company’s existing number on Dun & Bradstreet’s website, https://www.dnb.com . • Number of Employees—The approximate number of people who work for your organization. • Year Founded—Enter the year in yyyy format. • Revenue—Select a currency range. If you prefer not to state your annual revenue, scroll to the bottom of the list and select Contact company for information. • Legal Form—Choose the type of business entity or legal status of your company from the dropdown. The list of values varies per country/region. • Business Type—Check the business types that apply to your company. • Industries—Select the industries your company serves. • Marketing Collateral—Click Add marketing collateral. Choose Attachment to attach any files you want to make available to suppliers, such as customer presentations, case studies, and certifications. Choose External link to enter a URL and a description for each additional site. You must preface URLs with “https://”. For example: https://www.Your-Company.com/service. 3. If you want to share more details about your transaction requirements with trading partners, choose Account Settings Manage Profile . Then on the Configuration page, choose Extended Profile Settings and Information. a. Fill out the questions with the information you want to share with your suppliers. You do not need to answer all questions. Your suppliers will be able to see only the completed questions. b. Click Save. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Your Company Profile PUBLIC 27 -- 7 of 10 -- Related Information Uploading Your Logo [page 28] Editing the Main Contact Uploading Your Logo SAP Business Network can display your organization’s logo on fax, email, and online Inbox purchase orders. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the Company Information permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. • File format: GIF • Maximum file size: 200 KB • Maximum width/height: 250 pixels • Color or black and white • Transparency is supported • Animation is not supported  Restriction If you upload a file containing multiple images, only the first one is used. Context You might want to add your logo so suppliers can tell who the customer is at a glance. Logos also appear on all emails and faxes sent to suppliers registering through the supplier enablement method. Logos do not appear on cXML or EDI orders. Your test account and production account each use their own logo. You might want to create a logo for your test account that clearly indicates that the orders are test orders. You cannot configure different logos to display to your suppliers. To save an existing logo on your computer, right-click it and select Save As in your web browser. 28 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Your Company Profile -- 8 of 10 -- Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Company Profile . This opens the Company Profile page. 2. From the navigation pane on the left, click the  Edit company logo icon. 3. In the Upload company logo dialog box, click Browse to navigate to and select your logo file. 4. Click Open. SAP Business Network displays the uploaded logo in the dialog box. 5. Click Save to save your changes. Your logo is active immediately. Editing the Main Contact The main company contact encompasses the overarching contact information for the organization as a whole, including general details such as email, phone, and fax. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Company Information permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. Context The main company contact is defaulted to the information of the account creator (administrator). You have the flexibility to edit and update this information as needed. To edit the main contact information in your company profile, follow these steps: Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Company Profile . This opens the Company Profile page. 2. From the navigation pane on the left, choose Contacts. 3. On the Company Contact Information tab, click the Edit button. 4. Update Email, Phone, Fax of your company as needed and click Save. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Your Company Profile PUBLIC 29 -- 9 of 10 -- Showing or Hiding Your Company Profile in Discovery Postings When you create a public posting on SAP Business Network Discovery, your company profile information is by default visible to suppliers. If you want to prevent suppliers from viewing your company profile information, use this procedure to hide it. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Company Information permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. Context Showing your company profile in postings can help potential suppliers feel more comfortable with doing business with your organization, resulting in increased responses to your posting. Although you can choose to hide your company profile information, SAP recommends that you show it. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Company Profile . 2. In the upper-right corner of the Company Profile page, choose the  Options menu, and the Profile settings command. 3. Toggle the Make my profile visible to supplier in postings option as needed. Profile Data Federation This feature enables your company profile data to be replicated across SAP Business Network's global data centers, making your profile visible to trading partners in different regions. For more information, refer to How Profile Data Federation Works [page 31] and Enabling Profile Data Federation. 30 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Your Company Profile -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/BuyerAdminGuide includi.content: SAP Business Network Users and Roles By creating roles and then adding users to them, the SAP Business Network administrator controls who can sign in to your organization’s account and which areas of the service each user can access. SAP Business Network Roles [page 291] SAP Business Network Users [page 296] SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306] Revoke User Access and Remove a User's Personal Information [page 315] Configure Retention Period and Manage Deletion of Revoked Users in SAP Business Network [page 318] Prevention of Manual Sign In by SAP Business Network Buyer Users [page 319] Multifactor Authentication [page 320] SAP Business Network Roles A user with the Administrator role can create a role with certain permissions and assign the role to a buyer user. A role defines a user function within SAP Business Network, such as Purchase Order Generator. Each role has a unique name and set of associated permissions that specify what users who are assigned to the role can see and do in SAP Business Network. A role can be assigned to any number of users. Using the Administrator Role After you complete registration, SAP Business Network creates a single default role named Administrator. The Administrator role is automatically linked to the user name and sign in that you entered during registration. The Administrator role should be assigned to the individual at your organization who is responsible for setting configuration options, managing supplier relationships and contacts, and maintaining the account over time. The account administrator serves as the primary point of contact for users with questions or problems. As the SAP Business Network account administrator, you control who can sign in to your organization’s SAP Business Network account and which areas of the service each user can access. To do this, you create roles and then add users. As a best practice, create roles that reflect the way your company does business to prevent confusion for your account users and maximize the efociency of your team once roles are in place. Only one SAP Business Network user can be assigned to the Administrator role. You cannot modify this role, but you can assign it to another user. The account administrator can assign user management capabilities to non-administrator buyer users, called user administrators. For more information, see the following topics: • Transferring Administration Ownership [page 303] • Assigning User Management Capabilities to Users [page 304] SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 291 -- 1 of 10 -- SAP Business Network Predefined Roles Predefined roles are visible only in accounts that were created before roles and permissions were introduced on SAP Business Network. If you registered with SAP Business Network after roles and permissions were implemented, Administrator is the only predefined role. To minimize disruption to these older users, SAP Business Network provides a small set of predefined roles to be used as templates for custom roles. SAP Business Network assigned the Full Access role to all preexisting users when it introduced roles and permissions. Administrators for these older supplier accounts should review the predefined roles and their permissions and consider using them as the basis for custom roles. The predefined roles are listed in the following table: This Role… Grants a User Access To… Administrator All areas of the account, including Settings Users and test account management Catalog Manager Catalogs Customer Catalogs Account Settings Manage Profile Notifications Catalog Service Full Access All areas of SAP Business Network, except areas that are reserved for administrators Purchasing Manager Give access to incoming and outgoing transaction documents and the following configuration pages: Account Settings Manage Profile Default Transaction Rules Account Settings Manage Profile cXML Setup Account Settings Manage Profile Notifications (transaction-related notifications only) Vendor Manager Supplier Enablement Current Relationships Supplier Enablement Contacts Account Settings Manage Profile Notifications Supplier Account Settings Company Profile Product Manager Catalogs Network Catalog Product Approver Catalogs Network Catalog The Administrator role includes all available permissions. These permissions grant the Administrator role access to all areas of your SAP Business Network account. Creating a Role [page 293] Modifying a Role [page 294] Reassigning Users to a Different Role [page 295] Deleting a Role [page 296] 292 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles -- 2 of 10 -- Creating a Role Buyer administrators and users assigned a role with the User Administration permission can define new roles with a specific set of user permissions that determine what the assigned users can see or do in SAP Business Network. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. • Before creating your first role, you might want to review the list of permissions. This list is useful for planning your approach to roles. Some companies create broadly defined roles that include all or most of the available permissions, while others create specialized roles that include narrow sets of permissions. By planning your approach to roles, you can prevent confusion for your account users and maximize the efociency of your team after roles are in place. • Before creating new roles, use the Permission dropdown menu to filter the Roles table for existing roles that already include that permission. Context A role defines a user function within SAP Business Network. You assign roles when you create users.  Restriction • You can create no more than 25 custom roles. • SAP Business Network does not notify users of changes to roles. Before you make changes, you might want to inform users who will be affected. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . The Account Settings Users page appears with the Manage Roles tab selected by default. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 293 -- 3 of 10 -- Figure 34: Manage Roles Tab 2. Click the Create Role icon  at the top right of the role results table. 3. Enter a distinctive name for the role. 4. Enter a description to record your intentions for this role. Descriptions can be useful later, if you want to review or revise the structure of your roles. 5. Select one or more permissions for the new role. Each role must have at least one permission.  Note You can also select all permissions by clicking on the checkbox at the top left of the list of permissions. 6. Click Save. Results SAP Business Network creates the role and returns you to the Manage Roles page. Modifying a Role Buyer administrators and users assigned a role with the User Administration permission can edit a role's name, description, and assigned permissions. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. 294 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles -- 4 of 10 -- • You have informed users about role changes that can affect them. SAP Business Network does not notify users of changes to roles. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. On the Manage Roles tab, search for a Permission using the search filters, or scroll down and locate the role you want to modify. 3. In the Role Name column of the search results table, select the role you want to modify. 4. Check Show me all the available permissions and select the permissions you want or uncheck the permissions you don't want for that role. 5. Choose Save. SAP Business Network applies your changes to all users assigned to the role. Changes take effect for each user at their next sign in. Reassigning Users to a Different Role Buyer administrators and users assigned a role with the User Administration permission can change the role assigned to users. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. • You have informed users about role changes that will affect them.SAP Business Network does not notify users of changes to roles. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. On the Manage Roles tab, scroll down to the role you want to investigate. 3. Click the role in the Role Name column. 4. Scroll down to the Assigned Users table. 5. Using the checkboxes, select the users you want to move to another role. 6. Click Move to another role. 7. Click Save to return to the Manage Roles page. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 295 -- 5 of 10 -- Deleting a Role Buyer administrators and users assigned a role with the User Administration permission can delete roles that they no longer need. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. • You have informed users about role changes that will affect them. SAP Business Network does not notify users of changes to roles. • No users can be assigned the role you want to delete. To change a user to another role, see Reassigning Users to a Different Role [page 295]. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. On the Manage Roles tab, you can perform a search for the role you want to delete, if necessary. Search for a Permission using the search filters. Or, scroll down and locate the role you want to delete. 3. In the Actions column of the roles results table, click the Delete  icon. Results SAP Business Network deletes the role and returns to the Users page. SAP Business Network Users Access to a buyer account is secured with individual user identities and levels of permissions. A user is an SAP Business Network sign in (user name and password) that enables one individual in your organization to sign in to your account. The administrator adds users to the SAP Business Network account and assigns each user exactly one role, which typically corresponds to the user’s real-world job responsibilities. 296 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles -- 6 of 10 -- Best Practices in Managing User Accounts When the administrator of an SAP Business Network account creates users and assigns roles, it is mandatory that the administrator assigns a unique user name with an appropriate assigned role for each individual who needs to access the account. Users must not share their user name or password with other users. This is important for SAP Business Network and your company in managing data privacy and integrity on SAP Business Network. For security, account administrators and users who have PCard access but are not the PCard owner are required to update their password every 90 days. As a best practice, users should not share their secret question and secret answer. To ensure your organization and users have secure accounts on SAP Business Network, create individual user accounts for different roles in the organization. By default, add one role per user. Users can have multiple related roles, depending on the tasks assigned to the user. How Roles Control User Interface Access Every user can see the Configuration Personal Information area, which contains basic contact information and a preferred language setting for that specific user. Beyond that, the only areas that a user is permitted to see are those allowed by their role permissions. For example, if the administrator created a role that included the Contact Administration permission, a user assigned to that role could see only the Configuration Personal Information area and the Supplier Enablement Contacts area of your SAP Business Network account. While users can update their own personal information, the administrator is responsible for overall user maintenance, which includes deleting users or reassigning user sign ins when individuals leave the company, and resetting user passwords. Creating a User [page 298] Changing a User’s Role and Resetting the Password [page 300] Reassigning a User Sign In [page 301] Deleting a User [page 302] Transferring Administration Ownership [page 303] Assigning User Management Capabilities to Users [page 304] Mass Uploading Users Using an Excel Template [page 304] Updating Users Using an Excel Template [page 305] Related Information SAP Business Network Roles [page 291] SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 297 -- 7 of 10 -- Creating a User You can set up sign in credentials and assign permissions to access an SAP Business Network account. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. • Before you create a user, you can use the Filter function from the Manage Users tab on the Account Settings Settings Users page to search for a user. 1. Click the dropdown arrow and select which search attribute you wish to use: User Name, Email Address, or First or Last Name. 2. Enter a search attribute value in the text box, then click the add  icon to the right. 3. Enter additional search values for the same search attribute as desired, up to 10.  Note You can search with only one attribute type at a time. 4. Click Apply. Context  Restriction • You can create no more than 6,000 users. • When an account has more than 1,000 users, SAP Business Network displays a simplified view of the Manage Users page. • You can create only one user for each employee who performs tasks on SAP Business Network. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. The Manage Users tab appears. 298 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles -- 8 of 10 -- 3. Scroll down to the top right of the user results table and click the Create User  icon. The Create User page appears. 4. Enter a user name, email address, first and last name, and optionally a phone number for this user. 5. Select a role in the Role Assignment section. 6. Scroll down and click Done. Results On the Manage Users page, at the top right of the user results table, note the Export Contact List  and Table Options Menu  icons. • The Export Contact List function downloads all roles and associated user permissions in a CSV file for ofnine review. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 299 -- 9 of 10 -- • The Table Options Menu controls what columns to show in the user results table. After you create a user, SAP Business Network sends an email message to that user with a randomly generated password. Each new user should sign in and change the password to something they can remember. Next Steps • Remind users to store their user names and passwords in a safe place. • Users who forget their user name can go to the Sign In page, click Forgot User Name and follow the instructions for regaining access to their account. • If a user forgets their password, an administrator can reset it. You can change a user’s role assignment at any time. See Changing a User’s Role and Resetting the Password [page 300]. • If an employee leaves your company or changes jobs, and no longer uses the SAP Business Network account, an administrator can delete the user. See Deleting a User [page 302]. Changing a User’s Role and Resetting the Password You can select a different role for an existing user or reset the password. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. Context Users can forget their sign in information if they do not sign in to SAP Business Network regularly. SAP Business Network provides a secure and relatively quick way for users to recover sign in information. However, even with this process in place, loss of user names and passwords can cause frustration and lost productivity for you and your users. If you do not want to reset a user’s password, instruct him or her to click Forgot Your Password? on the SAP Business Network Sign In page. After a user submits a user name, SAP Business Network Accounts Services sends the user an email containing steps to reset the password. 300 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/BuyerAdminGuide includi.content: Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. Cick Edit for the user whose password you want to reset. 4. Do one of the following: • To change a user’s role, select a different role in the Role Assignment section and click Save. • To reset the user’s password, click Reset Password. 5. Click Save. SAP Business Network returns to the Users page. Results If you reset the user’s password, SAP Business Network sends an email to the user containing a new randomly- generated password. The password update takes effect immediately. Reassigning a User Sign In If a user has left the company, you can reassign that user’s sign-in to another individual, to retain the user setup and data. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. Context When an employee leaves the company or changes jobs and no longer uses the SAP Business Network account in their name, the administrator should either delete the user or reassign the user’s sign-in to another individual. If you want to retain the user’s setup and data, reassign the sign-in. If you want to delete the user’s setup and data, delete the user. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 301 -- 1 of 10 -- Procedure 1. Sign in using the user’s user name and password. If you do not know the password, click Help Support to contact SAP Business Network Support. 2. Choose Account Settings Manage Profile . 3. On the Configuration page, choose Personal Information. 4. Change the user name and password and optionally other information. 5. Click OK. 6. On the Configuration page, choose Notifications. 7. Make any modifications to notification emails based on the user sign in reassignment. 8. Click OK. Deleting a User If a user has left the company, you can delete the user to prevent its further use to access SAP Business Network. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. Context When an employee leaves the company or changes jobs and no longer uses the SAP Business Network account, the administrator should either delete the user or reassign the user’s sign in to another individual. • If you want to retain the user’s setup and data, reassign the sign in. See Reassigning a User Sign In [page 301]. • If you want to delete the user’s setup and data, perform this procedure. User deletion is permanent. There is no way for SAP Business Network or you to recover a deleted user. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. Search for the user you want to delete. See Creating a User [page 298] for the steps to perform. 302 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles -- 2 of 10 -- 4. In the user results table, check the checkbox for the user you want to delete. 5. In the Actions column, click the Delete  icon in the row of the user you want to delete. Results SAP Business Network deletes the account and refreshes the page content. It does not maintain a record of deleted users. Transferring Administration Ownership The current account administrator can reassign ownership of the SAP Business Network account to another person. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Context Account administrators can quickly and easily transfer the Administrator role to another user. After the Administrator role is transferred to a new user, SAP Business Network sends a notification to the new account administrator, alerting them that they now have the Administrator role.  Note If you do not know who the account administrator is, contact SAP Business Network Support. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. Select the user you want to transfer the Administrator role to. 4. Choose Actions Make Administrator . The Assign a Role page opens. 5. Select a new role for your account, and click Assign. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 303 -- 3 of 10 -- Assigning User Management Capabilities to Users The current account administrator can create a role with the User Administration permission and assign it to non- administrator buyer users, called user administrators. User administrators can perform administrative functions, such as tasks relevant to user management and buyer user access to SAP Business Network. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. On the Manage Roles page, click the  icon. 3. Enter a distinctive name for the role. Enter a description to record your intentions for this role. 4. Go to the last page of permissions, and select the User Administration permission. 5. Click Save. 6. Click Manage Users. 7. On the Manage Users page, select the user you want to assign the user administrator role to. 8. Choose Actions Edit . 9. In the Role Assignment area of the Edit User page, select the user administrator role you created. 10. Click Save. Mass Uploading Users Using an Excel Template Account and user administrators can create and update users through mass upload using an Excel template. Using an Excel template, user administrators can perform the following actions: create or update users, assign roles, assign business units, authorization profile assignments. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. • For the mass upload capability using an Excel template, all required fields must be filled out in the Excel template before uploading it. • List of the required fields in the Excel template: 304 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles -- 4 of 10 -- • Action • User Name • Corporate User Name (if SSO is enabled) • Email Address • First Name • Last Name • Has Limited Access; if this value is set to "No", at least one role must be assigned • Only Excel files in the .XLSX format can be uploaded • Only five roles, business units, and authorization profiles can be assigned using an Excel template. These roles, business units, and authorization profiles must exist already, and cannot be created using Excel upload. If additional ones are needed, they can be added from the user interface. • Change of first name, last name, or email address fields is not allowed when updating user details using Excel upload, consistent with the handling in the user interface. • The number of users entered in the Excel file must not exceed 500. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. Click the Upload Users button on the Manage Users page. 4. Click the Upload button on the Upload Users page. 5. Click the Download template link on the Upload File dialog box. 6. Open the Excel template and fill out the required fields. 7. Click the Browse button on the Upload Files dialog box, choose the filled out Excel template from your computer and enter a descriptive name. 8. Click the Upload button. 9. Click the Refresh Status button on the Upload Users page and wait until it shows status Completed. If the status is Completed With Errors or Failed, select the download icon ( ) in the Log column to see the reasons for errors and to correct them. 10. Click the Done button. This opens the Manage Users page where you can see the uploaded users. Updating Users Using an Excel Template Account and user administrators can update multiple users using an Excel template. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 305 -- 5 of 10 -- Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. Click the Upload Users button on the Manage Users page. 4. Click the Upload button on the Upload Users page. 5. Click the Download template link on the Upload File dialog box. Alternatively, if you already have an uploaded Excel template you can reuse it by selecting the download icon ( ) in the File column on the Upload Users page 6. Open the Excel template and fill out or update the required fields and click the Upload button on the Upload Users page. 7. Click the Browse button on the Upload Files dialog box, choose the Excel template from your computer and enter a descriptive name. 8. Click the Upload button. 9. Click the Refresh Status button on the Upload Users page and wait until it shows status Completed. If the status is Completed With Errors or Failed, select the download icon ( ) in the Log column to see the reasons for errors and to correct them. 10. Click the Done button. This opens the Manage Users page where you can see the updated users. SAP Business Network Permissions A permission grants access to a certain area of the SAP Business Network user interface. Each role includes one or more permissions. For example, the Archive Access permission grants access to the Archived Invoices tab and the functionality of the Invoices area. Any user who is assigned a role that includes the Archive Access permission can access the Archived Invoices tab. You can view the list of available permissions while creating a role. See Creating a Role [page 293]. The Administrator role, which can be assigned to only one user for your account, includes all permissions. Some permissions are exclusive to the Administrator role, and only the user assigned the Administrator role can see them. The following table lists SAP Business Network permissions in alphabetical order. The right-hand column briefly describes what each permission enables a user to do and specifies the area in your SAP Business Network account to which the permission grants access. 306 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles -- 6 of 10 -- This permission… Enables a user to… Access to order confirmation approvals Access order confirmation approvals in Supply Chain Monitor.  Note This permission is for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyer ac- counts only. Analytics dashboard access Access predefined stories (presentation-style documents that describe data) under Reports Analytics on the menu bar. Archive Access View and search archived items. Grants access to this area: Invoices Archived Invoices Buyer Dashboard for Supply Chain Collaboration Grants access to the Buyer Dashboard for Supply Chain Collaboration.  Note This permission is for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyer ac- counts only. Buyer Discount Management Program Administrator Create, maintain, and deactivate Discount Management rules. You must also specify the Payment Activities permission to view and manage discounts. Grants access to these areas: • Manage Profile Ariba Discount Management • Reports (Discount Acceptance, Discount Metrics, Early Payment Limit, and Failed Dynamic Discounting Credit Memo Creation reports only) Buyer Treasury Agent Accept or reject early payment requests. Grants access to this area: Manage Profile Catalog Management Set up and manage customer catalog-related activities. Grants access to this area: Catalogs Customer Catalogs Product Manager View staged products and online products, add products, edit product data, pre- view product details page that will be visible to buyers when they search for your product, view and resolve validation errors, send products for approval, move products from online version to staged version, and delete staged products. Gives access to the Catalogs Network Catalog page to manage staged products and online products. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 307 -- 7 of 10 -- This permission… Enables a user to… Product Approver Review product data of the products that are sent for approval, preview the product details page that will be visible to buyers when they search for your product, and approve or reject the products that are sent for internal approval. Gives access to the Catalogs Network Catalog page to manage pending approval products. Company Data Deletion Configuration Request recurring or one-time deletion of transaction data. Grants access to this area: Manage Profile Data Deletion Criteria Company Information Review and update company profile and website information. Grants access to this area: Company Profile Component planning collaboration View the Component planning collaboration tile in the Workbench. Contact Administration Set up and maintain company-wide and supplier-specific contact assignments. Grants access to this area: Supplier Enablement Contacts Copy Partner Update Bulk add or replace copy partners.  Note This permission is for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyer ac- counts only. Create and manage postings in Ariba Discovery Create, modify, close, and award postings on SAP Business Network Discovery. Customization Editor Create and edit customization projects from the Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service page.  Note This permission is for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyer test accounts only. Customization Publisher Publish customization projects from the Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service page.  Note This permission is for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyer pro- duction accounts only. 308 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles -- 8 of 10 -- This permission… Enables a user to… Customized Content Administration Review and approve customized content.  Note This permission is visible only to users assigned the Administrator role. cXML Configuration Configure your account for cXML transactions, including specifying the cXML version you support, your authentication method, and profile URL. Grants ac- cess to this area: Manage Profile cXML Setup Download Current Transactions Download your account's transaction data for any period up to 90 days. Grants access to this area: Quick Links Current Transactions Forecast Visibility Grants access to forecast and commit visibility.  Note This permission is for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyer ac- counts only. Goods Receipt Report Administration Create, delete, modify, run, and download goods receipt reports. Grants access to this area: Reports (Goods Receipt report only) Inbox and Order Access View and search incoming transaction documents and take actions based on your role. This permission includes viewing invoices, order confirmations, ship notices, and notifications, as well as performing a search for invoices, order confirmations, and ship notices. Invoice Report Administration Create, delete, modify, run, and download invoice reports. Grants access to this area: Reports (Invoice Report only) Manage Time and Expense Sheets View time and expense sheets. Grants access to this area: Fulfillment Time and Expense Sheets Mobile Application Access Access the SAP Business Network mobile application. Outbox Access View and search outgoing transaction documents and take actions based on your role. This includes viewing orders and transaction audit reports, as well as performing a search for orders and download results. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 309 -- 9 of 10 -- This permission… Enables a user to… Part status for planning collaborations Change part status for material items to Active or Inactive.  Note This permission is for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyer ac- counts only. .  Note Part status actions are not supported in a combined view of forecast and supplier-managed inventory. This view is identified by a Multiple value in the Process type column. Payment Activities View payments in the Payments area, view complete PCard account numbers on purchase orders, and maintain your company’s payment account. Grants access to this area: Payments For increased security on SAP Business Network, users with this permission are required to change their password every 90 days. PCard Configuration and Notifications Enable PCard settlement, maintain card administrator information, and maintain email addresses for card processing notifications. Grants access to these areas: • Manage Profile Settlement PCard Settlement Services • Manage Profile Settlement PCard Administrator Information • Manage Profile Settlement PCard Charge Methods • Manage Profile Settlement PCard Processing Notifications This permission is available to the administrator account if the organization is enabled for payment. If you created roles before your account was enabled for payment, you can revise roles and add this permission. Permission to approve or reject date deviation Allow users to approve or reject a supplier’s date deviations from the order in Supply Chain Monitor.  Note This permission is for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyer ac- counts only. Permission to approve or reject price deviation Allows user to approve or reject a supplier’s price deviations from the order in Supply Chain Monitor.  Note This permission is for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyer ac- counts only. 310 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/BuyerAdminGuide includi.content: This permission… Enables a user to… Permission to approve or reject quantity deviation Allow users to approve or reject a supplier’s quantity deviations from the order in Supply Chain Monitor.  Note This permission is for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyer ac- counts only. Planning Collaboration Visibility Grants access to planning collaboration visibility.  Note This permission is for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyer ac- counts only. Planning Settings Authorization Grants access to planning settings.  Note This permission is for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyer ac- counts only. Premium Membership and Services Management Manage your premium service subscriptions. Proof Of Service Approval Access Allow buyers to approve or reject a proof of service sent by suppliers. Proof Of Service Create Access Allow suppliers to create a proof of service. Proof Of Service Create On Behalf Access Allow suppliers to create a proof of service on behalf of the contractor. This is useful when the supplier contractor does not have the resources to create a proof of service. This permission in the SAP Business Network proof of service workflow is ap- plicable while creating service calls (proof of service) using SAP Field Service Management. Proof Of Service Report Access Allow users to create the report of all proof of service based on specified criteria, such as start date or status. Proof Of Service Review Access Allow a supplier supervisor to review the proof of service created by a supplier or contractor. The supplier supervisor can then reject the proof of service or submit the proof of service for approval. The supplier supervisors can view the details only for the proof of service for which they are specified as reviewers. Purchase Order Report Administration Create, delete, modify, run, and download purchase orders, failed purchase or- ders, and order summary reports. Grants access to this area: Reports (Order, Failed Order, and Order Summary reports only) SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 311 -- 1 of 10 -- This permission… Enables a user to… Quality Collaboration Access Allow users to view the Quality collaboration tab.  Note This permission is for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyer ac- counts only. Quality Inspection Access Allow suppliers to view quality inspection documents.  Note This permission is for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain supplier administrator accounts only. Quality Inspection Creation Allow suppliers to create quality inspection documents.  Note This permission is for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain supplier administrator accounts only. Quality Inspection Signature Allow suppliers to electronically sign quality inspection results.  Note This permission is for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain supplier administrator accounts only. The supplier's personal data will be transferred to the electronic signature provider enabled for the supplier's account. Quality Notification Access Allow suppliers to view quality notification documents.  Note This permission is for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain supplier administrator accounts only. Quality Notification Creation Allow suppliers to create quality notification documents.  Note This permission is for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain supplier administrator accounts only. Quality Review Access Allow users to view quality review documents. 312 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles -- 2 of 10 -- This permission… Enables a user to… Quality Review Admin Perform administrative functions on quality reviews. This permission includes enabling a buyer to open a Closed quality review, and in an open quality review to delete attachments and set or unset a legal hold.  Note This permission is for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyer ac- counts only. Quality Review Creation Allow users to create quality review documents. Service Sheet Report Administration Create, delete, modify, run, and download service sheet reports. Grants access to this area: Reports (Service Sheet and Service Sheet Activity Log reports only) Supplier Enablement Configuration Configure supplier invitation letters, tasks, activities, and the Supplier Informa- tion Portal. Supplier Enablement Program Administrator Manage supplier relationships. Configure the supplier enablement process, up- load vendors, start supplier enablement, manage supplier enablement tasks, and access the vendor data export reports. If approved, the user can’t sign in to SAP Business Network any longer, and their personal information is no longer visible to users, including in transaction documents shared and exchanged with business partners.  Note For audit and compliance purposes, the user's personal information is still visible to the user who is the administrator for your SAP Business Network account. Restrictions • Comments or attachment files associated with transaction documents aren’t affected when users remove personal information. Therefore, avoid entering personal information in comments or attached files. • After a user’s revocation of user access request is approved, their personal information is pseudonymized in SAP Business Network transaction documents. However, transaction documents that were integrated with other systems (such as an ERP) or downloaded before the request was approved may still have the user’s personal information. The customer needs to take additional action, including informing impacted business partners, to remove it. • If a customer needs to re-identify a user that has been pseudonymized for legal purposes, the administrator of the account can provide that information. Workflow for Removing Personal Information for a User from SAP Business Network [page 315] Requesting Removal of Personal Data for a Buyer User [page 316] Approving or Rejecting a Buyer User's Request to Remove Their Personal Information [page 317] Viewing and Exporting Revoked Buyer Users [page 317] Workflow for Removing Personal Information for a User from SAP Business Network This procedure describes the workflow for removing personal information for an SAP Business Network user: Figure 35: Workflow for Removing Personal Information for a User SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 315 -- 5 of 10 -- 1. A user signs in to the SAP Business Network portal to request the removal of their personal information. 2. The administrator for the account receives an email notifying them of the user's request. 3. The administrator signs in to the SAP Business Network portal and approves or rejects the user's request. 4. If the administrator approved the request, the user's personal information is removed. 5. If the administrator approved the request, the user can't sign in to SAP Business Network. Requesting Removal of Personal Data for a Buyer User SAP Business Network users can request the administrator for their account to remove their personal information from the system. If your request is approved, your personal information is removed, and you can't sign in to SAP Business Network. Prerequisites If you are currently assigned the Administrator role for your account, you can't perform this task until after you transfer the Administrator role to another user. See Transferring Administration Ownership [page 303]. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose Manage Profile. 2. Click Personal Information. The Personal Information page opens. 3. In the Personal information usage section, check the Request to remove my personal information option. 4. Click Save. Results The administrator is notified of your request, and they can approve or reject it. 316 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles -- 6 of 10 -- Approving or Rejecting a Buyer User's Request to Remove Their Personal Information As an administrator, you can approve or reject a user's request to remove their personal information from SAP Business Network. If you approve the request, the user's personal information is removed, and they can't sign in to SAP Business Network. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. In the Users table, select the user who requested revocation of access. In the AN Access column, the value is Revocation request pending. 4. Click Actions, and choose one of the following actions: • Accept Revocation Request • Reject Revocation Request 5. Click OK. Viewing and Exporting Revoked Buyer Users As an administrator, you can view the list of revoked users and export the table to an XLS file. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Revoked Users. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 317 -- 7 of 10 -- 3. The Revoked Users table lists all users whose access to SAP Business Network has been revoked.  Tip You can filter the table by User Name, Email Address, or First or Last Name. 4. To export the table, click the  Table Options Menu icon, and choose Export All Rows. Results An XLS file containing the list of revoked users downloads to your computer. Configure Retention Period and Manage Deletion of Revoked Users in SAP Business Network As a buyer administrator, configure a retention period for revoked users. SAP Business Network users can request the administrator of their account to remove their personal information from the system. This is called a revocation request. If the request is approved, users cannot sign in to SAP Business Network any longer, and their personal information is no longer visible to other users. As an administrator, you can configure a retention period for the user data of all the revoked users in your organization. The data of revoked users is automatically removed from SAP Business Network after this retention period is reached. In the meantime, you can view the list of revoked users in the Revoked Users tab. You must have configured the retention period before accepting or rejecting any revocation request. If the retention period for an organization is not configured, SAP Business Network prompts you to configure the retention period before you can act on a revocation request. You can change the retention period at any time before the previously configured retention period is reached. The newly configured retention period takes effect immediately. The retention period must be configured in months, and must be between 1 and 999 months.  Note • Only users with non-administrator roles can request revocation of their access from SAP Business Network. Administrators cannot raise a revocation request. If administrators want to request revocation of their access from SAP Business Network, they must transfer their administrator role to another user. For more information, see Transferring Administration Ownership [page 303]. • Transaction documents such as purchase orders and invoices created by users before they were revoked will remain unchanged in SAP Business Network even after revocation and subsequent permanent deletion of such users. 318 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles -- 8 of 10 -- Configuring Retention Period for Revoked Users in Your Organization As an administrator, you can configure the retention period of user data for revoked users in your organization. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. Click Account Settings Settings Users . 3. Click Manage User Deletion. 4. Enter a retention period between 1 and 999 in the Retention period in months box. The data of all revoked users in your organization will be retained for a period that you configure here. 5. Click Save. • After the retention period is over, user data will be deleted permanently from SAP Business Network. • You cannot act upon a revocation request unless you configure the retention period first. • Revoked users' data is available for you to view for purposes such as regulatory audits. • All the data of an organization (including users' data - both revoked as well as deleted) is deleted when an organization is permanently deleted. Prevention of Manual Sign In by SAP Business Network Buyer Users Buyers whose SAP Business Network accounts are configured for single sign-on (SSO) corporate authentication can prevent users from signing into the SAP Business Network manually, outside of the single sign-on (SSO) configuration. This SAP Business Network feature is applicable to all buyers who use single sign-on (SSO) corporate authentication for accessing the SAP Business Network. This feature does not affect SAP Business Network suppliers. Preventing users from signing in manually enhances the security of SAP Business Network accounts using single sign-on (SSO) authentication. When this feature is enabled, users cannot sign in to the SAP Business Network in any way other than through single sign-on (SSO). They cannot sign in by entering the URL buyer.ariba.com directly into a browser. Even users with the Administrator role cannot sign in manually. Users who try to sign in manually will receive an error message that says The user name and password pair you entered was not found. If this feature is not enabled, users can use their user name and password to manually sign in to the SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 319 -- 9 of 10 -- Enabling This Feature This feature is disabled by default. To enable this feature, ask your Designated Support Contact to log a case (formerly Service Request). An SAP Business Network Support representative will follow up to complete the request. Enabling the feature involves SAP Business Network setting an option in the single sign-on (SSO) configuration for the SAP Business Network account to disable manual sign in. Multifactor Authentication Multifactor authentication is a two-step verification process where you are required to authenticate yourself a second time using a time-based verification code. As compared to the single step authentication process, the multifactor authentication process provides enhanced security. If multifactor authentication is enabled for critical fields, you are required to perform the two-step verification process while attempting to update the values of critical fields such as email addresses, phone numbers, remittance information and so on. With multifactor authentication enabled for sign in, you are required to perform the two-step verification process to sign in to SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network administrators can now enable the following functionalities for users in their organization by selecting the desired users from a table: • Require multi-factor authentication for critical fields • Require multi-factor authentication for login  Note • Only buyer administrators with the required permissions can disable multifactor authentication for sign ins. • SAP Business Network does not prompt newly created users to complete the multifactor authentication setup immediately after a successful sign in. New users are recommended to set up multifactor authentication for sign in after they change their initial password. Prerequisites When multifactor authentication is enabled for your organization, you must install an authenticator application such as SAP Authenticator from iTunes (for iOS devices) or from Google Play (for Android devices) in your hand-held devices to generate a time-based verification code (also called time-based one-time password). The time-based verification code setup is also compatible with third-party authenticators such as Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator.
