file://SBN/split/BuyerAdminGuide includi.content: Setting Up Multifactor Authentication Using a New Device (Buyer User) [page 324] Enabling Multifactor Authentication for Sign In Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage User Authentication. The Multi-factor Authentication User Setup page is displayed. 3. Select the box Require multi-factor authentication for sign in. 4. Click Yes in the dialog box that appears. 5. Select the desired users by checking the boxes against their user names from the table, and click Enable.  Note Only the selected users are enabled for "multifactor authentication for sign in". If you do not select any user from the table, none of the users in your organization will be enabled for multifactor authentication. Configuring Multifactor Authentication Settings Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage User Authentication. 3. Click Configure MFA Settings. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 321 -- 1 of 10 -- The Configure Multi-factor Authentication Settings page appears. 4. Enter a value in the Time allowed to skip multi-factor authentication setup box. This field specifies the maximum number of days the user can skip the multifactor authentication setup when an administrator has enabled it for that user. The default value is 5 days. 5. Enter a value in the Number of invalid multi-factor authentication attempts allowed box. This field specifies the maximum number of invalid multifactor authentication attempts that the user can make. The default value is 5 attempts. After the number of invalid attempts specified in this field, the user account is locked. It can be unlocked only by an administrator. 6. Enter a value in the Retry period for locked out users box. • After the number of minutes (the default value is 120 minutes) specified in this field, the user account is automatically unlocked and can be re-used. • If the user gets locked a second time, the default value becomes 240 minutes, and the user is unlocked only after 240 minutes. • If the user gets locked a third time, the user account is locked for good, and can be unlocked only by an administrator.  Note Users can contact their administrator at any time during this period to get their account unlocked. 7. Select the Enable the Remember me option check box. This checkbox (unchecked by default) specifies if users can choose the Remember me option for multifactor authentication in the one-time password input screen. If this box is checked, an input box Remember device for is displayed. 8. Enter a value in the Remember device for box. This field specifies the maximum number of days the user's device and browser will be remembered, during which they will not be prompted for the multifactor authentication passcode during login. The default value is 5 days. 9. Click Save. Managing Multifactor Authentication for Users Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage User Authentication. 322 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles -- 2 of 10 -- 3. Select the desired multifactor authentication check boxes. 4. Select the users (from the table) for which you want to manage multifactor authentication. 5. Click the following buttons depending on what you wish to do: • Enable: Enables multifactor authentication for the selected users. • Disable: Disables multifactor authentication for the selected users. • Reset: Resets multifactor authentication for the selected users. These users must either enter the secure key displayed on the user interface, or scan a new QR code during their next sign in session. • Send Email Reminder: Sends a reminder email to the selected users. • Unlock: Unlocks the selected users. 6. Click Save. Setting Up Multifactor Authentication (Buyer User) Context You can set up multifactor authentication after your SAP Business Network administrator has enabled the feature. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, click Personal Information. The Personal Information page appears. 3. Below the User Name text box, click the Set up multi-factor authentication link. The Set up Multi-factor Authentication page appears. 4. Download and install SAP Authenticator or any compatible authenticator application such as Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator on your hand-held device. 5. Open the authenticator application that you have installed on your mobile device and do either one of the following: 1. Scan the QR code displayed on the page, and enter the code in the Time-based Verification Code input box, or 2. Enter the secure key displayed on the page in the Time-based Verification Code input box. 6. Click Done. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 323 -- 3 of 10 -- Setting Up Multifactor Authentication Using a New Device (Buyer User) Context When you change your mobile device, you can reset the multifactor authentication that had been configured using your old device. Using the verification code from the old device, you can set up multifactor authentication on your new device. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, click Personal Information. The Personal Information page appears. 3. Below the User Name text box, click the Reset multi-factor authentication link. 4. Enter the verification code from your old mobile device. 5. Set up multifactor authentication again, using a new QR code on your new mobile device. 6. Click Done. 324 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles -- 4 of 10 -- SAP Ariba Buying Integration with SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass Description This section covers onboarding an SAP Fieldglass supplier on SAP Business Network and vice versa. Buyers can onboard the suppliers either in SAP Fieldglass or SAP Business Network ensuring unified user experience for suppliers across SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network. If SAP Ariba Buying that is part of SAP Ariba Procurement solutions uses SAP Fieldglass (restricted access) for service procurement, buyer cannot onboard a supplier on SAP Fieldglass. The buyer can leverage the SAP Business Network onboarding feature to onboard and manage suppliers. For more information on buyers and suppliers connection, see the How Buyers and Suppliers Connect section in the SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide.  Note • Buyer can invite a supplier on SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass only if the buyer exists on both. • Only the active supplier accounts can be integrated. • Synchronization of supplier profile is not supported between SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass. • After the supplier registers in SAP Fieldglass by approving the collaboration type as Service and establishes a connection with the buyer in SAP Fieldglass, a situation may arise wherein the buyer deletes the relationship or the supplier rejects the approved releationship in SAP Business Network. In that case, the relationship in SAP Fieldglass continues and it is not automatically deleted, you must manually deactivate the relationship. • Only one remote external identity provider (IDP) is allowed to login to SAP Business Network. Therefore, while connecting to SAP Fieldglass, use only the SAP Fieldglass IDP. • The Copy SES option on SAP Business Network is not supported in this integration scenario. • Creation of service sheets from Orders tile is not supported for SAP Fieldglass suppliers. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Ariba Buying Integration with SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass PUBLIC 325 -- 5 of 10 -- Onboarding SAP Fieldglass Supplier on SAP Business Network Description This section covers onboarding an SAP Fieldglass supplier on SAP Business Network. If a supplier fulfilled both material and services, the supplier is required to log in to SAP Business Network as well as SAP Fieldglass separately for different processes. SAP Fieldglass now has the ability to initiate the onboarding of SAP Fieldglass suppliers on to SAP Business Network. The supplier can switch between the applications using single sign-on (SSO). Prerequisites • Ensure that the buyer exists on both SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass. • Ensure that you enable the Allow multiple private IDs per supplier buyer entitlement for the SAP Fieldglass buyer. Contact the Designated SAP Support contact to enable this feature. • Ensure that the SAP Fieldglass supplier is subscribed to Fieldglass Onboarding Service permission to get the option to register with SAP Business Network. • We recommend that you set the relationship acceptance type to auto-approved. Restrictions • The supplier accounts on SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network must be present on US data centre. • The supplier accounts on SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network must be active. • SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network account integration does not support profile synchronization. • Only one remote external identity provider (IDP) is allowed to login to SAP Business Network and in this flow it is SAP Fieldglass IDP. While using this flow, you cannot use any another IDP. • Creation of service sheets from Orders tile is not supported for SAP Fieldglass suppliers. • Supplier must create the custom role FIELDGLASS_REMOTE_USER_DEFAULT_ROLE with the following three permissions before registering with SAP Fieldglass: • Invoice Generation • Inbox Access • Outbox Access Otherwise, the users that are created using the SCIM API are not granted the role. For more information on permissions, see Permissions You Can Assign to Users. 326 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Ariba Buying Integration with SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass -- 6 of 10 -- How the Integration Benefits the Customer • Supplier does not need to create an account of SAP Fieldglass user again on SAP Business Network. The supplier sub-users from SAP Fieldglass are automatically replicated in SAP Business Network. • A user can perform actions on both SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network using single-sign-on. • When a new supplier is onboarded on SAP Fieldglass by a buyer that exists on both SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network, the supplier is onboarded on to SAP Business Network too. User Interface Changes for Fieldglass Suppliers When a new supplier gets registered on SAP Fieldglass, the system displays an option as Complete SBN Registration. Clicking this option redirects the supplier to SAP Business Network to create a new account or integrate with an existing account on SAP Business Network. For existing suppliers, SAP Fieldglass displays the Complete SBN Registration option if the account is not already integrated with an account on SAP Business Network. When a service order is sent to SAP Fieldglass, SAP Business Network displays the statement of work number as a hyperlink. On clicking the hyperlink, the corresponding statement of work document gets displayed on SAP Fieldglass. SAP Fieldglass provides the option to return to SAP Business Network purchase order page. Workflow of Onboarding a SAP Fieldglass Supplier on SAP Business Network The following steps explain the workflow of onboarding a SAP Fieldglass supplier on SAP Business Network . 1. SAP Fieldglass buyer invites a supplier to onboard on SAP Fieldglass. 2. A new registration link is sent to the supplier via an email. 3. Supplier registers on SAP Fieldglass using the link. 4. The registration page displays a link to Complete SBN Registration. Suppliers on SAP Fieldglass that have the relationship with a buyer on both SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network, are displayed a link to Complete SBN Registration. The link is displayed until the supplier's account on both the applications are linked. 5. Complete SBN Registration provides the following two options: • Create New Account • Use Existing Account 6. Clicking the Create New Account opens the Registration page on SAP Business Network that pre-populates with the supplier's profile data from SAP Fieldglass. Modify the necessary fields on the SAP Business Network page, except the UserID field. 7. When a new supplier account is created on SAP Business Network, a relationship is created with the buyer ANID, account is enabled for single-sign-on, and a default role is assigned to that supplier. 8. When a supplier uses an existing account on SAP Business Network, the system does one of the following: • If the supplier exists and relationship with SAP Business Network buyer does not exist, then the relationship is created, account is enabled for single-sign-on, and the default role is assigned to the user. • If the supplier exists and relationship with SAP Business Network buyer is already established, then the account is enabled for single-sign-on and the default role is assigned to the user. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Ariba Buying Integration with SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass PUBLIC 327 -- 7 of 10 -- • If the supplier exists and the remote login and default role is assigned, but the relationship with the SAP Business Network buyer is not established, then only the relationship is created. 9. All the sub-users of the supplier on SAP Fieldglass are migrated to SAP Business Network.  Note The sub-users are migrated only when the scheduled job is run. Onboarding SAP Business Network Supplier on SAP Fieldglass Description This section explains onboarding a SAP Business Network supplier on SAP Fieldglass, which is mandatory in the following situations: • If a buyer that uses SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass sends a purchase order containing serviceable items, to a supplier in SAP Business Network • If a buyer uses SAP Ariba Buying to manage service orders, then the buyer can leverage the SAP Business Network onboarding feature to onboard and manage suppliers. The suppliers on SAP Business Network can create a new account or use the existing account and link that to a new or existing account on SAP Fieldglass. SAP Ariba Buying that is part of SAP Ariba Procurement solutions uses SAP Fieldglass (restricted access) for service procurement. After the supplier is registered on SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass, the supplier can use the SAP Business Network portal to view the service orders and navigate to SAP Fieldglass to manage the statement of work. If the buyer has a trading relationship with a supplier, then they can send a service collaboration request to the supplier to onboard them on SAP Fieldglass. The supplier can approve or reject the request. On approval, the supplier gets a notification to either create a new account or use an existing account on SAP Fieldglass. When the supplier creates a new account or uses an existing account, the supplier account in SAP Business Network is linked to the supplier account in SAP Fieldglass and single-sign-on is enabled. Prerequisites • Ensure that the buyer exists on both SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass. • Ensure that the buyer has a trading relationship with a supplier. Only then the buyer can send a service collaboration request to the supplier to onboard them on SAP Fieldglass. • Ensure that the buyer Fieldglass ID (FGID) is included in SAP Business Network in the Fieldglass configuration section. 328 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Ariba Buying Integration with SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass -- 8 of 10 -- • In the buyer profile, ensure that the Enable Supplier Onboarding option is selected while configuring SAP Fieldglass. Restrictions • Buyer can invite a supplier on SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass only if the buyer exists on both the applications. • Synchronization of supplier profile is not supported between SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass. • There is always one-to-one link between SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass account. User Interface Changes for Buyer • The Configure Fieldglass Routing URL screen includes a new field Fieldglass ID. The buyer must specify the Fieldglass ID to integrate SAP Business Network buyer account with the buyer account on SAP Fieldglass buyer account. • The Active Relationships page under Supplier Management has a new option Services in the Add Collaboration pop up. • The statement of work associated with a service order sent to SAP Fieldglass can be accessed using a new hyperlink on Purchase Order page in SAP Business Network. • The Enable Allow exchange of documents between Ariba Network, SAP Fieldglass, and SAP S/4HANA or SAP S/4HANA Cloud, for services procurement transaction rule is no longer available. User Interface Changes for Supplier • If the supplier has configured to auto-accept the relationship requests, then: • the service collaboration type request is auto-approved. • a new notification is displayed under the bell icon on the Supplier home page to register on SAP Fieldglass. • If the supplier has configured to manually accept the relationship requests, then: • the supplier should approve the service collaboration type request. • a pop-up is displayed to the supplier to register on SAP Fieldglass. • a new notification is displayed under the bell icon on the Supplier home page to register on SAP Fieldglass. Establishing Relationship Between SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass Buyer The buyer should establish a relationship between the SAP Business Network buyer account and the SAP Fieldglass buyer account, to onboard a SAP Business Network supplier on SAP Fieldglass. 1. Navigate to Configure Fieldglass Routing URL screen and enter the valid Fieldglass ID. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Ariba Buying Integration with SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass PUBLIC 329 -- 9 of 10 -- 2. Select Enable Supplier Onboarding. 3. Click Save. 4. Navigate to Customer Relationships, click Advanced View, select the supplier, select Add Collaboration from More Actions, and then select Services to send an invite to the SAP Business Network supplier to onboard on SAP Fieldglass. Workflow of Onboarding a SAP Business Network Supplier on SAP Fieldglass This section explains the workflow of onboarding a SAP Business Network supplier on SAP Fieldglass. 1. If a supplier does not exist on SAP Business Network, then the SAP Business Network buyer admin invites a new supplier to onboard on SAP Business Network. 2. An invitation email is sent to the supplier contact to either create a SAP Business Network account or link an existing SAP Business Network. 3. On successful registration, the supplier gets onboarded on to SAP Business Network with a transactional relationship. 4. SAP Business Network buyer then sends the collaboration fulfillment request to establish a trading relationship with the supplier using the Customer Relationships page.  Note You must switch to Advanced View to send the collaboration fulfillment request. 5. On acceptance from the supplier, the trading relationship with the buyer and the supplier is established. 6. If the trading relationship with the buyer and the supplier is already established on SAP Business Network, then the SAP Business Network buyer can send the collaboration service request inviting the supplier to register on SAP Fieldglass. Navigate to Customer Relationships, click Advanced view, select the supplier, select Add Collaboration from More Actions, and then select Services. 7. Supplier receives an email about the request, reviews it, and then approves or reject the request. • If the supplier has configured to auto-accept the relationship requests, then: • the service collaboration type request is auto-approved. • a new notification is displayed under the bell icon on the Supplier home page to register on SAP Fieldglass. • both the buyer and supplier receive an email informing that the collaboration service has been setup. • If the supplier has configured to manually accept the relationship requests, then: • the supplier should approve the service collaboration type request. • a pop-up is displayed to the supplier to register on SAP Fieldglass. • a new notification is displayed under the bell icon on the Supplier home page to register on SAP Fieldglass. • If the supplier rejects the collaboration service request, both the buyer and the supplier receives email for the information. SAP Business Network displays a notification message that account linking is mandatory, under the bell icon. 8. The supplier can either create a new account on SAP Fieldglass or login to an existing account. 9. The SAP Fieldglass registration page auto-populates with the supplier account details from SAP Business Network if the supplier creates a new account. 330 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Ariba Buying Integration with SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass -- 10 of 10 --

Fill in the necessary fields and click Accept and Continue. A new supplier account is created on SAP Fieldglass and relationship is established with the SAP Fieldglass buyer. The supplier accounts on SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass are synchronised and the account is enabled for single-sign-on. 11. If a supplier account already exists on SAP Fieldglass, log in to SAP Fieldglass. The SAP Fieldglass supplier ID is linked to the Fieldglass ID of the buyer on SAP Fieldglass and relationship is established. The supplier accounts on SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network are synchronised and the account is enabled for single-sign-on. 12. Depending on whether the SAP Fieldglass user ID is same or not, SAP Business Network stores the SAP Fieldglass user ID as follows: • If both SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network user ID are the same, then the SAP Business Network user ID is enabled for single-sign-on. • If both SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network user ID are different, then SAP Fieldglass user ID is enabled for single-sign-on. Single-Sign-On Between SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass After the supplier accounts are integrated the supplier can use single-sign-on to work on both SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass. The supplier can use the SAP Business Network portal to view the service orders and navigate to SAP Fieldglass to manage the statement of work. When a service order is sent to SAP Fieldglass, SAP Business Network displays the statement of work number as a hyperlink on the Items to service page.. On clicking the hyperlink, the corresponding statement of work document gets displayed on SAP Fieldglass. SAP Fieldglass provides the option View in SAP Business Network to return to SAP Business Network purchase order page. From the Items to service page, you can create a service sheet for a line item by clicking the Actions and then clicking Create service sheet. This takes the user to SAP Fieldglass, where you can create a timesheet or an event. From SAP Fieldglass, you can either go to SAP Business Network workbench or statement of work page by clicking the appropriate options. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Ariba Buying Integration with SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass PUBLIC 331 -- 1 of 10 -- SAP Ariba Buying Integration with SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass Descripiton SAP Ariba Buying that is part of SAP Ariba Procurement solutions uses SAP Fieldglass (restricted access) for service procurement. The buyer can leverage the SAP Business Network onboarding feature to onboard and manage suppliers. The suppliers can create a new account or use the existing account on SAP Business Network and link that to a new or existing account on SAP Fieldglass. For more details, see Onboarding SAP Business Network Supplier on SAP Fieldglass [page 328]. Both SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network can be accessed using single-sign-on. See, Single-Sign-On Between SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass [page 331] . For new account, the Allow exchange of documents such as orders, service sheets, and invoices between SAP S/HANA Cloud, SAP Fieldglass, and Ariba Network for services procurement transaction rule does not exist. Related Information Setting Up SAP Ariba Buying 332 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Ariba Buying Integration with SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass -- 2 of 10 -- Trading Partner Search The trading partner search on the SAP Business Network homepage helps buyers to discover and connect with trading partners and initiate transactions. You can search for trading partners by product and service category, product name or description, supplier or manufacturer name, part ID, ship-to or service location, or a combination of them. The search results prioritize relevant, reliable, and engaged trading partners based on several factors: • Relevant catalogs: Trading partners offering the specific item in your search rank higher. • Verified businesses: Trading partners with verified businesses rank higher. • Trading relationships: Trading partners having established trading relationships with more buyers rank higher. • Complete profiles: Trading partners with complete profiles that include accurate industry and capability- specific terms rank higher. In the search results, trading partners with verified businesses are marked with an (Verified Business) icon next to their names. Trading partners that have reported sustainability ratings in their profiles are marked with an  (Reported Sustainability Ratings) icon. You can also use search filters to narrow down the results. For example, you can apply a Trading Partner Status filter to locate trading partners with verified businesses or those having established trading relationships with you. Clicking a trading partner's name takes you to their public company profile. Searching for Trading Partners on SAP Business Network [page 333] Searching for Trading Partners on SAP Business Network Use the search functionality on SAP Business Network to find trading partners and their catalog offerings. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. On the homepage, make sure Trading partners is selected in the search bar and enter your search terms. Your search terms can include product and service category, product name or description, supplier or manufacturer name, part ID, ship-to or service location, or a combination of them. As you type, SAP Business Network displays suggestions of what you intend to type below the search bar. You can accept a suggestion by selecting it or continue typing. 3. Click the  (Search) icon to start the search. On the search results page, you can: • Refine your results by selecting one or more filters from the Filters pane. • Access a trading partner's company profile by clicking the trading partner name. • Query information from a trading partner by clicking Request for Information. • Save a trading partner by clicking the  (Save Supplier) icon. You can easily find saved trading partners by clicking the Account Settings user icon in the upper-right corner of the window and choosing Saved Suppliers. • Search a trading partner's public catalog by clicking View Catalog, if available. • If product thumbnails are displayed for a trading partner, click a thumbnail to view product details and request more information. • View additional search results by clicking the page numbers (if any) at the bottom. 334 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Trading Partner Search -- 4 of 10 -- Supplier Network Catalog Suppliers use network catalog to easily maintain a master catalog that includes products from all categories, regardless of how it is measured, priced, or delivered. All the buyers on SAP Business Network can easily search and view these products and send a Request for Information (RFI) which results in possible new business for buyers and suppliers. Buyers access network catalog products using the product search solution on the SAP Business Network trading partner portal homepage to see what you offer and to make purchases from suppliers. Buyers can search for products using product title, description, category, or manufacturer name. The search results are displayed in the form of product preview tiles with basic information such as product name, image, supplier name, price, and Check Price button. Also, the search results are displayed in the language that is defined in the buyer’s web browser. Buyers can view more detailed information about the product on the Product Details page. The product details will be displayed in the language specific to the buyer’s delivery location. If the product data is not available in the buyer’s regional language, then the product details are displayed in the English language. Buyers can perform the following actions on the search results page: • Request for price using the Check Price button on each product preview tile. • Filter products by category, manufacturer name, and price. • View the Product Details page of the desired product by clicking on the product preview tile. Buyers can perform the following actions on the Product Details page: • View detailed information about the product such as product name, images, supplier name, manufacturer name, category, specifications, and description. • Select the required quantity and view the price of the selected product quantity. • Send a check price request for the selected product quantity. • Add inputs for the supplier if any and set the response deadline. When buyers submit the check price request, a private posting will be created in SAP Business Network Discovery. A pop-up message is displayed with the posting ID and buyers can view the Posting Details page by clicking on the posting ID link. Buyers can also search and view the posting details using the posting ID or product title on the SAP Business Network Discovery page. The supplier receives a notification that a posting has been created. When the supplier responds to the posting, the buyer receives a notification with a link to the Posting Details page to view the supplier response. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Network Catalog PUBLIC 337 -- 7 of 10 -- Supplier Customer Catalogs Suppliers use electronic customer catalogs to describe the products and services they provide. You can download customer catalogs, subscribe to them to have updates automatically downloaded, and view content online. Suppliers publish customer catalogs in either of two formats: Catalog Interchange Format (CIF) or commerce eXtensible Markup Language (cXML). For more information on customer catalog formats, see the Customer Catalog Format Reference. Customer catalogs are simple text files. To use a customer catalog to which you are not subscribed, you can download it manually. Manually downloading a customer catalog does not create a subscription nor does it download a supplier’s profile. Your suppliers can also upload a customer catalog containing items with the advanced pricing details. Before a supplier can publish a private customer catalog for your organization, it must qualify the catalog for your organization—check the catalog against your catalog validation preferences. Related Information Subscribing to a Public Catalog [page 341] Downloading a Supplier’s Customer Catalog [page 338] SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Customer Catalogs PUBLIC 343 -- 3 of 10 -- Payments SAP Business Network facilitates payment and discount processing for the SAP Ariba Payables solution. The SAP Ariba Payables solution combines SAP Ariba cloud services features and third-party services related to payments, supply chain finance, and discounting. The SAP Ariba Payables solution offers the following capabilities and services: • Payment (US) • Payment (Canada) • Payment (Germany) • Check payment • Card payment • Supply chain finance • Discounting The SAP Ariba Payables solution offers the following features: • Remittance delivery to supplier via portal, email, EDI, VAN, cXML • Payment status visibility • Track and trace display of payments • Supplier self-service portal • ACH payment processing • Prenotification validation • Fraud reduction through payment provider activity monitoring • Supplier remittance name, address, and bank account changes report • Enablement status (with supplier contact information changes) and payment transaction reports • Supplier-maintained bank account information • ACH returns and notification of change processing • Compatibility with any bank • Payment cancelation Basic ACH Payment Workflow The follow high-level steps describe the workflow for the SAP Ariba Payables solution: 1. An invoice ok2pay file is sent to the ERP system. 2. The ERP system schedules payments. 3. The ERP system sends payments and remittances to SAP Business Network. 4. Depending on the capability or service you are using, one of the following occurs: • The ERP system transmits payments to the buyer's bank. • SAP Business Network transmits payments to the buyer's bank via ACH. 344 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Payments -- 4 of 10 -- • For payment (US) or payment (Canada), SAP Business Network transmits payments to the payment provider; the payment provider processes them and sends payment instructions to the buyer's bank. 5. SAP Business Network sends remittance advice to suppliers. 6. The buyer's bank settles with suppliers. For detailed information about the supply chain finance service and discounting capability, please see the Payments and Discounting Buyer Guide. Pre-Notification and Validation of Remittance Bank Information [page 345] Supplier Remittance and Bank Account Change Reporting [page 347] Creating a Supplier Remittance Report [page 348] Payment Capability (US, Canada, Germany) Overview [page 351] Card Payment Capability [page 354] Check Payment Capability [page 355] Before You Configure Payment Through SAP Business Network [page 357] Payments Integration Between SAP Business Network and Your ERP System [page 357] Payment Batches [page 364] Remittance Advice Documents [page 367] Collaboration with Suppliers on Payments [page 373] Cancel Payments [page 375] Pre-Notification and Validation of Remittance Bank Information ACH pre-notification or pre-note is a zero dollar transaction that is sent to the bank to verify the accuracy of bank account information. This ensures that payments are sent correctly to your supplier’s bank or financial institution. When there is a change in your supplier’s remittance bank information, SAP Business Network sends a pre-note to the bank. Once the bank receives the pre-note, it verifies the information and, if necessary, sends a Notification of Change (NOC) email message to SAP Business Network. Once SAP Business Network receives the NOC, it alerts the supplier, who can then update the remittance information in their supplier account. The pre-notification process takes approximately 10 business days. SAP Business Network generates a pre-note when: • A trading relationship is established between a supplier (who has ACH remittance information in their supplier account) and an ACH-enabled buyer, or, • A supplier either configures ACH remittance information in their supplier account, or updates existing ACH remittance information (assuming that a trading relationship already exists between ACH-enabled buyer and supplier). A pre-note impacts the supplier’s remittance information status as follows: If the supplier has configured multiple ACH remittance addresses in their account, a separate pre-note is generated for each of those addresses. Each pre-note results in a zero-dollar payment, which is transmitted to the disbursing SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Payments PUBLIC 345 -- 5 of 10 -- bank. This remittance information is associated with one of the following statuses: Unverified, Verifying, Verified, or Incorrect bank information. When a pre-note document is generated, the remittance information status automatically changes from Unverified to Verifying, SAP Business Network waits for a period of ten days to receive the NOC/RTN (Notification of Change/ Return) from the bank. If no NOC/RTN is received from the bank within the stipulated 10 days, the remittance information is automatically marked as Verified. The supplier remittance information status changes to Verified when SAP Business Network receives the NOC from bank, and is updated to Incorrect bank information upon receipt of a RTN.  Note There is no guarantee that the bank will send a NOC/RTN if there is a problem with the remittance information. It is not mandatory for the bank to respond with a NOC/RTN when they receive a pre-note document from SAP Ariba. Regardless, the pre-note verification process, services as one of the many business controls that reduce the risk of a payment failure or problem. Batching of Pre-Notes Previously, SAP Business Network sent pre-notes as separate EDI 820 files to the bank, typically resulting in a $25 (USD) charge per (pre-note) file received. Now, the pre-note validation process becomes more cost-effective, due to the ability to batch pre-notes into a single EDI 820 file prior to sending them to the designated bank. The batching is done on a daily basis usually transmitted to the bank five hours before the bank’s cut-off time. In case the supplier creates or modifies the remittance information after the pre-note batch is created for the current day, the remittance information will be generated the next day. Bank Holiday Calendar Configuration and Transmission Cut-Off Time Your SAP Ariba Support representative will work with you to ensure proper configuration of your bank’s calendar, including bank holidays. You are expected to set up your ERP to incorporate NACHA guidelines and ensure that funds settle in your supplier’s bank account on the net due date; this implies that you transmit your payment files one business day prior to the expected settlement date. SAP Ariba will also work with you to establish the appropriate transmission cut-off time for your bank. In doing so, SAP Ariba will provide enough buffer time (approximately two hours) to ensure timely delivery of files, thereby allowing you to address exceptions. By default, SAP Ariba sends payment batches to the bank immediately. However, you can choose to hold payment batches until the daily cut-off time. If you choose to hold payment batches until the daily cut-off time, you can cancel pending payment batches before the daily cut-off time. For more information about holding payment batches and canceling payments, see Cancel Payments [page 375]. The following are some important considerations to keep in mind regarding how SAP Ariba configures bank transmission cut-off times: • SAP Business Network sends the transmission to bank immediately upon receipt of clean file by default. 346 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Payments -- 6 of 10 -- • SAP Business Network sends email notifications upon bank transmission, so you know when payments are held up by your bank. These notifications help you reconcile the payment run and complete the bank-defined authorization process. See Configuring Payment Batch Notifications [page 363] for more information on these types of notifications. • You can sign in to SAP Business Network directly by clicking on the batch ID link contained in the notification email to see the batch details. • If a batch contains exceptions or if it is a duplicate, SAP Business Network issues a separate notification. (Notification subjects include the batch number.) • If the payment is received after the bank cut-off time, SAP Business Network transmits the payment on the next business day (10 am PST/1 pm EST) Zero Net Payments An ERP payment run may result in a vendor payment with a net value of $0 (that is, the invoice payment is offset by a credit memo for the same amount, resulting in a net payment to the supplier of $0). Buyers may include such netting or clearing transactions within a payment batch to mark the related invoices or credit memos as “Paid.” However, banks often reject $0 payments. Ariba Payment Professional automatically filters $0 payments from the transmission to the bank. This filtering not only reduces the risk that the bank will encounter problems when processing your payment transmission but also any exceptions that necessitate follow-up and investigation by your Accounts Payable department. This process helps to eliminate unnecessary bank processing fees for something the banks ultimately will reject. However, SAP Ariba does send $0 remittance advice to suppliers so that their Accounts Receivable department can perform the appropriate reconciliation on their side. Supplier Remittance and Bank Account Change Reporting You can obtain supplier account change information by creating a Supplier Remittance Information report. The Supplier Remittance Information report allows you to keep your ERP system’s vendor master in sync with supplier changes, block vendors for payment if necessary, and obtain the correct supplier bank account information. The report serves as an alert that a supplier has enrolled so that you may change the payment method in your ERP system’s vendor master to begin sending ACH payments via your disbursing bank and the SAP Ariba process. Supplier remittance information reports provide a summary of your suppliers’ payment details, including the address (or remit-to) information, preferred payment method, and financial institution account information. These reports can help track any changes your suppliers make to their address, payment, and bank information. This report displays status information in the ACH Pre-Note Status column which helps to identify whether the pre-note sent for a supplier’s remittance information was processed successfully. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Payments PUBLIC 347 -- 7 of 10 -- The following statuses are displayed in the ACH Pre-note Status column: Column Value Denotes The... Verified Pre-note was processed successfully for the ACH remittance address. Ariba provides the disbursing bank a 10 day window to send a NOC/RTN (Notification of change/return) to indicate that there is a problem with the suppliers’ bank account configu- ration. Once the 10 day window closes, the ACH remittance address is “Verified.” Unverified ACH Remittance address was created or changed by the supplier Verifying Pre-note was created and sent to the bank for verification on the ACH remittance informa- tion. Incorrect Bank Information Pre-note failed and the bank sent an “Incorrect bank information” status for the pre-note sent by SAP Business Network. Creating a Supplier Remittance Report You can create supplier remittance information reports to help track any changes your suppliers make to their address, payment, and bank information. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the Supplier Remittance Information Report permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. • To view the “ACH Pre-note Status” column, your account must be enabled for the ACH payment method. See Setting Up ACH Payment [page 358]. Procedure 1. Choose Reports Reports . 2. Click Create and then select Supplier Remittance Information from the Report type drop-down list. 3. Enter a title, description, and set the time zone and language in the fields provided. 4. Click Next to finish creating the report and enter scheduling and additional report criteria in the fields provided. Payment Process and Control Points The following diagram provides more specifics on the payment process and control points between your ERP system, SAP Ariba, and your bank. You can review the various control points with your auditor that help you ensure secure, reliable & accurate payments. 348 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Payments -- 8 of 10 -- Figure 36: Payment Process and Control Points The process points and control points are as follows: 000 - Payment Capability (US, Canada, Germany) Overview The payment capability offerings, available to SAP Ariba Payables customers, are fast, reliable ways for you to pay your suppliers through SAP Business Network. Your back-ofoce ERP system transmits payment request batches as CSV files to SAP Business Network, where they flow through to the payment provider, and then to your and your suppliers’ bank accounts. Your bank account is debited and the supplier’s bank account is credited. Multiple status updates during the payment cycle let buyers and suppliers track payments in progress. Your suppliers can sign in to their accounts to download the remittance information into their accounts receivable systems, print it, or save it into an XML format. Suppliers can use this detailed remittance information, including identified differences, to quickly and easily reconcile payments to related invoices and orders. Payment capabilities deliver: • Security and fraud protection: the payment provider vets supplier financial information and issues the supplier an AribaPay Merchant ID, which is a unique identifier that you use to pay the supplier. You do not have to maintain any banking information for the supplier in your systems. • Incentives for suppliers to engage with you on SAP Business Network and start accepting electronic payments. • Reduced payment processing costs, including fewer supplier payment inquiries. Payment capability (US) is only available for transactions that originate from and are settled in banks in the United States of America. Payment capability (Canada) is only available for transactions that originate from and are settled in banks in Canada. Payment capability (Germany) is only available for transactions that originate from and are settled in banks in Germany. Test transactions through the payment provider are not supported. You cannot make USD, CAD, and EUR payments with a single APMID; you must have a separate APMID for each USD, CAD, and EUR. You can optionally choose to make payments with the CTX payment format. The CTX payment format combines payment information and a variable-length record, called an addendum (or remittance), which contains payment information such as invoice numbers, allowing multiple payments to trade creditors in a single transfer of funds. The CTX payment format allows up to 9,999 addenda with approximately 800,000 characters. With this capability, CTX allows full and complete remittance information to be transmitted with payments through the entire ACH network, ultimately allowing a single CTX payment to cover multiple invoices. If you are interested in or want more information about payments in the CTX payment format, please contact your SAP Ariba Support Specialist; a representative of the payment provider will work with you to help you choose the best payment format for your needs. About Payment Capability (Canada) The ability to make payments in CAD is only available to customers in Canada. Contact your SAP Ariba Support Specialist to enable payments in CAD. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Payments PUBLIC 351 -- 1 of 10 -- USD-to-CAD and CAD-to-USD payments are not supported. You cannot make CAD and USD payments with a single APMID; you must have a separate APMID for each CAD and USD. Payments in CAD are transmitted with consideration of the Canadian Bank Holiday Calendar. About Payment Capability (Germany) The ability to make payments in Euro (EUR) in accordance with Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) standards and processes, is only available to customers in Germany. Contact your SAP Ariba Support Specialist to enable payments in EUR. Payments in EUR are transmitted to the payment provider for processing each business day at 11 AM CET, with consideration of the German Bank Holiday Calendar. Payment Capability Workflow The following diagram describes the workflow for payment capability (US) and payment capability (Canada). Figure 37: Payment Capability Workflow There is a specific supplier enablement activity for payment capability (US) or payment capability (Canada). For more information, see Supplier Enablement Considerations for Payment Suppliers [page 374] and Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network. The following high-level steps describe the workflow for enabling a supplier for the payment capability and issuing payments: 1. You decide to pay suppliers using the SAP Ariba Payables payment capability, contact SAP Ariba to start an enablement program, and identify the suppliers you want to pay this way. 2. The SAP Ariba enablement team enables a payment capability in your account. 3. You configure your ERP payment systems to generate payment batches, then configure your SAP Business Network account for payment integration and configure the SAP Ariba integration toolkit to upload payment 352 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Payments -- 2 of 10 -- batch files; see Payments Integration Between SAP Business Network and Your ERP System [page 357] for more information. 4. On SAP Business Network, you start a supplier enablement activity called AribaPay for each selected supplier. 5. If the supplier has not already enabled the payment capability for another customer, they enable it now, are issued an AribaPay Merchant ID, and then notify you that they have activated it, either by contacting you directly or by completing the Confirm AribaPay for This Relationship task. You can also track enablement status for suppliers using Supplier Enablement Status and Supplier Enablement Task Status reports; see Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network for details on these reports. 6. You make sure that your ERP system is ready to issue payments to the supplier. You can then mark the optional Customer Is Ready to Use AribaPay for This Relationship task for the AribaPay activity complete; otherwise, it is marked complete automatically when you issue your first payment to the supplier. 7. Your payment system generates payment batches and transmits them to SAP Business Network using the SAP Ariba integration toolkit. 8. SAP Business Network validates the payment batch and sends it to the payment provider for processing. 9. SAP Business Network creates remittance advice for the payment. 10. The payment provider processes the payment and issues payment instructions to your bank. Your bank account is debited and the supplier’s bank account is credited. During this process, SAP Business Network updates the remittance advice available to both you and the supplier with status updates from the payment provider. Bank Holiday Calendar Configuration and Transmission Cut-Off Time Payment capability (US) and payment capability (Canada) payments use the bank holiday calendar, business day, and transmission cut-off information for the payment provider to calculate settlement dates. Payment batches transmitted before the 7pm EST cut-off time settle in 3 banking days. Payment batches transmitted after the 7pm EST cut-off time settle in 4 banking days. Payment batches should specify the current date as the payment date. If a batch contains payment dates in the past, SAP Business Network updates those dates to a future date based on the settlement date calculations described above. If a batch contains payment dates in the future, SAP Business Network processes those payments when they are loaded. By default, SAP Ariba sends payment batches to the bank immediately. However, you can choose to hold payment batches until the daily cut-off time. If you choose to hold payment batches until the daily cut-off time, you can cancel pending payment batches [page 375] before the daily cut-off time. Card Payment Capability The SAP Ariba Payables solution supports payments by card. Card payments sent trhough SAP Business Network generate a single-use card and securely deliver funds to suppliers. You can use the credit card payment method in cXML payment batches sent to SAP Business Network to pay vendors and suppliers using a temporary, single-use card. Your supp;liers do not have to exist on SAP Business Network to pay them with the credit card payment method. SAP Ariba creates a private supplier account for any supplier not already registered for SAP Business Network. For this reason, payment batches with the credit card payment method must include the supplier email address in the PaymentPartnercontact role="payee" information. Card payment capability is available to customers in the United States only, and limited to payments in USD. Please contact your SAP Ariba Support Specialist to enable card payments. The payment provider assings you a static card account number during the enablement process. You must include the first six and last four digits of your assigned card acfcount number and the expiration date in payment batches with thte credit card payment method. See the cXML Solutions Guide for more information. Workflow for Card Payments The following describes the basic workflow for card payment capability:. 1. A supplier sends an invoice to a buyer. 2. The buyer sends a cXML payment batch to SAP Business Network; SAP Business Network sends the payment batch to the payment provider. 3. The payment provider initiates a fund transfer from the buyer, depositing into a prepaid account. 4. The payment provider sends a single-use virtual card and PIN to the supplier's payment email address, as specified by the buyer. The virtual card and PIN are delivered in two separate emails for security purposes. 5. The payment provider sends status updates to SAP Business Network and SAP Business Network sends status updates to the supplier. 6. The supplier authorizes and settles the payments within seven days. 7. The payment provider moves funds from the pre-paid account to the supplier's bank account. 354 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Payments -- 4 of 10 -- Check Payment Capability Payment by paper check continues to represents significant portion of noncash business-to-business payments in the United States. SAP Ariba offers payment by check to all SAP Ariba Payables customers, subject to regional limitations as to where it can be used. The check payment capability offers buyers who outsource their payment processing a complete payment solution, without the need to maintain multiple payment providers or separate reconciliation processes. You can submit payment batches with the Check payment type. Check payments are automatically printed and mailed by the payment provider and delivered to the supplier, even if the supplier is not registered on SAP Business Network. Check payments use the visual payment tracking feature to provide detailed information to you and your registered suppliers about the status of the payment. Check payment is available to customers in the United States only. Contact your SAP Ariba Support Specialist to enable check payments. All checks are printed in and mailed from Salt Lake City, Utah. Check printing occurs on business days and Saturdays, excluding holidays. Check payments are printed with your bank account information on the check. You can choose to include your company logo on printed checks; SAP Ariba Support collects your logo information during the enablement process. Check comments are commented to the first 20 characters. Check stubs are printed with invoice date, invoice number, and invoice net payment amount. Checks are mailed via first-class mail. Checks are mailed with your return address on the envelope. You must map a Payment Method Identifier to the check payment method and include this identifier in payment batches for payment by check. You are responsible for your own stop payments and bank reconciliation. You must include check numbers in the payment batch sent by SAP Business Network. Check Payment Restrictions Check payments must originate from a bank in the United States. SAP Business Network does not validate the Payee (supplier) address. Company logos on checks are printed in black and white only. Stop payment is not supported for check payments. Payment batches with the check payment method are processed at 8 PM ET each business day. Buyers can only submit payment batches with a single payment type; payment batches with multiple payment types are not supported. The total value of a single check payment must be greater than $0 USD and can not exceed $99,999,999.99 USD. Workflow for Check Payments The following describes the basic workflow for check payment after a buyer has completed the enablement process: 1. A buyer creates a payment batch that includes payments with the check payment type and sends it to the SAP Business Network. SAP Ariba forwards the payment batch to the payment provider. 2. SAP Business Network checks if the payee (supplier) has a registered SAP Business Network account. If the supplier has not registered on the SAP Business Network, a new vendor and private supplier is created to process the payment. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Payments PUBLIC 355 -- 5 of 10 -- 3. The payment provider validates the payment batch and buyer bank account information and sends a confirmation that the check payment request was received. SAP Ariba forwards the confirmation to the buyer and supplier (if registered). 4. The payment provider prints the check and mails it to the supplier's remittance address as specified by the buyer. 5. The payment provider sends check payment details and status updates to SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network sends payment details to the buyer. 6. The supplier deposits the check in their bank account. The supplier bank presents the check to the buyer bank. The buyer bank transfers funds to the supplier bank. Mapping a Payment Method Identifier to the Check Payment Method Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Context Before you send payment batches with the check payment method to SAP Business Network, you must map a new alphanumeric value to be included in payment batches that will indicate to the SAP Business Network which payment method to use. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. Click Payment Integration Toolkit. 3. In the Payment Method Mapping section, click Create. 4. Enter a Payment Method Identifier. You must include this alphanumeric value in payment batches to indicate payment by check. 5. Choose Check as the Payment Method. 6. Choose the Use Ariba Network Payment checkbox. 7. Click Save. 8. Click Save. 356 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Payments -- 6 of 10 -- Before You Configure Payment Through SAP Business Network Many of the procedures and data needed to configure your account for making payments through SAP Business Network will be handled for you by your SAP Business Network account representative before you can proceed. When this rule is selected, supplier remittance information will always be considered as mismatched and the payment batch rejected when the supplier remittance information in the supplier account is in either of the following states: Unverified, Verifying, or Incorrect bank information. The payment provider works with a large number of banks. Contact SAP Business Network Support for information on whether or not your bank is supported.  Note Payment capability (US) is only available for payments that originate in, and are settled in, banks in the United States of America; payment capability (Canada) and payments that originate in and are settled in banks in Canada. On the Configuration page, choose Payment Profile. 3. Click the AribaPay tab. Configuring Payment Batch Notifications You can specify options for receiving payment batch notification emails. Click Save. Payment Batches Payments are generated on your ERP system and then uploaded as payment batch files to SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network supports payment batches with the following restrictions: • Not support for multiple currencies in a single payment batch • Maximum of 20,000 payment lines per batch • Maximum of 10,000 invoices per payment line • Maximum of 100,000 invoices per payment batch You can view details of these batch files online. To view details of a payment batch file, including transmission errors, click a link in the Batch ID column. To view the history details for this batch, click the History tab. Viewing Payment Batch Files in SAP Ariba Invoice Management or SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing Context You can easily view payment batch information from within SAP Ariba Invoice Management or SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing without having to sign in to your SAP Business Network account first.
