Dependency Between Unit Price Currency and Unit Price Tolerance Rules Unit price currency and tolerance rules affect what suppliers can enter for line items on order confirmations. If you check the Apply line item unit price tolerance to order confirmations rule, the resulting functionality of the Allow suppliers to change the currency for unit price on order confirmations rule depends on the tolerance you specify, as described in the following table: Allow suppliers to change the currency for unit price on order confirmations Tolerance Result Checked Not specified Supplier can change the Unit Price and the Currency and create order confirma- tions with the new Unit Price and Cur- rency values. Checked 0 Supplier can change the Currency and create order confirmations with the new Currency value, but the Unit Price cannot exceed the value in the purchase order. Checked Numeric value greater than zero Supplier can change the Unit Price and the Currency and create order confirma- tions with the new Unit Price and Cur- rency values. Unchecked Not specified Supplier can change the Unit Price and create order confirmations with the new Unit Price value, but cannot change the Currency. Unchecked 0 Supplier cannot change the Unit Price or Currency. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 81 -- 1 of 10 -- Allow suppliers to change the currency for unit price on order confirmations Tolerance Result Unchecked Numeric value greater than zero Supplier can change the Unit Price and create order confirmations with the new Unit Price value, but cannot change the Currency. Calculation of Quantity Tolerance Compliance Quantity tolerance for a line item is subject to a two-part check. 1. Is confirmed quantity plus backordered quantity within the range allowed for the quantity to be confirmed plus the tolerance? If the sum of these is outside the tolerance range, an error message is displayed to the supplier. 2. Is the sum of confirmed quantity, backordered quantity, and rejected quantity within the range allowed for the quantity to be confirmed plus the tolerance? If the sum of these is outside the tolerance range, an error message is displayed to the supplier. Setting the Delivery-Date Tolerance in Ship Notices for All Suppliers You can limit how late or early your suppliers can ship the items you order. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Transaction Configuration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. Context  Note To instead configure delivery-date tolerances in ship notices for one or more subsets of suppliers, go to Setting the Delivery-Date Tolerance in Ship Notices for Supplier Groups [page 83]. Tolerances apply to ship notices for purchase orders, scheduling agreement releases, and scheduling agreements. When you configure delivery-date tolerances for ship notices, SAP Business Network validates the ship notices sent to you by your suppliers as follows: • If the ship notice is created by flipping the purchase order, SAP Business Network compares the value of Delivery Date in the ship notice to the Delivery Date of the first schedule line of the purchase order line item. • If the ship notice is created by selecting schedule lines from the Items to Ship workbench tile, the system compares the value of the Delivery Date in the ship notice to the Delivery Date of each selected schedule line. 82 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration -- 2 of 10 --  Note When the delivery date for a ship-notice is provided at the header level, the date must be within tolerances for each line item or schedule line in the ship notice. If a delivery date in a ship-notice exceeds your tolerances, the ship notice fails submission, and error messages display to the supplier to identify which items exceed the tolerances. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile Default Transaction Rules . 2. Scroll to the Order Confirmation and Ship Notice Rules section to find transaction rule Apply delivery-date tolerances to ship-notice line items. 3. Enter in one or both of the rule's fields the number of days' difference to allow: • Days (Maximum before the requested delivery date.) • Days (Maximum after the requested delivery date.) 4. Click Save. Setting the Delivery-Date Tolerance in Ship Notices for Supplier Groups You can limit how late or early the suppliers in a supplier group can ship the items you order. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Transaction Configuration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 306]. Context  Note To instead configure delivery-date tolerances in ship notices for all your suppliers, go to Setting the Delivery- Date Tolerance in Ship Notices for All Suppliers [page 82]. When you configure for a supplier group any delivery-date tolerances for ship notices, SAP Business Network validates the ship notices sent to you by members of the supplier group. The system compares the value of Delivery Date in a ship notice to the value of Delivery Date in its order, to verify that the ship notice is within the SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 83 -- 3 of 10 -- configured tolerances. The tolerances apply to ship notices for purchase orders, scheduling agreement releases, and scheduling agreements.  Note When the delivery date for a ship-notice is provided at the header level, the date must be within tolerances for each line item or schedule line in the ship notice. If a delivery date in a ship-notice exceeds your tolerances, the ship notice fails submission, and error messages display to the supplier to identify which items exceed the tolerances. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Supplier Groups . 2. Do one of the following: • Click the name of an existing supplier group. • Click Create to configure a new supplier group. The Edit Supplier Group page opens. 3. Click Supplier Group Transaction Rules. The Supplier Group Transaction Rules page opens. 4. Click Enter supplier group specific transaction rules.. When this radio button is enabled instead of the Use default transaction rules. radio button, all rule settings on this page override how the same rules are set on the Default Transaction Rules page, for suppliers in this supplier group.. 5. Scroll to the Order Confirmation and Ship Notice Rules section to find transaction rule Apply delivery-date tolerances to ship-notice line items. 6. Enter in one or both of the rule's fields the number of days' difference to allow: • Days (Maximum before the requested delivery date.) • Days (Maximum after the requested delivery date.) 7. Click Ok. Service Sheet Rules If services invoicing is enabled for your account, you can configure these transaction rules for service sheets. Require suppliers to provide start and end dates on service sheets Check At line level to require suppliers to include both start and end dates for service sheet line items. The rule applies only to service items, not material items. Check At header to require suppliers to include both start and 84 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration -- 4 of 10 -- end dates at the service sheet header. When either option is checked, the subrule Do not allow service sheets for services that are still in progress is available. Both options apply whether suppliers create service sheets manually or whether SAP Business Network creates them automatically when an order is flipped to an invoice. Default setting (for both line level and header): No Do not allow service sheets for services that are still in progress. Requires suppliers to include either today’s date or a date in the past as the service end date when submitting service sheets for service items. Therefore, when this rule is checked, suppliers cannot submit service sheets for service items that are not completed. This rule applies to both manually created service sheets and those generated automatically when an order is flipped to an invoice. Default setting: No Require suppliers to create an order confirmation before creating a service sheet. Requires suppliers to partially or fully confirm an order before creating any service sheets from it. Default setting: No Require suppliers to provide approver information on service sheets. Requires suppliers to provide the email address of the person at your company responsible for approving the service sheet (and therefore that the work was completed according to the service sheet description) when creating a service sheet. Default setting: Yes Allow suppliers to send service sheet attachments. Allows suppliers to add attachments to service sheets. Service sheets only support attachments at the header level. Default setting: No SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 85 -- 5 of 10 -- Your procurement application can download service sheet attachments (MIME multipart messages). Allows your procurement application to download header-level service sheet attachments if you allow suppliers to add them. The additional setting, Send URLs to view attachments on Ariba Network, is also unchecked by default. Default setting: No Require suppliers to send service sheet attachments. Requires suppliers to add at least one attachment to each service sheet. If you check this rule, you must also check the Allow Suppliers to send service sheet attachments rule.  Note There is no way for suppliers to add attachments to service sheets uploaded as CSV files. If you check this rule for suppliers who upload service sheets as CSV files, their uploads will fail and they must log into SAP Business Network and edit and resubmit the failed service sheets with attachments. Default setting: No Allow suppliers to add ad hoc line items to service sheets. Allows suppliers to add items to service sheets that were not included in the original order. If you place unplanned service orders and your SAP Business Network buyer account is not integrated with SAP Ariba Procurement solutions, you should check this setting so that suppliers can add items as they fulfill the orders. Default setting: No Require suppliers to provide description for ad hoc line items Requires suppliers to provide part descriptions in ad hoc line items. Default setting: No Require suppliers to provide line item quantity for ad hoc line items Requires suppliers to provide line item quantities in ad hoc line items. Default setting: No 86 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration -- 6 of 10 -- Allow suppliers to change units of measure on service sheets. Allows suppliers to change units of measure on service sheets. If you check this rule, the Allow suppliers to increase item quantities on service sheets rule is automatically checked as well. You cannot set an exception tolerance when this rule is checked. Default setting: No Allow suppliers to increase item quantities on service sheets. If you uncheck this rule, suppliers can only increase item quantities on service sheets up to the tolerance level you specify. The default exception tolerance is 0%.Allows suppliers to increase item quantities on service sheets without restriction. You cannot set an exception tolerance when this rule is checked. Default setting: No Allow suppliers to change unit prices on service sheets. Allows suppliers to change unit prices on service sheets without restriction. You cannot set an exception tolerance when this rule is checked. If you uncheck this rule, suppliers can only change unit prices on service sheets within the tolerance level you specify. To set unit price tolerance, select Check Price Tolerance. Default setting: No Allow suppliers to change subtotal amounts on service sheets Allows suppliers to increase itemAllows suppliers to change subtotal amounts on service sheets without restrictions. You cannot set exception and absolute amount tolerances when this rule is checked. If you uncheck this rule, suppliers can only change subtotal amounts on service sheets up to either the exception tolerance or the absolute amount tolerance, whichever computed amount is smaller. For example, if the subtotal is $100 and you set an exception tolerance of 15% and an absolute amount tolerance of $100, the supplier can increase the subtotal up to $115. However, if the subtotal is $1000, the supplier can only increase the subtotal to $100, since 15% of $1000 is $150 and exceeds the absolute amount tolerance. The default exception tolerance is 0%; there is no default absolute amount tolerance.  Note This rule does not apply to unplanned order lines. Default setting: No SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 87 -- 7 of 10 -- Allow suppliers to create multiple service sheets for an amount-based service item Allows suppliers to create multiple service sheets for an amount-based service item. If you check this rule, suppliers can create multiple service sheets on amount-based lines on a service purchase order. If this rule is unchecked, suppliers can create only one service sheet for amount-based lines on a service purchase order. If a supplier attempts to create multiple service sheets against an amount-based service line purchase order when the rule is unchecked, SAP Business Network displays an error message. Default setting: Yes Allow suppliers to include taxes, freight, special handling, discounts, allowances, and charges, on automatically-generated service sheets Allows suppliers to include other charges such as taxes, freight, special handling, discounts, allowances, and charges on automatically-generated service sheets if your procurement application supports them. These charges also appear on the related invoice. If your procurement application does not support the processing of additional charges on a service sheet, you should uncheck this rule. If the rule is unchecked, additional charges are excluded from automatically-generated service sheets. Default setting: No Allow suppliers to include multiple parent PO lines per service sheet Allows suppliers to include multiple parent PO lines per service sheet. If you check this rule, suppliers won't be prompted to select an outline item when they create a service sheet or an invoice for the order. Instead, all parent PO lines are automatically added to the service sheet and the invoice. If the rule is unchecked, suppliers can include only one parent PO line per service sheet. Default setting: No Allow suppliers to reuse service sheet numbers Allows suppliers to reuse a service sheet number if the service sheet has been rejected or failed. Select at least one of the two options, Rejected and Failed. If you disable this rule, suppliers can’t reuse service sheet numbers. If a service sheet is rejected or failed, they must use a new number when they resubmit it. Default setting: No 88 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration -- 8 of 10 -- Require suppliers to create service entry sheets where the line item quantity is not zero Prevents suppliers from creating service entry sheets where the line item quantity is zero. Buyers can enable this rule to ensure that suppliers submit service sheets only after they replace the value U (Unknown) with the appropriate account assignment category values. Suppliers can punch in to SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing to retrieve the appropriate value for the account assignment category and then submit their service sheets. Default setting: No Allow suppliers to create correction service sheets Allows suppliers to create a correction service sheet for those service sheets which are invoiced. You must have SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA directly connected to SAP Business Network to receive the final service sheet indicator in service sheets. You must have SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA directly connected to SAP Business Network to receive the final service sheet indicator in service sheets. On the Default Transaction Rules page, when the Allow suppliers to reuse service sheet numbers is enabled, the Allow service sheet numbers to be reused for service sheets with the following statuses now includes the Canceled checkbox. file://SBN/split/CIGConfigSup_Part2.pdf.content: Defining Authorizations After you install the add-on components for SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network, you must define the authorization for users. The authorizations allow the users to send SAP information for transactions to SAP Business Network and SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. To define the required authorizations, use the authorization objects, class, and program that SAP Ariba provides. You must use the following out-of-the-box authorization objects for SAP ERP users. SAP Ariba provides the following authorization objects and classes: • ACIS: Authorization object class • ARBCIS_CLS: Authorization Object for Ariba Class Objects • ARBCIS_PRG: Authorization object for program execution • ARBCIS_SPR: Authorization Object for SPRO Node SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Installation Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers Defining Authorizations PUBLIC 11 -- 1 of 6 -- Configuring the SAP Cloud Connector Connect SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network with your SAP ERP using SAP Cloud Connector (cloud connector).  Note If you are using the same SAP ERP as a buyer and as a supplier, you cannot use the cloud connector configured for buy-side to connect with SAP ERP configured for sell-side. To connect SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network with your SAP ERP as a supplier, you must configure the cloud connector once again for the sell-side. The cloud connector serves as the link between SAP Cloud Platform and existing on-premise systems. The cloud connector runs as on-premise agent in a secured network and acts as a reverse invoke proxy between the on- premise network and SAP Cloud Platform. Due to its reverse invoke proxy support, you don't need to configure the on-premise firewall to allow external access from the cloud to internal systems. New installation and configuration You must install and configure cloud connector for test and production environments. For information on how to install and configure cloud connector, see Cloud Connector. Add the new subaccounts and configure cloud connector to connect to SAP ERP.  Note For high availability, you must configure multiple subaccounts. When creating subaccounts for cloud connector, enter the following information: Table 1: Table 1: Subaccount information Region Host Environment Subaccount name eu1.hana.ondemand.com Test aff5426a3 a18a6fc8f riph868phi Production a8f3ed22c ab9e90b64 a278d9ec7 a508aae51 fh7owkbn5n t6u5sulpil 12 PUBLIC SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Installation Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers Configuring the SAP Cloud Connector -- 2 of 6 -- Region Host Environment Subaccount name uajqgqv8l3 us4.hana.ondemand.com Test xf014edd7 x60abf046 Production b3bcoyxwro x691dbc6d x1e1a8cfb x8713dd41 fnpxlbn69y ald178slao Prerequisite • Use Java version 1.8 or above (JAVA SE 8 or above) for the cloud connector component. Perform the following task for each subaccount associated with the data center that you are connected to. 1. Log on to cloud connector. 2. Choose New Subaccount. 3. Enter the subaccount details. Refer Table 1: Subaccount information. 4. Enter the following information: • Subaccount User: Enter the P user ID and password that you received in the email when SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network was enabled on SAP Ariba solution. • Display Name: (Optional) Enter a name to easily recognize the subaccount in the user interface. • Location ID: (Optional) Enter the same LocationID that you had previously configured in SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. If you are a new customer, define an ID to identify the location of this cloud connector for the subaccounts. The location ID must be unique per subaccount and should be an identifier that can be used in a URL. • Description: (Optional) Enter a brief description of the connection. 5. Click Save. After configuring the subaccounts, you must configure cloud connector to allow SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network to access SAP ERP. Configure the backend systems in the cloud connector access control management. For more information, see the Cloud Connector section in the SAP BTP Connectivity guide. If you want to configure cloud connector for mutiple ERP systems, you must configure multiple connections on the Cloud To On-Premise page. Configuring existing installation of cloud connector If you already have an installation of cloud connector, you can configure it to connect to your SAP ERP. You must ensure that you are using Java version 1.8 or above (JAVA SE 8 or above). file://SBN/split/CIGOverviewSup_Part2.pd.content: Outbound Delivery Suppliers create an outbound delivery to notify the buyers that their orders are about to be shipped. SAP ERP add-on for suppliers supports the following features for outbound delivery: • Complete and partial outbound delivery only against standard sales orders. • Comments at the header and line-item levels. Restrictions SAP ERP add-on for suppliers does not support the following for outbound delivery: • Multi ANID with respective shipping point for one customer. • Update and cancellation of outbound delivery. • Service, consignment, subcontracting, return, blanket, scheduling agreement, and scheduling agreement release. • Attachments. • Serial number and Buyer Batch ID. • Single outbound delivery for multiple sales orders. • Packing or handling unit for material for outbound delivery. • Unit of Measure (UOM) other than the ISO standard. Billing Document Buyers create a purchase order to request for products or services using their SAP ERP and send them to suppliers on SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network then sends the purchase order to the supplier SAP ERP using SAP Business Network. The inbound purchase order is then converted to a sales order in the supplier SAP ERP. Suppliers create a billing document against sales orders sent by buyers. SAP ERP add-on for suppliers supports the following features for billing document: • Billing document referring to a single sales order. • Billing document for outbound delivery. • Credit memos for single sales order. • Billing document with taxes at header and line-item level. • Comments at the header and line levels. • Billing document with special handling charges at header and line-item level. • Billing document with shipping charges at the header level. • Partner functions such as ShipTo and BillTo addresses. SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers PUBLIC 11 -- 1 of 8 -- Restrictions SAP ERP add-on for suppliers does not support the following for billing documents: • Single billing document for multiple sales orders. • Single billing document referring to multiple outbound deliveries. • Line-level credit memos for multiple sales orders. • Standard invoice referring to single or multiple sales orders, when PO reference is not readily available, as in case of credit memo. • Non-PO invoice. • Invoice cancellation. • Credit memo for return orders. • Partial credit memo. • Discounts. • Attachments. • Shipping charges at the line-item level. • Partner functions such as SoldTo addresses. • Mapping due amount. Forward Error Handling Forward error handling (FEH) functionality allows the monitoring and processing of errors asynchronously on SAP ERP. When a document sent from an SAP Ariba solution to SAP ERP fails for any reason, it can be checked and processed again on SAP ERP. When FEH is enabled, the error message for every failed inbound transaction is transferred to Post Processing Ofoce (PPO). Status update request (SUR) for the transaction is sent to the sender when the transaction is successful or when the message is discarded. With FEH enabled and the business processes configured, if the system detects an error in an inbound transaction, the user can read the message and do one of the following: • Update the required information and reprocess the transaction. For example, if the error is due to a mapping error, the user can edit the payload and process the transaction again. The user can correct the error and reprocess the transaction until it is successful. An SUR is sent to the sender when the transaction is successful. • Reprocess the transaction immediately. For example, if the error is because the purchase order is still open, the user can submit the transaction for reprocessing. An SUR is sent to sender when the transaction is successful. • Discard the message in FEH if the sender has to take action on the transaction. In this case, a rejection message is sent to the sender as an SUR. Prerequisites • Activate FEH. • Define process data. • Define postprocessing. 12 PUBLIC SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers -- 2 of 8 -- • Define resolution stategy. • Define business process. • Assign proxy method to FEH. Navigate to the Integration Profile page. 2. Click one of the document-type tiles. The questionnaire for that document type opens. 3. Answer the questions for the tile. If the questionnaire contains multiple tabs, select each tab to move through the different sections of questions. 4. Click one of the following buttons: Button Description Save Save your answers. Your progress answering the questions for the tile is calculated, and the Integration Profile page displays. Only required questions count toward your progress. You do not need to complete all required questions for one document type before answering questions for other document types. The Save button only displays if you have the Integration Management Full Access permis- sion. Cancel Exit the questionnaire for this document type without saving your answers. Results After you complete all required questions for the document type, SAP Business Network creates buyer templates for the document type for all your existing buyers. Guided Integration for Trading Partners Guided Integration for Trading Partners PUBLIC 11 -- 1 of 10 -- View Your Compatibility with Your Trading Partners Use the compatibility dashboard to check compatibility with your buyers. Prerequisites You must have one of the following permissions: • Integration Management Read-Only Access • Integration Management Full Access After you complete the integration management questionnaire, you can use the compatibility dashboard to search for existing buyers to integrate with for additional business processes. You use this dashboard to compare the information from your integration profile with the business rules set by your buyers. The dashboard helps you locate compatibilities and incompatibilities with prospective buyers and find new buyers to integrate with for different business processes. It also helps you identify gaps in your business processes that you may want to address to be compatible with more buyers. The following are some examples of these types of gaps: • Order confirmations document – You do not update order confirmations when there are changes to previously- confirmed information like the order quantity. However, a majority of your existing buyers want their suppliers to be able to do this. • Invoice document – You only send invoices for orders transmitted from SAP Business Network. A buyer you would like to do business with for invoices requires their suppliers be able to send invoices from orders not transmitted from SAP Business Network (that is, non-PO invoices). For information about the compatibility dashboard, see Using the Guided Integration for Trading Partners Compatibility Dashboard [page 12]. Using the Guided Integration for Trading Partners Compatibility Dashboard You can use the compatibility dashboard to check your compatibility with your buyers. Prerequisites You must have one of the following permissions: • Integration Management Read-Only Access • Integration Management Full Access 12 PUBLIC Guided Integration for Trading Partners Guided Integration for Trading Partners -- 2 of 10 -- Procedure 1. From the Integration Overview page, click View Compatibility. The View Compatibility page opens. 2. Optional: Click a buyer to check your compatibility with them. The compatibility details page for that buyer opens. You can click each tab to check your compatibility with the buyer for the different document types. One of the following symbols displays in the Compatibility column: Guided Integration for Trading Partners Guided Integration for Trading Partners PUBLIC 13 -- 3 of 10 -- •  Checkmark icon – You are compatible with this buyer for this business rule. Either the buyer supports this business rule, or both you and the buyer do not support it. •  X icon – You are not compatible with this buyer for this business rule since you support it, but the buyer does not support it. Being incompatible for a business rule does not mean that you cannot integrate with this buyer. •  Question mark icon – You have not answered the corresponding question for this business rule. It is unknown whether you are compatible with this buyer for this business rule. • Checkmark with a dot icon - You are compatible with your trading partner, but you or your trading partner haven't answered the questionnaires. 3. From the View Compatibility page, choose one to three buyers to check compatibility with and click Compare. The Compare Compatibility page opens. 4. Review your compatibility with your selected buyers. If needed, scroll down the page to view all the business rules your buyers support . 14 PUBLIC Guided Integration for Trading Partners Guided Integration for Trading Partners -- 4 of 10 -- The information displays in two sections: 1. Buyer Overview – This section shows general information about the buyer as related to the document type. For example, the following rows display for the purchase order document type: • Total Amount (Last 12 Months) – The amount of purchase orders this buyer sent to you for the last 12 months. • Transactions (Last 12 Months) – The number of purchase order transactions between this buyer and you for the last 12 months. • Compatibility – This value indicates how compatible your purchase order processes are with this buyer's processes. A -- value in this column indicates the compatibility cannot be calculated yet since you have not completed the questionnaire for this document type. 2. Business Rules – Each row in this section contains a buyer business rule for the document type. The answers you have provided on the Integration Profile page, displays your compatibility with buyers who support each business rule. The value in the Buyer Coverage column shows the number of existing buyers you agree with for the rule. In each buyer's column, a  checkmark icon,  X icon,  question mark icon, or a checkmark with a dot icon. Refer to Step 2 for an explanation of these symbols. 5. Optional: Edit your answers. If you want to change your answers for a business rule, follow these steps to either answer a question you did not answer or change your answer to a previously answered question. a. Click the pencil ( ) icon to edit your answers. The popup for the business rule displays. b. Answer the question associated with the business rule.  Caution A changed answer will affect compatibility for all your buyers. c. Click Save to save your answer. Guided Integration for Trading Partners Guided Integration for Trading Partners PUBLIC 15 -- 5 of 10 -- 6. Optional: Click Reconcile Template for the buyer you want to integrate with for this business process. See Compare and Reconcile Templates with Guided Integration for Trading Partners [page 16] for information about reconciling templates. Compare and Reconcile Templates with Guided Integration for Trading Partners Compare your business processes with those of a prospective buyer and resolve any incompatibilities. Prerequisites You must have one of the following permissions: • Integration Management Read-Only Access • Integration Management Full Access Buyers and suppliers use cXML to transact business by sending and receiving documents with SAP Business Network. Buyers and suppliers need compatible business processes for these transactions to succeed. For example, suppose you are a supplier who sells t-shirts that buyers purchase to customize and resell. If a buyer purchases t-shirts from you, they need to be able to include the quantity for each size and color. If size and color are not already fields in your purchase order document, you will need to add them to be compatible with these buyers. Do the following two tasks to identify and resolve incompatibilities with selected buyers: 1. Compare templates for a document type. You can use different types of templates to do the comparison. Following are descriptions of these templates: • SAP Supplier Super Template – You have your own SAP Supplier Super Template for each document type. This is a customized template that matches all your buyer relationships in SAP Business Network. This template contains the common cXML for all buyers that you have a relationship with for the document type. SAP Business Network creates your initial SAP Supplier Super Template using the buyers you transacted with during the last 12 months for the document type. If you have no transactions with any buyers during the last 12 months for the document type, you will not have a SAP Supplier Super Template for the document type. When you add buyers for a document type, you can use Guided Integration for Trading Partners to update your SAP Supplier Super Template to include any new fields these added buyers require. • SAP Golden Template – Each document type has a SAP Golden Template. This is a standard template that matches the most used fields in SAP Business Network. For example, the SAP Golden Template for purchase orders contains the common fields buyers use for purchase orders. SAP Business Network automatically generates the SAP Golden Template for each document type. When generating these templates, it uses intelligence derived from a cross section of existing buyer and supplier relationships across different industries. • Buyer Template – This template is specific to a buyer for a document type. It is generated on the fly based on your transaction documents for this document type with this buyer. If the Buyer Template is not available in SAP Business Network, you can upload a local version of it. The template will not be available if you do not have any transaction documents for this document type with 16 PUBLIC Guided Integration for Trading Partners Guided Integration for Trading Partners -- 6 of 10 -- this buyer yet. You will need to continue to upload a local version of the Buyer Template until you have transaction documents for this document type with this buyer. • Document Type Definition (DTD) Template – cXML is thoroughly defined by a set of Document Type Definitions (DTDs). DTDs for all versions of cXML are available on cXML.org. The DTD template is the cXML.org template for the document type. Since DTDs define the syntax and order of all cXML fields for a document type, you may want to use the DTD template to find missing fields and attributes in your SAP Supplier Super Template. 2. Reconcile differences between templates. After comparing templates, you can reconcile any differences. If you have the Integration Management Full Access permission, you can save the reconciled template, download it, and share it with your middleware teams. Your middleware teams may need to make additional modifications to the template. For information about comparing and reconciling templates, refer to Comparing and Reconciling Templates with Guided Integration for Trading Partners [page 17]. Comparing and Reconciling Templates with Guided Integration for Trading Partners Compare your business processes with those of a prospective buyer, and then reconcile any incompatibilities. Prerequisites You must have one of the following permissions: • Integration Management Read-Only Access • Integration Management Full Access Procedure 1. From the Integration Overview page, click Reconcile and Download Template. The Reconcile Template page opens with the document type displayed at the top of the page. If needed, you can select a different document type from the pulldown menu. A default template that is suitable for you appears as My Latest Template in the My Workspace panel. Guided Integration for Trading Partners Guided Integration for Trading Partners PUBLIC 17 -- 7 of 10 -- Click the Document Type Definition (DTD) link at the bottom of the page to view, and optionally download, the Document Type Definition (DTD) cXML reference file for the document type. Note that you can only download the DTD file by clicking this reference link; you cannot download it by selecting Document Type Definition Template from the Source column. 2. Choose a Source template. The choices for the Source template include the following: • SAP Supplier Super Template – Customized template that matches all your buyer relationships in SAP Business Network. • SAP Golden Template – Standard template that matches the most used fields in SAP Business Network. • Buyer Template – The template specific to a buyer for this document type. • Document Type Definition Template – The standard cXML template that defines the document type. 18 PUBLIC Guided Integration for Trading Partners Guided Integration for Trading Partners -- 8 of 10 -- 3. Choose a My Workspace template. The choices for the My Workspace template include the following: • Draft Template – The last draft template you saved for the selected document type. • My Latest Template – The latest template you saved for the selected document type. • SAP Supplier Super Template – Customized template that matches all your buyer relationships in SAP Business Network. • SAP Golden Template – Standard template that matches the most used fields in SAP Business Network. • Upload Supplier Template – Upload your template to use it to compare and reconcile. The uploaded file must be a cXML file (XML file extension) with a maximum size of 5 MB. Guided Integration for Trading Partners Guided Integration for Trading Partners PUBLIC 19 -- 9 of 10 -- 4. Click Compare and then review the results. Only cXML elements that differ are expanded. 20 PUBLIC Guided Integration for Trading Partners Guided Integration for Trading Partners -- 10 of 10 --

The 92 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration -- 2 of 10 -- Code Type for quality notification data is "Type". The following example shows CSV data for quality notification types: Code Group Code Group Description Code Name Code Description Code Type Q6 Complaint from customer Q6A Delivery inspection Type Q6 Complaint from customer Q6B Goods receipt inspection Type Q6 Complaint from customer Q6C Audit inspection Type Q7 Complaint from vendor Q7A Production inspection Type Q7 Complaint from vendor Q7B Component inspection Type Q7 Complaint from vendor Q7C Customer return Type Configuring Quality Collaboration Notifications Use this procedure to define settings for quality documents. Prerequisites • Buyers: Your account is entitled for the quality collaboration component. • Suppliers: You have a trading relationship with a buyer entitled for the quality collaboration component. Context Buyers and suppliers can enable notifications for different types of documents and different events. Procedure 1. Choose Quality Settings . The Quality Settings page opens. 2. Click Edit. 3. If you are a supplier, choose one of the following options: • Same rule for all customers – Applies these quality settings to all of your customers. • Separate rules for each customer – Applies separate quality settings to each customer. If you choose this option, click Add customer to specify a customer to define settings for. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration PUBLIC 93 -- 3 of 10 -- For quality reviews only, when a quality review event occurs, all users who have their settings configured to receive quality review notifications from you for that type of event will receive them. 4. If you are a buyer, choose one of the following options: • Same rule for all suppliers – Applies these quality settings to all of your suppliers. • Separate rules for each supplier – Applies separate quality settings to each supplier. If you choose this option, click Add supplier to specify a supplier to define settings for. For quality reviews only, when a quality review event occurs, all users who have their settings configured to receive quality review notifications from you for that type of event will receive them. 5. Check the email notification options you prefer for Quality inspections, Quality notifications, and Quality reviews. 6. Click Submit. Overriding the Rule Determining Release Type for Shipping Use this procedure to override scheduling agreement release rules for a supplier. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Transaction Configuration permission. Context For a specific supplier, a buyer can override the rule determining the release type suppliers use for shipping. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . 2. In the Current Suppliers table, for a supplier for whom you want to override the rule, click More Actions Edit . 3. Under the heading Scheduling Agreement Release Setup Rules, check Override the following default scheduling agreement release rules.  Note Make sure Allow scheduling agreement release collaboration remains checked. 94 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration -- 4 of 10 -- 4. Check either of these rules to enable that rule for this specific supplier. • Allow suppliers to use only JIT for shipping. • Allow suppliers to use only Forecast for shipping. 5. Click Save. Customizing Planning, Forecast, and Manufacturing Visibility Business Rules for Specific Suppliers Use this procedure to change what rules apply to certain suppliers or supplier groups. Prerequisites You must be an administrator. Context You can create a custom configuration of settings for the Forecast, and Manufacturing Visibility planning processes. Procedure 1. Choose Buyer User Profile Settings Transactions Supplier Group Rules Supplier Rules . 2. In the upper right corner of the page, choose Add to create a new custom configuration. Configuration fields appear for the configuration's name, type of supplier and their names, and rules to set in Planning process and Forecast sections. 3. Enter your configuration choices. a. Type the name to give the new configuration. b. Add the suppliers or supplier groups the custom configuration applies to.  Restriction A mix of individual suppliers and supplier groups is not supported. c. Set the desired Forecast, and Manufacturing Visibility settings. The following table shows the available settings and their default values, if any. No Forecast Allow suppliers to view forecast data When this rule is set to Yes, suppliers can view forecast data from buyers. No Allow suppliers to commit to forecast data When this rule is set to Yes, suppliers can commit to forecast data to buyers. The Allow suppliers to view forecast data setting must be Yes to be able to change this setting. No Forecast commit horizon, in days (does not affect B2B mes- sages) To limit the period for which the supplier can commit to quanti- ties forecast, enter a number into the days field for the transac- tion rule. The Allow suppliers to view forecast data setting must be Yes to be able to change this setting. 1095 Forecast commit lock horizon, in days (does not affect B2B messages) Once a time series reaches the commit lock period, the supplier can no longer change that quantity. Forecast commit lock horizons are enforced in Forecast down- loads from the Quick Links Upload/Download Jobs tab, when the job criteria uses the Daily time period. A supplier is prevented from editing commit key figures for a time series that is within the locked period. The Allow suppliers to view forecast data setting must be Yes to be able to change this setting. 0 96 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration -- 6 of 10 -- Planning Process Setting Default Value Use Time series end date to populate Forecast data When set to Yes, each forecast quantity is posted to the end date of its time period, instead of the start date. The Allow suppliers to view forecast data setting must be Yes to be able to change this setting. No Forecast commit time bucket If the buyer selects All, the supplier can choose the time series granularity to use for each planning item. When the buyer se- lects a specific time series granularity (Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, or Yearly), the supplier is only allowed to commit fore- casts using that time series granularity. Daily Refresh forecast data from current date When this setting is enabled, a product activity message with changes to forecast information clears all forecast information between the current date and the earliest date in the message. The Allow suppliers to view forecast data setting must be Yes to be able to change this setting. No Match transaction quantities to transactional key figures even if coming from a different system ID When this setting is enabled, the transactional key figures no longer check for matching System ID values in their calculations. Instead, they validate that a product activity message has the same values for Customer part no., Supplier part no., Vendor ID, and Customer location as the purchase order it's for, before performing their calculations. No Clear buyer-sent key figures in forecast when planning item with no time-series data is received When this rule is set, if the buyer sends a forecast-type product activity message in cXML that does not include data in its de- tails section for the ORDER_FORECAST key figure or any buyer- sourced custom key figures, SAP Business Network clears the key figure data for those missing key figures from both the buy- er’s and the supplier's planning tables.  Caution Buyers should be careful when clearing key figure data from planning tables with cXML. After SAP Business Network processes the cXML message, the key figure data is gone and cannot be retrieved. No Component planning collaboration Enable component planning collaboration When this setting is set, if a planning item matches a finished good or a component stored in a BOM in SAP Business Network, its corresponding component planning collaboration item is cre- ated or updated. Next Steps If a member of a supplier group that is assigned a custom planning configuration is assigned as an individual supplier to another configuration, settings are applied to that supplier in the following priority: 1. Individual-supplier configuration 2. Supplier-group configuration 3. System default settings 98 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration -- 8 of 10 -- SAP Business Network Users and Roles By creating roles and then adding users to them, the SAP Business Network administrator controls who can sign in to your organization’s account and which areas of the service each user can access. SAP Business Network Roles [page 99] SAP Business Network Users [page 104] SAP Business Network Permissions [page 113] Prevention of Manual Sign In by SAP Business Network Buyer Users [page 122] SAP Business Network Roles A user with the Administrator role can create a role with certain permissions and assign the role to a buyer user. A role defines a user function within SAP Business Network, such as Purchase Order Generator. Each role has a unique name and set of associated permissions that specify what users who are assigned to the role can see and do in SAP Business Network. A role can be assigned to any number of users. Using the Administrator Role After you complete registration, SAP Business Network creates a single default role named Administrator. The Administrator role is automatically linked to the user name and sign in that you entered during registration. The Administrator role should be assigned to the individual at your organization who is responsible for setting configuration options, managing supplier relationships and contacts, and maintaining the account over time. The account administrator serves as the primary point of contact for users with questions or problems. As the SAP Business Network account administrator, you control who can sign in to your organization’s SAP Business Network account and which areas of the service each user can access. To do this, you create roles and then add users. As a best practice, create roles that reflect the way your company does business to prevent confusion for your account users and maximize the efociency of your team once roles are in place. Only one SAP Business Network user can be assigned to the Administrator role. You cannot modify this role, but you can assign it to another user. The account administrator can assign user management capabilities to non-administrator buyer users, called user administrators. For more information, see the following topics: • Transferring Administration Ownership [page 113] • Assigning User Management Capabilities to Users SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 99 -- 9 of 10 -- SAP Business Network Predefined Roles Predefined roles are visible only in accounts that were created before roles and permissions were introduced on SAP Business Network. If you registered with SAP Business Network after roles and permissions were implemented, Administrator is the only predefined role. To minimize disruption to these older users, SAP Business Network provides a small set of predefined roles to be used as templates for custom roles. SAP Business Network assigned the Full Access role to all preexisting users when it introduced roles and permissions. Administrators for these older supplier accounts should review the predefined roles and their permissions and consider using them as the basis for custom roles. The predefined roles are listed in the following table: This Role… Grants a User Access To… Administrator All areas of the account, including Settings Users and test account management Catalog Manager Catalogs Customer Catalogs Account Settings Manage Profile Notifications Catalog Service Full Access All areas of SAP Business Network, except areas that are reserved for administrators Purchasing Manager Give access to incoming and outgoing transaction documents and the following configuration pages: Account Settings Manage Profile Default Transaction Rules Account Settings Manage Profile cXML Setup Account Settings Manage Profile Notifications (transaction-related notifications only) Vendor Manager Supplier Enablement Current Relationships Supplier Enablement Contacts Account Settings Manage Profile Notifications Supplier Account Settings Company Profile Product Manager Catalogs Network Catalog Product Approver Catalogs Network Catalog The Administrator role includes all available permissions. These permissions grant the Administrator role access to all areas of your SAP Business Network account. file://SBN/split/SupplyChainCollaboratio.content: Creating a Role Buyer administrators and users assigned a role with the User Administration permission can define new roles with a specific set of user permissions that determine what the assigned users can see or do in SAP Business Network. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 113]. • Before creating your first role, you might want to review the list of permissions. This list is useful for planning your approach to roles. Some companies create broadly defined roles that include all or most of the available permissions, while others create specialized roles that include narrow sets of permissions. By planning your approach to roles, you can prevent confusion for your account users and maximize the efociency of your team after roles are in place. • Before creating new roles, use the Permission dropdown menu to filter the Roles table for existing roles that already include that permission. Context A role defines a user function within SAP Business Network. You assign roles when you create users.  Restriction • You can create no more than 25 custom roles. • SAP Business Network does not notify users of changes to roles. Before you make changes, you might want to inform users who will be affected. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . The Account Settings Users page appears with the Manage Roles tab selected by default. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 101 -- 1 of 10 -- Figure 1: Manage Roles Tab 2. Click the Create Role icon  at the top right of the role results table. 3. Enter a distinctive name for the role. 4. Enter a description to record your intentions for this role. Descriptions can be useful later, if you want to review or revise the structure of your roles. 5. Select one or more permissions for the new role. Each role must have at least one permission.  Note You can also select all permissions by clicking on the checkbox at the top left of the list of permissions. 6. Click Save. Results SAP Business Network creates the role and returns you to the Manage Roles page. Modifying a Role Buyer administrators and users assigned a role with the User Administration permission can edit a role's name, description, and assigned permissions. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 113]. 102 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles -- 2 of 10 -- • You have informed users about role changes that can affect them. SAP Business Network does not notify users of changes to roles. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. On the Manage Roles tab, search for a Permission using the search filters, or scroll down and locate the role you want to modify. 3. In the Role Name column of the search results table, select the role you want to modify. 4. Check Show me all the available permissions and select the permissions you want or uncheck the permissions you don't want for that role. 5. Choose Save. SAP Business Network applies your changes to all users assigned to the role. Changes take effect for each user at their next sign in. Reassigning Users to a Different Role Buyer administrators and users assigned a role with the User Administration permission can change the role assigned to users. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 113]. • You have informed users about role changes that will affect them.SAP Business Network does not notify users of changes to roles. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. On the Manage Roles tab, scroll down to the role you want to investigate. 3. Click the role in the Role Name column. 4. Scroll down to the Assigned Users table. 5. Using the checkboxes, select the users you want to move to another role. 6. Click Move to another role. 7. Click Save to return to the Manage Roles page. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 103 -- 3 of 10 -- Deleting a Role Buyer administrators and users assigned a role with the User Administration permission can delete roles that they no longer need. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 113]. • You have informed users about role changes that will affect them. SAP Business Network does not notify users of changes to roles. • No users can be assigned the role you want to delete. To change a user to another role, see Reassigning Users to a Different Role [page 103]. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. On the Manage Roles tab, you can perform a search for the role you want to delete, if necessary. Search for a Permission using the search filters. Or, scroll down and locate the role you want to delete. 3. In the Actions column of the roles results table, click the Delete  icon. Results SAP Business Network deletes the role and returns to the Users page. SAP Business Network Users Access to a buyer account is secured with individual user identities and levels of permissions. A user is an SAP Business Network sign in (user name and password) that enables one individual in your organization to sign in to your account. The administrator adds users to the SAP Business Network account and assigns each user exactly one role, which typically corresponds to the user’s real-world job responsibilities. 104 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles -- 4 of 10 -- Best Practices in Managing User Accounts When the administrator of an SAP Business Network account creates users and assigns roles, it is mandatory that the administrator assigns a unique user name with an appropriate assigned role for each individual who needs to access the account. Users must not share their user name or password with other users. This is important for SAP Business Network and your company in managing data privacy and integrity on SAP Business Network. For security, account administrators and users who have PCard access but are not the PCard owner are required to update their password every 90 days. As a best practice, users should not share their secret question and secret answer. To ensure your organization and users have secure accounts on SAP Business Network, create individual user accounts for different roles in the organization. By default, add one role per user. Users can have multiple related roles, depending on the tasks assigned to the user. How Roles Control User Interface Access Every user can see the Configuration Personal Information area, which contains basic contact information and a preferred language setting for that specific user. Beyond that, the only areas that a user is permitted to see are those allowed by their role permissions. For example, if the administrator created a role that included the Contact Administration permission, a user assigned to that role could see only the Configuration Personal Information area and the Supplier Enablement Contacts area of your SAP Business Network account. While users can update their own personal information, the administrator is responsible for overall user maintenance, which includes deleting users or reassigning user sign ins when individuals leave the company, and resetting user passwords. Creating a User [page 106] Configuring an Authorization Profile [page 108] Changing a User’s Role and Resetting the Password [page 110] Reassigning a User Sign In [page 111] Deleting a User [page 112] Transferring Administration Ownership [page 113] Related Information SAP Business Network Roles [page 99] SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 105 -- 5 of 10 -- Creating a User You can set up sign in credentials and assign permissions to access an SAP Business Network account. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 113]. • Before you create a user, you can use the Filter function from the Manage Users tab on the Account Settings Settings Users page to search for a user. 1. Click the dropdown arrow and select which search attribute you wish to use: User Name, Email Address, or First or Last Name. 2. Enter a search attribute value in the text box, then click the add  icon to the right. 3. Enter additional search values for the same search attribute as desired, up to 10.  Note You can search with only one attribute type at a time. 4. Click Apply. Context  Restriction • You can create no more than 6,000 users. • When an account has more than 1,000 users, SAP Business Network displays a simplified view of the Manage Users page. • You can create only one user for each employee who performs tasks on SAP Business Network. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. The Manage Users tab appears. 106 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles -- 6 of 10 -- 3. Scroll down to the top right of the user results table and click the Create User  icon. The Create User page appears. 4. Enter a user name, email address, first and last name, and optionally a phone number for this user. 5. Select a role in the Role Assignment section. 6. Scroll down and click Done. Results On the Manage Users page, at the top right of the user results table, note the Export Contact List  and Table Options Menu  icons. • The Export Contact List function downloads all roles and associated user permissions in a CSV file for ofnine review. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 107 -- 7 of 10 -- • The Table Options Menu controls what columns to show in the user results table. After you create a user, SAP Business Network sends an email message to that user with a randomly generated password. Each new user should sign in and change the password to something they can remember. Next Steps • Remind users to store their user names and passwords in a safe place. • Users who forget their user name can go to the Sign In page, click Forgot User Name and follow the instructions for regaining access to their account. • If a user forgets their password, an administrator can reset it. You can change a user’s role assignment at any time. See Changing a User’s Role and Resetting the Password [page 110]. • If an employee leaves your company or changes jobs, and no longer uses the SAP Business Network account, an administrator can delete the user. See Deleting a User [page 112]. Configuring an Authorization Profile Buyer administrators can create a profile that authorizes the assigned buyer to access only certain business areas. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Context Authorization profiles for buyer users provide a way for buyer administrators to segregate duties, visibility, and actions based on buyer roles and responsibilities. This capability helps organizations meet legal, financial, or security needs to limit what information a particular buyer can access. Procedure 1. Select Administration Users Manage Authorization Profiles . 2. Click Create Profile. 3. Enter a profile name, the authorized responsibilities, and the buyer users you want to assign these responsibilities. • Click Order Collaboration to specify the following values: 108 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles -- 8 of 10 -- • Company Code • Location • Purchasing Organization • Purchasing Group • Planner Code • System ID • Vendor ID • Program: This attribute is displayed only in the FedRAMP environment. • Contract: This attribute is displayed only in the FedRAMP environment. • SIP: This attribute is displayed only in the FedRAMP environment. • Click Quality Collaboration to specify the following values: • Line of Business • Location • System ID • Click Planning Collaboration to specify the following values: • Planner Code • Location • Line of Business • Product Family • Program Code • Click Additional Settings to enable or disable Do not allow users in this authorization profile to see or download other users’ jobs in the Upload/Download section.  Note This setting also applies to job uploads. 4. Click Save. The profile is added to the table in the Manage Authorization Profiles section. Results Assignment of an authorization profile affects a buyer user's access to data in the following ways: • Authorization profiles apply only to data displayed in the SAP Business Network user interface. • Buyer users can see on the Orders Orders and Releases page only data that matches the values in their assigned profile. Data that has a different value than is specified in the profile, or has no value, is not visible. • Documents with no Company code value are visible only to buyer users whose assigned profile has no Company code values set. • If a buyer user is assigned a profile that restricts access to data for which the buyer has configured alerts, alerts are no longer created for the restricted area. • The Upload/Download and Report tabs do not show filters for segregated duties. • A buyer user who is not assigned an authorization profile has no data visibility restrictions. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 109 -- 9 of 10 -- • If Do not allow users in this authorization profile to see or download other users’ jobs in the Upload/ Download section is enabled, the buyer user cannot see any jobs or downloads for other buyer users with the same authorizations. Changing a User’s Role and Resetting the Password You can select a different role for an existing user or reset the password. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 113]. Context Users can forget their sign in information if they do not sign in to SAP Business Network regularly. SAP Business Network provides a secure and relatively quick way for users to recover sign in information. However, even with this process in place, loss of user names and passwords can cause frustration and lost productivity for you and your users. If you do not want to reset a user’s password, instruct him or her to click Forgot Your Password? on the SAP Business Network Sign In page. After a user submits a user name, SAP Business Network Accounts Services sends the user an email containing steps to reset the password. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. Cick Edit for the user whose password you want to reset. 4. Do one of the following: • To change a user’s role, select a different role in the Role Assignment section and click Save. • To reset the user’s password, click Reset Password. 5. Click Save. SAP Business Network returns to the Users page. 110 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SupplyChainCollaboratio.content: Results If you reset the user’s password, SAP Business Network sends an email to the user containing a new randomly- generated password. The password update takes effect immediately. Reassigning a User Sign In If a user has left the company, you can reassign that user’s sign-in to another individual, to retain the user setup and data. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 113]. Context When an employee leaves the company or changes jobs and no longer uses the SAP Business Network account in their name, the administrator should either delete the user or reassign the user’s sign-in to another individual. If you want to retain the user’s setup and data, reassign the sign-in. If you want to delete the user’s setup and data, delete the user. Procedure 1. Sign in using the user’s user name and password. If you do not know the password, click Help Support to contact SAP Business Network Support. 2. Choose Account Settings Manage Profile . 3. On the Configuration page, choose Personal Information. 4. Change the user name and password and optionally other information. 5. Click OK. 6. On the Configuration page, choose Notifications. 7. Make any modifications to notification emails based on the user sign in reassignment. 8. Click OK. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 111 -- 1 of 10 -- Deleting a User If a user has left the company, you can delete the user to prevent its further use to access SAP Business Network. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 113]. Context When an employee leaves the company or changes jobs and no longer uses the SAP Business Network account, the administrator should either delete the user or reassign the user’s sign in to another individual. • If you want to retain the user’s setup and data, reassign the sign in. See Creating a User [page 106] for the steps to perform. 4. In the user results table, check the checkbox for the user you want to delete. 5. In the Actions column, click the Delete  icon in the row of the user you want to delete. Results SAP Business Network deletes the account and refreshes the page content. It does not maintain a record of deleted users. 112 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles -- 2 of 10 -- Transferring Administration Ownership The current account administrator can reassign ownership of the SAP Business Network account to another person. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. Select the user you want to transfer the Administrator role to. 4. Choose Actions Make Administrator . The Assign a Role page opens. 5. Select a new role for your account, and click Assign.
