Grants access to this area: Account Settings Manage Announcements Quick Links Create Announcement Prevention of Manual Sign In by SAP Business Network Buyer Users Buyers whose SAP Business Network accounts are configured for single sign-on (SSO) corporate authentication can prevent users from signing into the SAP Business Network manually, outside of the single sign-on (SSO) configuration. This SAP Business Network feature is applicable to all buyers who use single sign-on (SSO) corporate authentication for accessing the SAP Business Network. This feature does not affect SAP Business Network suppliers. Preventing users from signing in manually enhances the security of SAP Business Network accounts using single sign-on (SSO) authentication. When this feature is enabled, users cannot sign in to the SAP Business Network in any way other than through single sign-on (SSO). They cannot sign in by entering the URL buyer.ariba.com directly into a browser. Even users with the Administrator role cannot sign in manually. Users who try to sign in manually will receive an error message that says The user name and password pair you entered was not found. If this feature is not enabled, users can use their user name and password to manually sign in to the SAP Business Network. Enabling This Feature This feature is disabled by default. To enable this feature, ask your Designated Support Contact to log a case (formerly Service Request). An SAP Business Network Support representative will follow up to complete the request. Enabling the feature involves SAP Business Network setting an option in the single sign-on (SSO) configuration for the SAP Business Network account to disable manual sign in. 122 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles -- 2 of 10 -- SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits This section provides topics that describe the key features and benefits of SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. Orders and Releases Features [page 123] Multitier Order Collaboration [page 136] Inventory Features [page 136] Invoicing Features [page 144] Quality Features [page 145] Supply Chain Monitor Feature [page 186] Freight Collaboration Feature [page 201] Orders and Releases Features This section describes SAP Business Network for Supply Chain features for purchase orders and scheduling agreement releases. Purchase Order Line Items [page 124] Direct-Material Fields for Order and Invoice Collaboration [page 125] External Information Sources [page 125] High-Tech Industry Fields for Order Collaboration [page 127] The Items to Confirm List [page 128] Order change requests Tile for the Buyer Workbench [page 128] Scheduling Agreement Releases [page 131] Search Filters in Order and Forecast Collaboration [page 132] Stock Transport Orders [page 132] Subcontract Enhancements for Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul Scenarios [page 133] Supplier Copies of Documents [page 134] SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 123 -- 3 of 10 -- Purchase Order Line Items A purchase order contains one or more line items. Deleting Line Items Buyers can select which of their integrated suppliers should receive delete indicators when they delete line items in a purchase order. To select suppliers, buyers follow the steps documented in Enabling PO Line Item Delete Indicator [page 125]. Buyers only select suppliers who have not already implemented their own logic to determine which line items were deleted in a purchase order. The operation attribute in an ItemOut element in a cXML OrderRequest document defines actions associated with line items in purchase orders. When a buyer deletes a line item from a purchase order, they include operation="delete" in the ItemOut element. When a line item is deleted, it is crossed out on the Purchase Order Order Details page, and the Change column shows the line item as Deleted. Note that the information about deleted line items is visible even if the user clicks Hide Changes. Information about deleted line items is included in emails about updated purchase orders and in downloaded PDF files for purchase orders.  Note If the buyer undoes the deletion of a line item in a purchase order, that line item is still mapped to a new line item in the supplier's sales order since the supplier mapped the line item to a new line item in the sales order before the buyer undid the deletion. Retaining Order Confirmations for Purchase Order Line Items Buyers can retain their order confirmations when they match the supplier's confirmation even if the item has changed. The supplier is not required to reconfirm fulfilled items with conditions set at the schedule line level. If the rule Retain confirmation status for changed line items on change orders that match supplier confirmation is active and the order confirmation deviation approval is deactivated the confirmation status of unchanged line items on the previous order is retained on change orders. When this rule is applied, the following requirements are met: • Validate if the change order items have changed and match the confirmation status at the schedule line level. • The order confirmation is retained if the change order items have changes that match any confirmation status items from the last order confirmation. • New and old versions of the order confirmations are retained. • Items with Confirmed and Backordered status are retained. • Items with Rejected status are not included in the evaluation. When this rule is active and applied, the following schedule line-item level fields are evaluated to determine if the new version of the order matches the order confirmation: 124 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 4 of 10 -- • Line Items: Requested Quantity, Requested Delivery Date, Unit Price • Schedule Lines: Quantity, Requested Delivery Date Enabling PO Line Item Delete Indicator Buyer can select suppliers who should receive the purchase order with the Deleted line items indicator, as follows: Procedure 1. Run the transaction code SPRO. The Customizing: Execute Project screen appears. 2. Click SAP Reference IMG. The Display IMG screen appears. 3. Navigate to Integration with Other SAP Components Managed Gateway for Spend&Network for Buyer SAP Business Network Integration General Settings Enable Vendors 4. Click the IMG-Activity icon for Enable Vendors. The Change View "SAP Business Network Vendor Table": Overview screen appears. 5. Enter X in the Send PO Del Ind field for the integrated supplier who should receive purchase order with the Deleted line items indicator. Direct-Material Fields for Order and Invoice Collaboration Buyers and suppliers can view shared direct-material order information. Suppliers and buyers often collaborate in the creation of purchase orders, invoices, and ship notices for direct- material orders. This collaboration requires the exchange of information specific to direct-material orders. Direct-material fields for order and invoice collaboration facilitate the collaboration process for purchase orders, invoices, and ship notices by allowing a more detailed description of materials being procured. These fields also allow the supplier to collaborate through the SAP Business Network user interface. This is particularly helpful for suppliers that do not have EDI, cXML, or other integrated business-to-business mechanisms in place. External Information Sources Buyers can securely share information with suppliers through links to external sources. Buyers can provide links to external information sources in line items of purchase orders, scheduling agreements, and scheduling agreement releases. External information sources can include anything that you want to add as supportive information for a line item of a purchase order, a scheduling agreement, or a scheduling agreement SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 125 -- 5 of 10 -- release. Examples of such sources are a link to a technical drawing or to a website containing item specifications. Suppliers can click the links that are included in the line item of the purchase order, the scheduling agreement, or the scheduling agreement release on SAP Business Network to access external information sources using single sign-on (SSO). To provide an external information source reference for an order item, you add to the order cXML an AttachmentReference element in the item's ItemDetails element. For more information, see "AttachmentReference" in the cXML Reference Guide . URLs added in the links can use the HTTP(S) or FTP(S) protocols. When a supplier user clicks a link to external information sources, SAP Business Network sends a SAML assertion through the supplier web browser to the target system for authentication while the supplier web browser is being redirected to the URL of the link. The SAML assertion is issued by SAP Business Network that contains the necessary information for identifying a supplier user uniquely such as the ANID of the supplier organization and the supplier user's email address.  Note You must import the appropriate SAML metadata from SAP Business Network to the target system that validates the SAML assertion issued by SAP Business Network. You can get this information by requesting the SAML metadata and importing it to your target system. Ask your Designated Support Contact (DSC) to log a case (formerly referred to as a Service Request). A SAP Business Network support representative will follow up to complete your request for the SAML metadata.  Note It is the responsibility of the buyer to provide a supplier with access to an external information source. There is no SAP Business Network involvement in opening an external information source. Access is handled between the buyer and the supplier only. SAP Business Network uses a share icon to identify a line item with one or more external information sources. This icon shows in the Line Items section of an order details page, next to the line item's part number. The line-item details page also has an Additional Sources table with the following fields, which are populated with the values in AttachmentReference elements for the item: • Source Name – The name of the document or other external information source. The source name is not an active hyperlink for buyers. • Version – The source version. • Description – A description of the additional source.  Note If the SAML <saml:Audience> tag with a hardcoded value is required to be sent in the SAML assertion, please request your DSC to add the value by reaching out to SAP. A dynamic value in <saml:Audience> is not supported. Related Information External Document Sources Report [page 274] 126 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 6 of 10 -- High-Tech Industry Fields for Order Collaboration Buyers and suppliers can better manage their inventory and production levels for high-tech components. With real-time visibility into the supply chain, original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), contract manufacturers, and suppliers can match production orders to required materials and capacity. They can collaborate in real time to keep component inventories at optimum levels, and to reduce inventories of finished goods. The high-tech industry fields for order collaboration support this real-time supply-chain collaboration. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain supports high-tech extensions to key fields in the following documents (in cXML documents and in the user interface): • Purchase orders • Purchase order confirmations • Ship notices • Component consumption documents Workflow With high-tech industry fields for order collaboration, the ordering process for contract manufacturing typically follows the following steps: 1. A customer sends a purchase order to a supplier via an ERP system. 2. The supplier receives the purchase order, and the component supplier receives a copy of the purchase order. 3. The customer sends any changes to the purchase order to the supplier. 4. The supplier receives the purchase order revisions and sends a copy of them to the component supplier.The following elements and attributes provide high-tech industry fields for order collaboration: 5. The supplier sends a purchase order confirmation to the customer, and sends a copy of the purchase order confirmation to the component supplier. 6. The customer receives the purchase order confirmation. 7. The supplier sends a ship notice to the customer, and sends a copy of the ship notice to the component supplier. 8. The component supplier sends a goods receipt to the customer based on the shipment from the supplier. 9. The customer receives the goods receipt. cXML Elements for High-Tech Industry Fields for Order Collaboration • OrderRequestHeader • OrderRequestHeaderIndustry • ItemOut • thirdParty • requestedShipmentDate • ComponentConsumptionDetails • type SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 127 -- 7 of 10 -- • ReferenceDocumentInfo For more information, see the cXML Reference Guide . The Items to Confirm List The Items to Confirm list enables the supplier to efociently and accurately confirm incoming purchase orders across multiple customers. In the order collaboration process for direct materials, suppliers typically strive to establish long-term, repeat business with their customers. From the supplier perspective, a successful business model involves a continual flow of incoming purchase orders from a number of buying customers. The supplier must efociently process incoming purchase orders: confirming line items when confirmation is required, creating ship notices, and shipping goods. Also, the supplier must process purchase orders that have been changed. Further, the supplier must not confirm orders for quantities or delivery dates that are not achievable. The process of confirming orders quickly and correctly therefore can be very challenging because of the sheer volume of data and the level of detail required. The Allow suppliers to send order confirmations on line item level and Allow suppliers to send order confirmations to this account rules control the visibility of purchase order line items in supplier Items to Confirm lists and whether they are actionable. For more information, see Order Confirmation and Ship Notice Rules [page 76]. Order change requests Tile for the Buyer Workbench The Order change requests tile in the buyer Workbench helps buyers send and monitor change requests to their suppliers.  Restriction • The Order change requests tile does not support change requests for scheduling agreements or scheduling agreement releases. • A supplier can make only one response or proposal per change request. • A buyer can make only one response or proposal to a supplier response per change request. The Order change requests tile in the buyer Workbench is a configurable tile that provides information about the purchase-order change requests that a buyer has received. The tile includes the following elements: • The tile shows the number of change requests that meet the filter criteria and also need a response. • The search results table shows the change requests that meet the filter criteria. For details about the available filters, see Editing Filters for the Order change requests Tile [page 129]. • The search results table includes the following columns, which by default are not shown: • Supplier Proposed Delivery Date • Supplier Proposed Quantity • Rejected reason 128 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 8 of 10 -- • Estimated Cost • Comments Editing Filters for the Order change requests Tile Buyers can use filters to refine the information that shows on the Order change requests tile. Context The Order change requests tile on the buyer Workbench page provides search filters to refine what data it shows. Click Edit filter to show or hide the filters. The following table lists the names and descriptions of the tile filters. Filter Description Suppliers One or more supplier names. Order numbers Purchase order ID. Set the search to Partial match (the default) or Exact match.  Note When you choose the Exact match radio button in the Order numbers filter, only the Suppliers and Order numbers filters remain visible. Customer locations Unique identifier for one or more locations in the buyer organization. Company codes One or more company-code IDs. Order line-item numbers Line number for the purchase order item. Schedule-line numbers Schedule-line number for the purchase order line item. Customer part numbers One or more part numbers used by the customer for the item. Creation date A range of dates when a change request was created. Filter choices are from Last 24 hours to Last 365 days or to set a Custom date range. Default is Last 31 days. Customer proposed delivery date A range of item delivery dates that a customer proposed as changes to original delivery dates. Filter choices are None (the default), date ranges from Last 7 days toNext 365 days, or set a Custom date range. Change by number of days The number of days that a Customer proposed delivery date is earlier or later than the order's current Delivery date. Filter choices are None (the default), Days earlier, or Days later. For the Days earlier and Days later choices, the filter also shows Min and Max fields. In these fields, you specify the minimum and maximum number of days difference that you want to include in the search results. The Min and Max fields have the following requirements: • At least one of these fields, Min or Max, must contain a value. Valid values are a number from 0 to 999. Both fields can be the same number. • The value of Min must not be greater than the value of Max. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 129 -- 9 of 10 -- Filter Description Priority One or more priority levels for the requested change. Filter choices are determined by the buyer. If you leave the filter empty, the search includes all possible priorities. Reason codes One or more numeric or text codes that provide a high-level reason for the requested change. Possible values are provided by the buyer.  Note If the filter shows no choices of reason codes, the buyer doesn't require them and you can leave the filter empty. Rejected reason One or more numeric or text codes that provide a high-level reason for rejecting the change request. Possible values are provided by the buyer.  Note If the filter shows no choices of rejected reason, the buyer doesn't require one and you can leave the filter empty. Customer response status One or more statuses for a buyer's response to a change-request response from a supplier, or to a change request by the buyer that received no supplier response. Status choices are Accepted, Pending, and Rejected. Supplier response status One or more statuses for a supplier response to a change request from a buyer. Status choices are Accepted, Pending, Proposed, and Rejected. Procedure 1. For filter fields that allow multiple values, enter each value that you want to add in the same field. a. Click an empty area of the filter field. b. Enter a value, which can be more than one word. c. Click outside the entry field to complete that entry. 2. For filter fields that show the input hint Select or type selections and a value-help icon ( ), choose the desired values. a. Click in the field to expand the dropdown. b. Select from the dropdown one or more of the choices. file://SBN/split/SupplyChainCollaboratio.content: Scheduling Agreement Releases A scheduling agreement release defines the quantities and dates for the shipments desired for a specific item. Buyers often want to procure pre-defined quantities of materials in releases to be received on pre-determined dates. For example, a buyer might order 100 items, but might want them delivered, 10 items at a time, on a weekly basis. A buyer might therefore send a scheduling agreement release to a supplier. A scheduling agreement release can have multiple schedule lines for any single line in a purchase order or other business document. A single schedule line contains fields for delivery date and time, and for scheduled quantity and unit of measure. Buyers create schedule agreement releases with external ERP systems. Scheduling agreement releases are visible in the SAP Business Network user interface. Buyers can periodically communicate releases to their suppliers; and suppliers can create ship notices for materials requested through scheduling agreement releases. From the Items to Ship tab, a supplier can create a single ship notice containing items from several purchase orders that all are due by the same date. Schedule lines include shipment progress information in the Shipment Status column. When the shipped quantity is equal to or greater than the requested quantity, the schedule line displays an icon that indicates the line has been fully shipped. The next schedule line displays an icon with the text This is the next line to ship; this status can apply to partially shipped schedule lines in addition to those that have not yet shipped. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain consumes requested quantities from the earliest to the latest schedule line based on Delivery Date without consideration of which schedule lines were selected during ship notice creation from the workbench. Scheduling agreement release collaboration is disabled by default. To enable it, you must enable the Allow scheduling agreement release collaboration transaction rule. When this rule is enabled, the buyer can send scheduling agreement release documents for collaboration with suppliers. And suppliers who are enabled for supply chain collaboration functionality can create ship notices from scheduling agreement releases. Restrictions • You cannot use scheduling agreement release collaboration for invoices, except those invoices created as carbon copies by direct material buyers. • You cannot use scheduling agreement releases for order confirmations. The processing of non-scheduled items is not affected by scheduling agreement releases. cXML Elements for Scheduling Agreement Releases The following elements and attributes support scheduling agreement releases: • isSchedulingAgreementRelease (an attribute of the OrderRequestHeader element) • ReleaseInfo • ScheduleLineReleaseInfo • agreementType (an attribute of the MasterAgreementIDInfo element) • ShipNoticePortion SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 131 -- 1 of 10 -- Additional References • cXML Solutions Guide • cXML Reference Guide . Search Filters in Order and Forecast Collaboration You can use filters to aid in searching orders and forecast documents. Users search differently for different kinds of items. Here are three examples: • A buyer searches forecasts for a product based on the product internal program code • A supplier getting ready to send order confirmations searches for line items for a certain customer by the customer planner code • A supplier getting ready to send ship notices searches for all items belonging to a certain product family On the Planning Forecast page, you can filter searches for items to confirm, items to ship, and order confirmations: • For planner code  Note Information for planner codes that you are not authorized to access are excluded from the search results. • For product group Additionally, you can browse for filters in the following product-grouping hierarchies: • Line of business • Product family • Product subfamily • Internal program code • Program code • Part type • Part family Stock Transport Orders Buyers can identify and view stock transport orders. A stock transport order is a type of purchase order that is used to move stock between two plants within an organization or between different organizations. On the Orders Orders and Releases page, the search results table identifies stock transport orders by showing Stock Transport Order in the Type column, rather than Order for standard purchase orders. Search only stock transport orders in the page's Search filters limits search results to stock transport orders only. 132 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 2 of 10 -- When you open the details page of a stock transport order, the Line Items table includes a Stock Transfer Type column, which shows which kind of transfer to make for a line item. The column's values are: • Intra – Intracompany. A stock transfer between plants in the same company. • Inter – Intercompany. A stock transfer between plants in different companies. Restrictions • Only purchase orders are supported as stock transport orders. Scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases are not supported for stock transport orders. • The following capabilities are not supported for a stock transport order: Invoice creation Handling units • Stock transport order quantities are not counted in the calculation of transactional key figures.  Note Transactional key figures include the Firmed orders (ALL_ORDERS), Total shipment (ALL_ASN), ASN received (ASN_RECEIPT), Order received (PO_RECEIPT), and Goods received (RECEIPT_DATE_GOODS_RECEIPT) key figures. Subcontract Enhancements for Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul Scenarios Buyers can identify in a purchase order what service a subcontractor needs to provide. With the subcontracting enhancements for maintenance, repair, and overhaul scenarios feature, suppliers can now more effectively handle the subcontracting process for subcontracted maintenance, repair, and overhaul. Buyers can set a Subcontract type in purchase order line items for suppliers who act as subcontractors, to indicate which type of service the subcontractor would provide. Workflow for Subcontracting Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul Scenarios The end-to-end workflow for subcontracting maintenance, repair, and overhaul scenarios starts with a buyer creating a maintenance order, and ends with the buyer sending a goods receipt to the supplier who then creates an invoice. Workflow scenarios vary, depending on the individual requirements defined between buyers and suppliers.The following example describes a possible workflow: 1. The buyer creates a maintenance order. The order defines the type of service: SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 133 -- 3 of 10 -- • A repair (no material change) • An upgrade (material change) 2. In response to the maintenance order, the buyer system automatically sends a subcontracting purchase order to SAP Business Network. 3. The supplier assesses the defect material, makes a quote for the repair cost, and optionally determines a delivery date. 4. The supplier confirms the purchase order with the new date, if applicable, and with an updated price (the quote). 5. The supplier sends the order confirmation, which contains the added details, to enable the buyer to trigger related back-end processes. 6. The buyer can optionally send the subcontracting purchase order with the updated price to SAP Business Network. 7. After repair or maintenance of the material is done, the supplier ships the goods and informs the buyer by creating the ship notice. 8. The buyer creates a goods receipt based on the purchase order. 9. The buyer sends a goods receipt to the supplier, indicating that the supplier can create the invoice, the last step of the process. Supplier Copies of Documents Buyers can send suppliers a copy of a transaction document but exclude confidential buyer information from the copy. In a multitier supply chain, tier-one suppliers can receive copies of orders, order confirmations, and ship notices. Document copies provide necessary information to suppliers about transactions without compromising the buyer's financial information; all fields containing financial information in the document copy are masked, preventing suppliers from seeing the following information: • Prices • Taxes • Payment terms • PCard Information • BillTo Information 134 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 4 of 10 -- Figure 2: Document-Copy Workflow Example To create copies of documents for suppliers, the requesting transaction document, such as a purchase order, includes a Path element containing a copy node in the header, as shown in the following example: <Header> <From> <Credential domain="NetworkID"> <Identity>AN990000000168</Identity> </Credential> </From> <To> <Credential domain="NetworkID"> <Identity>AN990000000169</Identity> </Credential> </To> <Sender> <Credential domain="NetworkID"> <Identity>AN990000000168</Identity> <SharedSecret>welcome</SharedSecret> </Credential> <UserAgent>Ariba Buyer 7.0</UserAgent> </Sender> <Path> <!-- Contract Manufacturer --> <Node type="copy"> <Credential domain="NetworkId"> <Identity>AN01000000170</Identity> </Credential> </Node> </Path> <!-- Original order to copy --> <OriginalDocument payloadID="989280592595-5564367883689744433@10.11.128.149"/> </Header> SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 135 -- 5 of 10 -- Multitier Order Collaboration With a multitier supply chain, an Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) buyer and multiple suppliers collaborate to produce a finished product. Multitier order collaboration provides end-to-end visibility and collaboration features for a multitier ordering process. It allows supply chain partners to view copies of orders, order confirmations, and ship notices (with financial fields masked) and create component receipts after receiving shipments. OEM buyers can manage their copy documents and view component shipments and receipts from tiered suppliers. Extended Collaboration Tab [page 136] Extended Collaboration Tab The Extended Collaboration tab on the Fulfillment page contains documents used to collaborate with your extended supply chain. Tab Description Component Inventory Shows a component inventory snapshot for a given point in time. Component Shipments Shows the actual component issue date, quantity, tracking number, receipt sta- tus, and other information. You can select multiple component ship notices to perform an action, such as creating a component receipt. Component Receipts Shows receipts for subcontracting components sent to the buyer. You can click a receipt number to open it and access its attachments. Component Consumption Shows component consumption messages sent to the buyer. Return Shipments Shows return shipments from the buyer. Inventory Features This section describes SAP Business Network for Supply Chain features for inventory. Contract Manufacturing Collaboration [page 137] Consignment Collaboration [page 139] Manufacturing Planning Visibility [page 140] Forecast Collaboration [page 141] Supplier-Managed Inventory [page 143] 136 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 6 of 10 -- Contract Manufacturing Collaboration With the contract manufacturing collaboration feature, buyers and contract manufacturers can manage the supply of component materials and finished goods through SAP Business Network. Large organizations can reduce costs by transferring the manufacture, assembly, or processing of parts to third- party contract manufacturers. Contract manufacturers are suppliers who build the parts for these buyers. The contract manufacturing collaboration feature includes the following functionalities: • Buyers can create subcontract purchase orders which can be transmitted to contract manufacturers via SAP Business Network. • Contract manufacturers can view all the data of subcontract purchase orders, including all the component information under the purchase order line item, in the schedule line section. • Contract manufacturers can confirm orders for finished goods purchased by buyers. • Buyers can create ship notices for subcontracting components, and can send them to contract manufacturers. • Contract manufacturers can create receipts for subcontracting components, and can send them to buyers. • Contract manufacturers can create ship notices for finished goods to be shipped to buyers. • Contract manufacturers can send component consumption information to buyers for components used to manufacture the finished goods on the subcontract purchase order. The following types of messages support direct materials buyers and contract manufacturers: Subcontracting Purchase Order A subcontracting purchase order is a purchase order that is sent from a buyer to a contract manufacturer to request the production and delivery of finished goods. The subcontracting purchase order has been enhanced to carry, not only item level and schedule line level information, but also subcontracting component information. Subcontracting components are the raw materials that are used for manufacturing the finished goods specified at the item level. Component Ship Notice A component ship notice is a type of ship notice that informs the contract manufacturer of the shipment of subcontracting components. Component Receipt A component receipt is a type of goods receipt that informs the buyer of the receipt of subcontracting components. The contract manufacturer can issue the component receipt against one or more component ship notices. Component Consumption (Backflush) Message The ship notice message has been enhanced to include consumption details in a backflush component message. A backflush component consumption message is a type of ship notice request that informs the buyer of the completion of finished goods from subcontracting components. Unlike real-time component consumption reporting, backflush reporting is done only once, at the end of the production process. Component Consumption (Real- time) Message A real-time component consumption message informs the buyer of consumption of components at any phase of the production cycle. Component Inventory Message A component inventory message has been added to inform suppliers about quantities of components available for manufacturing. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 137 -- 7 of 10 -- Figure 3: Contract Manufacturing Workflow Example  Note For general information about integrating your ERP system with SAP Business Network, see Buyer System Integration with SAP Business Network [page 11]. For information about configuring SAP Business Network with SAP ERP to enable contract management features, see the Best Practice Guide on the Subcontracting page of the SAP Best Practices site. On the home page, under Materials Management, click the Subcontracting button, and then click the i icon. Best Practice guides give guidance on the configuration of contract management in SAP ECC. However, system administrators must refer to the ofocial SAP ECC Deployment Guides on help.sap.com. Restrictions If a subcontracting purchase order has been uploaded or downloaded via CSV, a supplier will not see the component level on the downloaded subcontracting purchase order. 138 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 8 of 10 -- Consignment Collaboration Suppliers and buyers can monitor materials on consignment and invoice consignment movements. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain provides ways for suppliers to view a list of materials on consignment, for suppliers to create invoices for consignment movements, and for buyers to create self-billing invoices for consignment movements. The supplier sends consignments to the buyer, but retains ownership of the consignments until the buyer pays for the consignments the buyer consumes, through a pre-arranged purchase-order method. Consignments stocked in the buyer’s warehouses or production facilities are not paid for until they have been used. The transfer of ownership, and often of location, to the buyer at the time of consumption is called a consignment movement. Workflow The following describes the general workflow for consignment collaboration: 1. The buyer creates or changes a consignment purchase order, and sends it, via SAP Business Network, to a supplier. 2. The supplier finds a purchase order for a consignment item, clearly differentiated as such in the item category field. The supplier creates a consignment fill-up order, and sends a consignment purchase order confirmation, via SAP Business Network, to the buyer. 3. The supplier creates a ship notice for the consignment purchase order and sends it, via SAP Business Network, to the buyer, who receives notice of an inbound delivery. 4. The buyer reports the transfer of materials from consignment to the buyer's own stock, via SAP Business Network, to the supplier. 5. The supplier views consignment movements in SAP Business Network. 6. Either of the following: • The buyer executes a consignment settlement, and sends a settlement invoice, via SAP Business Network, to the supplier. • The supplier creates an invoice against one or more consignment movements, and sends the invoice, via SAP Business Network, to the buyer. Consignment Data A generated Consignment job for Upload/Download creates an Excel template that consolidates goods receipt and consignment movement data for a specified supplier or buyer. When a line item in a goods receipt and a consignment movement share the same consignment tracking ID, a generated Consignment template can retrieve the related purchase order, line item, and ship notice numbers. If no tracking ID is provided, the job attempts to find line items with other matching data, such as purchase order number and ship notice number. A Consignment template also shows stock-on-hand and consignment stock values. These values are derived from cXML ProductActivityMessage documents with a matching buyer part number, supplier part number, location, and process type, and which contain ConsignmentInventory or ConsignmentMovement elements with the processType attribute set to Consignment. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 139 -- 9 of 10 -- To execute a consignment settlement, a buyer may send a consignment movement cXML file that does not contain any batch information to their supplier. SAP Business Network checks if the consignment movement cXML file contains batch information. If it does not, SAP Business Network retains the existing batch information. Related Information Consignment Template for Upload/Download [page 249] Manufacturing Planning Visibility When suppliers upload CSV files for manufacturing visibility types, their buyers can use the data to plan and supply transaction elements to contract manufacturers. Typically, in contract manufacturing, Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) maintain only critical bill of materials (BOMs) while their contract manufacturers maintain exhaustive lists of components. The manufacturing planning visibility feature allows suppliers to upload CSV files for the sub-types Inventory, Supplier Data, and All. You can also search for these documents by type. Manufacturing planning visibility gives the following capabilities to contract manufacturers and their OEMs: • The supplier can send commitments against buyer-generated forecast quantities. • The supplier can send inventory snapshots to the OEMs. Manufacturing visibility Settings To configure the Manufacturing visibility settings, buyers must be enabled for one of the following: • The inventory collaboration component. • The forecast collaboration component. • SAP Business Network Planning Collaboration, which does not also require SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. Buyers can set the two settings in the Manufacturing visibility section of the Planning Settings Assign suppliers page: 1. Planning horizon, in number of days – This setting controls the number of days in the future that suppliers can send Manufacturing Planning Visibility planning records. The default value is 180 days. 2. Must match Customer part ID and Customer location with existing records – When this setting is set to Yes, all incoming Manufacturing Planning Visibility planning items are validated to make sure they match at least one existing planning item with an active status sent by the buyer for a planning process. The validation check occurs when suppliers do one of the following: • Upload Manufacturing Planning Visibility planning items from the ... Upload/Download Uploads tab. • Send cXML product replenishment messages for Manufacturing Planning Visibility planning items. 140 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SupplyChainCollaboratio.content: Workflow The following describes the general workflow for manufacturing planning visibility upload: 1. The supplier downloads the CSV file upload template customized for one of the manufacturing planning visibility types. 2. The supplier enters data into a CSV file based on the template selected. 3. After the supplier uploads the manufacturing-planning CSV file, SAP Business Network generates a corresponding cXML file and triggers a transaction based on the cXML file. 4. The buyer receives the manufacturing planning visibility data in the Manufacturing Planning view. The buyer can use the information provided by a manufacturing planning visibility upload to drive the planning and supply of transaction elements to contract manufacturers. cXML Elements for Manufacturing Planning Visibility The following elements support manufacturing planning visibility: • ProductReplenishmentMessage • ProductReplenishmentHeader • ProductReplenishmentDetails • ReplenishmentTimeSeries • TimeSeriesDetails • TimeSeriesQuantity • UpsideQuantity For more information, see the cXML Reference Guide . Forecast Collaboration Suppliers can provide buyers their commitments to deliver quantities of goods to supply upcoming demands forecast by buyers. With forecast collaboration, a supplier could build commonly-used subassemblies based on an anticipated demand from a buyer. For another example, a supplier could schedule deliveries of parts in advance of an anticipated increase in demand, minimizing last-minute rush shipments and stock run-outs. Additionally, forecast collaboration enables suppliers to make commitments to deliver quantities of goods specified in buyer forecast demands. Alternatively, suppliers can send commits to buyers about forecast quantities and can request revisions. The forecast collaboration feature provides the following to suppliers: • A simple table view of buyer forecast demand • The ability to commit to forecast quantities based on supplier capacity and inventory • Daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and yearly time-bucket views of forecast demand • Integration with other ERP and planning systems, both for buyers and for suppliers SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 141 -- 1 of 10 -- cXML Elements for Forecast Collaboration The following elements support forecast collaboration: • ProductReplenishmentMessage • ProductReplenishmentHeader • ProductReplenishmentDetails • ReplenishmentTimeSeries • ForecastConfirmation • TimeSeriesDetails • TimeSeriesQuantity • UpsideQuantity For more information, see the cXML Reference Guide . Restrictions for Suppliers • SAP Business Network displays scheduling agreement releases with schedule line forecasts based on the Product Activity field. If SAP Business Network has a scheduling agreement release stored as orders, SAP Business Network does not display the scheduling agreement release with schedule line forecasts. • Order confirmations are not considered in ordered quantity calculations. Restrictions for Buyers • The SAP Business Network buyer user interface does not show the forecast details sent to the supplier. • The size limit for forecast collaboration cXML messages is 10 MB. Workflow The following describes the general workflow for forecast collaboration: 1. The buyer extracts net demand data after material requirements planning or forecast planning, and transmits this data to SAP Business Network via cXML. 2. The supplier logs on to SAP Business Network to view forecast demand data, enter commits, or download the forecast demand data to an Excel file. 3. If the supplier downloads the Excel file, the supplier can edit the commits in it to show supply commitments or proposed changes—including upside commitments—and email it to the buyer. 4. The buyer receives a cXML file from the supplier. 142 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 2 of 10 -- Related Information Customizing Planning, Forecast, and Manufacturing Visibility Business Rules for Specific Suppliers [page 95] Supplier-Managed Inventory Suppliers can manage the goods they own that are stored in customer warehouses for future ownership. With the supplier-managed inventory feature, suppliers can use SAP Business Network for Supply Chain to manage goods that are in their customers' warehouses, a process referred to as supplier managed inventory (SMI) or vendor managed inventory (VMI). If the supplier owns the stock until the customer consumes it, the stock is called consigned stock. If the customer takes ownership of the stock on receipt, the stock is called non-consigned stock. Buyers can configure the planning view based on their business requirements. Also, suppliers can view their inventory data all together, and can manage their commitments to forecast demand through a flexible user interface. Both buyers and suppliers can benefit from supplier-managed inventory, with benefits including: • Improved inventory turns • Improved service • Increased sales Workflow for Supplier-Managed Inventory The end-to-end workflow for supplier-managed inventory starts with a buyer designating materials for a supplier to manage, and ends with the supplier creating ship notices for managed materials. Typically, the supplier-managed inventory workflow follows these steps: 1. The buyer designates the materials for the supplier-managed inventory program and shares the gross-demand information with the supplier. 2. The supplier-managed inventory conditions are translated and the buyer creates a blanket order or a scheduling agreement. 3. The buyer shares the inventory information, including various stock levels, and minimum and maximum stock information. 4. The supplier determines the need for replenishment of stock at the buyer location, based on the gross demand, inventory on hand, and minimum and maximum stock levels. The supplier communicates the following to the buyer: • Estimated shipment plans • Updated shipment plans • Shipment data 5. The supplier-planned shipments create schedule lines in the buyer system, which are communicated back to the supplier for creating ship notices. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 143 -- 3 of 10 -- The following diagram describes the typical workflow for supplier-managed inventory (SMI): Invoicing Features This section describes SAP Business Network for Supply Chain features for invoicing. Invoice Workflow for Self-Billing and Scheduling Agreement Releases Buyers can transmit self-billing invoices for direct-material orders. Direct-material suppliers and buyers can deploy self-billing invoices when they have agreed to not require the supplier to manually create invoices for order transactions, but instead to use an automated routine called Evaluated Receipt Settlement (ERS). SAP Business Network can automatically transmit self-billing invoices based on data in purchase orders, scheduling agreements, and goods receipts. The buyer creates a self-billing invoice in an external business system and sends it to a supplier over SAP Business Network. ERS determines the invoice amount for ordering transactions from the prices entered in the order, the terms of payment, the tax information, and the delivery quantity entered in the goods receipt. Buyers and suppliers can employ self-billing invoices for scheduling agreements as well as for purchase orders. 144 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 4 of 10 -- Workflow The following describes the general workflow for self-billing invoicing: 1. A buyer creates a self-billing invoice for a purchase order or scheduling agreement release in an ERP system. 2. The buyer ERP system publishes the self-billing invoice to a supplier through SAP Business Network. 3. The supplier receives the self-billing invoice either through the SAP Business Network user interface, or through the supplier's ERP system. 4. The buyer's ERP system processes the self-billing invoice, generates payments, and publishes payment status updates to the supplier via SAP Business Network. 5. The supplier receives payment status updates through the SAP Business Network user interface, or through the supplier's ERP system. Quality Features This section describes SAP Business Network for Supply Chain features for quality. Quality Inspection Collaboration for Buyers [page 145] Quality Notification Collaboration for Buyers [page 152] Planning and Forecast Collaboration Features [page 176] Quality Review Collaboration for Buyers [page 184] Quality Inspection Collaboration for Buyers Buyers and suppliers can exchange information though SAP Business Network to facilitate quality inspections. During the delivery of components, buyers and suppliers can collaborate on quality inspection of finished goods or subcontracting components to achieve improved overall quality metrics. Quality inspection collaboration supports the following functionality: • Buyers can request the supplier to perform a quality inspection based on a specified inspection lot. • Suppliers can perform the inspection and send inspection results and an attached certificate of analysis to the buyer. • Buyers can review the inspection results and lock them, preventing the supplier from making further changes. • Buyers can respond to the inspection results by sending the usage decision for the inspection lot to suppliers. • Buyers and suppliers can receive email notifications for quality inspection documents. • Supplier managers can assign roles to users to view or edit inspection results. Buyers create quality inspection documents outside SAP Business Network and submit them through cXML. However, they can view quality inspections on the Quality Inspection tab. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 145 -- 5 of 10 -- Electronic Signatures for Quality Inspections Buyer administrators can require that their suppliers electronically sign quality inspection results before submitting them. Refer to Electronic Signatures for Quality Inspections [page 150]. Workflow for Quality Inspection [page 146] Viewing Quality Inspections [page 149] Electronic Signatures for Quality Inspections [page 150] Workflow for Quality Inspection The end-to-end workflow for quality inspection starts with a buyer sending an order to a supplier, and ends with the buyer sending a usage decision to the supplier for the inspection lot quantities. Buyers can initiate inspections for different types of goods movements. Inspection lots can be created automatically after a ship notice is sent for material goods or when a product is processed at goods receipt. They can also be created manually before the goods are shipped or received. The following is an example of a quality inspection done after a ship notice: 1. The buyer sends an order to the supplier. 2. Optionally, the supplier sends an order confirmation to the buyer. 3. The supplier sends a ship notice. 4. The buyer creates an inspection lot and sends an inspection request to the supplier, and optionally sends a copy to a third-party supplier. 5. The supplier sends inspection results either online or through cXML to the buyer. 6. The buyer updates the inspection request, locking it to prevent the supplier from making further changes. 7. The buyer sends a usage decision to the supplier, indicating what to do with the inspection lot quantities. 146 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 6 of 10 -- Figure 4: Quality Inspection After Ship Notice The following is an example of a quality inspection done before goods are shipped or received: 1. The buyer sends an order to the supplier. 2. Optionally, the supplier sends an order confirmation to the buyer. 3. The buyer creates an inspection lot and sends an inspection request to the supplier. 4. The supplier sends inspection results either online or through cXML to the buyer. 5. The buyer updates the inspection request, locking it to prevent the supplier from making further changes. 6. The buyer sends a usage decision to the supplier, indicating what to do with the inspection lot quantities. 7. The supplier sends a ship notice. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 147 -- 7 of 10 -- Figure 5: Quality Inspection Before Ship Notice (Manual) Copy Suppliers Buyers can provide read-only copies of quality inspections to third parties, also referred to as copy suppliers. Buyers trigger copies by including the <Node type=”copy”> element when sending cXML inspection requests. Here is an example: <Path> <Node type="copy"> <Credential domain="SAPBusinessNetworkUserId"> <Identity>test-testPT1@sap.com</Identity> </Credential> </Node> </Path> Buyers may want to add a copy supplier if, for example, they have a contract manufacturer responsible for a finished good. Copying this supplier will provide them with visibility about what is happening during an inspection process with the component(s) needed to make the finished good. Buyers view information about copy suppliers from the Quality Inspection page. If a quality inspection has one or more copy suppliers, the Multi Tier column is checked and the Copies column contains a link. When you click this link, a popup with information about the copies opens. Suppliers view information about copy suppliers from the Multi-Tier Quality Inspection tab on the Inbox Extended Collaboration page. 148 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 8 of 10 -- Additional Steps for Electronic Signatures If the Activate DocuSign for quality inspection documents rule is set, these steps are added to the workflow after the buyer sends an inspection request to the supplier. 1. The supplier fills in the inspection results, selects signers, and sends the results to be electronically signed. SAP Business Network assembles a document packet, including the signer information and the PDF file with the results, and sends it to DocuSign. 2. DocuSign creates the signature envelope and emails all the selected signers to request they electronically sign the quality inspection document. 3. The signers review and sign the inspection results in DocuSign. 4. If the quality inspection results are successfully signed, SAP Business Network sends the PDF file with the results, including the signatures, to the Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system.  Note Only inspection results sent through the SAP Business Network user interface, not inspection results sent through cXML, can be electronically signed. Viewing Quality Inspections Buyers can view in SAP Business Network the quality inspections they sent to suppliers. Prerequisites The buyer system is enabled for the quality collaboration component. Context Quality inspection documents are created in an external system such as an ERP. Procedure 1. Choose Quality Inspection . 2. Click a customer inspection number to open it. 3. View the Details or History tabs. 4. To export the quality inspection, click Export cXML and choose one of the following options. • Request cXML—Quality inspection request. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 149 -- 9 of 10 -- • Result cXML—Quality inspection results. Available only if the supplier has submitted inspection test results. • Decision cXML—Quality inspection usage decision. Available only if you have submitted a usage decision for the inspection lot. Electronic Signatures for Quality Inspections Buyer administrators can require that their suppliers electronically sign quality inspection results before submitting them using DocuSign. Electronic signatures help guarantee the truthfulness of information displayed in documents and are often required by regulatory entities. Prerequisites • The buyer administrator is enabled for the quality collaboration component. • The buyer administrator has a license from DocuSign. Additionally, if the buyer administrator wants their suppliers to comply with FDA 21 CFR Part 11 regulations, the buyer administrator must subscribe to the DocuSign Part 11 module. For more information about this module, refer to How the DocuSign Part 11 Module Fits with 21 CFR Part 11 . • The buyer administrator has created a generic user in DocuSign for SAP Business Network to use when it sends requests to DocuSign to generate electronic envelopes. • The buyer administrator has successfully submitted the necessary DocuSign fields on the Administration Configuration DocuSign Integration Setup page. • The buyer administrator has set the Activate DocuSign for quality inspection documents rule. • All suppliers who are potential signers have the Quality Inspection Signature permission. To enable electronic signature of quality inspections, buyer administrators must do the following: 1. Create a generic user in DocuSign for SAP Business Network to use when it sends requests to DocuSign to generate electronic envelopes. 2. Complete the necessary one-time setup tasks from the Administration Configuration DocuSign Integration Setup page. Refer to Configuring DocuSign for Electronic Signatures [page 151]. 3. Set the Activate DocuSign for quality inspection documents rule. The PDF file containing the quality inspection results is automatically generated by SAP Business Network. This PDF file is what is electronically signed in DocuSign.  Note If needed, you can customize the quality inspection results layout. Refer to Custom PDF Layouts for Quality Inspections. 150 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SupplyChainCollaboratio.title: SupplyChainCollaborationConfiguration_Part16
file://SBN/split/SupplyChainCollaboratio.content: Configuring DocuSign for Electronic Signatures Buyer administrators must set up three fields on the DocuSign Integration Setup page before using DocuSign for electronic signatures. Prerequisites You have a license from DocuSign. Additionally, if you want your suppliers to comply with FDA 21 CFR Part 11 regulations, you must subscribe to the DocuSign Part 11 module. For more information about this module, refer to How the DocuSign Part 11 Module Fits with 21 CFR Part 11 . Procedure 1. Sign in to your DocuSign account. 2. Choose Settings from the DocuSign account top menu. 3. Go to Admin > INTEGRATIONS. 4. Find your DocuSign API Account ID. a. Click Apps and Keys. b. Locate your API Account ID in the My Account Information section. c. Copy your API Account ID to a file. 5. Set up a secret key.  Note The following instructions are from DocuSign's How to set up HMAC (Hash-based Message Authentication Code) security with your app page. a. Click Connect. b. Choose Connect Keys. c. Choose + ADD SECRET KEY. The screen shows the added secret key. d. Copy the secret key to a file. 6. Set up a generic user to handle creating electronic envelopes in DocuSign. a. Click Users. b. Click ADD USER. c. Create a user. Refer to the User Management section of the DocuSign eSignature Admin Guide for instructions.  Note You must assign the user the DS Sender permission to allow the user to create electronic envelopes in DocuSign. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 151 -- 1 of 10 -- d. From the Users page, click the row for the newly-created generic user to display the user profile. e. Copy the User ID to a file. 7. In the SAP Business Network user interface, go to Administration Configuration and choose DocuSign Integration Setup. 8. Copy your API Account ID from the file where you saved it, paste that ID in the API Account ID field, and click Submit. 9. Copy your secret key from the file where you saved it, paste that key in the Secret key field, and click Submit. 10. Copy your User ID from the file where you saved it, paste that ID in the User ID field, and click Submit. DocuSign opens a popup window for you to grant consent for the generic user. 11. Grant consent for the generic user in DocuSign. a. Sign in to DocuSign with the generic user. b. Click ACCEPT to permit that user to create and send electronic envelopes in DocuSign. c. Exit DocuSign. 12. In the SAP Business Network user interface, click Close. The Administration Configuration page opens. Quality Notification Collaboration for Buyers Viewing Quality Notifications [page 153] Customized Quality Notifications [page 153] 152 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 2 of 10 -- Viewing Quality Notifications Buyers can view quality notifications submitted by their ERP system or by suppliers. Prerequisites The buyer system is enabled for the quality collaboration component. Procedure 1. Choose Quality Notification . The Quality Notifications page opens. 2. To search for a quality notification, expand the Search filters, enter values in the search fields, and then click Search.  Note When you choose the Exact match radio button below the Customer deviation no. or the Supplier deviation no. filter, only that filter and the Supplier filter display. 3. Click a quality notification number to open it.  Note You cannot edit the quality notification. It is read-only. Customized Quality Notifications Buyers can apply customizations to quality notification documents. A customization project for quality notifications contains one or more customizations. These customizations help buyers obtain better requirements compliance and reduce unnecessary communications with their suppliers. The following are examples of customizations that buyers can add to a customization project: • Set a default value for a field. • Make a field required. • Provide a tooltip message for a field. Buyers can define customizations for their suppliers to use, both when creating new and editing existing quality notifications. For example, buyers can make a field required when suppliers create a quality notification, but make the field read only after that. Buyers specify which mode (Create mode or Edit mode) to apply a customization to when defining rules for their customization project. For details, see Adding Field Rules to a Customization Project [page 161]. By default, customizations apply to both modes when buyers do not add rules to define the mode. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 153 -- 3 of 10 -- Buyers edit and test their customization project until they have set up all of the customizations correctly. When they are done editing and testing, they publish their customization project and assign it to selected suppliers. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Restrictions Customizations are available only for quality notifications, not for quality inspections or quality reviews. Customization Project Workflow The tasks involved in the customization process are divided into two parts, editing tasks and publishing tasks. 1. The editing tasks are done by the Editor from the buyer test account. The Editor creates or updates customization projects and tests them. For details, see Creating a Customization Project for Quality Notifications [page 156]. 2. The publishing tasks are done by the Publisher from the buyer production account. The Publisher publishes customization projects. For details, see Publishing a Customization Project for Quality Notifications [page 172]. For more information about creating customization projects, see Workflow for Creating and Publishing a Customization Project for Quality Notifications [page 155]. Working with Customization Projects You can create a new version of a customization project and make changes to it. For details, see Creating New Versions of Customization Projects [page 173]. You can delete customization projects that have not been published yet. For details, see Deleting Unpublished Customization Projects [page 175]. Available Customizations You can make the following customizations to a quality notification document: • Customize fields – For details, see Adding Field Customizations to a Customization Project [page 159]. • Add rules – For details, see Adding Field Rules to a Customization Project [page 161]. 154 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 4 of 10 -- • Add new fields – For details, see Adding Fields to a Customization Project [page 165]. • Customize sections – For details, see Customizing Quality Notification Sections [page 167]. • Hide tabs – For details, see Hiding Tabs in a Customization Project [page 170]. • Hide sections – For details, see Hiding Sections in a Customization Project [page 171]. Workflow for Creating and Publishing a Customization Project for Quality Notifications [page 155] Creating a Customization Project for Quality Notifications [page 156] Publishing a Customization Project for Quality Notifications [page 172] Creating New Versions of Customization Projects [page 173] Deleting Unpublished Customization Projects [page 175] Workflow for Creating and Publishing a Customization Project for Quality Notifications The Editor creates the customization project from the buyer test account, and the Publisher publishes it from the buyer production account.  Restriction The Editor can only use a test account, not a production account, to develop and test customizations for quality notifications. 1. The Editor logs on to the buyer test account and creates a new or edits an existing customization project to apply to suppliers when they create quality notifications. 2. The Editor edits the customization project to add customizations to fields, rules to fields, and new fields. 3. The Editor pushes the customization project to the supplier test account. 4. The Editor logs on to the supplier test account and validates the customization project. 5. From the buyer test account, the Editor requests to publish the customization project to the production system. 6. The Publisher logs on to the supplier test account and validates the customization project.  Note When the Editor is also the Publisher, this step is skipped. 7. The Publisher logs on to the buyer production account and assigns suppliers to the customization project. 8. The Publisher publishes the customization project. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 155 -- 5 of 10 -- Creating a Customization Project for Quality Notifications Buyers can create, edit, and test customizations for quality notifications. Prerequisites • You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. • The supplier groups that you want to assign your customization project to already exist in your account. Procedure 1. Sign in to your buyer test account. 2. Click Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service .  Note Account Settings is the user icon on the top right of the page. The Customization – Self Service page opens. 3. Choose Create Project to create a new customization project. The Create Project page opens showing the first step, What project do you want to create? 4. Enter your information in the customization project fields. The following fields are required. Field Description Project name Enter a unique name. Project description Enter a description. 156 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 6 of 10 -- Field Description Document type Choose Quality notification.  Note By default, the Create option is selected. Customizations will be applied to the creation of the quality notification. Suppliers Choices are: • All (default) • None  Note If you choose None, you will not be able to check your customizations in the supplier test account since the customization project will not be assigned to any suppliers. • Selected supplier groups – When chosen, a dropdown arrow shows. Click the arrow to show the list of supplier groups. Customization area By default, the Create option is selected. Customizations will be applied to the creation of the quality notification. Customized languages English (en) is required and always chosen. To add other languages, click the add ( ) icon to choose the languages. Click Done when you finish selecting languages.  Note When you add new fields to your project, to better support your customers, you should also add translations for the field labels. Field label translations are provided for stand- ard fields, but not for added fields. The translations you add will be available for all future customization projects. If the translations for one or more standard field labels need to be enhanced, you can add translations for them too. Field label translations also affect the filters for quality notifications and the table where the quality notifications are listed. 5. Choose Next or Save. If you choose Next, continue with Step 7. If you choose Save, the Customization – Self Service page opens in the Projects tab, showing your project in the list of customization projects. 6. In the row for your customization project, choose the more ( ) icon in the Actions column, then from the dropdown choose Edit customization. The Create quality notification page for your customization project opens. Create quality notification refers to the quality notification creation page that suppliers use when creating quality notifications. You are creating customizations for this page for your suppliers. 7. Make one or more of the following customizations. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 157 -- 7 of 10 -- • Add customizations for fields. Refer to Adding Field Customizations to a Customization Project [page 159]. • Add rules for fields. Refer to Adding Field Rules to a Customization Project [page 161]. • Add new fields. Refer to Adding Fields to a Customization Project [page 165]. On the quality notification design page, customized fields display a blue dot to the right of the field label. Additionally, the following customization changes are visible for customized fields: • Field label • Default value • Tooltip message  Note The quality notification design page does not provide a real-time view of the customized report, which means some customizations are not visible. To view all customizations, push your customization project to test and sign in to the supplier test account to create a document. 8. When you finish making your customizations, click the back arrow ( ). The Customization – Self Service page displays. 9. In the row for your customization project, choose the more ( ) icon in the Actions column, then from the dropdown choose Push to supplier test account. The Push project to supplier test account popup displays. 10. Choose Push. The customization project is pushed to the supplier test account. The project Status changes to Pushed to Test. 11. Optional: Assign the project to suppliers for testing. This step is only needed when no suppliers have been assigned to the project. a. In the row for your customization project, choose the more ( ) icon in the Actions column, then from the dropdown choose Edit project details. b. Select the suppliers. c. Click Save. The Suppliers popup displays asking if you want to save the updates you made. d. Click OK. 12. Check your customizations. a. Sign in to a supplier test account you have assigned the customization project to. b. Go to Quality Notification . c. Create a quality notification. d. Review the fields you customized to confirm they are set up correctly. 13. Return to your buyer test account and click Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service . The Customization – Self Service page opens. 14. Click the more ( ) icon in the Actions column for your customization project and select Request to publish. The Request to publish to production popup opens. 158 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 8 of 10 -- 15. Click OK. Your customization project is sent to production for the Publisher to review and publish. The project Status changes to Requested to Publish. Adding Field Customizations to a Customization Project [page 159] Adding Field Rules to a Customization Project [page 161] Adding Fields to a Customization Project [page 165] Customizing Quality Notification Sections [page 167] Hiding Tabs in a Customization Project [page 170] Hiding Sections in a Customization Project [page 171] Adding Field Customizations to a Customization Project Buyers can add customizations for fields in a customization project. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Procedure 1. From the customization project's Create quality notification page, hover over the dropdown ( ) icon of a field you want to customize, then click the edit ( ) icon that appears. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 159 -- 9 of 10 -- The Edit field panel opens with the Properties tab displayed. 2. Make your customizations. Examples of customizations you can make include: • Set a default value for a field – you may want to set default values for some fields. • Make a field required – some fields are already set as required. A required field displays with an asterisk. • Hide a field – required fields display with an asterisk and cannot be hidden. • Add a field – you can add custom fields. • Rename a field label – the field label helps the user determine the purpose of the field. • Set a minimum and maximum length for a field – you can enter a minimum length, a maximum length, or both. • Provide a tooltip message for a field – you can provide a tooltip message in all the languages selected for your customization project. 3. Click Save. Results On the quality notification design page, customized fields display a blue dot to the right of the field label. Additionally, the following customization changes are visible for customized fields: • Field label • Default value • Tooltip message  Note The quality notification design page does not provide a real-time view of the customized report, which means some customizations are not visible. To view all customizations, push your customization project to test and sign in to the supplier test account to create a document. 160 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 10 of 10 --
