file://SBN/split/SupplyChainCollaboratio.content: Adding Field Rules to a Customization Project Buyers can add rules to a customization project for quality notifications. You can apply these rules to creating a quality notification, editing a quality notification, or both. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Context You add rules to enforce certain characteristics for customizations of quality notifications. For example, if you create a rule to hide a field when the value of the Quality notification type is Q7, the field will not be included in the quality notification when the Quality notification type has this value. Procedure 1. From the customization project's Create quality notification page, hover over the dropdown ( ) icon of a field you want to customize, then click the edit ( ) icon that appears. The Edit field panel opens with the Properties tab displayed. 2. Click the Rules tab, then click the add ( ) icon to add a new rule. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 161 -- 1 of 10 -- 3. Choose a property: Hide, Read only, or Required.  Note By default, the chosen property applies both when creating and when editing quality notifications. 4. Enter a condition for the rule by selecting values from each dropdown menu. 162 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 2 of 10 -- a. In the first setting for the condition, configure the type. Choose Field to add a field rule or System to add a system rule. b. In the second setting for the condition, configure the field. Choose the appropriate value for your choice in the first setting: • Field rule – Choose Quality notification type. • System rule – Choose Document mode. c. In the third setting for the condition, choose contains. d. In the fourth setting for the condition, configure the value. Perform the following instructions for the type of rule you are adding. • Field rule – Choose one or more values for the Quality notification type field.  Remember If you add a rule for the Quality notification type field with a value that is a custom quality notification code, you need to make sure that the custom quality notification code is uploaded to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 163 -- 3 of 10 -- the buyer test account and actual account. Refer to Uploading Quality Notification Codes [page 89]. • System rule – Choose one or both document modes: • Create mode – Define a rule for creating quality notifications. • Edit mode – Define a rule for editing quality notifications.  Note Suppliers cannot edit any of the following fields after the quality notification is created: Customer Quality notification type Supplier deviation no. Customer location Customer part no. Customer routing identifier – This field only appears if the buyer has a multiple-ERP environment. Supplier part no. Purchase order no. Purchase order line item no. Ship notice no. Ship notice line item no. Subcontracting component 5. Optional: If you want to enter a second condition for the rule, click the add ( ) icon and choose the And if or Or if conditional operator. Follow the procedure described in the previous step to define the second condition. 6. Click Save. 164 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 4 of 10 -- The new rule displays in the Edit field window. 7. Click Save to save the new rule and exit the Edit field window. Adding Fields to a Customization Project Buyers can add fields to a customization project. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Procedure 1. From the customization project's Create quality notification page, click the edit ( ) icon in the section where you want to add a field. A window titled with the section name opens. 2. Click the add ( ) icon to the right of the Fields label to add a new field. The Create field popup opens. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 165 -- 5 of 10 -- 3. Enter the information about the field. Existing fields are referred to as intrinsics, meaning they are intrinsic to the document. New fields are referred to as extrinsics. Extrinsic fields add additional information to the document. The new field has the same properties and rules as existing fields. If a rule is needed for the field, configure it first. Refer to Adding Field Rules to a Customization Project [page 161]. The field information includes: • New field name – the extrinsic name that is displayed in the cXML. In the cXML, the new field is added as the name element in an Extrinsic tag. Each new field is unique per cXML element (header, task element, and so on), and spaces are not allowed in field names. For example, if the New field name is RevisionLevel, and the revision level is 11, the corresponding cXML is: <Extrinsic name="RevisionLevel">11</Extrinsic>. • Label – the label that is displayed for the field. • Hide • Read only • Required • Tooltip message • Default value • Character length 166 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 6 of 10 -- The legal disclaimer at the bottom of the window reminds you that new fields cannot include sensitive personal data (for example, Social Security numbers) or personal data (for example, phone numbers) since they are not set up with appropriate data protection measures. 4. When you are done entering the field information, click Save.  Note The added field is available for any future customization projects you create. To use the field in another customization project, follow the steps to add a field, and when prompted for the New field name, enter the field's extrinsic name. The translations for the field are also available when you use the field in another customization project. Results The new field displays on the quality notification design page at the end of the section where it was added. The blue dot to the right of the field label indicates it is a customized field. When you generate a quality notification report, new fields are added as columns to the end of the report. The column name for each new field is its corresponding extrinsic name. Customizing Quality Notification Sections Buyers can customize certain sections in a quality notification. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Context You can customize the following sections in a quality notification: • Required tasks • Activity log • Defects • Defects-Causes • Defects-Required tasks • Defects-Activity log SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 167 -- 7 of 10 -- Procedure 1. From the customization project's Create quality notification page, click the edit ( ) icon of the section you want to customize. 2. Click the Rules tab. 3. Choose a property. You can only choose one property: • Hide – The section will be hidden. • Read only – The section will be read only. For example, if you select this property when customizing the Activity log section, your suppliers will be unable to either create new Activity log sections or remove existing Activity log sections when editing quality notifications. • Limit creation – When selected, the Cannot be created more than field displays. Enter a number from 1 to 99 to specify the maximum number of sections of this type.  Note The limit you enter is the total number of sections. For example, if you specify to create a maximum of 10 Required tasks sections and the supplier already entered 7 of these sections, they can only enter a maximum of 3 more. • Cannot be removed while editing – Your suppliers will be restricted from removing this type of section when they edit quality notifications. The customization shown in the screenshot applies to suppliers when they edit quality notifications with a Quality notification type of Q6. A maximum of 10 Activity log sections can be created. 168 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 8 of 10 -- SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 169 -- 9 of 10 -- 4. Enter a condition for the rule by selecting values from each dropdown menu. For information about entering conditions for a rule, see Step 4 and Step 5 in Adding Field Rules to a Customization Project [page 161]. 5. Click Save. The new rule displays in the Edit field window. 6. Click Save to save the new rule and exit the Edit field window. Hiding Tabs in a Customization Project You can customize a quality notification document to hide tabs. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Procedure 1. From the customization project's Create quality notification page, click the more ( ) icon in the upper right corner of the page, and then select the Page editor link that displays. A side panel opens, showing checkboxes for the four tabs of a quality notification document. 2. To hide a tab, uncheck its checkbox.  Restriction Only the Defects and Partner info tabs can be hidden. Tabs that cannot be hidden show a grayed-out checkbox. 3. Click Save. 170 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SupplyChainCollaboratio.title: SupplyChainCollaborationConfiguration_Part18
file://SBN/split/SupplyChainCollaboratio.content: Hiding Sections in a Customization Project You can customize a quality notification document to hide sections. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission.  Restriction • Only sections that do not contain required fields can be hidden. For example, the Activity log and Required tasks sections do not have any required fields, so these sections can be hidden. • The Customer and part section can be hidden only when transaction rule Allow suppliers to send quality notifications for indirect orders without part numbers is enabled. When this transaction rule is not enabled, the Customer location and Customer part no. fields in this section are required fields, so the section cannot be hidden. Procedure 1. From the customization project's Create quality notification page, click the edit ( ) icon of the section you want to hide. 2. Check Hide under the Properties tab. 3. Click Save. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 171 -- 1 of 10 -- Publishing a Customization Project for Quality Notifications After the Editor requests publication of a customization project, the Publisher can test and publish it. Prerequisites • You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Publisher permission. • The supplier groups that you want to assign your customization project to already exist in your account. Procedure 1. Validate the customization project.  Note If you are both the Editor and the Publisher, you can skip this step since you already validated the project. a. Sign in to your supplier test account. b. Go to Quality Notification . c. Create a quality notification. d. Review the customized fields to confirm they are set up correctly. 2. Sign in to your buyer production account. 3. Click Administration Customization – Self-Service . The Customization – Self Service page opens. 4. Optional: Assign suppliers to the customization project.  Note You can assign suppliers to the customization project before or after publishing it. a. From the Customization – Self Service page, click the more ( ) icon in the Actions column for your customization project, and select Edit project details. The Edit Project page opens. 172 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 2 of 10 -- b. Edit the Suppliers section to assign suppliers to the customization project. Select All, None, or Selected supplier group(s) and click Save. • All – customization project added to all suppliers. • None – customization project removed from all suppliers. • Selected supplier group(s) – customization project added to the suppliers in the supplier group(s) and removed from all other suppliers. The Suppliers popup opens asking you if you want to save the updates you made to the suppliers assigned to the customization project. Click OK to save the updates. 5. From the Customization – Self Service page, click the more ( ) icon in the Actions column for the customization project you want to publish, and select Publish. The Publish to production popup opens. The popup reminds you that your customization project will apply to your chosen suppliers in your production account. 6. Click OK to publish the customization project. Creating New Versions of Customization Projects Buyers can create a new version of an existing customization project and make changes to it. The existing customization project must have the Published status. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 173 -- 3 of 10 -- Procedure 1. Sign in to your test account. 2. Click Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service .  Note Account Settings is the user icon on the top right of the page. The Customization – Self Service page opens. 3. Click the more ( ) icon in the Actions column for the Published customization project you want to create a new version for, and choose Create new version from the Project section. The following actions occur when you create a new version: • A warning message displays stating that the new version will be generated and the currently published version will not be affected. • The new version's major number is incremented. For example, if a new version is created from published version 1.3, the new version's number is 2.00. • The new version initially has status In Progress.  Remember Follow the normal workflow for projects to move the new version from In Progress to Pushed to Test and then to Requested to Publish. Results Suppliers assigned to a customization project always use the latest published version of the project. When you request to publish a new version, a warning message displays to remind you that this will affect all suppliers assigned to the project. After a new version of a customization project is published, suppliers will see this version in the user interface. For example, consider a new version of a customization project for quality notifications. The default behavior for the Serial no. field in the quality notification is to display the field. Since the Serial no. field is not a mandatory field, it can be hidden. If the field is hidden in the latest published version of a customization project, suppliers will not see the field when editing an existing quality notification, even though they may have previously inserted a value in the field. However, the Serial no. field information is still visible when suppliers download the cXML for the quality notification. 174 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 4 of 10 -- Deleting Unpublished Customization Projects Buyers can delete customization projects that have the status Draft, In Progress, Pushed to Test, or Requested to Publish. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Context You can only delete a customization project when it is not yet published; that is, the project has the status Draft, In Progress, Pushed to Test, or Requested to Publish. You cannot delete a customization project that has the Published status. Procedure 1. Sign in to your test account. 2. Click Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service .  Note Account Settings is the user icon on the top right of the page. The Customization – Self Service page opens. 3. Click the more ( ) icon in the Actions column for the customization project you want to delete, and select Delete project from the Project section. A warning message displays to inform you that the version of the customization project will be permanently deleted. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 175 -- 5 of 10 -- Results When you delete a customization project, only the latest version of the project is deleted. The table on the Customization – Self Service page has one row for each customization project, which shows information about the latest version of the project. • When you delete a customization project that was never published, the row is removed from the table. • When you delete a customization project that was previously published, the row for that project now shows information about the previously published version. For example, if you create version 2.0 and then delete it, and the previously published version is 1.3, the row for the project shows information about version 1.3. Planning and Forecast Collaboration Features This section describes SAP Business Network for Supply Chain features for planning and forecast collaboration. Component Planning Collaboration [page 176] Component Planning Collaboration Component planning collaboration lets buyers and suppliers view the forecast planning data for a finished good and its components together. Forecast planning items are created or updated when buyers send product activity messages and when suppliers send product replenishment messages. When component planning collaboration is enabled, in addition to forecast planning items, component planning collaboration items are also created or updated. For a component planning collaboration item to be created or updated, the item must be included in a Bill of Materials (BOM) stored in SAP Business Network. Each finished good has a component planning collaboration record. These records are created from Bill of Materials (BOM) records extracted from SAP Business Network. A BOM contains the list of components needed to manufacture a finished good. For more information about how BOM data is used for component planning collaboration, see Component Planning Collaboration Use of BOM Data [page 181]. To enable component planning collaboration, the buyer administrator edits the settings to toggle Enable component planning collaboration on. When this setting is set, if a planning item matches a finished good or a component stored in a BOM in SAP Business Network, its corresponding component planning collaboration item is created or updated. Component planning collaboration items are only created or updated when there is a match. Component planning collaboration uses the Component planning collaboration view. This view has two sections, Finished good section and Component section. Each section has its own key figures. For more information about the key figures in the Component planning collaboration view, see Key Figures Reference for the Component Planning Collaboration View [page 37]. Buyer administrators can also add custom key figures to both sections. Component planning collaboration data displays on the component planning collaboration list and details pages. • For more information about the component planning collaboration list page, see Component Planning Collaboration List Page [page 177]. 176 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 6 of 10 -- • For more information about the component planning collaboration details page, see Component Planning Collaboration Details Page [page 178]. Prerequisites • You must have both the Supply chain collaboration and Planning collaboration entitlements enabled. • The buyer administrator has set the Enable component planning collaboration setting on the Planning Settings Assign suppliers page. • The buyer administrator has imported the Bill of Materials (BOM) for the finished goods from the SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to SAP Business Network. Refer to Importing Bill of Materials from SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to SAP Business Network. • To view the Component planning collaboration tile in the Workbench tab, you must have the Component planning collaboration permission. Restrictions • The Component planning collaboration view does not support customer-defined attributes. • Component planning collaboration does not support Planning Collaboration authorization profiles. Component Planning Collaboration List Page [page 177] Component Planning Collaboration Details Page [page 178] Component Planning Collaboration Use of BOM Data [page 181] Component Planning Collaboration List Page On the component planning collaboration list page, you can view a table of component planning records for finished goods. To view the component planning collaboration list page, click Workbench, then click the Component planning collaboration tile.  Note If the Component planning collaboration tile does not display, follow the instructions on Customizing Tiles on Your Workbench [page 209] to add it. You must have the inventory collaboration entitlement enabled for the Component planning collaboration tile to display in the list of tiles you can add.  Restriction You cannot download information from the list view of the Component planning collaboration table to a spreadsheet file such as Excel. The page displays a table of component planning collaboration records. Each record represents a finished good. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 177 -- 7 of 10 -- The Component count column lists the number of components for each finished good and includes the number of active components in parenthesis. You can use the following filters to filter the finished goods: • Customer (supplier view) or Supplier (buyer view) • Customer location • Supplier part no. • Customer part no. • Components used – Select one or more components from the pulldown to list only finished goods that include one of the selected components. You can also sort the table by any column. Component Planning Collaboration Details Page On the component planning collaboration details page, you can view the planning items for a finished good and its active components. To open the component planning collaboration details page for a finished good, from the component planning collaboration list page, click the detail-view ( ) icon from the Actions column.  Restriction A maximum of 30 components are supported for each finished good. If a finished good has more than 30 components, only the first 30 components (in alphabetical order) display. General information about the finished good displays in the section at the top of the page. If the customer has uploaded a company logo, it displays in this section. Click the dropdown ( ) icon to expand this section. 178 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 8 of 10 -- The Bill of materials section displays the details of the BOM for the finished good. Click the feeder arrow ( ) icon to expand this section. When you open the details page, the Finished good section is expanded and the key figures for the finished good display with the standard planning time series table format. The time series tables on the component planning collaboration details page have the same functionality as they do on other planning pages. The only difference is that, when you click Send data, data is sent for both the finished good and its components. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 179 -- 9 of 10 -- The Components with shortage key figure shows the count of the components used by the finished good that have a shortage on each date in the time bucket. Values greater than or equal to 1 display in red.  Note The Components with shortage key figure row only appears in the planning table when you use Daily granularity. You can view component planning items using any available granularity (Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, or Yearly). However, you can only edit component planning items using Daily granularity since component planning is used for planning shorter timeframes. The header lines for the finished good and its components list the finished good or component name, description, and amount of stock on hand. Component header lines also include the following: • Vertical status bar – The status bar is green if the component does not have any shortages. The status bar is red if the component has one or both of the following shortages: • Current stock on hand – The component is out of stock. • Projected stock – The component will run out of stock on a future date based on the component's inflow and outflow. • Newspaper icon – Click the newspaper ( ) icon in the component header line to open the Where used? popup. This popup shows which finished goods use the component. • Message-warning icon – If a component has a shortage, a message-warning icon ( ) displays on its header line. Click the icon to view the shortage information.  Note The message-warning icon and shortage information display only for shortages that will occur in the next 30 days. Click the feeder-arrow ( ) icon next to a component to open its time series table to view and edit its key figures. 180 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SupplyChainCollaboratio.content: Standard calculated key figures that have values less than or equal to 0 display in red.  Caution Forecast commit locks are not supported for component planning. If you set Forecast commit lock horizon, in days to a value other than 0, you will not be able to commit from the component planning collaboration details page. To navigate back to the component planning collaboration list page, click the back-arrow ( ) icon at the top of the page. Component Planning Collaboration Use of BOM Data Component planning collaboration records are created using Bill of Materials (BOM) records in SAP Business Network. A BOM is a list of components needed to manufacture a finished good. Each component planning collaboration record contains one finished-good planning item and zero or more component planning items. Prerequisites The buyer administrator has imported the Bill of Materials (BOMs) for finished goods from the SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to SAP Business Network. Refer to Importing Bill of Materials from SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 181 -- 1 of 10 -- Creating and Updating Component Planning Collaboration Items Component planning collaboration items are created for finished goods and components when a product activity message is sent by the buyer and the following two conditions are true: • The buyer or supplier has the Enable component planning collaboration setting set. This setting is set by the buyer administrator on the Planning Settings Assign suppliers page. • The values of the Material ID and Plant ID in the message match the values of the Material ID and Plant ID in an active BOM at the header or component level. When both items are true, if the match of the Material ID and Plant ID values is at the header level, a finished- good planning item is created. If the match of the Material ID and Plant ID values is at the component level, a component planning item is created. Before creating a new planning item, SAP Business Network checks whether a planning item already exists. • If one exists, SAP Business Network updates it. • If one does not exist, SAP Business Network creates a new finished-good or component planning item.  Note • If the component data arrives before the finished-good data, the component planning item is created, but it is not displayed, until its finished-good planning item is created. A component planning item only displays on its finished good's component planning collaboration details page. • The component planning item is included in the component planning collaboration records of all finished goods that use it, and its data is always in sync in these records. • A planning item can be both a finished good and a component as illustrated in Example 3 below. Examples These are the BOM records used in the examples: BOM: 0001 Header Material: Classic promo pack Plant ID: 1000, 2000 Components: BBQ chips, Peanuts BOM: 0002 Header Material: Party pack Plant ID: 2000, 3000 Components: BBQ chips, Salt chips, Pistachios BOM: 0003 Header Material: Wholesale pallet Plant ID: 3000 Components: Party pack, Variety pack The product activity messages are shown for each of the following examples. The bullets after each message list the BOM where SAP Business Network finds the match and what action SAP Business Network takes as a result of the match. 182 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 2 of 10 -- Example 1: Simple component planning collaboration item generation These examples show simple generation of component planning collaboration items. • Message 1: Forecast for Material ID Classic promo pack/Plant ID 1000 1. Match Material ID/Plant ID with the BOM 1 header. 2. Create and populate the finished-good planning item. • Message 2: Forecast for Material ID Peanuts/Plant ID 1000 Match Material ID/Plant ID with the BOM 1 component. 1. Create and populate the component planning item for Peanuts under the finished-good planning item for Classic promo pack/1000. Example 2: Component used in multiple finished goods These examples show the generation of component planning collaboration items for a component used in more than one finished good. • Message 1: Forecast for Material ID Classic promo pack/Plant ID 2000 1. Match Material ID/Plant ID with the BOM 1 header. 2. Create and populate the finished-good planning item. • Message 2: Forecast for Material ID Party pack/Plant ID 2000 1. Match Material ID/Plant ID with the BOM 2 header. 2. Create and populate the finished-good planning item. • Message 3: Forecast for Material ID BBQ chips/Plant ID 2000 1. Match Material ID/Plant ID with both BOM 1 and BOM 2 components. 2. Create and populate component planning items for BBQ chips for finished-good planning items Classic promo pack/2000 and Party pack/2000. The data for the BBQ chips component planning item in the component planning collaboration records for these two finished goods is always in sync. Example 3: Material is both a component and a finished good These examples show the generation of component planning collaboration items when a material is both a component and a finished good. • Message 1: Forecast for Material ID Party pack/Plant ID 3000 1. Match Material ID/Plant ID with the BOM 2 header. 2. Create and populate the finished-good planning item. 3. Since the Material ID/Plant ID also matches the BOM 3 component, a component planning item for Party pack is also created. This planning item is not visible until the finished-good planning item for Wholesale pallet/3000 is created. • Message 2: Forecast for Material ID Pistachios/Plant ID 3000 1. Match Material ID/Plant ID with the BOM 2 component. 2. Create and populate the component planning item for Pistachios under the finished-good planning item for Party pack/3000. • Message 3: Forecast for Material ID Wholesale pallet/Plant ID 3000 1. Match Material ID/Plant ID with the BOM 3 header. 2. Create and populate the finished-good planning item. 3. The Party pack/3000 component planning item previously created (see Message 1 in this example) is now visible as a component in the component planning collaboration record for the Wholesale pallet/3000 finished good. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 183 -- 3 of 10 -- Quality Review Collaboration for Buyers Buyers and suppliers can exchange information though SAP Business Network to facilitate quality reviews. With the quality review collaboration feature, SAP Business Network for Supply Chain enables buyers to do the following: Batch records Collaborate on batch-record reviews, finalize batch record information, and allow quality releases of product bulk materials. The supplier can initiate the batch record process after the quality inspection process is completed for the final batch documentation. Complaints Collaborate on product complaint investigations from the buyer’s customer. Buyers usually receive complaints through a third-party system but reports them to suppliers and CMOs through quality reviews. Change requests Collaborate on material changes, processes, or equipment. General Collaborate on quality process-type definitions. Buyers can create or update quality review requests by choosing Quality Review . Quality reviews can reference purchase orders, ship notices, quality inspections, and quality notifications. Quality Review Request Statuses SAP Business Network for Supply Chain displays one of the following statuses for each quality review request: New The default status, set automatically when the quality review request is created. In process Indicates that the other party responded to the quality review request.  Note Either the supplier or the buyer can change Complete to In process. Complete The status selected by the supplier to indicate a review has been completed. Only the supplier can choose this status. Close The status selected by the buyer when a review has been closed. Only the buyer can set this status.  Note A closed review can no longer be edited. 184 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 4 of 10 -- Creating a Quality Review Request Use this procedure to request quality reviews for goods. Prerequisites The buyer system is enabled for the quality collaboration component. Context Suppliers can report quality issues that need investigation and resolution. Procedure 1. Choose Quality Review . The Quality review page opens. 2. Click Create Quality Review. The Create quality review page opens. 3. Fill in the Subject field, and choose details as desired from the drop-down menus. 4. Write your comment in the Comment field. Click Submit. Responding to a Quality Review Notification by Email Buyers and suppliers can post a comment through email or attach files to the associated quality review. Prerequisites • Buyers: Your account is entitled for the quality collaboration component. • Suppliers: You have a trading relationship with a buyer entitled for the quality collaboration component. • Buyers and suppliers: Your SAP Business Network account is configured to receive quality review notifications. See Configuring Quality Collaboration Notifications [page 93].  Restriction • You can’t reformat or delete parts of the original quality review notification message. Otherwise, SAP Business Network can’t process the message. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 185 -- 5 of 10 -- • You can’t change the To address in the reply email. However, you can add recipients. • In your reply email, don’t enter line breaks or exceed 1024 characters. SAP Business Network removes line breaks and excess characters before posting your comment to the quality review. • Files you attach to the reply email can’t exceed 1 GB in total size. • When the quality review status changes to Closed, no more notification responses can be received. • You can send a reply to a quality review notification only within 30 days of receiving it. After 30 days, replies to the quality review notification won’t be posted, though you can still edit the quality review in the SAP Business Network portal. Procedure 1. Open the email notification in your email client. 2. Create a reply to the email, observing the above restrictions. 3. Send the email. The text from your email reply is encrypted for transport and is posted as a comment to the quality review. Any files you attached to the email are automatically attached to the quality review. Supply Chain Monitor Feature The Supply Chain Monitor feature provides a simple and flexible way to access the transaction alerts information you want. The Supply Chain Monitor filters and settings give you greater control of which criteria generates an alert, which alerts data you see, and how the information is presented. Prerequisites • The buyer user is granted permissions by the buyer administrator to view Supply Chain Monitor and, if appropriate, to change its administration settings. For more information about Supply Chain Monitor access requirements, see Supply Chain Monitor Component Requirements [page 58]. • The buyer user is enabled for any collaboration component required by a particular Supply Chain Monitor exceptions group or chart. • For an exception group or chart whose functional area requires an additional permission, the buyer user is granted that permission. For more information about permission requirements, see the documentation for the exception group or chart. • For an exception group or chart whose functional area requires a collaboration component, the buyer user is entitled for that collaboration component. For more information about collaboration component requirements, see the documentation for the exception group or chart. • Each exception group or chart that the buyer user wants to see is checked in the Supply Chain Monitor settings  popup. 186 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 6 of 10 -- Restrictions • The maximum combined number of alerts that can exist, across all alert types, is 1 million. When new alerts are generated after this limit is reached, an equal number of the oldest alerts are automatically deleted. Otherwise, alerts are kept for 90 days, then automatically deleted. • Excel download is not available for alert type details pages. Order Confirmation Deviation Alerts [page 187] Order Confirmation Deviation Approval Alerts [page 188] Supplier-Managed Inventory Alerts [page 197] Quality Notification Chart [page 199] Forecast Alerts [page 200] Related Information Supply Chain Monitor Configuration [page 58] Order Confirmation Deviation Alerts Order confirmation deviation alerts in the Supply Chain Monitor dashboard inform you immediately when order confirmations deviate from certain purchase order requirements. Buyers, planners, and other stakeholders within a buying organization need visibility into the incoming supply. The order confirmation deviation alerts tile of the Supply Chain Monitor dashboard can identify immediately: • Orders at risk of being late • Quantities that deviate from the purchase order • Missing order confirmations Prerequisites This feature requires that: • SAP Ariba Support has enabled this tile. Have your Designated Support Contact log a case (formerly Service Request), and an SAP Ariba Support representative follows up to complete the request. • The buyer user is granted the Buyer Dashboard for Supply Chain Collaboration and Inbox and Order Access permissions by the buyer administrator. See Configuring Supply Chain Monitor Access [page 63]. • The buyer user is also granted the Supply Chain Monitor Settings Administration permission, to permit changes to Supply Chain Monitor administration settings. • Confirmation alerts is checked in the Supply Chain Monitor settings  popup. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 187 -- 7 of 10 -- Restrictions • Date deviations alert types are not generated for purchase order line items with multiple schedule lines. • Excel download is not available for alert type details pages. • Date deviations alerts might be generated in error due to time zone differences. • Confirmation alerts are not generated for scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases. User Interface • On the Supply Chain Monitor page, the Supply Chain Monitor order confirmation deviation alerts feature has a tile for order confirmation exceptions group alerts. The tile contains an interactive donut chart and list of alert types. • Buyers without the Supply Chain Monitor Settings Administration permission can see, but not set, order confirmation alerts. • When you hover over an alert type name in the list, a filter icon  displays to the right of the name. Clicking this icon opens a filter popup to refine which alerts data is displayed. Certain fields have a type-ahead feature that lists known valid choices as you type. You can set each filter to apply to the individual alert type or apply for all alert types in the exceptions group.  Caution Setting Apply to all alerts in this exception group overrides existing settings for that filter in all alert types of the same exceptions group. • Clicking the donut chart or an alert type opens a details page for that data. This page has a dropdown to select which alert type data to show, and has an Export CSV download link. Buyers can select and clear an alert from the details page.  Note An alert is removed for all buyers when: • A buyer clears an alert. • The generation date of an alert becomes more than 90 days before today. Order Confirmation Deviation Approval Alerts The Supply Chain Monitor dashboard can notify buyers when an order confirmation does not meet certain approval requirements. Suppliers can submit an order confirmation for a purchase order even when it is out of tolerance (for quantity, delivery date, or price). Suppliers can also submit an order confirmation for a scheduling agreement or a scheduling agreement release even when it is out of tolerance for quantity and/or delivery date; price deviations are not possible because the unit price cannot be changed in SAP Business Network for these documents. When a deviation occurs in the order confirmation process, an alert is automatically generated in the Supply Chain Monitor tab of the SAP Business Network buyer portal. 188 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 8 of 10 -- If you want to receive email notifications of deviation alerts, you can configure email settings in the Administration Configuration Notifications Order Confirmation Deviation Approval page of the SAP Business Network buyer portal. You can choose to receive emails every hour, three hours, six hours, 12 hours, or 24 hours. Each email notification contains a maximum of 100 of the most recently confirmed orders with deviations. By default, the emails are sent to the purchasing agent indicated in the purchase order cXML document. This information is received under the element Contact in the purchase order cXML document and it must have the Role attribute equal to purchasingAgent. You can include up to five email addresses under the Contact element, with each address under its own Email element. You can configure up to three alternative email addresses to send the emails to when the purchasing agent is missing. You can decide whether to approve or reject an order confirmation deviation from the Order confirmation deviation approval alerts page of the Supply Chain Monitor dashboard. As a result, order confirmation deviations do not go to your backend ERP system until you proactively resolve them. Deviation alerts are generated per line item. An item can have multiple deviations (for example, both a date deviation and a quantity deviation). The order type filter on the Order confirmation approval alerts page can be set to Orders, Stock Transport Orders, or Scheduling agreements. The confirmation statuses shown on this page display the schedule line number information. For purchase orders, this information is only displayed when it is available. Schedule line information is always available for scheduling agreement and scheduling agreement release confirmations. The following screenshot shows an example Order confirmation approval alerts page. Prerequisites • Buyers must enable the order-confirmation approval process for suppliers by checking the following rule and one of its approval-process levels: Allow suppliers to send order confirmations that do not comply with defined tolerances and require buyer approval • Single-level approval process • Multilevel approval process • To limit which types of deviations this rule allows to exceed defined tolerances, buyers can set one or more of the rule's exceptions. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 189 -- 9 of 10 --  Caution Before enabling an exception rule, the buyer first needs to reject from all partially confirmed orders any existing deviations that the desired exception rule does not allow. This task prevents possible unexpected behavior due to conflicts after an exception rule becomes enabled. Except quantity deviations Except delivery date deviations Except unit price deviations • For scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases, the Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases rule must be set. One or both of the following subrules must also be enabled: • Allow scheduling agreement collaboration • Allow scheduling agreement release collaboration Restrictions • The order confirmation deviation approval process only supports material items; service items are not supported. • The order confirmation deviation approval process does not apply to purchase orders that contain the cXML element <Extrinsic name="OCDeviationApproval">notAllowed</Extrinsic>. • When single-level deviation approval is used, buyers cannot approve and update orders with line items that have more than one unit price. • The Approve deviation and update order action is only available for purchase orders. It is not available for scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases. • Since deviations are approved at the line-item level, if an item has a deviation, it is not possible to ship or invoice the item until the deviation is cleared. Behavior Differences for Order Confirmation Deviations That Are Allowed with Buyer Approval [page 191] Configurations for Deviation Approval [page 192] Workflows for Order Confirmation Deviation Approval [page 195] Approving or Rejecting Confirmation Deviations [page 196] Related Information Approving or Rejecting Confirmation Deviations [page 196] 190 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SupplyChainCollaboratio.content: SAP Business Network and SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Deployment Process Overview Stage Description High level design • Explore the ERP starting point of the buyer organization • Discuss the documents and processes that the buyer wants to support • Identify the connection types and authentication methods the buyer wants to implement Technical design • Identify the exact documents and processes that the buyer wants to support • Plan in detail for the installation and configuration of an adapter to connect the buyer’s ERP system with SAP Business Network • Set up and configure the buyer’s SAP Business Network account and test ac- count. Generic SAP Business Network business rules and rules specific to supply chain collaboration can be configured. • Enable suppliers on SAP Business Network. Suppliers might also be enabled for supply chain collaboration functionality at this stage. Mapping • Create mappings between fields used by buyers in their business documents and messages and cXML elements and attributes that can be passed through SAP Business Network. Installation and configuration of adapt- ers • Buyer organization installs and configures the adapter Unit testing • End-to-end (buyer ERP through SAP Business Network to supplier and back) testing performed for each document type. UAT testing • System tested internally by buyer organization users Production • System goes live for collaboration between the buyer and their suppliers Buyer System Integration with SAP Business Network Hardware and software solutions enable SAP Business Network to communicate with different buyer systems. Organizations communicate with SAP Business Network using commerce eXtensible Markup Language (cXML) documents. Unless a buyer is using an SAP Business Network procurement solution, they will create these cXML documents on an ERP system that is external to SAP Business Network. The buyer’s ERP system, therefore, must be integrated with SAP Business Network in order to communicate over SAP Business Network and make use of its extensions. For enterprise customers of SAP Business Network using SAP Netweaver, SAP Business Network offers out-of-the- box adapters that allow the exchange of cXML documents with SAP Business Network. The adapters also provide complete mapping services between SAP Netweaver and SAP Business Network. An adapter is software that is installed at the customer site, behind the customer's firewall. For more information about integrating ERP systems with SAP Business Network, see the Integrating SAP Business Network for Supply Chain with SAP ERP and and SAP S/4HANA guide and the Transport Adapter Implementation Guide. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 11 -- 1 of 10 -- For more information about integration services, contact your SAP Business Network Account Manager. Buyer Integration Options The SAP Business Network Adapter for SAP NetWeaver is an add-on module for SAP business applications. This adapter enables integration between SAP Business Network and your SAP ERP system. It enables your SAP ERP system to send and receive cXML documents to and from SAP Business Network by mapping data elements between IDoc and cXML documents. Buyer System Entitlement for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain SAP Business Network Support enables your account to access SAP Business Network for Supply Chain functionality. To have your SAP Business Network account entitled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain features, ask your Designated Support Contact to log a case (formerly Service Request). An SAP Business Network Support representative will follow up to entitle your company to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. For buyers using external ERP systems, such as SAP ERP, adapter support for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain is available. Contact your SAP Business Network Account Manager for more information about integration services. Supplier Relationship Configuration This section provides topics that describe how buyer administrators can configure SAP Business Network for Supply Chain relationships with suppliers. Enabling or Disabling SAP Business Network for Supply Chain for Suppliers [page 13] Using a Vendor CSV File to Enable or Disable SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Relationships [page 14] Requesting a Logistics Relationship with a Supplier [page 15] Configuring Buyer-Controlled Routing of Orders [page 16] 12 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers -- 2 of 10 -- Enabling or Disabling SAP Business Network for Supply Chain for Suppliers Use this procedure to grant a supplier access to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain functionality. Prerequisites To enable suppliers for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain and industry-specific functionality, buyer administrators must have the Supplier Enablement Task Management permission. Context Buyer administrators who are enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain enable suppliers for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain functionality. Buyer administrators can also enable suppliers for industry- specific functionality, which is an additional layer of SAP Business Network for Supply Chain functionality that sits on top of the base SAP Business Network for Supply Chain functionality. When a supplier is enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain functionality by one buyer, they are automatically enabled for that functionality with all other buyers with which they have an active relationship.  Note You can alternatively use a CSV file to enable or disable suppliers in bulk. See Using a Vendor CSV File to Enable or Disable SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Relationships [page 14]. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account as an administrator. 2. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . 3. Choose the suppliers for whom you want to enable or disable collaborative supply chain or retail-industry functionality. 4. Choose the Actions menu at the bottom of the supplier table, then choose Enable/Disable Supply Chain Collaboration. 5. Check or uncheck the relevant boxes to enable or disable collaborative supply chain functionality for the selected suppliers: • Collaborative supply chain • Retail industry fields • Aerospace and Defense fields 6. Click OK. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 13 -- 3 of 10 -- Using a Vendor CSV File to Enable or Disable SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Relationships Use this procedure to grant SAP Business Network for Supply Chain access to multiple suppliers in one operation. Prerequisites • Assume a role with the Supplier Enablement Program Administrator permission. • Have available one of the following vendor CSV files, populated with vendor records: • Vendor Data Export report – This report prepopulates all fields that have existing data, including SAP Business Network for Supply Chain enablement settings. For more information, see Generating and Downloading Reports in the SAP Business Network buyer administration guide. • Upload Vendor template – Add vendor data to the template before you perform this procedure. For more information, see Creating a Vendor CSV File in Enabling suppliers on SAP Business Network . Context Buyer administrators can use a vendor CSV file to enable or disable multiple SAP Business Network for Supply Chain relationships in one operation.  Note You can alternatively enable or disable suppliers from the user interface. See Enabling or Disabling SAP Business Network for Supply Chain for Suppliers [page 13]. Procedure 1. Open the vendor CSV file for editing. 2. Enter in the Proposed Enablement Mode column your desired enablement settings, then save the file. Valid values are the following: Enablement Value Description EnableSCCWithRetail Enables the vendor for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, including retail indus- try fields. EnableSCCWithoutRetail Enables the vendor for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, excluding retail industry fields. DisableSCC Disables the vendor for all SAP Business Network for Supply Chain enablement. Observe these guidelines: 14 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers -- 4 of 10 -- • To include other text in the same field, enter that text first, followed by a pipe character (|) and the enablement value. For example: Your comment | EnableSCCWithRetail  Tip To avoid setting the wrong enablement value, enter only one enablement value in the field. Because this field accepts free text, more than one enablement value could be entered, but only the last value in the field is applied when you upload the file. • You can set provisional enablement values for standard account suppliers and private suppliers. The setting becomes active after the supplier is fully registered. • If the vendor CSV file has multiple records with the same Network ID value but different enablement values, the value of the record nearest the end of the file is applied. • Enablement values for a private supplier are ignored if the private supplier consolidates to an existing vendor. The private supplier inherits the enablement values of the existing supplier. 3. Choose Supplier Enablement Manage Vendors . 4. Click Upload, then choose Vendors from the dropdown. 5. On the Upload Vendors page, choose your edited CSV file and click Upload. Results On the Supplier Enablement Active Relationships page, the Supply Chain Collaboration column reflects the updated SAP Business Network for Supply Chain enablement settings. Requesting a Logistics Relationship with a Supplier Use this procedure to enable an SAP Business Network for Supply Chain relationship with a third-party logistics provider. Prerequisites Before you can request logistics services from a third-party logistics provider, you must do the following: • Be an administrator with the Supplier Enablement Task Management permission. • Establish a logistics relationship with the supplier. A logistics relationship allows a supplier to receive transport requests and to send and receive transport confirmations. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 15 -- 5 of 10 -- Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account as an administrator. 2. Choose Supplier Enablement Manage Vendors . 3. Click Search For Suppliers. 4. Enter information in the Company name, Company name starts with, or ANID fields, then click Search. Matching suppliers appear in the Search Results table. 5. In the Search Results table, find the supplier you're looking for, then in that row choose Request Relationship in the Actions column. The Supplier Detail page opens. 6. Check I have reviewed and verified the profile of SupplierName. 7. Click Request a Logistics Relationship. A message appears saying that the logistics relationship has been established. 8. Click Done. Configuring Buyer-Controlled Routing of Orders Use this procedure to override the default routing method of one or more suppliers. Prerequisites You must be an administrator with the Supplier Enablement Task Management permission. Context As a buyer administrator, you can override the supplier’s default routing method for orders that match one or more conditions. Doing this prevents those orders from being routed to an external integration channel. Procedure 1. Do one of the following: • To override the order routing method for an individual supplier, choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships , find the desired supplier, then in that row choose More Actions Edit . The Edit Preferences for Supplier page opens. • To override the order routing method for all suppliers, choose Administration Configuration Default Transaction Rules . The Default Transaction Rules page opens. 16 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers -- 6 of 10 -- 2. In the Purchase Order Rules section, make sure Override default purchase order rules is checked. Checking this rule shows the override rules you can set. 3. Check Override supplier's routing method for orders that match buyer's conditions, then click Configure. The Routing conditions for orders page opens. 4. Specify a value for one or more conditions. In the Condition column, select is or is not from the dropdown. For the Planning Type setting, the is empty condition is also available. Type Value cXML mapping Order Type Type of order. Select one of the following values: • regular – Standard order • release – Release against a master agreement or against a blanket purchase order • blanket – Blanket purchase order Request.OrderRequest.Order- RequestHeader.orderType External Document Type Enter a string for a document type from an external system. Request.OrderRequest.Order- RequestHeader.OrderReques- tHeaderIndustry.ExternalDocu- mentType.docType Planning Type Item-level planning strategy. Select one of the following values: • MTO – Make to Order • MTS – Make to Stock • ATO – Assemble to Order • CTO – Configure to Order Request.OrderRequest.Item- Out.ItemOutIndustry.planning- Type Item Category Item-level category, which indicates how a component or material is procured. Select one of the following values: • subcontract – Procuring a material by providing compo- nent information to a contract manufacturer that makes the finished product. • consignment – Managing a material through a special process where the payment to supplier is withheld until the material or service is consumed by the buyer. • thirdParty – Procuring a material from a third-party ven- dor. Request.OrderRequest.Item- Out.itemCategory Extrinsic Transaction Category Type Enter the cXML extrinsic Transaction Category Type (transactionCategoryOrType). You can enter multiple val- ues separated by commas. Request.OrderRequest.Or- derRequestHeader.Extrin- sic.name="transactionCategor- yOrType" 5. To enable a condition, check its Enable box. 6. Click OK to save the conditions. 7. Click Save to save purchase order rules. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 17 -- 7 of 10 -- Next Steps To avoid communication interruption, be sure to tell suppliers which orders are subject to buyer-controlled routing of orders. Suppliers aren’t notified by email when their default routing method for an order is overridden by the buyer. Advanced Packaging Configuration Buyer administrators can enable suppliers to specify a packing plan for ship notice items as they create a ship notice. The advanced packaging with handling units feature provides suppliers with a packaging wizard, to guide them through the steps of packing ship notice items. As a buyer administrator, this feature enables you to do the following tasks, to provide your requirements for the packaging wizard to use: • Upload packaging instructions for the supplier and configure automatic numbering of handling units. • Provide multiple packing instructions when a single packing instruction can't cover all materials. • Use a template to create packaging instructions. • Provide handling unit labels for suppliers to print. • Configure profiles to grant extra capabilities to suppliers when using advanced packaging for handling units. Workflow for Handling Unit Labels [page 18] Automated Transfer of Updated Handling-Unit Packaging Instructions [page 19] Configuring Auto-Numbering of Handling Units [page 20] Configuring GTL Numbering [page 22] Creating Packaging Instructions [page 23] Creating a Handling Unit Profile [page 26] Workflow for Handling Unit Labels The end-to-end workflow for handling unit labels starts with a buyer contacting SAP Ariba Services to define a template, and ends with the supplier printing labels for a ship notice. The following describes the workflow for printing handling unit labels: 1. An SAP Business Network customer engages with SAP Ariba Services to define a custom layout template for handling unit labels. The template is an Extensible Stylesheet Language Transformations, or XSLT, file. 2. SAP Ariba Services uploads custom PDF layout templates to the customer account. When more than one version of a template has been uploaded, the latest uploaded file is active. 3. A supplier opens a ship notice in the SAP Business Network user interface and clicks the printer icon in a handling unit line item to print a handling unit label in PDF format. Handling unit labels are available to all suppliers. 18 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers -- 8 of 10 -- Automated Transfer of Updated Handling-Unit Packaging Instructions Buyers can configure their ERP system to send packaging instructions to SAP Business Network for them whenever any instructions are added or updated. When a buyer creates or updates packaging instructions in their SAP S/4HANA ERP system, this feature coordinates with SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network the automatic transfer of those instructions to SAP Business Network. This feature doesn't change or interact with packaging instructions that are manually uploaded to SAP Business Network with an Upload/Download template in Excel. The manual creation and upload of packaging instructions using Upload/Download remains supported. For details about this manual upload method, see Creating Packaging Instructions [page 23]. In addition, a buyer who uses more than one type of ERP system can receive automatic transfers of updated packaging instructions on SAP S/4HANA systems, and manually update SAP Business Network with changes made in their other ERP systems. Prerequisites To activate automated transfer of new or updated packaging instructions, a buyer system must meet the following configuration requirements. • The buyer ERP system uses SAP S/4HANA. • The buyer ERP system is configured with SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. For details, see High-Level Steps for Integrating SAP ERP with SAP Business Network. • The buyer has followed instructions in the following SAP Notes: • 3230454 • 3261333 • 3265218 Restrictions • Quantities in the capacity fields in packaging instructions must be whole numbers. Quantities with decimal places aren't supported. • This feature doesn't automatically transfer generic packaging instructions. Details of the Automated Transfer Process • This SAP Business Network feature coordinates with other functionality to support automatic import of updates in packaging instructions from the buyer ERP. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 19 -- 9 of 10 -- When a buyer ERP system that uses SAP S/4HANA receives additions or changes to packaging instructions, SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network automatically retrieves those instructions and updates the data in SAP Business Network. The transferred instructions are then available to suppliers who use the SAP Business Network for Supply Chain advanced packaging wizard to create ship notices for that buyer. • This feature supports buyers with packaging instructions in more than one supported ERP system. Packaging instructions transferred to SAP Business Network include the systemID of the source ERP system. When revisions to packaging instructions are automatically transferred to SAP Business Network, this feature verifies that the instructions to update have the same systemID as the source ERP system. • When a supplier creates a ship notice with the advanced packaging wizard, this feature ensures that the wizard provides the right packaging instructions. When the wizard searches for valid packaging instructions to use, this feature chooses packaging instructions whose systemID and order number matches the systemID and order number of the purchase order to be shipped.  Note Buyers can still upload packaging instructions manually when desired. • This feature automatically populates the values for vendor ID, plant, and validity period in packaging instructions in the ERP system. Supplier You can select the supplier from the dropdown. 20 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers -- 10 of 10 --
