file://SBN/split/SupplyChainCollaboratio.content: Behavior Differences for Order Confirmation Deviations That Are Allowed with Buyer Approval The result of a deviation approval varies for the types of item changes and conditions. Purchase Orders If the rule Allow suppliers to send order confirmations that do not comply with defined tolerances and require buyer approval is checked, confirmation status is retained even if the item changed. This behavior is true even if the Retain confirmation status for unchanged line items on change orders rule is unchecked. However, there are two exceptions to this behavior: • If the previously confirmed quantity for an item is higher than the item’s revised quantity in the change order, the confirmation status is NOT retained. • If the previously confirmed price for an item is higher or lower than the revised price in the change order, the confirmation status is NOT retained. The following matrix further explains this behavior: Condition of Line Item in a Change Order Confirmation Status Approval Status Confirmed quantity is higher than the quantity in the new version of the order Not retained Not retained Item price in the new version of the order is higher or lower than the confirmed item price Not retained Not retained Item delivery date or quantity has changed and is not within tolerance Retained, but requires reconfirma- tion Changed to Awaiting supplier reconfirmation Item hasn’t changed in the new version of the order Retained Retained Item has changed, other than a change to unit price, and is within tolerance Retained Changed to Approved • If confirmation status is retained for a line item, the following logic also applies: • The confirmation status (for example, Confirmed With Changes) is recalculated based on the new version of the item. • All previous deviation alerts for order confirmation approval are deleted for the item. • If the item hasn’t changed in the new version of the order, the approval status is retained. If this item had any deviation alerts, they’re regenerated. • If an item has changed, other than the price, and it’s within tolerance, the approval status is changed to Approved. • If an item price has changed, within tolerance or not, the approval status is changed to Awaiting supplier reconfirmation. Deviation alerts are not generated because the supplier must first reconfirm the item. • If an item's delivery date or quantity has changed and it's not within tolerance, the approval status is changed to Awaiting supplier reconfirmation. Deviation alerts are not generated because the supplier must first reconfirm the item. • If an item’s approval status changed and the supplier has configured notifications for approval status changes, the supplier receives a notification. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 191 -- 1 of 10 -- Scheduling Agreements and Scheduling Agreement Releases If the rule Allow suppliers to send order confirmations that do not comply with defined tolerances and require buyer approval is checked, when a new version of a scheduling agreement or scheduling release agreement is received, previous confirmations for schedule lines are retained except when: • The schedule line is dropped in the new version. • The schedule line quantity changes in the new version. • The schedule line delivery date changes in the new version. The exception to this is when a confirmation status matches the schedule line's quantity and delivery date. When this occurs, the confirmation of the schedule line is retained. The confirmation of a schedule line with a changed quantity in the new version is retained if there is a confirmation status that matches the schedule line's quantity and date. When a schedule line has more than one confirmation status related to it, the system matches one of the confirmation statuses to the new schedule line. To match, both the quantity and the delivery date must be the same in the confirmation and the new schedule line. In either case, the confirmation status must be recalculated. This logic is applied even when the Allow suppliers to send order confirmations that do not comply with defined tolerances and require buyer approval rule is not set. If the rule is set, the buyer confirmation approval status is also recalculated. If a line item changes and the confirmation remains within tolerance (at line-item level or schedule-line level, depending on how rules are configured), the line-item confirmation approval status is changed to Approved. If a line item changes and the confirmation is not within tolerance (at line-item level or schedule-line level, depending on how rules are configured), the line item's confirmation approval status is changed to Awaiting supplier reconfirmation. Related Information Approving or Rejecting Confirmation Deviations [page 196] Configurations for Deviation Approval Buyers can customize how they approve order confirmations and handle approval deviations. Customers can choose between two configurations for deviation approval: • Single-level deviation approval—Provides a single level of approval. Customers approve deviations directly in the buyer portal. • Multilevel deviation approval—Provides multiple levels of approval. Customers approve deviations first in the buyer portal, then in the customer’s backend ERP system. Multilevel approval only applies to quantity and/or price deviations. The configuration type defines which actions are allowed per deviation type. The following actions are available: • Approve—Buyer approves the deviation and updates the item’s confirmation in their ERP. 192 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 2 of 10 -- • Approve and Update—Buyer approves the deviation and updates the order in their ERP with the confirmation information.  Note A line item with more than one unit price cannot be updated with single-level deviation approval.  Note This action is only supported for purchase orders. It is not supported for scheduling agreements or scheduling agreement releases. • Reject—Buyer rejects the deviation and nothing is updated in the ERP. Items revert to being unconfirmed in SAP Business Network. Configuration Settings for Single-Level Deviation Approval Purchase Orders Deviation Approve Approve and Update Reject Date Yes Yes Yes Price No Yes Yes Quantity Yes Yes Yes  Note A line item with more than one unit price cannot be updated with single-level deviation approval. Scheduling Agreements and Scheduling Agreement Releases Deviation Approve Reject Date Yes Yes Quantity Yes Yes Configuration Settings for Multilevel Deviation Approval Purchase Orders Deviation Approve Approve and Update Reject Date Yes Yes Yes Price No Yes Yes Quantity No Yes Yes SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 193 -- 3 of 10 -- Scheduling Agreements and Scheduling Agreement Releases Deviation Approve Reject Date Yes Yes Quantity Yes Yes Configuring Deviation Approvals When you set the Allowed actions for order confirmation deviation approval rule from the Administration Configuration Default Transaction Rules page, you can select Approve, Approve and update, or both. By default, both actions are checked. The selected approval actions apply for both single-level and multilevel deviation approval. The following list describes what happens when one or both actions are checked. • Both Approve and Approve and update are checked. The Purchase Orders tables in the Configuration Settings for Single-Level Deviation Approval and the Configuration Settings for Multilevel Deviation Approval sections show which deviations can be approved or rejected. • Only Approve is checked. The following table shows which deviations can be approved or rejected. This table only applies to single-level deviation approval since if you configure multilevel deviation approval, the Approve and update action is selected by default, and you cannot uncheck it. Deviation Approve Approve and Update Reject Date Yes No Yes Price No No Yes Quantity Yes No Yes  Note For single-level deviation approval of a price deviation, the new supplier-proposed price cannot be updated in the buyer's backend system since the price information cannot be updated in the Confirmations tab. • Only Approve and update is checked. The following table shows which deviations can be approved or rejected. The table is the same for single-level and multilevel deviation approval. Deviation Approve Approve and Update Reject Date No Yes Yes Price No Yes Yes Quantity No Yes Yes 194 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 4 of 10 -- Workflows for Order Confirmation Deviation Approval Deviation Approval Workflow – Single-Level Configuration The following diagram shows the workflow for single-level approval of order confirmation deviations: Figure 6: Deviation Approval Workflow for Single-Level Configurations  Note A line item with more than one unit price cannot be updated. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 195 -- 5 of 10 -- Deviation Approval Workflow – Multilevel Configurations The following diagram shows the workflow for multilevel approval of order confirmation deviations: Figure 7: Deviation Approval Workflow for Multilevel Configurations Approving or Rejecting Confirmation Deviations You can use Supply Chain Monitor to make your deviation decisions. Prerequisites • You are assigned the following permissions: • Permission to approve or reject date deviation • Permission to approve or reject price deviation • Permission to approve or reject quantity deviation • Access to order confirmation approvals • You have access to Supply Chain Monitor and to the Confirmation alerts tile. For more information, see Supply Chain Monitor Component Requirements [page 58] and Order Confirmation Deviation Approval Alerts [page 188]. Procedure 1. Go to Supply Chain Monitor. 196 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 6 of 10 -- 2. View the chart of confirmation alerts to see the number of deviations you received. 3. Above the chart, click You have order confirmation approvals due. The Order confirmation approval alerts page appears. 4. Optional: Filter deviations by Supplier, Part number, Purchase order, Purchasing group, Purchasing org, Planner code, and order type, or click tiles to show a subset of deviations. Types of deviations include date deviations, quantity deviations, price deviations, and deviations awaiting ERP approval. 5. Reject deviations by following these steps: a. Select one or more deviations in the table. b. Click Reject. A popup window appears. c. Optional: Enter a comment. d. Click Save. Rejected items revert to being unconfirmed. 6. Approve deviations by following these steps: a. Select one or more deviations in the table. b. Click Approve. A popup window appears. c. Choose one of these options:  Note Depending on your configuration, document type, and type of deviation, only one option may be available. See Configurations for Deviation Approval [page 192]. • Approve deviation – Approves the deviation and updates the item’s confirmation in your ERP. • Approve deviation and update order – Approves the deviation and updates the order in your ERP with the confirmation information.  Note Line items with more than one unit price cannot be updated with single-line deviation approval. d. Optional: Enter a comment. e. Click Save. Supplier-Managed Inventory Alerts Buyers can use the Supply Chain Monitor dashboard to monitor alerts for supplier-managed inventory, including replenishment orders. With supplier-managed inventory alerts tile on the Supply Chain Monitor dashboard, also called the supply-chain dashboard, you can configure and monitor supplier-managed inventory alerts. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 197 -- 7 of 10 -- Prerequisites This feature requires that: • SAP Ariba Support has enabled this tile. Have your Designated Support Contact log a case (formerly Service request), and an SAP Ariba Support representative follows up to complete the request. • The buyer user is granted the Buyer Dashboard for Supply Chain Collaboration and Planning Collaboration Visibility permissions by the buyer administrator. See Configuring Supply Chain Monitor Access [page 63]. • The buyer user is granted the Supply Chain Monitor Settings Administration permission, to be able to change Supply Chain Monitor administration settings. • The buyer user is entitled for the inventory collaboration component. • Supplier managed inventory alerts is checked in the Supply Chain Monitor settings  popup. Restrictions Excel download is not available for alert type details pages. User Interface • On the Supply Chain Monitor page, the Supply Chain Monitor supplier-managed inventory alerts feature provides a tile of exceptions group alerts for supplier-managed inventory. The tile contains an interactive donut chart and list of alert types. • Buyers without the Supply Chain Monitor Settings Administration permission can see, but not set, supplier- managed inventory alerts. • When you hover over an alert type name in the list, a filter icon  displays to the right of the name. Clicking this icon opens a filter popup to refine which alerts data is displayed. Certain fields have a type-ahead feature that lists known valid choices as you type. You can set each filter for an individual alert type or set it for all alert types in the exception group.  Caution Setting Apply to all alerts in this exception group overrides existing settings for that filter in all alert types of the same exception group. • Clicking the donut chart or an alert type opens a details page for that data. This page has a dropdown to select which alert type data to show and an Export CSV download link. Buyers can select and clear an alert from this page.  Note An alert is removed for all buyers when: • A buyer clears an alert. • The generation date of an alert becomes more than 90 days before today. • When a product activity message, product replenishment message, or sales order is sent, existing related alerts are updated. 198 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 8 of 10 -- • If a material status becomes Inactive, existing related alerts are deleted. • When a product activity message, product replenishment message, or sales order is sent and an individual planning item has a combination of Out of Stock, Below Minimum, and Above Maximum deviations in different weeks, only one alert is generated. That alert is based on the following priority ranking: 1. Out of Stock alerts 2. Below Minimum alerts 3. Above Maximum alerts Quality Notification Chart The Supply Chain Monitor dashboard can identify which materials or suppliers were issued the most quality notifications in a given period. The Supply Chain Monitor chart summarizes the top ten materials or suppliers that were issued the highest number of quality notifications during a selected period. The chart provides filters to refine the data it reports. Prerequisites This feature requires that: • The buyer user is granted the Buyer Dashboard for Supply Chain Collaboration permission by the buyer administrator. See Configuring Supply Chain Monitor Access [page 63]. • The buyer user is granted the Supply Chain Monitor Settings Administration permission, to be able to change Supply Chain Monitor administration settings. • The buyer is entitled for the quality collaboration component. • Quality notification is checked in the Supply Chain Monitor settings  popup. User Interface • The Supply Chain Monitor page has a Quality notifications tile. The tile contains a bar chart with the following filters: • A View by dropdown to group quality notifications by Material or Supplier. • A date-range dropdown to choose the range of quality notifications by creation date, from Last 3 months to Last year. • Hovering on a bar displays a popup with summary details for New, In-Process, Completed, and Closed quality notifications. • Clicking a bar opens the details page for that group of quality notifications. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 199 -- 9 of 10 -- Forecast Alerts You can receive notice of risks to supply forecasts in the Supply Chain Monitor dashboard. The forecast alerts tile in the Supply Chain Monitor dashboard, also called the supply-chain dashboard, can configure and monitor alerts for forecast and committed quantities of materials. Prerequisites This feature has the following requirements: • SAP Ariba Support has enabled this tile. Have your Designated Support Contact log a case (formerly Service Request), and an SAP Ariba Support representative follows up to complete the request. • You are enabled for one of the following: • The inventory collaboration component. • The forecast collaboration component. • SAP Business Network Planning Collaboration, which does not also require SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. • The buyer user is granted the Buyer Dashboard for Supply Chain Collaboration and Forecast Visibility permissions by the buyer administrator. See Configuring Supply Chain Monitor Access [page 63]. • To be able to change Supply Chain Monitor administration settings, the buyer user is also granted the Supply Chain Monitor Settings Administration permission. • Forecast alerts is checked in the Supply Chain Monitor settings  popup. The tile contains an interactive donut chart and list of alert types. • Buyers without the Supply Chain Monitor Settings Administration permission can see, but not set, forecast alerts. • When you hover over an alert type name in the list, a filter icon  displays to the right of the name. Clicking this icon opens a filter popup to refine which alerts data is displayed. Certain fields have a type-ahead feature that lists known valid choices as you type. You can set each filter for an individual alert type or for all alert types in the exception group.  Caution Setting Apply to all alerts in this exception group overrides existing settings for that filter in all alert types of the same exception group. 200 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 10 of 10 --

Freight Collaboration Feature This topic studies in detail, the relationship and collaboration between SAP Business Network for Supply Chain and SAP Business Network for Logistics. Overview In a supplier managed transportation scenario, shipment visibility turns out to be a key issue as the buyer often does not have reliable information about cargo movement or planned delivery timeline. This makes appointment scheduling, or goods receipt a challenge. Small suppliers do not enjoy economies of scale with Logistics Service Providers (LSP) / Carriers and therefore, pay relatively higher freight charges that ultimately inflates the landed cost of the product for the buyer. Inflated transportation bills can also be a reality in extreme cases. To overcome these supply chain issues, large buyers are increasingly turning their focus towards managing the transportation themselves with the help of partner LSPs (Logistics Service Provider) and carriers. Efocient management of the process directly and positively impacts the bottom line. By using economies of scale in transportation and enhanced supply chain visibility, the process can be made cost-effective. Prompt exception management and optimum resource allocation across the supply chain are ensured. Therefore, buyer managed transportation for inbound materials using LSP or carriers is expected to grow rapidly as a key differentiator in increasingly competitive supply chains. In short, the buyer organizations now need to create an end-to-end ‘source to stock’ process that seamlessly merges their procurement collaboration process with inbound transportation management. This is a singularly difocult collaboration where multiple business partners (such as supplier, LSP, Carrier) dispersed in a distributed supply chain need to strike a precise supply chain cadence. SAP Business Network, with a large partner eco- system and extensive connectivity, can effortlessly deliver this critical capability SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 201 -- 1 of 10 -- Related Information For more information, see Integration with SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration Prerequisites • The buyer and supplier must share a CSC relationship type. • The buyer is also onboarded on SAP Business Network for Logistics (BN4L). Contact SAP Support, provide your SAP Business Network for Supply Chain ANID and your SAP Business Network for Logistics LBN ID, to establish the relationship between both networks • Enable BN4L integration for Ship Notices must be enabled for the buyer account. Contact SAP Support to get this entitlement enabled. • The buyer must set a partner function called “ShippingNetwork,” with the value ‘BN4L’, on their system. This indicator is then included in the Purchase Order document. • The buyer must also provide, as part of the Purchase Order document, the Logistics Service Provider (LSP) identifier, by setting an additional partner function called “ForwardingAgent.” This value is flipped to the Ship Notice document generated from the Order, after which, it is transmitted to BN4L. Doing this enables the corresponding LSP to be assigned to the Transport Request. Process Flowchart Flowchart illustrating the process: 202 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 2 of 10 -- Feature Benefit Through the seamless fusion of procurement and logistics collaboration, using the Ship Notice document as the key connector, the buyer can monitor and manage the blended networks collaboration in a single unified flow. Procedure Context Perform the following steps: 1. The buyer sends the Purchase Order (PO) to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain with two indicators: the BN4L flag (which allows the application to route the ASN* to BN4L) and the LSP identifier (for SAP Business Network for Logistics (BN4L) to know to which LSP the ASN must be sent). *ASN = Advance Shipping Notification. 2. The supplier receives the PO in the Business Network (BN) portal, where the new BN4L indicator is visible and confirms the PO, depending on the configured business rules (configured by the buyer). 3. The supplier creates the ASN including all the required information. This ASN is sent to the buyer (backend) system, where an Inbound delivery is created. At the same time, the ASN is also routed to BN4L. 4. In SAP Business Network for Logistics (BN4L), a Transportation Requirement is created and propagated from the Shipper (who is the same SCC (Supply Chain Collaboration) Buyer in this scenario) to the corresponding LSP tenant. 5. The Transportation Requirement is forwarded from BN4L to the assigned carrier through an external API. 6. The carrier plans the shipment and sends this shipment plan to BN4L  Note A shipment plan carries the following statuses as a progress marker to the plan: - • In Planning: Status assigned after the ASN is being created and sent to LBN (Logistics Business Network) so the shipment can be planned • Planned: Status assigned when the shipment plan is generated by the carrier and comes from LBN • Planning not started: This status is assigned when the ship notice is not submitted, but there is a draft saved. 7. BN4L forwards the shipment plan to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain (SCC) and updates the following header information in the ASN: • Bill Of Lading • Service Level • Carrier • Transit Direction • Delivery Date 8. In the portal, the suppliers can visualize all the shipment details under a new tab in the ASN document. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 203 -- 3 of 10 -- 9. An updated version of the ASN (with the updated values) is also sent to the buyer and the inbound delivery is updated. 10. Optional Step: - An update or cancellation of the shipment plan can be done by the carrier for several reasons. For example: If the carrier updates the shipment plan by providing a different delivery date or if the assigned carrier cannot handle transportation and a new carrier is assigned, then a Shipment Plan Update is generated and BN4L sends it to SCC. 11. After every change to the shipment plan, the SCC creates a new ASN version and sends it to the buyer, where the inbound delivery is also updated. 12. On the planned pick-up date, the carrier picks up the items from the supplier warehouse and delivers it to the buyer warehouse. 13. Finally, the buyer can issue the goods receipt (GR) confirming receipt of the requested goods. Limitations • This new functionality applies to online Ship Notices and Ship Notices created through the Excel mass upload template only. B2B Ship Notices are not covered. • Only one shipment plan per Ship Notice is supported. UI Changes Table 1: New Fields / Filters Introduced UI Section New Fields / Filters Purchase Order page The Shipping Network: BN4L indicator is shown at the document level. Ship Notices created from this type of POs, are routed to SAP Business Network for Logistics. Orders and Items to Ship Workbench tiles The Shipping Network filter and column have been added. They help suppliers to identify this specific type of orders and items that belong to these orders, to facilitate the creation of the corresponding Ship Notice. Ship Notice page The Shipping Network: BN4L indicator is shown at the document level. • The Shipment Planning Status is displayed. Possible statuses are: In Planning, Planned and Planning Not Started. • Additionally, a new Shipment Details tab has been added to the Ship Notice UI. This new tab displays all the details related to the shipment plan that is generated (externally) by the carrier and comes from SAP Business Network for Logistics. Buyers and suppliers can see the planned pickup date, planned delivery date, information on all the transport stages, and more. 204 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits -- 4 of 10 -- UI Section New Fields / Filters Ship Notice Workbench tile A new workbench tile that lists all available ship notices has been introduced. New tile filters include: Customers/Suppliers, Packing Slip ID, Order Number, Creation Date, Ship Notice Type, Shipping Date, Delivery Date, Completion Status, Receipt Status, Routing Status Shipping Network, and Shipment Planning Status. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 205 -- 5 of 10 -- Tasks for Regular Business Users This section provides topics describing how regular business users, rather than administrators, use the system to perform supply chain collaboration tasks. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Home Page Components [page 206] The Workbench [page 208] Documents for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers [page 215] Resending a Document That Was Not Received [page 221] Resending Failed Orders for Private Suppliers [page 222] SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Home Page Components Home page features help you access and manage your transactions. Your SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Home page features simple navigation, a powerful search bar, an instant overview of your transactions in a tile-based design, and a My widgets section that you can customize. Overview Tile Bar [page 206] Home Page Widgets [page 207] Customizing Your Home Page Widgets [page 207] Overview Tile Bar The Overview tile bar displays the default tiles for your business role, or tiles that you have configured. On the SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Home page, up to five tiles are displayed in the Overview tile bar by default. You can reveal an additional five tiles with the More button. You can also configure which tiles are displayed from the Workbench. For more information, see The Workbench [page 208] The Overview tiles are displayed intelligently: if one or more Pinned documents exist, that tile is displayed first. Otherwise, it is moved to the end of the order. 206 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Tasks for Regular Business Users -- 6 of 10 -- Home Page Widgets Your Home page provides widgets to show at a glance current information for your business activities. The SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Home page displays role-based widgets. These widgets help you focus on important tasks, insights, key performance indicators, and benchmarks for your business. To customize the contents of your Home page, see Customizing Your Home Page Widgets [page 207]. Customizing Your Home Page Widgets Use this procedure to choose what displays on your SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Home page. Context You can add, remove, and rearrange widgets on your Home page from the Customize my widgets page. Procedure 1. On the Home page, click Customize in the My widgets area. 2. On the Customize my widgets page, do any of the following: • Click the plus sign icon ( ) to add a widget. • Click the minus icon ( ) to remove a widget. • Select the two line icon in the center of the widget to move the widget. 3. Click Save. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Tasks for Regular Business Users PUBLIC 207 -- 7 of 10 -- The Workbench The workbench displays configurable tiles based on transaction documents, statuses, and additional filters. Overview of the Workbench The workbench is a customizable page that allows you to get a quick overview of transaction documents and take action on them. It displays up to 25 customized tiles. When more tiles are available that can fit on your screen (based on your screen resolution), the tile bar displays a right arrow button ( ) to scroll through the tiles. Each tile displays a count or amount, title, and subtitle. 1. The count is the number of transactions, action items, or events that match the tile filter criteria, up to 1000; if the count is greater than 1000, the count displays 1000+. The amount is the total value of scheduled payments, remittances, or early payment offers contained in the tile. It is displayed in your local currency. 2. The title is the name of the base tile, a label describing the type of transaction, action item, or event that matches the tile criteria, such as Invoices. 3. The subtitle is a configurable label to further describe the contents of the tile, which is particularly useful when you create your own variant of a tile based on a complex combination of filters. Custom attributes Custom attributes you create with a customization project can be extended to workbench tiles, allowing you and your suppliers to view them as filters and columns. The actions column The Actions column displays a more button ( ) that allows you to complete actions on documents. The actions available are based on the document type and status. Some workbench tiles also support multi-select and bulk actions. Column grouping You can group workbench columns for many tiles. Grouping workbench columns is helpful when you need to perform bulk edits on similar line items. When you group columns for a workbench tile, the search results show documents that have the same values for the filters you've selected. For example, you can look for documents with the same description, order number, and item number. 208 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Tasks for Regular Business Users -- 8 of 10 -- The export button The workbench also features an export button ( ), which allows you to download the information displayed in the table as an .xlsx file. The download includes only the information currently displayed in the list view. Any lines or columns that are hidden from your current list view are not included in the .xlsx file. Customizing Tiles on Your Workbench [page 209] Filtering Workbench Tiles [page 210] Customizing Workbench Columns [page 212] Grouping Workbench Columns [page 213] Workbench Tile Reference [page 214] Customizing Tiles on Your Workbench Use this procedure to add workbench tiles, add custom subtitles to the tiles, and remove or rearrange tiles as needed. Procedure 1. On the Workbench page, click the Settings icon ( ) in the top-right corner. 2. Do any of the following: • Click the plus symbol ( ) to add a new tile. The value for the tile populates after you save your changes. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Tasks for Regular Business Users PUBLIC 209 -- 9 of 10 -- • Click the delete symbol ( ) to remove a tile. • Select the three lines icon ( ) in the center of the tile to move the tile. 3. Click Apply to save your changes. Next Steps Further customize your tile by adding filters. For more information, see Filtering Workbench Tiles [page 210]. Filtering Workbench Tiles When you open a workbench tile, all of the documents associated to that tile are displayed, but you can apply filters and refine which documents are shown. For example, you can choose to only see orders from a specific customer by using the Customers filter. Context When a tile is selected, SAP Business Network displays filter tags for any filters configured for that tile. The screenshot of the Orders tile below has the following filters and their values applied, Creation date: Last 365 days, Routing status: Sent, Max amount: 10,000, and Currency: USD. 210 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Tasks for Regular Business Users -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SupplyChainCollaboratio.content: You can edit the filter on some tiles, while others have set filters that cannot be changed. For example, the New orders tile is pre-set with the New status so that you only view new orders. The filters available are based on the tile type. Below is a screenshot of filters available for the Scheduled payments tile. Procedure 1. On the Workbench page, click the tile to which you want to apply filters. 2. Click Edit filter. 3. Set filters as needed, then click Apply. 4. Click Save filter. 5. Review the subtitle and enter a new one if necessary, then click Save. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Tasks for Regular Business Users PUBLIC 211 -- 1 of 10 -- Customizing Workbench Columns You can show, hide, and rearrange workbench columns as needed, which helps to speed up the search process. Procedure 1. On the Workbench page, click the tile you want to adjust the columns for. 2. Click the settings icon ( ). 3. In the Table setting dialog, do any of the following: • To show a new column, move the column from Available columns to Displayed columns. • To hide a column, move the column from Displayed columns to Available columns. 212 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Tasks for Regular Business Users -- 2 of 10 -- • Use drag and drop to rearrange the columns as needed. The order of the columns in this dialog, first to last, is presented from left to right on the workbench. 4. Click Apply to save your changes. Grouping Workbench Columns You can group workbench columns for many tiles. Grouping workbench columns is helpful when you need to perform bulk edits on similar line items. Context When you group columns for a workbench tile, the search results show documents that have the same values for the filters you've selected. For example, you can look for documents with the same description, order number, and item number, as shown in the screenshot below. Procedure 1. On the Workbench page, click the tile for which you want to group columns. 2. Click the settings icon ( ). SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Tasks for Regular Business Users PUBLIC 213 -- 3 of 10 -- 3. In the Table setting dialog, select Column grouping. 4. Use drag and drop to move columns from the Available columns list to the Grouping list. 5. Click Apply to save your changes. Procedure 1. Choose Fulfillment Extended collaboration and navigate to the component receipts. 2. Use search filters to refine the records shown. Viewing Component Ship Notices Buyers can see the component ship notices sent by component suppliers on the shipment of goods. Procedure 1. Choose Fulfillment Component Shipments . 2. Use search filters to refine the results shown.. Viewing Forecast Commitment Information from Suppliers Buyers can monitor their projected stock needs and what quantity their suppliers commit to deliver. Context To effectively collaborate with suppliers on forecast quantities, buyers must see the same forecast demand and forecast commitment data that their suppliers see. With the buyer view of forecast application feature, buyers can see the same forecast demand and forecast commit data their suppliers see. Procedure 1. Choose Planning Forecast . 2. Enter information in the Search filters fields to refine the information shown in the Forecast table. 216 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Tasks for Regular Business Users -- 6 of 10 -- Related Information Search Filters in Order and Forecast Collaboration [page 132] Viewing Multitier Orders Multitier orders are sent from an OEM buyer to multiple suppliers in different tiers in the supply chain, for example, contract manufacturers and component suppliers. Procedure 1. Choose Orders Orders and Releases . 2. Look in the Multi-Tier column. Any orders that request copies to be sent to other supply chain partners have a green checkmark . 3. To view details on copy documents, click the Copies link for a multitier order. 4. To open the order, click an order number. Viewing and Exporting Serial Number Lists in Orders If serial numbers are included with an order, you can view serial number details for each line item. Prerequisites The cXML file for the order must include serial number information. Procedure 1. Open an order that contains serial numbers for line items. 2. For any item contained in the order, click Details. 3. Find the Information on Ship Notice [Optional] > Serial Numbers section. • If serial numbers are specified as a profile or a range, they appear under Serial Numbers. • If the format is a list, click Details to open the Items serial number popup and see the list of serial numbers for the item. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Tasks for Regular Business Users PUBLIC 217 -- 7 of 10 --  Restriction The Items serial number window can display up to 500 serial numbers. If there are more than 500 serial numbers for the item, download the full list. • To advance to the next page, click the  icon. • To download the list, click the Download Serial Numbers  icon. • To print the list, click the Print Screen  icon. • When you are finished, click Done. Related Information Serial Number Report Viewing Transport Confirmations Buyers can see in SAP Business Network the transport confirmations sent by their third-party logistics providers. Context You can view transport confirmations sent to you by logistics providers. Transport confirmations inform you of the status of consignments in a transport request. Consignments can be confirmed, collected, rejected, or canceled. The documents are read-only. Procedure 1. Choose Fulfillment Transport Confirmations . 2. To find a transport confirmation, enter values in the following Search Filters fields, and click Search: Search filter Description Carrier The name of the logistics provider. Confirmation Number The transport confirmation number. file://SBN/split/SupplyChainCollaboratio.content: Resending a Document That Was Not Received Administrators can resend some documents that were not received because of errors. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Context Occasionally, documents sent through SAP Business Network are not received at their final destination because of errors in the documents or their lack of compliance with relevant business rules. Administrators can often resend these documents after correcting the errors. Procedure 1.  Note The path to the Documents to Resend feature is as follows: • For buyers – Quick links Documents to Resend • For suppliers – … Documents to Resend Choose Documents to Resend. The documents search results are displayed, with details about the causes of the failures. The Resolution Status search filters Show unresolved entries and Show resolved entries control which of the failed documents that meet the other search results are included. 2. Review the failed document's error message, make the correction, then click Resend in the Actions column.  Note Alternatively, you can choose these other actions in the Actions column: • Click Export cXML to export the affected document in cXML, then mark the document transmission issues as resolved. • Click Mark as Resolved if you do not want to resend the failed document. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Tasks for Regular Business Users PUBLIC 221 -- 1 of 10 -- Resending Failed Orders for Private Suppliers If copies of orders failed to be delivered to suppliers, you can resend them. Procedure 1. Choose Orders Orders and Releases . 2. Click View Failed Orders to Private Supplier. The Resend Failed Orders for Private Suppliers window appears. 3. Enter the supplier's Ariba Network ID (optional) and a date range, and then click Search. 4. In the result table, click a supplier's Ariba Network ID to view the failed multitier orders for that supplier. 5. Select one or more orders, and click Resend to resend the selected orders, or click Resend All to resend all failed orders. 6. Click Done twice to return to the Orders and Releases page. 222 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Tasks for Regular Business Users -- 2 of 10 -- Serial Numbers Enabled in Component Receipts Serial numbers are supported within subcontracting processes in Component Receipts whenever they are present in the Component Ship Notice. • The following business rules are enabled and are available at the default transaction and supplier group level: • Require serial numbers to be mandatory in the Component Receipt whenever they occur in the Component Ship Notice. • Require the serial numbers that are a part of the Component Ship Notice to be included in the Component Receipt. • Require the total count of component receipt serial numbers to match the total quantity received for line items in a component receipt. • • Serial numbers can be entered while creating the Component Receipt (CR) for the Component Ship Notice (CSN) in the user interface at the line item level. • When the supplier selects Add Serial Numbers in the Component Receipt (CR) page, a popup for the creation of the serial number is displayed with the possibility to change the serial numbers. • Serial numbers can be removed by selecting the Remove option. • When the supplier selects Autofulfill Quantity, the serial numbers populate the system. • The supplier can use the Reset button to clear all the serial numbers in the popup. • The Close button allows the supplier to return to the Component Receipt (CR) page. • The supplier can select Download template to download an excel templated of all the line items in the component creation screen. • The supplier can click on Browse to select the Excel file and then choose Upload Excel to upload the Excel file with the serial numbers. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Serial Numbers Enabled in Component Receipts PUBLIC 223 -- 3 of 10 -- Document Customization You can create custom attributes and include these attributes in customization projects for certain document types. Custom Attributes Custom attributes contain additional information relevant to your business and add to the standard SAP Business Network pages, Upload/Download job types, and Workbench tiles. You can create custom attributes for purchase orders, ship notices, and order confirmations. See Custom Attributes for Customization Projects [page 224]. Customization Projects You can create customization projects to add custom attributes to the Ship Notice Excel template for Upload/ Download and to the Items to Confirm, Orders, and Items to Ship tiles of the Workbench. See Customization Projects [page 229]. Custom Attributes for Customization Projects [page 224] Customization Projects [page 229] Custom Attributes for Customization Projects You can create custom attributes for purchase orders, ship notices, and order confirmations to be used in customization projects. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Restrictions You can create a maximum of thirty custom attributes to use across all document types. Custom attributes help you communicate information with your suppliers that is not already included on standard SAP Business Network pages, Upload/Download job types, and Workbench tiles. For example, you can create 224 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization -- 4 of 10 -- Size and Color custom attributes, and then create a customization project for the Items to Ship tile for the Workbench that includes these attributes. Applying these custom attributes to the Items to Ship tile for the Workbench lets your suppliers view this information on the list page and filter ship notices by these custom attributes. For details on creating custom attributes, see Creating a Custom Attribute for a Customization Project [page 225]. You can also edit and delete existing custom attributes. See Editing a Custom Attribute for a Customization Project [page 227] and Deleting a Custom Attribute for a Customization Project [page 228]. Creating a Custom Attribute for a Customization Project [page 225] Editing a Custom Attribute for a Customization Project [page 227] Deleting a Custom Attribute for a Customization Project [page 228] Creating a Custom Attribute for a Customization Project Use this procedure to create custom attributes to apply to document types. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission.  Restriction You can create a maximum of thirty custom attributes to use across all document types. Context Buyers can create custom attributes and add them to a centralized library of attributes. Procedure 1. Click Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service .  Note Account Settings is the user icon on the top right of the page. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization PUBLIC 225 -- 5 of 10 -- The Customization – Self Service page opens. 2. Click on the Create pulldown menu and select Attribute. The Create Attribute page displays. 3. Fill in the attribute fields. Field Description Attribute name Enter the display name for the attribute. Attribute description Enter a description for the attribute. Attribute type Choose Extrinsic or Characteristic. Data type Choose String. Level (Extrinsic only) Choose Header or Line item depending on whether the custom attribute is a header or a line-item extrinsic. Domain (Characteristic only) Enter the name of the domain attribute of the Characteristic element in the cXML. Extrinsic name (Extrinsic only) Enter the name of the extrinsic used in the cXML. Document type The Purchase order document type is always selected. You can also select one or both other document types. By selecting a document type, you indicate that the attribute can be used in a customization project for this type of document. SAP Business Network automatically builds and displays the cXML paths. For example, if you create an attribute that is a line-item level extrinsic, and you select all three document types, SAP Business Network displays the following cXML paths: • Order confirmation: ConfirmationRequest/ConfirmationItem/Extrinsic • Purchase order: OrderRequest/ItemOut/ItemDetail/Extrinsic • Ship notice: ShipNoticeRequest/ShipNoticePortion/ShipNoticeItem/Extrinsic What language(s) do you want to support? Choose what languages to support and enter the attribute name for each chosen language. English (en) is supported by default. Click the add  icon to choose more languages. 4. Click Save. The attribute is saved, and the attribute library page displays. 226 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization -- 6 of 10 -- Related Information Document Customization [page 224] Editing a Custom Attribute for a Customization Project Use this procedure to make changes to a custom attribute. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Context Buyers can edit a custom attribute in the attributes library. Procedure 1. Click Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service . The Customization – Self Service page opens. 2. Click the Attributes tab. The list of custom attributes in the attributes library displays. 3. In the Actions column, click the more ( ) icon for the attribute you want to edit, and click Edit. The Edit Attribute window opens. 4. Make your edits. 5. Click Save. The attribute is saved, and the attribute library page displays. Related Information Document Customization [page 224] SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization PUBLIC 227 -- 7 of 10 -- Deleting a Custom Attribute for a Customization Project Use this procedure to remove a custom attribute from the attributes library. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Context Buyers can delete a custom attribute from the attributes library. Procedure 1. Click Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service . The Customization – Self Service page opens. 2. Click the Attributes tab. The list of custom attributes in the attributes library displays. 3. In the Actions column, click the more ( ) icon for the attribute you want to delete, and click Delete. A popup displays asking you to confirm the deletion.  Caution You cannot delete an attribute that is included in a customization project with either the Requested to Publish or Published status. If you try to do that, a popup displays that includes a list of projects that have either status. 4. Click Delete. The custom attribute is deleted from the attributes library. Related Information Document Customization [page 224] 228 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization -- 8 of 10 -- Customization Projects You can create customization projects for the Ship Notice and Order Confirmation Excel templates for Upload/ Download and for some Workbench tiles. Prerequisites • You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. • The supplier groups that you want to assign your customization project to already exist in your account. • To publish a customization project, you must be a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Publisher permission. You can create customization projects to add custom attributes to the Ship Notice and Order Confirmation Excel templates for Upload/Download. Customization projects for these templates might include the following changes: • Choose which customer-defined columns to include or omit from the template. • Set an alternative name for a customer-defined column. • Change the order of the columns in the Excel template. You can also create customization projects to add custom attributes to the Workbench tiles for Items to Confirm, Orders, and Items to Ship. A customization project for one of these Workbench tiles might include the following changes: • Add a custom attribute as a column. A maximum of five columns can be added. • Add a custom attribute as a filter. A maximum of three filters can be added. • Edit custom attributes to display a different column name, including translations. The tasks involved in the customization process are divided into two parts, editing tasks and publishing tasks. 1. Editing tasks are done by the Editor from the buyer test account. The Editor creates or updates customization projects and tests them. For details, see Creating a Customization Project [page 231]. 2. Publishing tasks are done by the Publisher from the buyer production account. The Publisher verifies and publishes customization projects. A buyer who is both an Editor and a Publisher can publish their own customization projects. For details, see Publishing a Customization Project [page 242]. For an overview of the complete workflow, see Workflow for Creating and Publishing a Customization Project [page 230]. Workflow for Creating and Publishing a Customization Project [page 230] Creating a Customization Project [page 231] Publishing a Customization Project [page 242] Creating New Versions of Customization Projects [page 244] Deleting Unpublished Customization Projects [page 245] SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization PUBLIC 229 -- 9 of 10 -- Workflow for Creating and Publishing a Customization Project The end-to-end workflow for a customization project starts with an Editor creating or editing a project, and ends with a Publisher assigning suppliers to the published project.  Note The Editor creates the customization project from the buyer test account, while the Publisher publishes it from the buyer production account.  Restriction The Editor can only use a test account, not a production account, to develop and test customization projects. 1. The Editor logs on to the buyer test account. 2. The Editor creates a new or edits an existing customization project to apply to suppliers when they do one of the following: • Create or edit a quality notification. • Generate a Ship Notice Upload/Download job template in Excel. • Generate an Order Confirmation Upload/Download job template in Excel. • Review orders in the Workbench tile for Orders. • Create order confirmations in the Workbench tile for Items to Confirm. • Create ship notices in the Workbench tile for Items to Ship. 3. The Editor edits the customization project to add customizations. 4. The Editor pushes the customization project to the supplier test account. 5. The Editor logs on to the supplier test account and validates the customization project. 6. From the buyer test account, the Editor requests to publish the customization project to the production system. 7. The Publisher logs on to the supplier test account and validates the customization project.  Note When the Editor is also the Publisher, this step is skipped. 8. The Publisher logs on to the buyer production account and publishes the customization project. 9. The Publisher assigns suppliers to the customization project. 230 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SupplyChainCollaboratio.content: Creating a Customization Project Use this procedure create a customization project for a Ship Notice or Order Confirmation Upload/Download template, or for Workbench tiles for Items to Confirm, Orders, or Items to Ship. Prerequisites • You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. • The supplier groups that you want to assign your customization project to already exist in your account. Procedure 1. Sign in to your buyer test account. 2. Click Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service .  Note Account Settings is the user icon on the top right of the page. The Customization – Self Service page opens. 3. Choose Create Project to create a new customization project. The Create Project page opens showing the first step, What project do you want to create? 4. Enter your information in the customization project fields. The following fields are required. Field Description Project name Enter a unique name. Project description Enter a description. Document type Choose Order confirmation, Purchase order, Quality notification, or Ship notice. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization PUBLIC 231 -- 1 of 10 -- Field Description Suppliers Choices are: • All (default) • None  Note If you choose None, you will not be able to check your customizations in the supplier test account since the customization project will not be assigned to any suppliers. • Selected supplier groups – When chosen, a dropdown arrow shows. Click the arrow to show the list of supplier groups. Customization area Choose Workbench/Items to Confirm, Workbench/Orders, or Workbench/Items to Ship to customize the Workbench tile for the selected Document type. Or, when the Document type is Ship notice or Order confirmation, choose Excel to cus- tomize the Ship Notice or Order Confirmation Excel template for Upload/Download. Customized languages English (en) is required and always chosen. To add other languages, click the add ( ) icon to choose the languages. Click Done when you finish selecting languages. 5. Choose Save. The Customization – Self Service page opens in the Projects tab, showing your project in the list of customization projects. 6. In the row for your customization project, choose the more ( ) icon in the Actions column, then from the dropdown choose Edit. The Edit Project page opens with the second step, How do you want to customize your project, expanded. 7. Make your customizations. • For details about customizing an Excel template for Upload/Download, see Customizing an Excel Template for Upload/Download [page 233]. • For details about customizing Workbench tiles, see Customizing a Workbench Tile [page 239]. 8. When you finish making your customizations, click Save. The Customization – Self Service page displays. 9. In the row for your customization project, choose the more ( ) icon in the Actions column, then from the dropdown choose Push to test. The Push project to supplier test account popup displays. 10. Choose Push. The customization project is pushed to the supplier test account. The project Status changes to Pushed to Test. 11. Optional: Assign the project to suppliers for testing. This step is only needed when no suppliers have been assigned to the project. a. In the row for your customization project, choose the more ( ) icon in the Actions column, then from the dropdown choose Edit. b. Click the edit ( ) icon in the What project do you want to create? section. c. Select the suppliers. 232 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization -- 2 of 10 -- d. Click Save. 12. Sign in to a supplier test account you have assigned the customization project to and check your customizations. See Testing a Customization Project [page 241]. 13. Return to your buyer test account and click Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service . The Customization – Self Service page opens. 14. Click the more ( ) icon in the Actions column for your customization project and select Request to publish. The Publish to production popup opens. 15. Click OK. Your customization project is sent to production for the Publisher to review and publish. The project Status changes to Requested to Publish. Customizing an Excel Template for Upload/Download [page 233] Customizing a Workbench Tile [page 239] Testing a Customization Project [page 241] Customizing an Excel Template for Upload/Download Use this procedure to edit a customization project to customize an Excel template for Upload/Download. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Context If you completed the first step (What project do you want to create?) on the Create Project page and clicked Save to save your project information, start with Step 1. If you completed the first step and clicked Next, start with Step 2. Procedure 1. From the Customization – Self Service page, in the row for your customization project, choose the more ( ) icon in the Actions column, then from the dropdown choose Edit. The Edit Project page opens with the second step, How do you want to customize your project, expanded and active. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization PUBLIC 233 -- 3 of 10 -- 2. Optional: Customize the standard attributes in the template. See Customizing Standard Attributes in an Excel Template [page 234]. 3. Optional: Create additional custom attributes. If you need to create additional attributes to add to your customization project, click Create in the Available Attributes column next to Custom Attributes. For details, see Creating a Custom Attribute for a Customization Project [page 225]. 4. Optional: Customize the custom attributes in the template. See Customizing Custom Attributes in an Excel Template [page 236]. 5. Optional: Change the display order of columns. In the Selected attributes list, click the drag ( ) icon of an attribute you want to move, then drag and drop the attribute to the desired place in the list. 6. When you finish making your customizations, click Next. The page expands and makes active the third step, What will your project look like? 7. Review the preview of your customization project applied to the Upload/Download Excel template. 8. Optional: If you need to make any changes, click the edit ( ) icon in the section for the second step, How do you want to customize your project, and go back to Step 2 [page 234] to edit your project. Customizing Standard Attributes in an Excel Template You can customize standard attributes in an Excel template. Context Make one or more of the following customizations to the standard attributes you include in the template. Procedure 1. Optional: Add optional standard attributes. a. If the Standard Attributes section in the Available Attributes column is not expanded, click the feeder arrow ( ) icon to expand it. b. Click the blue add ( ) icon next to All to add all optional standard attributes, or separately select the optional standard attributes to add by clicking the blue add ( ) icon next to each one.  Note Required standard attributes are always included. 2. Optional: Remove optional standard attributes. In the Selected Attributes column, optional standard attributes display with a blue checkmark and required standard attributes display with a greyed-out checkmark as shown in the following screenshot. Uncheck any 234 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization -- 4 of 10 -- optional standard attributes you do not want to remove them from your customized template and hide them in the Excel file. 3. Optional: Edit standard attributes. a. In the Selected Attributes column, scroll to the standard attribute you want to edit. b. Hover over the standard attribute, then click the edit ( ) icon when it appears. The Edit Standard Attribute window displays. c. Optional: Make the standard attribute required. Click the Required checkbox under the Properties tab to make the standard attribute required.  Note For required standard attributes, the Required checkbox is always checked and the field is greyed out because it cannot be changed. d. Optional: Provide an alternative label and translation. The supported languages display under the Alternative label and translation dropdown menu. Enter the new column name in English and for any other selected language. Changes made to the standard attribute's label and translations will apply to all customization projects for that type of Upload/Download Excel template that include the standard attribute. e. Click OK. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization PUBLIC 235 -- 5 of 10 -- When you customize a standard attribute, a blue circle displays after its name in the Selected Attributes column. Customizing Custom Attributes in an Excel Template You can add custom attributes to the template and customize them as needed. Context Make one or more of the following customizations to the custom attributes you want to include in the template. Procedure 1. Optional: Add custom attributes. a. If the Custom Attributes section in the Available Attributes column is not expanded, click the feeder arrow ( ) icon to expand it. b. Click the blue add ( ) icon next to the All label to add all custom attributes, or separately select the custom attributes to add by clicking the blue add ( ) icon next to each one. 2. Optional: Remove custom attributes. In the Selected Attributes column, custom attributes and optional standard attributes display with a blue checkmark. Uncheck any custom attributes you do not want to remove them from your customized template. 236 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization -- 6 of 10 -- 3. Optional: Edit custom attributes. a. In the Selected Attributes column, scroll to the custom attribute you want to edit. b. Hover over the custom attribute, then click the edit ( ) icon when it appears. The Edit custom attribute window displays. c. Optional: Make the custom attribute read only. Check the Read only property to define custom attributes to be read only. You can only select this property when the Custom attribute's default value field is Purchase order since when this is the case, the custom attribute’s default value is taken from the purchase order. When the Custom attribute's default value is None, the supplier must fill in a value, which is why you cannot make the custom attribute read only. d. Optional: Make the custom attribute required. Check the Required checkbox under the Properties tab to make the custom attribute required. The supplier will be required to enter a value for this custom attribute in the Excel file. When you select the Required property for a custom attribute, its Include custom attribute in resulting cXML document field is checked automatically. e. Optional: Provide an alternative label and translation. The supported languages display under the Alternative label and translation dropdown menu. Enter the new column name in English and for any other selected language. Changes made to the custom attribute's label and translations will apply to all customization projects for that type of Excel template for Upload/Download that include the custom attribute. f. Optional: Provide an alternate data length. When the custom attribute was defined, the minimum and maximum length of its string value was set. If needed, you can change these lengths in the Alternate data length field. g. Optional: Enter a default value. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization PUBLIC 237 -- 7 of 10 -- The Custom attribute's default value field indicates which document the custom attribute’s default value is taken from. You can choose Purchase order or None. h. Optional: Include the custom attribute in the resulting cXML document. Check the Include custom attribute in resulting cXML document option to include the custom attribute in the cXML document that is generated when a supplier uploads the Excel template for that document type. i. Click OK. When you customize a custom attribute, a blue circle displays after its name in the Selected Attributes column. 238 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization -- 8 of 10 -- Customizing a Workbench Tile Use this procedure to create a customization project to customize the Workbench tile to include custom attributes as columns and filters. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Context You can customize the following Workbench tiles: • Items to Confirm • Orders  Note When you customize the Orders tile, the other tiles related to orders (New Orders, Changed Orders, Orders to Invoice, and Orders with service line) are also affected. • Items to Ship If you completed the first step (What project do you want to create?) on the Create Project page and clicked Save to save your project information, start with Step 1. If you completed the first step and clicked Next, start with Step 2. Procedure 1. From the Customization – Self Service page, in the row for your customization project, choose the more ( ) icon in the Actions column, then from the dropdown choose Edit. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization PUBLIC 239 -- 9 of 10 -- The Edit Project page opens with the second step, How do you want to customize your project, expanded and active. 2. Select up to five custom attributes to add to the Workbench tile. You can select all attributes, or you can individually select attributes from the Custom Attributes list. You can also click Create to create a new custom attribute; see Creating a Custom Attribute for a Customization Project [page 225] for instructions. 3. Optional: Edit your selected attributes. a. Click the edit ( ) icon next to an attribute to edit it. The Edit custom attribute popup opens. The attribute name displays on the second header line in the popup. 240 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization -- 10 of 10 --

Testing a Customization Project Use this procedure to check how an applied customization project will look before publishing it. Prerequisites • You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the permission. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization PUBLIC 241 -- 1 of 10 -- • You have completed steps 1 through 11 in Creating a Customization Project [page 231]. Procedure 1. If you have not already done so, sign in to a supplier test account that you have assigned the customization project to.Customization Editor 2. To test a customization project for a Workbench tile, proceed to Step 4 [page 242]. 3. Test customizations to the Upload/Download Ship Notice or Order Confirmation Excel template. a. Go to Quick Links Upload/Download Jobs and click Create. The Create/Edit Job popup opens. b. Create a job, run the job, and download the generated Excel template. Click the table ( ) icon to view the available columns and select the ones you want to display in the table. Publishing a Customization Project Use this procedure to test and publish a customization project. Prerequisites • You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Publisher permission. • The supplier groups that you want to assign your customization project to already exist in your account. 242 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization -- 2 of 10 -- Context After the Editor requests publication of a customization project to production, the Publisher can test and publish it. Procedure 1. Validate the customization project by logging on to your supplier test account and checking your customizations. See Testing a Customization Project [page 241].  Note If you are both the Editor and the Publisher, you can skip this step since you already validated the project. 2. Log on to your buyer production account. 3. Click Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service .  Note Account Settings is the user icon on the top right of the page. The Customization – Self Service page opens. 4. Optional: Assign suppliers to your customization project. You can assign suppliers before or after publishing the project. a. Click the more ( ) icon in the Actions column for the customization project you want to assign suppliers to and select Edit. The Edit Project page displays. b. Click the edit ( ) icon in the What project do you want to create? section. c. Select the suppliers. Choices are: • All (default) • None • Selected supplier groups – When chosen, a dropdown arrow shows. Click the arrow to show the list of supplier groups. d. Click Save. e. The Suppliers popup displays. Click OK. Your edits are saved, and the Customization – Self Service page displays. 5. Click the more ( ) icon in the Actions column for the customization project you want to publish and select Publish. The Publish to production popup opens. The popup reminds you that your customization project will apply to your chosen suppliers in your production account. 6. Click OK. The customization project is published. The Status column for the project shows Published. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization PUBLIC 243 -- 3 of 10 -- Creating New Versions of Customization Projects Buyers can create a new version of an existing customization project and make changes to it. The existing customization project must have the Published status. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Procedure 1. Sign in to your test account. 2. Click Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service .  Note Account Settings is the user icon on the top right of the page. The Customization – Self Service page opens. 3. Click the more ( ) icon in the Actions column for the Published customization project you want to create a new version for, and choose Create new version from the Project section. The following actions occur when you create a new version: • A warning message displays stating that the new version will be generated and the currently published version will not be affected. • The new version's major number is incremented. For example, if a new version is created from published version 1.3, the new version's number is 2.00. • The new version initially has status In Progress.  Remember Follow the normal workflow for projects to move the new version from In Progress to Pushed to Test and then to Requested to Publish. 244 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization -- 4 of 10 -- Results Suppliers assigned to a customization project always use the latest published version of the project. When you request to publish a new version, a warning message displays to remind you that this will affect all suppliers assigned to the project. After a new version of a customization project is published, suppliers will see this version in the user interface. For example, consider a new version of a customization project for quality notifications. The default behavior for the Serial no. field in the quality notification is to display the field. Since the Serial no. field is not a mandatory field, it can be hidden. If the field is hidden in the latest published version of a customization project, suppliers will not see the field when editing an existing quality notification, even though they may have previously inserted a value in the field. However, the Serial no. field information is still visible when suppliers download the cXML for the quality notification. Deleting Unpublished Customization Projects Buyers can delete customization projects that have the status Draft, In Progress, Pushed to Test, or Requested to Publish. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Context You can only delete a customization project when it is not yet published; that is, the project has the status Draft, In Progress, Pushed to Test, or Requested to Publish. You cannot delete a customization project that has the Published status. Procedure 1. Sign in to your test account. 2. Click Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service .  Note Account Settings is the user icon on the top right of the page. The Customization – Self Service page opens. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization PUBLIC 245 -- 5 of 10 -- 3. Click the more ( ) icon in the Actions column for the customization project you want to delete, and select Delete project from the Project section. A warning message displays to inform you that the version of the customization project will be permanently deleted. Results When you delete a customization project, only the latest version of the project is deleted. The table on the Customization – Self Service page has one row for each customization project, which shows information about the latest version of the project. • When you delete a customization project that was never published, the row is removed from the table. • When you delete a customization project that was previously published, the row for that project now shows information about the previously published version. For example, if you create version 2.0 and then delete it, and the previously published version is 1.3, the row for the project shows information about version 1.3. 246 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization -- 6 of 10 -- Upload/Download Templates for Data Retrieval and Update This chapter provides topics describing how to create custom transaction queries and generate spreadsheets to download, modify, and upload to update the information in SAP Business Network. Upload/Download Templates [page 247] Creating an Upload/Download Job [page 266] Running an Upload/Download Job and Making Data Changes to Upload [page 267] Deleting Download Files Created by an Upload/Download Job [page 269] Upload/Download Templates This section provides topics describing the search criteria and other information for individual Upload/Download job templates.
