Build priority Template for Upload/Download [page 247] Consignment Template for Upload/Download [page 249] Copy Partner Addition Template for Upload/Download [page 251] Copy Partner Replacement Template for Upload/Download [page 252] Forecast Template for Upload/Download [page 253] Inventory Template for Upload/Download [page 256] Manufacturing Visibility Template for Upload/Download [page 259] Order Change Requests Template for Upload/Download [page 261] Replenishment Template for Upload/Download [page 262] Transaction Document Report Template for Upload/Download [page 265] Build priority Template for Upload/Download You can generate an Upload/Download report in Excel format with forecast demand and purchase order quantities.  Note The path to the Upload/Download feature is as follows: • For buyers – Quick links Upload/Download SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Upload/Download Templates for Data Retrieval and Update PUBLIC 247 -- 7 of 10 -- • For suppliers – … Upload/Download The Build priority template file contains a row for each prioritized part, with the dates of the period in which the part is needed. The values for the first and last days of the week populate the Delivery Start date, Delivery End date, Shipment Start date, and Shipment End date fields for purchase order priorities, relative to the Requested Delivery date and Requested Ship date. Prerequisites To access this job type from the Upload/Download Jobs and Upload/Download Downloads tabs, you must have one of the following permissions: • Inbox and Order Access • Outbox Access • Forecast Visibility • Planning Collaboration Visibility To access this job type from the Upload/Download Uploads tab, you must have one of the following permissions: • Inbox and Order Access • Outbox Access  Note You cannot access the Uploads tab with only the Forecast Visibility or Planning Collaboration Visibility permission. Restrictions The Build priority template does not support: • File uploads of the Build priority download file • Reconfiguration of the download file layout or format Build priority Template Criteria The Upload/Download Jobs page provides the following search criteria for the Build priority job type: • Name – (Required) The name to give the job. • Type – (Required) Choose Build priority. • Customer – (Required, supplier view only) The name of the buyer whose data you want in the report. • Supplier – (Required) The name of the supplier whose data you want in the report. 248 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Upload/Download Templates for Data Retrieval and Update -- 8 of 10 -- • Demand type - Values are All (default), Forecast, or Purchase Order. • Date type - Values are Need By or Ship By. • Date Range – This field shows when a Date type value is chosen. • Start date • End date • Location • Supplier part number • Buyer part number • Product family • Product sub-family • Line of business • Program code • Planner code • Part category • Part type • Manufacturing type • Exclude zero forecast - Only for All or Forecast demand types. When checked, forecasts with a quantity of 0 are excluded from the results. Related Information Creating an Upload/Download Job [page 266] Running an Upload/Download Job and Making Data Changes to Upload [page 267] Deleting Download Files Created by an Upload/Download Job [page 269] Consignment Template for Upload/Download You can generate an Upload/Download report in Excel format to help reconcile your consignment records.  Note The path to the Upload/Download feature is as follows: • For buyers – Quick links Upload/Download • For suppliers – … Upload/Download This template consolidates goods receipt and consignment movement data for a specified supplier or buyer. When a line item in a goods receipt and a consignment movement share the same consignment tracking ID, the Consignment template retrieves the related purchase order, line item, and ship notice numbers. If no tracking ID is provided, the template attempts to find line items with other matching data, such as purchase order number and ship notice number. The Consignment template also shows stock-on-hand and consignment stock values. These values are derived from cXML ProductActivityMessage documents with a matching buyer part number, supplier part number, SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Upload/Download Templates for Data Retrieval and Update PUBLIC 249 -- 9 of 10 -- location, and process type, and which contain ConsignmentInventory or ConsignmentMovement elements with the processType attribute set to Consignment.  Restriction The stock-on-hand value is only populated if the user has the Planning collaboration entitlement or the Inventory collaboration entitlement. A Consignment job can generate data for up to the last 60 days. A maximum of 60,000 consignment report records can be downloaded. Reports with more than 60,000 records are truncated when downloaded. The Consignment job retrieves data for a single specified supplier or customer. Records in the download file are in alphanumeric order by a combination of Customer Part No., Supplier Part No., and Location values, in that order. Blank fields are sorted last. Each set of sorted records is then grouped by document type: goods receipt (Consignment In) and consignment movement (Consignment Out). Within each set of related goods receipt and consignment movement records, color highlighting identifies rows with the following calculations: • Blue highlighting—The total quantity of goods receipts or consignment movements for the record set. • Yellow highlighting—The most recent value of consignment inventory on hand for the record set. Consignment Template Criteria The Upload/Download Jobs page provides the following search criteria for the Consignment job type: • Name – (Required) The name to give the job. • Type – (Required) Choose Consignment. • Customer – (Required, supplier view only) The name of the buyer whose data you want in the report. • Supplier – (Required, buyer view only) The name of the supplier whose data you want in the report. • Start date • End date • Supplier part number • Buyer part number • Location Related Information Creating an Upload/Download Job [page 266] Running an Upload/Download Job and Making Data Changes to Upload [page 267] Deleting Download Files Created by an Upload/Download Job [page 269] 250 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Upload/Download Templates for Data Retrieval and Update -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SupplyChainCollaboratio.content: Copy Partner Addition Template for Upload/Download Buyers can use an Excel file to add a copy partner or logistics partner to multiple scheduling agreements, scheduling release agreements, and purchase orders in one operation. When you create and run a Copy Partner Addition type job from the Quick links Upload/Download Jobs page, you can download the generated Excel file and use it to add a copy partner to multiple orders: scheduling agreements, scheduling agreement releases, and purchase orders. The downloaded file can contain a maximum of 10,000 records. Files with more than 10,000 records are truncated when downloaded. Buyers send documents to the primary supplier, also copying the third-party logistic provider (copy supplier). Sometimes, the buyer might need to add the third-party logistics provider for the same documents, keeping the previous transaction data intact. The new copy partner has access and visibility to the new versions of the documents, while continuing business with the customer seamlessly. The former copy partner can no longer access the new versions of the documents. After adding or replacing the copy partner, an updated change purchase order with the latest copy partner information needs to be sent to the network, to replicate the current and subsequent documents for the new copy supplier.  Note Multiple copy suppliers cannot be added or replaced for the same purchase at the same time. A single updated change purchase order with the latest copy partner information must be processed successfully in the network before you can submit another new copy partner addition or replacement request. For each order you want to add the copy partner to, you change the value in the Partner to Use column of the Excel file to the supplier ANID of the copy partner. Then you upload the file using the Copy Partner Addition job type to submit your changes. The log for the uploaded file can contain a maximum of 10,000 records. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Copy Partner Update permission. Requirements The copy partner or logistics partner you want to add to the orders must be enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Upload/Download Templates for Data Retrieval and Update PUBLIC 251 -- 1 of 10 -- Copy Partner Replacement Template Criteria The Quick links Upload/Download Jobs page provides the following search criteria for the Copy Partner Replacement job type: • Name – (Required) The name to give the job • Type – (Required) Choose Copy Partner Addition. • Partner to add – (Required) The supplier ANID of the copy partner that you want to add to the orders. • Order creation start date • Order creation end date Related Information Creating an Upload/Download Job [page 266] Running an Upload/Download Job and Making Data Changes to Upload [page 267] Deleting Download Files Created by an Upload/Download Job [page 269] Copy Partner Replacement Template for Upload/Download Buyers can use an Excel file to change the copy partner or logistics partner in multiple scheduling agreements, scheduling release agreements, and purchase orders in one operation. After adding or replacing the copy partner, an updated change purchase order with the latest copy partner information needs to be sent to the network, to replicate the current and subsequent documents for the new copy supplier.  Note Multiple copy suppliers cannot be added or replaced for the same purchase at the same time. A single updated change purchase order with the latest copy partner information must be processed successfully in the network before you can submit another new copy partner addition or replacement request. For each order whose copy partner you want to replace, you change the value in the Partner to Use column of the Excel file to the supplier ANID of the new copy partner. Then you upload the file to submit your changes. The log for the uploaded file can contain a maximum of 10,000 records. 252 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Upload/Download Templates for Data Retrieval and Update -- 2 of 10 -- Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Copy Partner Update permission. Copy Partner Replacement Template Criteria The Quick links Upload/Download Jobs page provides the following search criteria for the Copy Partner Replacement job type: • Name – (Required) The name to give the job. • Type – (Required) Choose Copy Partner Replacement. • Partner to remove – (Required) The supplier ANID of the copy partner you’re replacing. • Supplier – (Optional) The primary supplier. • Order creation start date • Order creation end date Related Information Creating an Upload/Download Job [page 266] Running an Upload/Download Job and Making Data Changes to Upload [page 267] Deleting Download Files Created by an Upload/Download Job [page 269] Forecast Template for Upload/Download You can generate an Upload/Download file in Excel format for forecast data.  Note The path to the Upload/Download feature is as follows: • For both buyers and suppliers: Click the  Create icon and choose Upload/Download Jobs. To edit data in the Forecast spreadsheet, click the Aggregated - Supply Commit sheet if it exists, or click the Product sheet. Editable rows are highlighted, and also have the Forecast commit value in the Key figures column. Add values to the cells that are under date headings. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Upload/Download Templates for Data Retrieval and Update PUBLIC 253 -- 3 of 10 -- If a buyer sets a commit freeze horizon (by setting Forecast commit lock horizon, in days to a value other than zero), a Forecast job downloaded by a supplier from the Upload/Download Downloads tab applies the freeze to any time-series view the download uses: Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, or Yearly. A supplier is prevented from editing commit key figures for any time series within the locked period. You can create Forecast type jobs using any time series granularity (Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, or Yearly). When the buyer sets the preferred time series granularity to All, you can edit and commit Excel files in any time series granularity. However, when the buyer sets a specific preferred time series granularity, you can only edit and commit Excel files using that granularity. Suppliers can upload Forecast type jobs from the Upload/Download Jobs Uploads tab using any time series granularity (Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, or Yearly). If planning items contain attributes, attribute data is included when you download these items from the Upload/ Download Jobs tab. Suppliers can also upload planning items containing attributes from the Upload/ Download Uploads tab. Prerequisites To access this job type from the Upload/Download Jobs and Upload/Download Downloads tabs, you must have one of the following permissions: • Forecast Visibility • Planning Collaboration Visibility Suppliers may also access this job type from the Upload/Download Uploads tab if they have any of the permissions listed above. Restrictions The Excel file cannot be uploaded if the value in the part number field is entered as "0". When the template Excel file is uploaded, it is converted to one or more cXML documents in the backend. Each cXML document is limited to 500 items. If the template Excel file has more than 500 items, multiple cXML documents are created. Forecast Template Criteria The Upload/Download Jobs page provides the following search criteria for the Forecast job type:  Note When a supplier selects the Forecast job type, the Prepopulate Commit time series quantities with Forecast quantities checkbox also appears. Downloaded Excel files contain the key figures and attributes included in the view. • Sort by projected stock status – When this checkbox is checked, the records in the downloaded Excel file display in priority order based on their stock situation. The planning records in the planning horizon (defined by the Replenishment horizon, in number of days setting) are first sorted by their stock status severity using the following order: 1. Out of Stock. 2. Below Minimum (no Out of Stock). 3. Above Maximum (no Out of Stock or Below Minimum). 4. On Track. The planning records are then sorted within each of these four groups based on the date when the stock problem will occur.  Note Planning records not occurring in the defined planning horizon appear in the Excel file after the ones in the planning horizon even when their stock status severity is Out of Stock, Below Minimum, or Above Maximum. If the template Excel file has more than 500 items, multiple cXML documents are created. Time Bucket Maximum Date Range Daily 1825 days Weekly 260 weeks Monthly 60 months Quarterly 20 quarters Yearly 10 years • Start – The starting date in the time window. An additional field displays for you to enter a numeric value. • Custom – The starting date is a custom date. An additional field displays for you to enter a custom date. • End – The ending date in the time window. You can define the ending date in the following ways: • After – An additional field displays for you to enter a numeric value. The ending date is the date after the number of time buckets specified by this value. For example, if the Time bucket is Daily, and you enter 250 for the value, the ending date is after 250 days. An additional field displays for you to enter a custom date. • Download planning item attributes on all rows – Check to populate all cells in the Excel file with data. • Only download planning records with positive or negative time series data – Check to only include planning records that have at least one positive or negative value in the specified time window. • Supplier last modified – Date field. • Customer view – Choose All Views or choose a specific view. Restrictions • The Order Change Requests template for Upload/Download does not support change requests for scheduling agreements or scheduling agreement releases. • Buyers cannot upload responses with the Order Change Requests template. Order Change Request Template Criteria The Upload/Download Jobs page provides the following search criteria for the Order Change Request job type: • Name – (Required) A name to give the job. • Type – Choose Order Change Request. • Supplier – (Required) The name of the supplier whose data you want in the report. • Order number – The ID of the purchase order. • Company location • Company code • Order line-item number • Schedule-line number • Customer part number • Creation date – The creation date or range of creaiion dates to include. Field choices are: • Current Date Minus, with a Days field for the desired number of days before the current date • Current Date (default) • Current Date Plus, with a Days field for the desired number of days after the current date • Other, with fields to choose the Start date and End date of the time period • Customer-proposed delivery date – Field choices are the same as for Creation date. • Priority code • Reason code • Change by number of days – The number of days that a Customer proposed delivery date is earlier or later than the order's current Delivery date. Filter choices are None (the default), Days earlier, or Days later. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Upload/Download Templates for Data Retrieval and Update PUBLIC 261 -- 1 of 10 -- For the Days earlier and Days later choices, the filter shows Min and Max fields. In these fields, you specify the minimum and maximum number of days difference that you want to include in the search results. The Min and Max fields have the following requirements: • At least one of these fields, Min or Max, must contain a value. Valid values are a number from 0 to 999. Both fields can be the same number. • The value of Min must not be greater than the value of Max. The planning records are then sorted within each of these four groups based on the date when the stock problem will occur.  Note Planning records not occurring in the defined planning horizon appear in the Excel file after the ones in the planning horizon even when their stock status severity is Out of Stock, Below Minimum, or Above Maximum. 264 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Upload/Download Templates for Data Retrieval and Update -- 4 of 10 -- Related Information Creating an Upload/Download Job [page 266] Running an Upload/Download Job and Making Data Changes to Upload [page 267] Deleting Download Files Created by an Upload/Download Job [page 269] Transaction Document Report Template for Upload/ Download Buyer administrators can generate a custom list to show the status of of multiple types of transaction documents.  Note You must have buyer administrator authorizations.  Restriction The downloaded Transaction Document Report Excel file is for information only. You cannot use it to change and upload any values the file contains. The Transaction Document Report job type lets you retrieve information from multiple document types. A Transaction Document Report job can generate up to 20,000 records for download in Excel. The generated file displays each document, its status, error codes and error messages for failed documents, and other information. Transaction Document Report Template Criteria The Quick links Upload/Download Jobs page provides the following search criteria for the Transaction Document Report job type: Transaction Document Report Field Field Choices Supplier Specify a supplier name or leave blank to include all suppliers. Start date and End date Choose the dates during which included documents had any activity. • The date range can cover no more than seven days. • The Start Date can be no earlier than 180 days before the current date. The default is 7 days before the current date. • The End Date can be no later than the current date. The default is the current date. Monitoring status Choose from the dropdown menu. The default All includes all document statuses. Other possible values, listed in order of severity, are: Failed on Arrival, Failed, Delayed, In Process, and Successful. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Upload/Download Templates for Data Retrieval and Update PUBLIC 265 -- 5 of 10 -- Transaction Document Report Field Field Choices Document type Choose from the dropdown menu. The default All includes all document types. Report level Choose from the dropdown menu. • Default – Include the standard information. • Order Line Reference – Include the line-item number and buyer part number from the related purchase order. This filter only supports the Invoice, Order Confirmation, and Ship Notice document types. • Order Reference – Include the related purchase or- der number. This filter only supports the Component Consumption, Invoice, Order Confirmation, Quality Notification, and Ship Notice document types. Related Information Creating an Upload/Download Job [page 266] Running an Upload/Download Job and Making Data Changes to Upload [page 267] Deleting Download Files Created by an Upload/Download Job [page 269] Creating an Upload/Download Job Use this procedure to save customized queries to retrieve in spreadsheet form the transaction information you want from SAP Business Network. Prerequisites Review information about the Upload/Download job type you will use and what search information you will provide. See Upload/Download Templates [page 247]. Procedure 1. Click the  Create icon and choose Upload/Download Jobs. 2. The Jobs list is displayed. Click Create. 3. Enter a name for the job and select the job type from the Type dropdown. 4. Enter your search criteria and click Next Step. 266 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Upload/Download Templates for Data Retrieval and Update -- 6 of 10 --  Note For some filters, you can enter the first few letters of the term you want to search, instead of the exact term. The search result shows all the terms starting with the letters you entered. Multiple values can be selected for most of the filters. 5. If the Job needs to be executed On Demand by the user, then Run on Demand needs to be selected. If the Job needs to be executed by the system automatically in the background with specific schedules, then Schedule needs to be selected. 6. Once the schedule type is selected, then choose Next Step for Destination and Notification emails. Destination emails notify the users after the job is completed, with the link to download the file. Notification emails notify the users about the job status. If the job fails, the user can rerun, if required. Emails are not applicable to Run on Demand. 7. Click Review to go to the Review page to review your search criteria. Use Previous Step to go back to update any search criteria if needed. 8. Choose Create from the Review page to save the job definition. 9. When the schedule is selected, the frequency, start and end dates must be specified. Next Steps See Running an Upload/Download Job and Making Data Changes to Upload [page 267]. Related Information Deleting Download Files Created by an Upload/Download Job [page 269] Running an Upload/Download Job and Making Data Changes to Upload Use this procedure to generate a spreadsheet of transaction data to use to update information in SAP Business Network. Prerequisites The Upload/Download job you want to use is created. See Creating an Upload/Download Job [page 266]. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Upload/Download Templates for Data Retrieval and Update PUBLIC 267 -- 7 of 10 -- Procedure 1. Click the  Create icon and choose Upload/Download Jobs. 2. On the Jobs tab, locate the created job from the list, then click the  icon and choose Run from the menu.  Note The processing status will be updated automatically every 30 seconds because of auto refresh. 3. Switch to the Download tab. 4. Click the download icon  and open the file with your preferred editor. The template opens, already containing data from the selected transactions. The template spreadsheet is in Excel or CSV format, depending on the template type. If the query results exceed the maximum number of lines for the template, only the first lines up to the maximum amount are included. The rest of the lines are not included and no notification of excluded data is given.  Note All dates in an Upload/Download job download are shown by default in the user preferred time zone. This occurs regardless of the time zone used in the originating document, or the preferred time zone setting in your SAP Business Network account or operating system. 5. Enter values as desired. Make sure that required columns have values for each entry.  Note For some columns, you can enter the first few letters of the term you want to enter, instead of the exact term. The cell shows all the terms starting with the letters you entered. 6. Save the file. 7. Click the  Create icon and choose Upload/Download Jobs. 8. Click the Upload tab and choose Upload. The Upload file popup opens. 9. Upload your file. a. Choose the name of your template from the Type dropdown. b. Click Browse to choose the file to upload. c. Click Upload. The processing status will be updated automatically every 30 seconds because of auto refresh. Processing is finished when Completed shows in the Status column.  Note If the upload file has been Completed With Errors or failed , user can use the status column to view the log file and download as well, if required. 268 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Upload/Download Templates for Data Retrieval and Update -- 8 of 10 -- Related Information Deleting Download Files Created by an Upload/Download Job [page 269] Deleting Download Files Created by an Upload/ Download Job Use this procedure to delete accumulated download files for a specific Upload/Download job, and optionally delete the job that created those files. Context Performing this procedure deletes all files on the Download tab of the Download and Upload page that were created by the same job. You can delete downloads for one job at a time. You can also choose to delete the job.  Note Deleting job downloads, or deleting job downloads plus the job, cannot be undone. Procedure 1. Click the  Create icon and choose Upload/Download Jobs. 2. On the Jobs tab, locate the job whose downloads you want to delete, then click the  icon and choose Delete from the menu. A confirmation popup appears with two options: • Delete the job with downloads • Delete only downloads 3. Select the desired option and click Delete. 4. To delete a specific download, go to the Download tab and choose the  Delete icon for the corresponding download. file://SBN/split/SupplyChainCollaboratio.content: Component Shipment Report Buyers enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain can create a Component Shipment report in Excel format to show selected information from multiple component ship notices. Component Shipment Report Criteria Field Description Customer Choose a customer name, or use the default value (All Customers) Component Ship Notice No. To report on a component ship notice with a specific number, enter the number in the text box. This field is case sensitive. Tracking Number Enter the tracking number associated with the component ship notice. Order Number To report on an order with a specific number, enter the number in the text box. This field is case sensitive. Shipping Organization Code Enter the code for the organization that ships the components. Receipt Status Choose one or more statuses (Open, Partially Received, or Fully Received), or use the default value (All). Show Ship Notice By Choose which type of date from the ship notice to show and the date range to include. Choices are either Ship Notice Date, Estimated Delivery Date, or Actual Shipping Date. Maximum Results Returned Choose the maximum number of records returned by the re- port. The report supports up to 30,000 records. Component Shipment Report Sheets The Component Shipment Excel report organizes the information it retrieves in the following sheets: • Component Shipment – Lists all component shipments sent to suppliers at item level. Details include the names of the customer, supplier, and carrier, component details, and shipping details. • Serial Numbers – Lists the serial numbers associated with specific component shipments. Details include component ship-notice information, customer and supplier batch IDs, and component serial numbers. • Component Receipt Line Item – Includes component receipt numbers, line numbers, quantities, dates, and status. Related Information Creating a Report Template [page 287] Generating and Downloading Reports [page 288] Viewing a Generated Report with Double-Byte or Accented Characters [page 289] Open Orders Report The Open Orders report includes information on order status, routing status, schedule line-level, and line-item details. Prerequisites To use this report, you must belong to a role that provides the Purchase Order Report Administration permission. 274 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Reports for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain -- 4 of 10 -- To display all the scheduling agreements on the Open Orders Report, make sure that the value in the Quantity field is not less than the values in the received quantity, invoiced quantity, confirmed quantity, and cumulative ship quantity fields. Open Orders Report Criteria Field Description Customer (Suppliers only) By default, all buyers are included. Click Select to select buyers for the report. Supplier (Buyers only) By default, all suppliers are included. Click Select to select suppliers for the report. Search by supplier groups (Buyers only) Check this box, then click Select to select supplier groups for the report. Ship From Country (Requires SAP Business Network for Supply Chain) Select from the dropdown the country or region the order is shipping from. Start typing the name, then choose it from the list. Order Status Select one to nine values from the list to report on orders by fulfillment status. To create a broad report, use the default value, Any. Go to Reports Reports Criteria to view these columns and choose to display the columns and filters in the line item (current sheet) or schedule line (new sheet).  Note • New schedule line sheets are considered if order confirmations were completed at the schedule line. • Schedule line sheet, Additional information criteria, and the Block columns are available to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain only. • All dates are displayed in a separate column for time and timezone. • Protection is removed from the sheet and file. file://SBN/split/SupplyChainCollaboratio.content: Order Report with Serial-Number and Schedule-Line Information An Order report can include the serial numbers, schedule lines, quality certificates, or accounting information that customers provide in purchase orders. Prerequisites • You must be in a relationship that is enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. • You must belong to a role that provides the Purchase Order Report Administration permission.  Restriction If you generate a report from an Order report template that you created before this template supported serial-number and schedule-line information, the report generates in CSV format. However, if you open that report's definition and save it again, that process updates the template, and future reports generate in Excel. Order Report Criteria with Serial-Number and Schedule-Line Information Field Description Supplier (Buyers only) By default, all suppliers are included. Click Select to select suppliers for the report. Search by supplier groups (Buyers only) Check this box, then click Select to select supplier groups for the report. Customer (Suppliers only) By default, all customers are included. Click Select to select customers for the report. Order Number To report on an order with a specific number, enter an order number in the text box. Order Amount Enter an order amount. Do not enter currency symbols. Order Routing Status Choose a routing status, or use the default value, Any. Order Status Choose an order status, or use the default value, Any. Include active orders only Check this box to include only active orders in the results. Uncheck it to include shipped orders and obsolete orders. Order Date Select a range of order dates. The report can be run for a period up to 6 months. Max Results Returned Enter the maximum number or records returned by the report. The default is 100. The report supports up to 10,000 records. Include Spot Buy Marketplace Information Check this option to include spot buy information in the report. Include Line Item Information Check this option to include line item information in the report. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Reports for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain PUBLIC 281 -- 1 of 10 -- Field Description Include Order Confirmation Information Check this option to include order confirmation information in the report. This option is available only when Include Line Item Information is checked. Include Serial Number Information Check this option to include serial number information in the report. This option is available only when Include Line Item Information is checked and you are enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. Include Schedule Line Information Check this option to include schedule line information in the report. This option is available only when Include Line Item Information is checked and you are enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. Related Information Creating a Report Template [page 287] Generating and Downloading Reports [page 288] Viewing a Generated Report with Double-Byte or Accented Characters [page 289] Quality Inspection Report The Quality Inspection report type collects information from multiple quality inspections that meet the desired search criteria. Prerequisites The buyer system is enabled for the quality collaboration component. Restrictions If you generate a Quality Inspection report for an old quality inspection (that is, a quality inspection created before the Quality Inspection report became available), the report will only list information in the Inspections sheet. Quality Inspection Report Contents The Quality Inspection report type generates a spreadsheet in Excel format. Report information is organized in multiple sheets: • Inspections – Lists general information about each quality inspection in the report. 282 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Reports for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain -- 2 of 10 -- • Single Result – Records quality inspection characteristics containing multiple samples. • Summarized Recording – Records quality inspection characteristics containing a single sample. • Attachments – List of attachments for each quality inspection. Quality Inspection Report Search Criteria Field Description Customer (Suppliers only) Required. By default, all buyers are included. Click Select to select buyers for the report. Supplier (Buyers only) Required. By default, all suppliers are included. Click Select to select suppliers for the report. Customer Inspection No. The quality inspection number from the buyer system. Enter one value. Supplier Inspection No. The supplier identification number the supplier provided in the quality inspection. Enter one value. Purchase Order The purchase order number related to the quality inspection. Enter one value. Purchase Order Item The item number from the purchase order. Enter one value. Customer Location The buyer location identifier. Enter one value. Customer Part Number The buyer part number. Enter one value. Supplier Part Number The supplier part number. Enter one value. Customer Batch The buyer batch number. Enter one value. Supplier Batch The supplier batch number. Enter one value. Inspection Status Check one status to include, or leave no choice checked to include all statuses. Usage Decision The status of the usage decision. Check one value. Inspection Created Date Choose the dates during which included quality inspections were created. Inspection Due Date Choose the dates during which included quality inspections were due. Maximum Results Returned Choose from the dropdown the maximum number of results to include in the report. The lowest possible value is 100 results, and the highest possible value is 30,000 results.  Note When the number of results found exceeds the set maximum, the report shows a message and only the maximum allowed number of results is re- turned. Related Information Creating a Report Template Generating and Downloading Reports SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Reports for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain PUBLIC 283 -- 3 of 10 -- Viewing a Generated Report with Double-Byte or Accented Characters Quality Notification Report The Quality Notification Report shows information about problems reported by both buyers and suppliers. Quality Notification Report Criteria Field Description Supplier (Buyers only) By default, all suppliers are included. Click Select to choose individual suppliers for the report. Customer (Suppliers only) By default, all customers are included. Click Select to select customers for the report. Status Choose a status, or use the default value, Any. Quality notification type Choose a quality notification type, or use the default value, All. Supplier action Choose a supplier action, or use the default value, All. Creation date (Required) Set the range of creation dates, up to 30 days. Maximum Results Returned Enter the maximum number or records returned by the report. The default is 100. The report supports up to 10,000 records. Include Header Task Check this option to include header task information in the report. Include Header Activity Check this option to include header activity information in the report. Include Defect Check this option to include defect information in the report. Include Defect Task Check this option to include defect task information in the report. This option is available only when Include Defect is checked. Include Defect Activity Check this option to include defect activity information in the report. This option is available only when Include Defect is checked. Include Defect Cause Root Check this option to include defect cause root information in the report. This option is available only when Include Defect is checked. Include Defect Additional Batch Check this option to include defect addtional batch information in the report. This option is available only when Include Defect is checked. Related Information Creating a Report Template [page 287] Generating and Downloading Reports [page 288] Viewing a Generated Report with Double-Byte or Accented Characters [page 289] 284 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Reports for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain -- 4 of 10 -- Serial Number Report For orders that include serial numbers for line items, you can use the Serial Number Report template to generate serial number reports. The Serial Number Report contains information about lists of asset serial numbers contained in orders. When suppliers send a ship notice for an order, the buyer can require them to include unique asset serial numbers for each line item. This report helps you manage those serial numbers. Prerequisites • You must belong to a role that provides the Purchase Order Report Administration permission. • To generate serial number reports with data, orders must include serial numbers. Serial Number Report Criteria Field Description Supplier (Buyers only) By default, all suppliers are included. Click Select to choose individual suppliers for the report. Search by supplier groups (Buyers only) Check this box to include only certain supplier groups for the report. Customer (Suppliers only) By default, all buyers are included. Click Select to choose individual buyers for the report. Supplier Group Click Select to go to the Select supplier groups page and add one or more supplier groups for the report. When done, click OK to return to the report criteria page. Order Number To report on an order with a specific number, enter an order number in the text box. Order Amount Enter an order amount. Do not enter currency symbols. Order Routing Status Choose a routing status, or use the default value, Any. Order Status Choose an order status, or use the default value, Any. Include active orders only Check this box to include only active orders in the results. Uncheck it to also include shipped orders and obsolete orders. Order Date (Required) Select a range of order dates. The report can be run for a period up to 12 months. Max Results Returned Enter the maximum number of records the report can return. The default is 100. The report supports up to 100,000 records. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Reports for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain PUBLIC 285 -- 5 of 10 -- Serial Number Report Fields Field Description Order No. Purchase order number Supplier (Buyers only) Name of the supplier. Customer (Suppliers only) Name of the buyer. Line Number Order line number. Quantity Ordered quantity. UOM Unit of measure. Serial No Serial number value. Unit Price Unit price for the item. Unit Price Currency Currency associated with the unit price. Part Number Part number of the item. Customer Part Number Part number of the item in the buyer's system. Manufacturer Part Number Manufacturer part number. Need By The buyer’s need-by date from the order. Description Description of the item. Currency The currency used for monetary amounts in the order. Amount Amount for the item. Order Status The fulfillment status of the order. Version Version specified for the ordered item. Related Information Creating a Report Template [page 287] Generating and Downloading Reports [page 288] Viewing a Generated Report with Double-Byte or Accented Characters [page 289] 286 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Reports for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain -- 6 of 10 -- Creating a Report Template Use this procedure to define the information to retrieve in a report and when the report runs. Prerequisites See Report Types for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers [page 270] for topics about each report type that is available to buyers enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. Context When you create a report template, you set the type of report you want and criteria for which data to include in the generated report. You also set whether the report is generated manually or is run automatically at a schedule that you choose. Procedure 1. Choose Reports. The Reports page opens. 2. Click Create. The Reports creation wizard opens. 3. Enter a unique title to help you and other users easily identify this report from a list. For example, “Monthly Qualification Notification Report.” 4. Enter a description. The description is useful for identifying the scope and target of the report for all account users. For example, “Monthly report of all New and In-Process quality notifications.” 5. Choose a value from the Time zone list. Dates and times in your generated report use the time zone you select here, expressed as GMT +/-. In addition, SAP Business Network uses the time zone to determine the range of information collected for the report. 6. Choose a language. SAP Business Network uses this language for labels in the generated report file. The report displays data in the language in which the information was entered into the system. 7. Choose a report type. See Report Types for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers [page 270] for details about each report type. 8. Click Next. SAP Business Network displays the Schedule page with details for the report type you selected. 9. Click either Manual Report or Scheduled Report. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Reports for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain PUBLIC 287 -- 7 of 10 -- • You generate a manual report from the Reports page. For more information, see Generating and Downloading Reports [page 288]. • SAP Business Network automatically generates a scheduled report using the frequency that you specify. 10. If you chose Scheduled Report, SAP Business Network refreshes the page and displays the Scheduling section. Do the following: a. Select a date range. By default, a scheduled report includes 3 months, beginning with tomorrow’s date.  Note The maximum date range you can include in Order reports is 6 months. b. Choose a value from the Automatically Run list to set the report generation frequency. c. Enter up to three email addresses, each separated by single comma. SAP Business Network sends a notification to these addresses when the report status is Processed. 11. Click Next. 12. On the Criteria page, choose the parameters for the report. For information about the criteria available for your report type, see Report Types for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers [page 270]. 13. Click Submit. SAP Business Network puts your report into the queue. You can view and download it when its status is Processed. Related Information Generating and Downloading Reports [page 288] Viewing a Generated Report with Double-Byte or Accented Characters [page 289] Generating and Downloading Reports Use this procedure to generate a report from a report template or to edit and save an existing report. Prerequisites A report template that can retrieve the desired data was created. For more information, see Creating a Report Template [page 287]. 288 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Reports for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain -- 8 of 10 -- Context Your organization can generate a maximum of 100 reports, including up to 20 scheduled reports. SAP Business Network deletes generated reports from your account after 30 days. Procedure 1. Click Reports. The Reports page opens and shows the list of created report templates. 2. Determine your next step. • To download the existing version of a report, skip to Step 3. • To generate an updated report, choose the desired report template and click Run. SAP Business Network adds your report to the queue and returns you to the Reports page. To update the statuses of reports on the Reports page, click Refresh Status. You can view and download the report when its status changes to Processed. 3. To view and download an existing report, select the desired report template, click Download, then click one of the following: • Open to view the report. Your browser starts Microsoft Excel and displays the report. • Save to save the report to your hard disk. Related Information Viewing a Generated Report with Double-Byte or Accented Characters [page 289] Viewing a Generated Report with Double-Byte or Accented Characters Use this procedure to change encoding and delimiter settings of files that include double-byte or accented characters, which prevent correct display in some applications. Context To keep a record of a scheduled report, save the report to your hard disk each time the report runs. If a report file is over 1 MB, SAP Business Network stores it in zip format and displays a zip icon in the Size column for that report. SAP Business Network deletes generated reports from your account after 30 days. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Reports for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain PUBLIC 289 -- 9 of 10 -- Procedure 1. Choose Reports from the menu bar. 2. Select the report and click Download. Your browser prompts you to indicate whether you want to view the report or save it to disk. 3. Click Save. 4. Modify the file location and name, if necessary, and click Save. 5. Click Close. 6. Start a text viewer. 7. Click to open a file. 8. Choose All Files in the Files of type list. 9. Select the file you want to open. 10. Choose Unicode in the Encoding list. 11. Choose All Files in the Save as type list. 12. Click Save. If your browser prompts you to overwrite the existing file of the same name, click Yes. 13. Close the file and close the text viewer. 14. Start a spreadsheet application. 15. Click to open a file. 16. Choose All Files in the Files of type list. 17. Open your saved report file. 18. In Step 1 of the Text Import Wizard, choose Delimited for the Original data type, and click Next. 19. In Step 2 of the Text Import Wizard, choose Comma in the Delimiters section, and click Next. 20.Click Finish. The file displays in the spreadsheet application 290 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Reports for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SupplyChainCollaboratio.content: Field Description Data Identifier You can select the checkbox Include in Number Format for the data identifiers to be included in the numbering format. You can select the Handling Unit level structure from the following options: • Single Level Packing • Multi Level Packing • Mixed Multi Level Packing Issuing Agency Code You can enter the agency code. Company Identification Number You can enter your company ID. Serial Number You can enter the Start Value and End Value. Rolling From the dropdown, select Yes or No.  Note You can set GTL, handling unit, and advance ship notice numbering for documents from 1 to 100. If document 100 is reached, expect the following scenarios: • If you have rolling enabled, the document rolls back to 1. This results in duplicate document numbering. • If rolling is disabled, the following document must be created with a manually entered unique value— for example, Document 120. Context You can configure how the advanced packaging wizard for ship notices will automatically number handling units. Suppliers can choose to override this configuration with their own auto-numbering settings. Procedure 1. Choose Administration Configuration Document Number Preferences . 2. In the Handling Units section, click Create. 3. On the Configure Numbering page, enter the desired numbering criteria and constraints and click OK. 4. Verify the configuration and click Save. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 21 -- 1 of 10 -- Next Steps • Enable transaction rule Allow suppliers to use advanced packaging on ship notices for the suppliers you want to use this feature. • Provide your packaging instructions. See Create and upload packaging instructions [page 23]. Configuring GTL Numbering Use this procedure to set GTL numbering for handling units in a ship notice. Prerequisites You must be a buyer administrator. Context As a buyer administrator, you can configure Global Transport Level (GTL) numbering for the Handling Unit number range. Procedure 1. Sign in as a buyer administrator. 2. Go to Manage Profile. 3. Select Document Number Preferences from the list. 4. In the Handling Units tab, click Create. 5. In the Configure Numbering page, choose GTL as the configuration type.  Note You can set GTL, handling unit, and advance ship notice numbering for documents from 1 to 100. If document 100 is reached, expect the following scenarios: • If you have rolling enabled, the document rolls back to 1. This results in duplicate document numbering. • If rolling is disabled, the following document must be created with a manually entered unique value— for example, Document 120. 22 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers -- 2 of 10 -- Creating Packaging Instructions Use this procedure to provide suppliers their requirements for packing items for shipment. Prerequisites • Enable the Allow suppliers to use advanced packaging on ship notices rule for the suppliers you want to use the advanced packaging wizard.  Note When this rule is enabled, transaction rule Require suppliers to provide a unique Global Individual Asset ID for line items on ship notices is ignored. To allow GS1 numbering, enable the Require suppliers to provide a Global Individual Asset ID for line items on ship notices that conforms to the Serial Shipping Container Code (SSCC) format rule. • (Optional) Configure auto-numbering. See Configure auto-numbering of handling units [page 20]. Context You can download an Excel template to create packaging specifications for different types of material. You then upload the files for suppliers to use with the advanced packaging wizard. Procedure 1. Choose Quick links Upload/Download Uploads , then click Upload. 2. In the Upload File popup, choose Packaging Instructions from the Type dropdown. The Download template link displays. 3. Click Download template and choose where to save the file. The Packaging Instructions template downloads. 4. Open the template file and enter data for all desired material types. Only the most recently uploaded instructions are used. 5. Choose Quick links Upload/Download Uploads , then click Upload. 6. In the Upload File popup, enter a name to call the upload and choose Packaging Instructions from the Type dropdown. Then browse to choose the desired file and click Upload. The Uploads page opens and shows your uploaded file. • If the upload status is Processing, choose Refresh Status to update the status. • If the upload status is Completed, processing is finished. • If the upload status is Failed, choose the download icon  in the Log column for troubleshooting information. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 23 -- 3 of 10 -- Related Information Packaging Instructions Fields [page 24] Packaging Instructions Fields The following fields appear on the Instructions sheet of the Packaging Instructions template: Field Description Packaging Specification ID A unique ID for the packaging specification. Capacity Not used. Capacity information is taken from the Maximum Capacity field. Material The customer product ID of the product to be packed. Material Description Unit Required. The value of Unit from the ship notice. Packaging Level Packaging Material The packaging material to contain the product. Packaging Material Description Maximum Capacity The capacity value used by the system. Minimum Capacity Length Unit Length Height Unit Height Width Unit Width Volume Unit Volume Net Weight The total weight, excluding packaging. Gross Weight The total weight, including packaging. Unit Gross Weight Total Volume Unit Total Volume Parent Packaging Material The next larger packaging material that can contain a number of the packaging materials. 24 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers -- 4 of 10 -- Field Description Create Handling Unit Set to Yes to generate handling units automatically, based on these specifications. Valid values are Yes, No, and blank, which is the same as No. Default is blank. Allow Mixed Required. Set to Yes to allow different materials in the same innermost handling unit. Valid values are Yes, No, and blank, which is the same as No. Default is blank. Is Auxiliary Required. Set to Yes if the item as an auxiliary material, or set to No if the item is a handling unit. Valid values are Yes and No. A blank field is not valid. Is Printable Controls whether a printer icon  displays in the SAP Business Network user interface for printing the handling unit label. Valid values are Yes and No. If an entry has no value set, that entry is processed as having Is Printable set to No. Is Default Identifies whether the packaging instruction is preselected for the supplier by the packaging wizard. Valid values are Yes and No. If an entry has no value set, that entry is processed as having Is Default set to No. The following rule is introduced in the Handling Unit supplier profile that enables default packaging instructions as a default in addition to specific instructions: The Allow suppliers to choose default packaging instructions for buyer parts that already have part specific instruction rule is added to the handling unit supplier profile in Create handling unit profile for Ship Notice. When buyers check this rule, their suppliers can determine how to pack items that the buyers have already provided part- specific instructions about. These enhancements provide the capability to use the assignment information for generic packaging instructions. Earlier, this was limited to material specific packaging instructions. There are now more determination options available for generic packaging instructions, like those based on Vendor ID or Plant information. The following fields appear on the Supplier and Plant Assignment sheet of the Packaging Instructions template: Field Description Packaging Specification ID A unique ID for the packaging specification. Supplier ANID Ariba Network ID for the supplier. Plant ID Plant ID. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 25 -- 5 of 10 -- Creating a Handling Unit Profile Use this procedure to assign advanced packaging tasks to suppliers. Context As a buyer administrator, you can create handling unit profiles to assign to one or more suppliers or supplier groups. A profile enables the specified suppliers to do one or more of the following advanced packaging tasks: Handling-unit profile capability Description Enable suppliers to add handling unit Enabled by default. When enabled, suppliers can add a new handling unit to the advanced packaging wizard. Enable suppliers to move and rearrange the handling units on the Confirm Packing screen Enabled by default. When enabled, suppliers can move materials from one handling unit to another available handling unit. Enable suppliers to edit items on the Confirm Packing screen Enabled by default. When enabled, suppliers can edit the quantity of a handling unit. Enable suppliers to edit values on Define Instructions screen Enabled by default. Enable suppliers to edit the dimension values of handling units Disabled by default. When enabled, supplers can change the following values for a handling unit: • On the Define packaging instructions page, suppliers can change Length, Height, and Width. • On the Confirm packing plan page, suppliers can change Length, Height, Width, Gross weight, and Net weight.  Note The supplier cannot change dimension values on the Print labels page. Enable suppliers to add empty packaging material to a handling unit Disabled by default. When enabled, suppliers can add empty packaging material, such as boxes, to handling units in a packaging plan, except to the highest-level handling unit. The empty packaging material can be used to help stabilize items in a partially filled handling unit, with or instead of auxiliary material. Show auxiliary materials in auto packaging Disabled by default. When enabled, suppliers can see on the Confirm packaging page the auxiliary materials in an automatically generated packaging plan, and make any desired changes. When disabled, suppliers can still add or remove auxiliary materials to a packaging plan that is not automatically generated. 26 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers -- 6 of 10 -- Handling-unit profile capability Description Enable suppliers to remove auxiliary materials in auto packaging This task requires that the task Show auxiliary materials in auto packaging is also enabled. When enabled, suppliers can delete auxiliary materials from automatically generated packaging plans on the Confirm packaging page. Enable suppliers to add auxiliary materials in auto packaging This task requires that the task Show auxiliary materials in auto packaging is also enabled. When enabled, suppliers can add auxiliary materials to an automatically generated packaging plan on the Confirm packaging page. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Manage Profile Manage Handling Unit Profile for Ship Notice . 2. Click Create Profile. 3. Enter a profile name, specify which suppliers the profile includes or excludes, and choose what capabilities to assign. You can specify to include or exclude one or more suppliers, supplier groups, or a combination. In the Include or Exclude field, start typing a name, then choose one from the list. 4. Click Save. The new profile name and list of suppliers displays on the Manage Handling Unit Profile for Ship Notice page, with Edit and Delete actions for the profile. Freight Carrier List Configuration As a buyer administrator, you can upload customized freight carrier lists for your suppliers. Buyer administrators can upload any number of customized freight carrier lists. The most recently uploaded list is made available to suppliers when creating ship notices. If you use preferred carriers for shipments from your suppliers, you can upload them to your account from a CSV file. Otherwise, suppliers must select one of the following default freight carriers: • Airborne Express • DHL • FedEx • UPS • US Postal Service • Other SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 27 -- 7 of 10 -- Uploading a Customized List of Freight Carriers Use this procedure to upload freight carrier lists for supplier use in ship notices. Context As a buyer administrator, you can upload any number of customized freight carrier lists. The most recently uploaded list is made available to suppliers when creating ship notices.  Note If you upload an empty list, the uploaded file is ignored and the default list of all carriers is displayed to suppliers in the Carrier Name field when creating ship notices. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. Choose Supplier Enablement > Manage Vendors. 3. Click Upload > Carrier Codes. 4. Click Download template on the Upload Carrier Codes page. 5. Starting on row six of the template file, enter the carrier information.  Caution Do not change or delete the information in rows one to five of the template. • You can add details for up to 2500 carriers to the file. • You can upload the file as a CSV file, or you can upload a ZIP file that contains the CSV file. a. In column A, enter carrier codes. b. In column B, enter matching carrier names. c. Save the file. 6. Enter a name for the upload file in the Name field on the Upload Carrier Codes page. 7. Click Browse and browse for the saved CSV file or ZIP file. 8. Click Upload. If an error is found during upload, an error message appears, and the Upload button changes to Reload. Correct the file, browse for it again, and click Reload. Results The uploaded file displays in the Upload Details table. 28 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers -- 8 of 10 -- Editing a Freight Carrier List Use this procedure to edit carrier lists. Prerequisites You have signed in to your SAP Business Network buyer account as an administrator. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement > Manage Vendors. 2. Click Upload > Carrier Codes. 3. (Optional) Enter the name of the relevant CSV file in the Name field under Search Filters and click Search. 4. Click the name of the relevant CSV file in the Upload Details table. 5. Click Download File, make the required changes to the carrier list, save the file, and then upload it. Related Information Freight Carrier List Configuration [page 27] Uploading a Customized List of Freight Carriers [page 28] Replenishment Order Configuration Use this procedure to configure how suppliers manage their planned replenishments. Prerequisites • You must be a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Planning Settings Authorization permission. • If you plan to change the Replenishment time bucket setting in an existing custom configuration, prepare all affected suppliers for the change: • Tell all suppliers when you plan to make this change. • Tell suppliers to publish all their planned replenishments for existing time buckets, to avoid data loss. • Make sure all suppliers have completed publishing their planned replenishments before you change the setting. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 29 -- 9 of 10 -- Context By creating a custom configuration of settings, you can apply to certain suppliers a set of replenishment-order business rules that differ from the System default settings. Procedure 1. Choose Planning Settings Assign suppliers . 2. Click the edit ( ) icon of the desired custom configuration for the Replenishment orders process type. If you instead want to create a new custom configuration, click the Add configuration button in the upper right corner. Then in the section that opens, do the following: • Enter a name for the new configuration. • Set the Process type field to Replenishment orders. 3. Make your configuration choices in the Planning process section: Option Description Suppliers or Supplier groups Add the suppliers or supplier groups the custom configuration ap- plies to.  Restriction A mix of individual suppliers and supplier groups in the same custom configuration is not supported. If a member of a supplier group that is assigned a custom planning configuration is assigned as an individual supplier to another config- uration, settings are applied to that supplier in the following priority: 1. Individual-supplier configuration 2. Supplier-group configuration 3. System default settings Replenishment horizon, in number of days Enter the replenishment horizon. The default is 180 days. Replenishment time bucket Choose Daily (default) or Weekly. Refresh planning data from current date Choose Yes or No (default). When this setting is enabled, a product activity message with changes for planning collaboration informa- tion clears all planning information between the current date and the earliest date in the message. Allow suppliers to edit price Choose Yes or No (default). Require suppliers to replenish within the proposed range of minimum and maximum quantities Choose Yes or No (default). Allow suppliers to send planned replenishment Choose Yes or No (default). Maximum number of line items allowed in replenishment orders Enter the maximum number to allow. The default is 1,000 line items. 4. Click Save. 30 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers -- 10 of 10 --

Next Steps If you changed the Replenishment time bucket setting, tell all affected suppliers which view to now use: Daily or Weekly. Suppliers will no longer have edit access in the other view. Rejection Code Configuration for Order Change Requests Buyer administrators can use CSV templates to upload rejection codes for their suppliers. The Upload dropdown on the Supplier Enablement Manage Vendors page provides the following CSV templates: • Priority Codes • Reason Codes • Rejected Reason Codes Buyer administrators can download these templates, populate them with values for their suppliers to use, and upload the information to SAP Business Network. Their supplliers can then use these codes when rejecting a change request. All codes are maintained in the buyer's ERP system. For details, see Uploading Priority, Reason, and Rejected-Reason Codes [page 31]. Uploading Priority, Reason, and Rejected-Reason Codes Use this procedure to upload change-request rejection codes to SAP Business Network. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer user assigned a role with the User Administration permission. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 31 -- 1 of 10 -- Context Buyer administrators can use CSV templates to import to SAP Business Network the lists of codes to use in a buyer's change request or in a supplier's change-request rejection. You can upload codes multiple times. Each upload replaces the previous codes. Procedure 1. Go to Supplier Enablement Manage Vendors . 2. Choose Upload, then choose one of the following code types from the dropdown: • Priority Codes – Used by buyers in change requests. • Reason Codes – Used by buyers in change requests. • Rejected Reason Codes – Used by suppliers in change-request rejections. The Upload File page for the code type opens. 3. Click Download latest template version and save the template file.  Note To download a Rejected Reason Code template, first select Change Request Rejected reason codes from the Description field. 4. Open the downloaded template file for editing. 5. Starting on row 5 of the template file, enter each code and its description.  Caution Do not change or delete the information in rows 1 to 4 of the template. 6. For the Priority Codes, Reason Codes, and Rejected Reason Codes templates, enter in the Code Language column all languages that are valid for each code. The en value (English) is required for all codes. A list of the available language codes is provided in the template. 7. Save the edited template. 8. Choose Supplier Enablement Manage Vendors . 9. Choose Upload and select the code type to upload. The upload page for the code type opens. 10. Enter a name in the Name field to give to the file you're uploading. 11. Click Browse and select the saved template file you want to upload. 12. If you are uploading the Rejected Reason Codes template, click Description and choose Change Request Rejected reason codes. 13. Click the Upload button. The uploaded file's name is added to the Upload Details table at the end of the upload page. If necessary, click Refresh Status to update the file's upload status. If an error occurs during upload, an error message appears, and the Upload button changes to Reload. Correct the error in the file, browse for the file again, and click Reload. 32 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers -- 2 of 10 -- Planning and Forecast Configuration Buyer administrators can set up key figures, attributes, and views to use in planning and forecast collaboration. Key Figures [page 33] Attributes for Planning Views [page 46] Forecast and Planning Collaboration Views [page 52] Key Figures Buyers and suppliers can use key figures in planning and forecast collaboration. Key figures contain numeric data that is represented either as a quantity or as a monetary value. Buyers and suppliers use key figures for planning and forecast collaboration to communicate about goods and materials. Typically, buyers want information about a set of key figures, not just one or two. A set of key figures is referred to as a view. Suppliers provide buyers with information about key figures, either through the user interface from the Planning Planning Collaboration page or from the ... Upload/Download Jobs tab using Excel files. There are two types of key figures: • Standard – A standard key figure is a figure that cannot be derived or calculated from other figures, such as the number of employees in a company. Other examples are sales, fixed costs, variable costs, and quantity produced. One example of a standard key figure used in planning collaboration is ORDER_FORECAST. This key figure contains the order forecast quantity. • Calculated – A calculated key figure is a figure that is derived or calculated using other figures. For example, if you have the SALES_REVENUE and EMPLOYEES key figures, you can create a calculated key figure with the sales revenue per employee using formula SALES_REVENUE/EMPLOYEES. Key figures used in a formula for a calculated key figure can be either standard or calculated key figures. One example of a calculated key figure used in planning collaboration is FORECAST_DEVIATION. This key figure is a calculation of the accuracy of the actual forecast demand from the committed forecast demand. It is calculated by subtracting the order forecast quantity (ORDER_FORECAST) from the forecast committed quantity (FORECAST_COMMIT). The formula is FORECAST_COMMIT-ORDER_FORECAST. See Key Figures Reference for Planning and Forecast Collaboration Views [page 34] for a list of the key figures defined for the planning and forecast collaboration views. See Key Figures Reference for the Component Planning Collaboration View [page 37] for a list of the key figures defined for component planning collaboration. Creating Custom Key Figures Use this procedure to create key figures for planning collaboration views. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Planning Settings Authorization permission. Context Buyer administrators can create custom key figures for planning collaboration views. You can create up to 100 custom key figures across all views. Procedure 1. Select Planning Settings Manage views . 2. Choose a view. The view's details page displays with the Key figures tab open. 3. Click Create new. The New key figure popup opens. 4. Enter information in the Key figure display name field and optionally in the Description field. The Key figure display name value automatically populates the Configuration ID field. 5. Choose Buyer or Supplier as the data source. 6. To enable any of the following key figure options, move its toggle switch to the On position. • Visible - Makes the key figure visible in the view. • Editable by supplier - Allows suppliers to edit the key figure. • Show in Excel - Includes the key figure in the Microsoft Excel file. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 39 -- 9 of 10 -- • Time-based formula - Indicates the Expression field value is time-based. 7. Enter a value in the Expression field. • If the Time-based formula toggle switch is in the Off position, add to the Expression field the value of attribute customType in the PlanningTimeSeries cXML element. • If the Time-based formula toggle switch is in the On position, the formula editor appears. The right side of the editor displays numerals, operator symbols, and names of existing key figures to use in the formula. • Click an element to add it to the formula area on the left side of the editor. Some elements are not visible unless they are valid for the insertion point. • result[i-1]： Reference the value of the same key figure in the previous time bucket. • [i-1]： Reference the value of another key figure in the previous time bucket. • [i]： Reference the value of another key figure in the current time bucket. • CURRENT_DATE: You can use this element to add a condition before adding formulas for the current time bucket and future time buckets.  Note To make the formula effective, do either of the following: • Add an i === CURRENT_DATE ? condition before adding formulas with the result[i-1] or the [i-1] elements. • Use the result[i-1] element in the else part of the condition to reference the value of the same key figure in the previous time bucket. • To delete an added element, hover over the element and click the x that appears. 8. Click Save. The custom key figure is added to the view. Results If the key figure uses a formula, the formula is first validated. If the formula has an error, a message that describe the error displays. Example: Time-based formula when a divisor value might be less than 1 A key-figure value used to divide a number in a formula might be zero or a negative number. Dividing by zero or a negative number causes an error in the formula calculation. To prevent this error, you can construct your formula to test for such values and, if found, divide instead by a number you specify in the formula. For example, assume the following formula with A , B , C , and D as key figures: A[i] = B[i] + C[i] / D[i] 40 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers -- 10 of 10 --

D[i] : 1) This added syntax first tests whether the value of D[i] is greater than 0. If D[i] is not greater than 0, the formula is instead divided by 1, the number that is specified in the formula. Example: Time-based formulas that reference past key figure values You may need to show a calculated key figure in a planning view that is calculated by the value of the same key figure in the previous time bucket, or the value of another key figure in the previous time bucket. For example, suppose you are customizing formulas for MY_KEY_FIGURE. When editing the formula for future time buckets, you want to reference the value of ORDER_FORECAST in the previous time bucket. In this case, the formula is as follows: MY_KEY_FIGURE = i === CURRENT_DATE ? ORDER_FORECAST[i] : ORDER_FORECAST[i-1] + 100 If the date is the current date, the value of MY_KEY_FIGURE is equal to the value of ORDER_FORECAST in the current time bucket; if the date is a future date, the value of MY_KEY_FIGURE is equal to the value of ORDER_FORECAST in the previous time bucket plus 100. Using the previous example, suppose you want to reference the value of MY_KEY_FIGURE in the previous time bucket in the formula for future time buckets. In this case, the formula is as follows: MY_KEY_FIGURE = i === CURRENT_DATE ? ORDER_FORECAST[i] : result[i-1] + 200 If the date is the current date, the value of MY_KEY_FIGURE is equal to the value of ORDER_FORECAST in the current time bucket; if the date is a future date, the value of MY_KEY_FIGURE is equal to the value of MY_KEY_FIGURE in the previous time bucket plus 200.
