Attributes can be included in views along with key figures. There are two types of attributes: • Standard – Standard attributes are predefined. Some examples of standard attributes are the following: • Customer location • Customer part no. • Lead time • Planner code Planning items are defined by the unique combination of the standard attributes Customer part no. and Customer location. The display name and behavior of standard attributes is fixed and cannot be altered. • Customer-defined – You can use customer-defined attributes to add information to planning items. You can also use customer-defined attributes as additional identifiers for planning items. For example, you could add a customer-defined attribute called Promotion and use the value of this attribute to help identify planning items.  Note Unlike key figures, customer-defined attributes included in views are not automatically updated by transactions like purchase orders, ship notices, goods receipts, and so on. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 51 -- 1 of 10 -- Forecast and Planning Collaboration Views Buyers use views to help visualize planning data. Views are used in planning and forecast collaboration to share information between buyers and suppliers. A view is a collection of key figures (standard, calculated, and custom) and attributes (standard and customer-defined) that provide a window into the planning data. The following table lists the standard views: View Description Aggregated forecast across locations Aggregated version of the forecast view across multiple loca- tions Component planning collaboration view Component planning collaboration data for a finished good and its components.  Note The Component planning collaboration view does not support customer-defined attributes. External manufacturing visibility Data about external manufacturing items Forecast Forecast data for planning items Supplier managed inventory Information about supplier-managed inventory Supplier managed inventory days-of-supply Information about the days of supply left on the supplier's inventory Supplier managed replenishment Information about supplier-managed replenishment Supplier managed replenishment days-of-supply Information about the days of supply of replenishment You can configure views to contain the exact information you need. Some example configurations are hiding key figures, renaming key figure display names, adding custom key figures, and adding customer-defined attributes. See Customizing Key Figures and Attributes for a View [page 53] for more information about configuring views. In addition to the standard views, you can create custom views, each containing customized key figures and attributes. Custom views help make planning collaboration more efocient since only the fields that are needed for planning items are included. Tailoring multiple planning views to fit specific business needs, and assigning the most appropriate view to each planning item, ensures easier adoption for suppliers. It also minimizes errors and improves communication between trading partners. For example, you could create custom views for forecast planning items belonging to the Wholesale line of business and for forecast planning items belonging to the Retail line of business. Each of these views would have a different set of key figures and attributes. See Custom Views [page 54] for more information about custom views. This order is visible in all the view's planning records, both in the user interface and in downloaded Excel files created from running Upload/Download jobs. As a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Planning Settings Authorization permission, you can create a custom view. You do this by duplicating an existing view, standard or custom, customizing the newly-created view's key figures and attributes, and defining conditions for it. Prerequisites • You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Planning Settings Authorization permission. • You are enabled for one of the following: • The forecast collaboration component. • SAP Business Network Planning Collaboration, which does not also require SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. You can also rename a custom view by choosing Edit or delete a custom view by choosing Delete. 54 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers -- 4 of 10 --  Note • Both standard and custom views can be duplicated. • Standard views cannot be edited or deleted. You need to add one or more conditions to a custom view. Custom views use conditions to determine which planning items to assign to the view. See Defining Conditions for a Custom View [page 56]. If no conditions are defined for a custom view, the view will not be used for any planning items, and the view will be flagged on the Planning Settings Manage views page with a warning icon to indicate the view is incomplete.  Note Standard views cannot be assigned conditions since they are used when planning items do not match the conditions of any custom views for a process type. cXML Uploads SAP Business Network assigns a planning item to a view when cXML updates are made. If the planning item's view was deleted since the last cXML update, the standard view is used for the planning item. When a planning item's view is modified, the next time a cXML update occurs, the view criteria are reevaluated. The planning item’s view always matches the existing criteria at the last cXML update. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 65 -- 5 of 10 -- SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration SAP Business Network business rules allow buyer administrators to control aspects of how order confirmations, ship notices, and other documents are created and how they flow between suppliers and buyers. Two categories of SAP Business Network business rules are important for the supply chain collaboration solution: • Default Transaction Rules These rules are available on the Administration Configuration Default Transaction Rules page, and they are applied to all suppliers who are enabled for supply chain collaboration functionality. • Supplier Group Rules These rules are supplier-group specific rules that are enabled on the Supplier Group Transaction Rules page. Supplier group rules allow you to set confirmation and ship notice rules differently for specific sets of suppliers. For suppliers who are added to a group, rule settings that are created at the supplier group level override rule settings at the default transaction level. Suppliers can see the rules that were specified by the buyer on the Customer Details page of their SAP Business Network account. Notification Event That Triggers Notification Method General Notification Options A transmission failure has occurred. If you request immediate notification, SAP Business Network sends an email to the email addresses you set, without awaiting multiple retries. Notifications tell whether you can resolve issues on the local system, and provide the date/time stamp, document type, payload ID, document business number, last technical status, classification and severity, exception information, and a link to the affected docu- ment. You can also request a daily summary of notifications and choose whether to include notification of transient failures. You can choose to receive notifications of supplier-initiated docu- ment transactions that failed. Online and email Order An order is undeliverable, a supplier has updated an order’s status, or a supplier has generated an order confirmation or a ship notice. If you request a notification when a supplier updates the status of an order, SAP Business Network sends an email to the order requester, not to the email address specified for the notification. You can also include all line item details from the status update in the notification. SAP Business Network also sends an email to the order requester when a supplier acknowledges the order. By default, this option is enabled. If you do not want the order requester to receive a notification when the order is acknowledged, clear the check box for “Send a notification to the requester on the order when the order status changes.” Online and email Service Sheet A supplier has sent a new or updated service sheet. Online and email Invoice An invoice has arrived or been updated by a supplier. If you subscribe to an invoice conversion service, you can also re- ceive notification when an unassigned invoice is waiting for you. An unassigned invoice is an invoice on which the supplier does not match any of the suppliers with which the buying organization has a trading relationship. For information about working with unassigned invoices, see the SAP Business Network guide to invoice conversion. Component Consumption Download and Upload via Excel Files Business Details This feature adds the Component Consumption job type to Upload/Download in SAP Business Network. Buyers and suppliers can create and run Component Consumption jobs to download prepopulated Excel files with component consumption data. Buyers can review the component consumption data in these downloaded Excel files. Suppliers can also review these downloaded Excel files and can additionally edit and add data to them and then upload them. This provides suppliers with the capability to process component consumption data in bulk.  Note A supplier can upload up to 600 rows per Excel file. If a supplier tries to upload a file with more than 600 rows, the upload fails and an error message displays. The supplier can edit the Excel file and add data to it based on individual needs, and then upload the Excel file to report component consumption in bulk. Restrictions A supplier can upload up to 600 rows per Excel file. If a supplier tries to upload a file with more than 600 rows, the upload fails and an error message displays. Component Consumption Template Criteria The Upload/Download Jobs page provides the following search criteria for the Component Consumption job type: • Name – (Required) The name to give the job. • Type – (Required) Choose Component Consumption. • Customer (Required, supplier view only) or Supplier (Required, buyer view only) The name of the buyer (supplier view) or supplier (buyer view) whose data you want in the Excel file. • Order number – The ID of the purchase order. • Line-item level • Supplier part number • Supplier batch • Buyer part number • Buyer batch • Component level • Supplier part number SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration PUBLIC 73 -- 3 of 10 -- • Supplier batch • Buyer part number • Buyer batch Editing the Component Consumption Excel File • The Item Serial Numbers column in the Component Consumption Excel file accepts multiple values, separated by pipe ( | ) characters. The multiple serial numbers are separated and assigned to the component consumption items. When there is a direct linkage of the serial number at the component level with the serial number at the line-item level, rows in the Excel file may need to be repeated for a specific line item with a single quantity to allow reference to related serial numbers for one or multiple components consumed for the line item. When rows are repeated in the Excel file, the Component Line Group column is used to clarify the assignment of the component serial number to specific line item serial numbers; this column is needed because the line item's serial number cannot be used to indicate this assignment. The value in the Component Line Group column is a number used once only for each upload. The following figure shows some example data. • The Item Schedule Line and Component Line Number columns in the the Component Consumption Excel file are read only. The values in these two columns are populated from the orders for informational purposes. These columns are not evaluated by SAP Business Network when the supplier uploads the Excel file. Uploading the Component Consumption Excel File • When the buyer enables certain component consumption transaction rules or sets the requiresRealTimeConsumption control key in the corresponding line item of the cXML file for the order, SAP Business Network performs additional validation during upload that may result in a validation failure. For example, if a buyer enables the Do not allow consumption to exceed balance quantity in component inventory rule, an uploaded Component Consumption Excel file fails validation if its entries do not all meet this rule. • After a supplier uploads a Component Consumption Excel file, its entry on the Upload/Download Uploads page shows one of the following statuses: • Completed – The upload processed without any errors. • Completed with Errors – The upload contained errors. The rows without errors were processed. • Failed – All rows had errors. The entry also displays a link to a log file that reports the upload status for successful and failed rows. • When a supplier uploads a Component Consumption Excel file, if there are any empty Consumption ID fields, a unique ID is autogenerated, and the empty Consumption ID fields are filled with this unique ID. The autogeneration of the unique ID occurs in the backend system. The unique ID is not added to the Excel file. 74 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration -- 4 of 10 -- Related Information Creating an Upload/Download Job [page 266] Running an Upload/Download Job and Making Data Changes to Upload [page 267] Deleting Download Files Created by an Upload/Download Job [page 269] Order Change Request Rules Buyer administrators enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain can configure additional transaction rules for order change requests. The following order change request rules are available for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyers on the Administration Configuration Default Transaction Rules page, in the Order Change Requests Rules section. For additional transaction rules available to all SAP Business Network buyers, see Default Transaction Rules in the SAP Business Network buyer administration guide. • Allow suppliers to respond to a change request with a different quantity than the buyer proposed. When this rule is checked, suppliers can propose another quantity when they respond to a change request from a buyer for a purchase-order schedule line. Suppliers can request a different quantity only once per change request. • Allow suppliers to respond to a change request with a different delivery date than the buyer proposed. When this rule is checked, suppliers can propose another delivery date when they respond to a change request from a buyer for a purchase-order schedule line. Suppliers can request a different delivery date only once per change request. • Allow suppliers to request an additional cost when responding to a buyer request to change a schedule line. When this rule is checked, suppliers can request an additional charge for accepting a buyer's requested change to a purchase-order schedule line. Suppliers can request an additional charge only when the buyer has proposed a different quantity or delivery date. The supplier can split the response created by a change request. The supplier can send up to 2 responses corresponding to a change request. The split allows the supplier to propose 2 different dates when the deliveries can be made. The supplier can enter any one of the following values: • Supplier proposed delivery quantity • Estimated cost • A newly split change request can be deleted using the Delete action. When the user selects the split action for a change request, a new row is introduced below the selected change request which is being split. The Split action is available under the Actions column for each change request.The supplier can enter the following information for both the response lines (main and the split lines) • Supplier proposed delivery date • Supplier proposed delivery quantity • Estimated cost • Comment The only way to uniquely identify a parent and its split line or child is by entering 'one' and 'two'. If the change request is not split, there is empty data for it. If any change request has been split, the parent is shown using SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration PUBLIC 75 -- 5 of 10 -- 'one' and the split using 'two'. There is a dedicated column for it called the Change request response line number which is also present in the Excel file the is uploaded by the supplier. To simulate a 'split' on the Excel file, the supplier will have to enter value in that column as 'one' and 'two'. Order Confirmation and Ship Notice Rules Buyers enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain can configure these transaction rules for order confirmation. The following order confirmation rules are available for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyers on the Administration Configuration Default Transaction Rules page, in the Order Confirmation and Ship Notice Rules section. For additional transaction rules available to all SAP Business Network buyers, see Default Transaction Rules in the SAP Business Network buyer administration guide.  Note Estimated shipping and delivery dates are attributes of the cXML itemOut element. Therefore, any estimated shipping and delivery date, even when defined at the header level, is applied at the line-item level without consideration of any transaction rules that prevent suppliers from editing line items. To prevent suppliers from editing estimated shipping and delivery dates, you must request a customization project to hide the Est. Shipping Date and Est. Delivery Date fields in order confirmations. Rule Default Setting Description Require suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders at the schedule line-item level. No This rule is available only when the following two rules are also checked: • Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders. • Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders at the line item level. (This rule is visible only when the rule before it's enabled.) When this rule is checked: • Every supplier confirmation must reference a specific schedule line. • Suppliers can't use the following methods to upload mass order confirmations: • From the … Upload/Download Uploads page, an Order Confirmation Excel file. • From … Order Confirmation , in the CSV Upload sec- tion, a CSV file that is missing any schedule-line information. Suppliers can still upload a CSV file with complete schedule-line information. 76 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration -- 6 of 10 -- Rule Default Setting Description Validate tolerance for quantity, delivery date, or both at the schedule- line level. No This rule is available only when Require suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders at the schedule line-item level is checked. This rule has two validation options. You can set one or both options: • Quantity tolerance – Set this tolerance value with order confirma- tion control key QuantityTolerance or by enabling the rule Apply line item quantity tolerance to order confirmations. • Date tolerance – Set this tolerance value with order confirmation control key TimeTolerance or by enabling the rule Apply line item delivery date tolerance to order confirmations. For further information, see Calculation of Quantity Tolerance Compli- ance and Tolerance Hierarchy for Quantity, Delivery Date, and Unit Price. Allow suppliers to edit components in order confirmations. When this rule is checked, suppliers can edit subcontracting component assignments and batch information as part of the order confirmation process. Otherwise, suppliers can't edit subcontracting components on order confirmations. Allow suppliers to send a ship notice for a material in an open quality notification with no purchase order reference, only after the quality notification is closed or the buyer has accepted the quality inspection for the purchase order. No This rule only applies to quality notifications without a purchase order reference. When enabled, suppliers must resolve the defect for a material (Customer part no.) referenced in an open quality notification before they can create a ship notice for a purchase order that contains the material. Suppliers can create a ship notice only when the quality notification for the material is closed or when the buyer accepts a quality inspection for the purchase order. This rule must be set to apply to buyers, suppliers, or both. Allow suppliers to edit estimated shipping dates, delivery dates, and quantities on the Items to Confirm tab. This rule allows buyers to permit suppliers to edit the estimated shipping and estimated delivery dates, and quantity, for line items when creating an order confirmation on the Items to Confirm tab.  Note This rule, whether enabled or disabled, doesn’t affect suppliers' abil- ity to edit estimated shipping and delivery dates when confirming orders in the SAP Business Network mobile app or when confirming entire orders at the header level. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration PUBLIC 77 -- 7 of 10 -- Rule Default Setting Description Allow check for estimated shipping or delivery dates in the past when order confirmations are submitted. Yes This rule allows buyers to control whether suppliers can submit order confirmations with estimated shipping or delivery dates that are in the past. The order confirmation can be for a scheduling agreement or a scheduling agreement release. When the rule is checked, SAP Business Network validates the estimated shipping and delivery dates on order confirmations when the order con- firmation is created. By default, if either date is in the past, an error is triggered.  Note This rule isn't enforced for unplanned lean service items or material items in an order confirmation. When the rule is unchecked, SAP Business Network doesn't validate these dates, so a supplier can submit an order confirmation with an estimated shipping or estimated delivery date that is in the past. Allow suppliers to send order confirmations on line item level. Yes This rule allows buyers to enable or disable the visibility to suppliers of purchase order line items in the Items to Confirm table. This rule is checked by default. When this rule is unchecked, purchase orders between the buyer and the supplier remain visible, but not actionable, in the supplier's Items to Confirm table. Allow suppliers to send order confirmations to this account. Yes This rule is checked by default. When this rule is unchecked, no purchase orders from this buyer are visible in supplier Items to Confirm tables. 78 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration -- 8 of 10 -- Rule Default Setting Description Allow suppliers to send order confirmations that do not comply with defined tolerances and require buyer approval. No This rule only applies to purchase orders. When this rule is checked, suppliers can send order confirmations with line items that are out of quantity, delivery date, or price tolerance. Such line items are updated with a status of Awaiting Approval. The quantity, delivery date, or price deviation from the order must be approved or rejected by the buyer.  Restriction This rule applies only to material items. This rule doesn't apply to purchase orders that are excluded from the deviation approval process in the cXML (<Extrinsic name="OCDeviationApproval">notAllowed</ Extrinsic>). This rule isn't enforced for unplanned material items in an order confirmation. This rule has two levels of deviation approval for order confirmations: • Single-level deviation approval – Provides a single level of approval. Customers approve deviations directly in the buyer portal. Default setting. • Multilevel deviation approval – Provides multiple levels of approval. Customers approve deviations first in the buyer portal, then in the customer’s back-end ERP system. When enabled, this rule shows the following checkboxes, which set ex- ceptions to the rule for their individual deviation types. If a supplier enters a value that is outside the permitted tolerance for an excepted deviation type, a message displays to indicate an error.  Caution A buyer who wants to set an exception to any deviation type needs to first reject from all partially confirmed orders any existing deviations of that type. This task prevents possible unexpected behavior that can be caused by conflicts after you set an exception rule. • Except quantity deviations – When checked, the rule isn't applied to quantity deviations in an order confirmation. • Except delivery date deviations – When checked, the rule isn't ap- plied to delivery-date deviations in an order confirmation. • Except price deviations – When checked, the rule isn't applied to unit-price deviations in an order confirmation. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration PUBLIC 79 -- 9 of 10 -- Rule Default Setting Description Allowed actions for order confirmation deviation approval. No When this rule is checked, you can configure the available deviation ap- proval actions to Approve, Approve and update, or both. By default, both actions are checked. The actions apply for both single-level and multilevel deviation approvals. If only Approve is checked, for a single-level deviation approval of a price deviation, the new supplier-proposed price can't be updated in the buy- er's back-end system, because price information can't be updated in the Confirmations tab.  Note • The Approve and Approve and update actions apply only to purchase orders. The actions don't apply to scheduling agree- ments or scheduling agreement releases. • When you configure multilevel deviation approval, the Approve and update action is checked by default, and you can't uncheck it. Allow suppliers to send ship notices only after receiving acceptance of inspection results. No When this rule is checked, suppliers can’t send ship notices for goods that require inspection, unless the buyer has accepted the inspection results. Otherwise, suppliers can send ship notices for goods that require inspection without receiving acceptance of inspection results. Require the quantity of a component receipt item to not exceed the component ship notice quantity. No When this rule is checked, a component receipt must report item quanti- ties that are equal to or less than the item quantities in the component ship notice. This rule excludes from a component receipt all flipped items that are already received, and shows an error message.  Note For this functionality, you need to set the frequency that your ERP system sends goods receipts to SAP Business Network to the short- est interval that is feasible for your organization. For example, you can choose to set your ERP to send goods receipts every 15 minutes. This ERP setting ensures that SAP Business Network can update a component ship notice to Partially received or Received in close to real time. SAP Business Network depends on these statuses to help determine whether a new component goods receipt would be a duplicate. 80 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SupplyChainCollaboratio.content: Rule Default Setting Description Require the quantity of a component receipt item to not exceed the multitier ship notice quantity. No When this rule is checked, a component receipt must report item quanti- ties that are equal to or less than the item quantities in the multitier ship notice. When Allow suppliers to create a component receipt for multiple multi-tier ship notices is also checked, this rule excludes from a com- ponent receipt all flipped items that are already received, and shows an error message.  Note For this functionality, you need to set the frequency that your ERP system sends goods receipts to SAP Business Network to the short- est interval that is feasible for your organization. For example, you can choose to set your ERP to send goods receipts every 15 minutes. This ERP setting ensures that SAP Business Network can update a component ship notice to Partially received or Received in close to real time. SAP Business Network depends on these statuses to help determine whether a new component goods receipt would be a duplicate. Do not allow suppliers to create a ship notice for order lines that have a change request. When this rule is checked, if a purchase order line item or schedule line has a change request, suppliers can't use the Orders Orders and Releases Items to Ship page to create a ship notice for that line item or schedule line. However, the supplier can still use other methods to create a ship notice for that item or schedule line, such as by using cXML or a spreadsheet upload. Order Confirmation, Ship Notice, and Component Receipt Attachment Rules Buyers enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain can configure these transaction rules for attachments in order confirmations, ship notices, and component receipts. The following attachment rules are available for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyers on the Administration Configuration Default Transaction Rules page, in the Order Confirmation, Ship Notice, and Component Receipt Attachment Rules section. For additional transaction rules available to all SAP Business Network buyers, see Default Transaction Rules in the SAP Business Network buyer administration guide. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration PUBLIC 81 -- 1 of 10 -- Rule Default Setting Description Allow suppliers to include attachments with component receipts Disabled Check this rule to allow suppliers to attach files to component receipts. Require suppliers to provide a quality certificate on ship notices Disabled When this rule is checked, suppliers must attach required quality certifi- cates to a ship notice. Purchase Order Rules Buyer administrators enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain can configure an additional transaction rule for purchase orders. The following purchase order rule is available for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyers on the Administration Configuration Default Transaction Rules page, in the Purchase Order Rules section. For additional transaction rules available to all SAP Business Network buyers, see Default Transaction Rules in the SAP Business Network buyer administration guide. • Override supplier's routing method for orders that match buyer's conditions If this rule is checked, the supplier’s default routing method is overridden for orders that match any of the specified conditions, thus preventing it from being routed to an external integration channel. Click Configure to specify one or more conditions. If an order matches any of the conditions, it is routed to the supplier on SAP Business Network. Quality Collaboration Rules Buyers enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain can configure transaction rules for quality collaboration. To use quality collaboration, buyers must be entitled for the quality collaboration component, and suppliers must have a trading relationship with a buyer entitled for the quality collaboration component. The following quality collaboration rules are available for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyers on the Administration Configuration Default Transaction Rules page in the Quality Collaboration section. For additional transaction rules available to all SAP Business Network buyers, see Default Transaction Rules in the SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide. 82 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration -- 2 of 10 -- Rule Default Setting Description Allow suppliers to create non-PO quality notifications in a multi-ERP environment No If this rule is checked, suppliers can create non-PO quality notifications and select which system they apply to when there are multiple routing end points. Otherwise, quality notifications are always sent to the default routing end point.  Note The buyer's account must be configured for multi-ERP support. Allow suppliers to send quality notifications for indirect orders without part numbers No If this rule is checked, suppliers can send quality notifications for line items without specifying a customer part number or customer location. This rule makes those two quality notification fields optional. Do not allow suppliers to send non- PO quality notifications No If this rule is checked, suppliers can only create quality notifications that reference an order. Otherwise, suppliers can create non-PO quality notifi- cations from the Quality tab. Activate DocuSign for quality inspection documents No If this rule is checked, suppliers must electronically sign quality inspec- tion results before submitting them. Currently DocuSign is the only sup- ported electronic signature provider. Scheduling Agreement Release Setup Rules Buyers enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain can configure these transaction rules for scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases. The following scheduling agreement and scheduling agreement release rules are available for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyers on the Administration Configuration Default Transaction Rules page, in the Scheduling Agreement Release Setup Rules section. For additional transaction rules available to all SAP Business Network buyers, see Default Transaction Rules in the SAP Business Network buyer administration guide. Rule Default Setting Description Allow scheduling agreement collaboration No When this rule is checked, the buyer can send scheduling agreement documents for collaboration with suppliers. And suppliers who are ena- bled for supply chain collaboration functionality can create ship notices from scheduling agreements. This rule is unchecked by default. Allow scheduling agreement release collaboration No When this rule is checked, the buyer can send scheduling agreement release documents for collaboration with suppliers. And suppliers who are enabled for supply chain collaboration functionality can create ship notices from scheduling agreement releases. This rule is unchecked by default. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration PUBLIC 83 -- 3 of 10 -- Rule Default Setting Description Allow suppliers to use only JIT for shipping This subrule is visible only when the Allow scheduling agreement release collaboration rule is checked. For suppliers that have both JIT (Just In Time) and Forecast release capability, make sure this rule is checked to restrict suppliers to using JIT for shipping. Allow suppliers to use only Forecast for shipping This subrule is visible only when the Allow scheduling agreement release collaboration rule is checked. For suppliers that have both JIT (Just In Time) and Forecast release capability, make sure this rule is checked to restrict suppliers to using Forecast for shipping. 84 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration -- 4 of 10 -- Rule Default Setting Description Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases No This rule can be enabled only when the Allow scheduling agreement collaboration rule, the Allow scheduling agreement release collaboration rule, or both, are checked. This rule also requires that the Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders at the line-item level rule is checked. When this rule is enabled, suppliers can confirm scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases. Suppliers can only confirm Firm schedule lines. Rules related to purchase order confirmation also apply to scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases. This rule provides the following subrule: Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases that do not comply with defined tolerances and require buyer approval. Values are Yes or No. When enabled, suppliers can send order confirma- tions that are out of tolerance for delivery date and/or quantity. Line item status is updated to Awaiting Approval, and the buyer must approve or reject the order confirmation. This subrule provides the following subrules: • Except quantity deviations. Values are Yes or No. When enabled, the rule is not applied to quan- tity deviations in an order confirmation for scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases. • Except delivery date deviations. Values are Yes or No. When enabled, the rule is not applied to de- livery-date deviations in an order confirmation for scheduling agree- ments and scheduling agreement releases.  Restriction SAP Business Network does not support order confirmations for scheduling agreements or scheduling agreement releases that are generated by using a release creation profile in the SAP ECC or SAP S/4HANA system. Schedule-line numbers in such order confirma- tions are incompatible with the SAP Business Network logic for re- taining a confirmation, which is based on the schedule-line number. When a supplier submits a changed order confirmation from SAP Business Network , the new order confirmation overwrites the previ- ous confirmation that was stored in the SAP ECC or SAP S/4HANA system. Retain schedule-line confirmations in a new version of a scheduling agreement or scheduling agreement release No When this rule is checked, confirmed schedule lines in a scheduling agreement or scheduling agreement release remain confirmed when a new version of the document is received. In the past, the retain logic was executed by default, but it is now controlled by this new rule. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration PUBLIC 85 -- 5 of 10 -- Ship Notice Rules Buyers enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain can configure these transaction rules for ship notices. The following ship notice rules are available for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyers on the Administration Configuration Default Transaction Rules page, in the Order Confirmation and Ship Notice Rules section. For additional transaction rules available to all SAP Business Network buyers, see Default Transaction Rules in the SAP Business Network buyer administration guide. Rule Default Setting Description Allow third-party suppliers to send multi-tier ship notices to this account When this rule is enabled, third-party suppliers can create ship notices for multitier orders. Require suppliers to close a quality notification for an item before they can create a ship notice for the complaint quantity If this rule is checked, suppliers must resolve a reported defect for an item and close the quality notification before they can create a ship notice to replace the complaint quantity for that item. Require suppliers to provide a unique asset serial number for each purchase order line item on a ship notice This rule applies within the scope of the order line item. Using the same serial number on any of the ship notice line items for this order line item is not allowed. If validation fails, the error message you receive is Asset serial numbers for item shipments must be unique. Require the total count of shipment serial numbers not to exceed the total quantity shipped for line items on ship notices Within a ship notice item, the number of serial numbers must be less than or equal to the quantity shipped. If validation fails the error message you receive is The total number of shipment serial numbers exceeds the quantity shipped for the line item. Require suppliers to provide asset serial numbers for the total shipped quantity of line items on ship notices This rule applies within the scope of the order line item. When this rule is checked, suppliers must provide an asset serial number for the total shipped quantity of line items. Require the Packing Slip ID to be unique on ship notices Duplicate shipment notice numbers (Packing Slip IDs) are not allowed. This rule is validated against all ship notice numbers for the particular supplier without time window restriction. If validation fails the error mes- sage you receive is This Packing Slip ID has already been used. Please enter a unique ID. Require ship notice type on ship notices When this rule is checked ship notices lacking a type are not allowed. For the type, the supplier must choose either actual or estimated. Allow suppliers to create invoice number automatically from Packing Slip ID when creating a ship notice When this rule is checked, it ensures that the Packing Slip ID value is copied to the Invoice # field automatically when a supplier is creating a ship notice. Require suppliers to provide a Global Individual Asset ID for line items on ship notices that conforms to the Serial Shipping Container Code (SSCC) format Requires that the asset IDs for line numbers on ship notices use the SSCC format used to identify logistics units, such as a case or pallet. The SSCC code is an 18-digit number, and the last digit is a check digit that ensures that the data is entered correctly. When this rule is checked, SAP Business Network uses the check digit algorithm to validate the number. For more information about SSCC, see http://www.gs1.org/ . Require suppliers to provide a unique Global Individual Asset ID for line items on ship notices Requires that when suppliers provide an asset ID for line items on ship notices, the ID must be unique for the customer-supplier relationship. It cannot be used on ship notices from other suppliers to that same customer. 86 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration -- 6 of 10 -- Rule Default Setting Description Allow suppliers to create a component receipt for multiple multi- tier ship notices When this rule is checked, suppliers can create a component receipt that references multiple multitier ship notices. Otherwise, each component receipt must reference only one multitier ship notice. Require all items in a ship notice to contain at least one consumed component When this rule is checked, suppliers must provide at least one consumed component in a ship notice. Setting Default Transaction Rules Use this procedure to set the business rules for submitted transaction documents. Prerequisites You have signed in to your SAP Business Network buyer account as an administrator or a buyer enabled for the Transaction Configuration permission. Context Buyer administrators enable or disable business rules by managing their profiles. Procedure 1. Go to Administration Configuration . 2. Choose Default Transaction Rules. 3. Check the boxes to enable any of the business rules in the Order Confirmation and Ship Notice Rules section. Uncheck the boxes to disable them. 4. Click Save. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration PUBLIC 87 -- 7 of 10 -- Setting Supplier Group Rules Use this procedure to set rules for a selected set of suppliers. Prerequisites You have signed in to your SAP Business Network buyer account as an administrator or a buyer with the Transaction Configuration permission. Context You can apply SAP Business Network business rules to specific groups of suppliers. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement > Supplier Groups. 2. Do one of the following: • To create a new group, choose Create and add group details. • To edit an existing group, select the group name. 3. Choose Supplier Group Transaction Rules. 4. Check Enter supplier group specific transaction rules and check the appropriate rule in the Order Confirmation and Ship Notice Rules section. 5. Choose OK to return to the Edit Supplier Group page, then choose OK on that page to save your supplier- group configuration. Configuring Quality Review Auto-Numbering Use this procedure to automatically assign custom numbering to quality reviews. Context When auto-numbering is configured, quality review numbers are auto-generated. 88 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration -- 8 of 10 -- Procedure 1. Choose Administration Configuration Document Number Preferences . 2. In the Quality Review section, click Create.  Note If you reach the maximum limit, a warning message displays. 3. On the Configure Numbering page, enter the desired numbering criteria and constraints and click OK. 4. Verify the configuration and click Save. 5. Click Edit to modify the desired numbering criteria, then click Save. Uploading Quality Notification Codes Use this procedure to upload the codes to be used in quality notifications. Context Quality notification codes define the metadata values used by your quality notification system. A buyer administrator must upload quality notification codes to populate the system with values that reflect your quality notification process. If you are integrating with an SAP ERP with Quality Notifications (QM-QN), upload the same quality notification codes used by your SAP ERP system. You can upload quality notification codes multiple times. Each upload replaces the previous codes. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Manage Vendors . 2. Click Upload > Quality Notification, Review Codes. The Upload Quality Notification and Review Codes page opens. 3. In the Description field, click Select and choose Notification codes from the dropdown. 4. Below the Upload button, click the Download latest template version link. 5. Save the template (a CSV file) to your computer. 6. Open the template file for editing. 7. Starting with the 6th row, add your quality notification code data in the following columns.  Caution The first 5 rows are headings and must not be edited. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration PUBLIC 89 -- 9 of 10 -- • Code Group – This field is optional if Code Type is Reason, Type, or Revision. • Code Group Description – This field is optional if Code Type is Reason, Type, or Revision. • Code Name – If this field contains data, the Quality Code Group, Quality Code Type, and System ID fields are ignored. • Code Description • Code Type – Valid values are: • Subject • Activity • Defect • Cause • Task • Reason • Type • Revision • Code Language • Quality Code Group • Quality Code Type • System ID • Quality Review Template 8. Save the CSV file. 9. On the Upload Quality Notification and Review Codes page, enter a name for the upload in the Name field. 10. In the Description field, click Select and choose Notification codes from the dropdown. 11. Click Browse, select the CSV file you saved, and click Open. 12. Click Upload. 13. In the Upload Status section, click Refresh Status to refresh the status of the upload. • If the Status is Done, the upload was successful. • If the Status is Error, there were errors in your file. Correct the errors in the file and upload it again. Related Information Example of Quality Notification Codes [page 91] 90 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration -- 10 of 10 --

SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network How to Guide for Suppliers About the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network PUBLIC 15 -- 5 of 10 -- The SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network also supports XRechnung format for invoices. The Peppol integration is currently supported for Germany, Belgium, Australia, and New Zealand. The feature has the following restrictions: • Only SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network administrators (Support, Lite Admin, and Full Admin) can view Peppol related transactions in the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. • Integration project configurations for Peppol transactions in the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network is not supported. PriceSheet Document Format for Price Sheet Catalogs [page 16] EDIFACT D98A Document Format [page 17] PriceSheet Document Format for Price Sheet Catalogs Starting release, SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network 2006, suppliers can send new price sheet catalogs in the PIDX document format for the oil and gas industry. SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network validates the PIDX price sheet catalogs and transforms them to the cXML document (CatalogUploadRequest) with the .cif catalog as an attachment. The .cif catalog format is based on the SAP Business Network catalog standards. On receiving the catalog, SAP Business Network validates the catalog and publishes it for customers. Then the buyer downloads and approves the catalog on their procurement system. SAP Business Network sends SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network an acknowledgment with the success or error response after receiving the catalogs.  Note The document type for PriceSheet on SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network appears as ProductCatalog. However, SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network sends the cXML document (CatalogUploadRequest) with the .CIF catalog as an attachment to SAP Business Network. Prerequisites You need the following to send the PIDX document format: • SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network • Ensure that you do the following: • Create a new project for SAP Business Network with the customer. • Set the connection with the following Transport Type: • Choose RNIF to send price sheet catalogs in the PIDX document format. • Set the URLs to connect to SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network and the trading partner. 16 PUBLIC SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network How to Guide for Suppliers About the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network -- 6 of 10 -- • Set the Document Format: • Choose PIDX to send price sheet catalogs in the PIDX document format. • Set the direction for the PIDX document format in the Mapping tab. • Ensure that you set the Document Type as PriceSheet to send the price sheet catalogs in the PIDX document format. • Ensure that the file size for the price sheet catalog does not exceed 10 MB. SAP Business Network does not support catalog attachments with file sizes exceeding 10 MB. • SAP Business Network • Ensure that as an account administrator, you have the necessary permissions to configure the EDI document routing on SAP Business Network. For more information, see the Configuring your Ariba Network account for EDI. • Configure the electronic routing in your SAP Business Network account to send the PIDX document format. For more information, see Configuring electronic order routing. EDIFACT D98A Document Format Suppliers can send new transaction documents through the EDI routing method in the EDIFACT D98A document format. This feature is available only to existing customers that have migrated from using the SAP Business Network EDI gateway to SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network release 2006. • If you are an existing customer that has migrated from using the SAP Business Network EDI gateway, you can send new transaction documents through the EDI routing method in the EDIFACT D98A document format. • If you are a customer using SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network with SAP Business Network, you cannot send transaction documents through the EDIFACT D98A document format. However, you can send the transaction documents using the existing EDI document formats. SAP Ariba supports the following document types and document formats for EDIFACT D98A: Document Type Document Format Order Request EDIFACT ORDERS D98A Confirmation Request EDIFACT ODRRSP D98A Ship Notice Request EDIFACT DESADV D98A Invoice Detail Request EDIFACT INVOIC D98A Status Update Request EDIFACT CONTRL D98A Status Update Request EDIFACT APERAK D98A Prerequisites You need the following to send the EDIFACT D98A document format: SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network How to Guide for Suppliers About the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network PUBLIC 17 -- 7 of 10 -- • SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network • Ensure that you do the following: • Create a new project for SAP Business Network with the customer. • Set the connection with the following Transport Type: • Choose AS2 to receive the EDIFACT D98A document format. • Set the URLs to connect to SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network and the trading partner. • Set the Document Format: • Choose AS2 to receive the EDIFACT D98A document format. • Set the direction for the EDIFACT D98A document formats in the Mapping tab. • SAP Business Network • Ensure that as an account administrator, you have the necessary permissions to configure the EDI document routing on SAP Business Network. For more information, see the Configuring your Ariba Network account for EDI. • Configure the electronic routing in your SAP Business Network account to send EDIFACT D98A document formats. For more information, see Configuring electronic order routing. Error Handling in the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Get to know how the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network does error handling and helps you configure your cloud integration project. Error Validation for Fields In case you miss to fill a required field or enter an incompatible value, the field will be highlighted in red when you are trying to save or activate a function. This validation is done for select boxes as well as free text fields. The gateway validates fields that require an entry in a specific format accordingly. An example is the URL within the project configuration which needs to have an https:// URL due to security reasons and you may not enter any other type of URL. 18 PUBLIC SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network How to Guide for Suppliers About the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network -- 8 of 10 -- Getting Started To connect to the Managed Gateway for Spend&Network for Supplier, you must have the following: • An active supplier account on SAP Business Network. For more information, see SAP Business Network Registration in Introduction to SAP Business Network. • A valid trading buyer-supplier relationship on SAP Business Network. For more information about configuring your SAP Business Network buyer account, go to SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide. • Configure your SAP Business Network account to send and receive transaction documents from Managed Gateway for Spend&Network for Supplier. • Configure your SAP Business Network account to send and receive EDI documents. For more information, see Configuring Document Routing. • Configure your system to support IETF Applicability Statement 2 (AS2) documents • Configure your digital certificates to use the HTTPS or AS2 transport. For more information about obtaining a digital certificate, see Obtaining a Digital Certificate in cXML Solutions Guide. file://SBN/split/aribaintegrationportal-.content: Accessing the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network You can access the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network from your SAP Business Network account or using the email inviting you to register on SAP Business Network. You need to set up the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network to access it. If you are a user who is newly added to the SAP Business Network account with permissions to access the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network, you receive an invitation to register on SAP Business Network. Enter your system information the first time you sign in to the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. The SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network stores the information you provide when you sign in. When you sign in again, the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network displays the Home page. You can edit the system information that you enter on the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network at Username Basic Data Edit . Related Information Adding Your ERP System Information [page 33] Configuring Your SAP Business Network Account to Access SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Suppliers using SAP Business Network can send and receive non-cXML transaction documents using the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. You need to set up the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network and also configure the routing method to send and receive non-cXML transaction documents from SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network to SAP Business Network. Supplier administrators need to assign roles and permissions for users to access the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. For more information about users, roles, and permissions, see SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide. SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network How to Guide for Suppliers Getting Started PUBLIC 21 -- 1 of 10 -- Related Information Signing In to the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network [page 22] Enabling the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network on SAP Business Network [page 23] Configuring the Routing Methods for Non-CXML Transaction Documents [page 24] Assigning User Permissions for the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network [page 25] Managing Authorization [page 52] Configuring Electronic Order Routing Signing In to the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network This procedure describes how to sign in to the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network. Context You can access the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network from your SAP Business Network account or using the email inviting you to register on SAP Business Network. You need to set up the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network to access it.  Note SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network displays an alert message to suppliers 30 days before the date of expiry of their certificate and enables them to update their certificate. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. In the right corner of the header bar, click the Account Settings icon and choose Settings Electronic Order Routing . 3. Click Configure SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network (non-native integration) . 4. If SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network routing is enabled, you will see a link to access the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and 22 PUBLIC SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network How to Guide for Suppliers Getting Started -- 2 of 10 -- SAP Business Network portal in the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network configuration screen. Click this to open the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network page. 5. Enter your ERP system information. You need to enter this information only the first time you sign in. 6. Click Save. Related Information All Procedures at a Glance [page 19] Enabling the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network on SAP Business Network Use this procedure to enable the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network on SAP Business Network. Context To send and receive non-cXML transaction document from the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network, you need to setup and enable the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network on SAP Business Network. You also need to configure your routing method to send and receive non-cXML transaction document from the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. In the right corner of the header bar, click the Account Settings icon and choose Settings Electronic Order Routing . 3. Click Configure SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network (non-native integration). 4. Check Enable Managed Gateway for Spend&Network. 5. Choose Save. A new link to access the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network appears. SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network How to Guide for Suppliers Getting Started PUBLIC 23 -- 3 of 10 -- 6. Click Close. Related Information Assigning User Permissions for the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network [page 25] All Procedures at a Glance [page 19] SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network routing based on data center location Configuring the Routing Methods for Non-CXML Transaction Documents You need to set up the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network before you configure the routing methods for non-cXML transaction documents using this procedure. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. In the right corner of the header bar, go to Account Settings Settings Network Settings and choose Electronic Order Routing . 3. On the Electronic Order Routing page, choose Managed Gateway for Spend&Network routing method from the dropdown menu in the Routing Method column. You need to specify the routing method for each of the transaction documents that you want to send in a non-cXML format. 4. Specify the corresponding configuration values in the Options column. 5. Choose Save and then Close. Related Information All Procedures at a Glance [page 19] 24 PUBLIC SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network How to Guide for Suppliers Getting Started -- 4 of 10 -- Assigning User Permissions for the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Use this procedure to assign user permissions for the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. Context Supplier administrators can assign predefined permissions to users accessing the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. You need to create a role and associate the required permissions for the role, before you can create users. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. In the right corner of the header bar, click the Account Settings icon and choose Settings Users . 3. On the Manage Roles page, click the Create Role icon  at the top right of the role results table. 4. Enter a distinctive name for the role. 5. (Optional) Enter a description for the role. Descriptions can be useful later, if you want to review or revise the structure of your roles. 6. Check the checkbox next to one or more of the following permissions for the new role. Each role must have at least one permission: • Managed Gateway for Spend&Network Configuration: Allows you to create, modify, and maintain projects on the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. • Managed Gateway for Spend&Network Access: Allows you to view and search for projects available on the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. 7. Click Save. Ariba creates the role and returns you to the Users page. 8. Click Create User to create a user for the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. For more information about SAP’s cloud platform, see SAP Cloud Platform. Using a cloud-based integration platform imposes dedicated security measures on the software vendor (SAP) that hosts the platform as well as on those (the customers) who use the platform. SAP processes customers' sensitive data and saves it on its own data center. Data centers are sensitive entities that are exposed to hazards on many fronts. SAP equips its data centers with security measures to protect customers' data from unauthorized access and hazards. For more information about the security aspects of SAP Cloud Platform, see Security in SAP Business Technology Platform. The SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network is currently hosted only in SAP’s Germany data center, St. Leon-Rot. For more information about the IP address range in the St. Leon-Rot data center, see the Regions, Hosts, and IP Ranges Available for the Neo Environment table in Regions and Hosts Available for the Neo Environment in SAP BTP, Neo Environment. A series of quality seals and certificates shows how compliant a given data center is with all the necessary security precautions. Every certification involves an inspection of certain parameters or criteria. Many certification organizations perform their inspections in accordance with various standards. Multiple auditing firms conduct audits based on national and international standards, such as ISO 27001, SOC 1 /SSAE 16 and SOC 2. The SAP data center is also audited according to these standards. Once the audit is successfully passed, the data centers receive a certificate or attestation report verifying their compliance with the respective standard. SAP ensures that these certificates are valid at every data center where cloud solutions are run. For more information about SAP’s certificates, see Certificates . For more information about the certification of St. Leon- Rot, see the Certificate page. SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network How to Guide for Suppliers Getting Started PUBLIC 31 -- 1 of 10 -- Viewing the Home Page The Home page displays the following: Integration Projects Display the table of projects. Allows you to create or edit a project. Gives you the opportunity to copy or delete a project. Tools Test Connectivity for testing your connection to SAP Business Network. Document Validator for testing your transaction documents. Transaction Tracker Track the transaction documents that you have sent and received. Download payloads and attachments.  Note If you are logged in to the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network portal from a test account, you can access only the transac- tions in the test environment. Only users logged in from their production account can view transactions on both test and production environments. In the top left corner of the application open the Navigation menu. From this menu you get access to the Home page from anywhere in the application. There, you also find the My Configurations, Resources, and the Test Central pages. My Configurations This is an overview page to have quick access to all configured projects, its connections, mappings, cross references, and authorizations. Resources This pages contains documentation and connection requirements. Test Central This page lists the available test scripts and also allows you to create custom test scripts. In case you need support with the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network, this information is helpful to connect you with the support team, which is best acquainted with your ERP system.
