Procedure 1. Click ..., and choose Deleted Transactions in the Document Archive section. The Deleted Transactions page appears. If files are available for download, they appear in separate tables for recurring deletion and one-time deletion. Figure 6: Deleted Transactions Page 2. To download a ZIP file, go to the Action column and click the  Download icon.  Tip You can filter the table of ZIP files to show files for which download has not yet started. Transaction Data Download The administrator for your SAP Business Network account and other users with appropriate permission can request to download your account's transaction data at any time for any period up to 90 days. If you would like to be notified by email when ZIP files are available to download, ask your administrator to set up notifications [page 34]. The following transaction documents can be downloaded: • Purchase orders (orders and blanket orders) • Order confirmations SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 91 -- 1 of 10 -- • Ship notices • Receipts • Service sheets • Invoices, credit memos, and debit memos • Payment documents • SAP Business Network for Supply Chain transaction documents • Notifications • Quote requests and quote messages SAP Business Network maintains transaction documents in cXML (Commerce eXtensible Markup Language) format, and you can download them in ZIP files. For more information about cXML, see the cXML Reference Guide at cXML.org . Downloading Transaction Data for SAP Business Network Suppliers [page 92] Downloading Transaction Data for SAP Business Network Suppliers You can download transaction documents from your SAP Business Network account at any time. Prerequisites • You need the Download Current Transactions permission to perform this task. • The age of a document is based on its creation date or the date of its last status update, whichever is later. • To receive an email notification when requested documents are ready for download, the administrator needs to set up notifications [page 34]. • After your download request is processed, you have 7 days to download ZIP files for the requested transaction documents. After that, the ZIP files are deleted. The original transaction documents are unaffected and remain on SAP Business Network. Procedure 1. Choose ... Current Transactions . The Current Transactions page appears. 2. Select a start date and an end date for transaction documents. The date range can be up to 90 days. 3. Click Request. 4. After your request is processed, you should receive an email notification informing you whether ZIP files are available for download. 5. If ZIP files are available, choose ... Current Transactions again. 92 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 2 of 10 -- 6. To download a ZIP file, go to the Action column and click the  Download icon.  Tip You can filter the table of ZIP files to show files for which download hasn't started yet. Analytics Data Export The administrator for your SAP Business Network account can request to export the analytics data from your account. Analytics data refer to your master data and transaction data (purchase orders, invoices, credit memos, and debit memos) used by SAP Business Network to provide analytics features such as the analytics dashboard. SAP Business Network exports analytics data in separate CSV (Comma-Separated Values) files, and you can download them. The data export and download won't affect the original data on SAP Business Network. Requesting Analytics Data Export for SAP Business Network Suppliers [page 93] Requesting Analytics Data Export for SAP Business Network Suppliers You can request to export your analytics data from your SAP Business Network account. Prerequisites • You are the administrator of your SAP Business Network account. • You know the ANID of your SAP Business Network account. • You have a secured email box for receiving encrypted email notifications when the requested data is ready for download. Context SAP Business Network uses part of your master data and transaction data (purchase orders, invoices, credit memos, and debit memos) to help you analyze your business activities in the analytics dashboard. If you want to export the data used in analytics, you can make a request. SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 93 -- 3 of 10 -- Procedure Create a case on component SBN-AN-ANL to request the analytics data export from your SAP Business Network account. Ensure to provide the ANID of your SAP Business Network account and a secured email box for receiving encrypted email notifications. For information on how to create a case, see Get Support Application Online Help . Results An SAP support representative verifies that you are the account administrator, then sends an encrypted email including a URL and a shared access key for downloading the requested data. You have 7 days to download the data. After that, the download package is deleted. The original data are unaffected and remain on SAP Business Network. API Management API management allows supplier organizations access to the SAP Ariba Developer Portal from within their SAP Business Network accounts. APIs for supplier organizations are published on the SAP Ariba Developer Portal. You can access the SAP Ariba Developer Portal and perform the configurations necessary to access, create, and authenticate API applications after you sign in to your SAP Business Network supplier account. You can: • use single sign-on (SSO) to access the SAP Ariba Developer Portal from the Account Settings page in SAP Business Network • access APIs that are created for use by supplier organizations • view details about APIs, including, but not limited to product documentation, runtime URLs, endpoint information, and swagger documentation For more information, see SAP Ariba APIs. Configuring Your API Client ID [page 95] Accessing the SAP Ariba Developer Portal from SAP Business Network [page 95] 94 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 4 of 10 -- Configuring Your API Client ID Use this procedure to configure your API client IDs in SAP Business Network. Context SAP Business Network is a calling application in the context of accessing supplier-oriented APIs from the SAP Ariba Developer Portal. Therefore, you must provide a client ID in the API Client ID Configuration section. The API client ID is required to enable the SAP Ariba Developer Portal to identify that this is a genuine and secure connection between SAP Business Network and the portal. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose Settings Account Registration . 2. Click the API Management tab. 3. In the API Client ID Configuration section, click Add. 4. Enter the Client ID. For more information, see Help for the SAP Ariba Developer Portal. 5. Click Add. 6. Click Save. Next Steps After you finish configuring your API client ID, click Close to return to your Home dashboard. Accessing the SAP Ariba Developer Portal from SAP Business Network Use this procedure to access the SAP Ariba Developer Portal from SAP Business Network. Prerequisites You must have the API Development Access permission to be able to view the section Ariba Developer Portal (Automatic Sign In) and to access the SAP Ariba Developer Portal. SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 95 -- 5 of 10 -- Context SAP Business Network allows supplier organizations access to the SAP Ariba Developer Portal from within SAP Business Network. If you have the API Development Access permission, you do not require any further sign-on credentials to access the SAP Ariba Developer Portal. Your sign-on session to SAP Business Network is sufficient.  Note Supplier users with administrator privileges have the API Development Access permission by default. The supplier administrator must first sign in to the SAP Ariba Developer Portal. The supplier organization is created in the SAP Ariba Developer Portal only after the supplier administrator signs in to the portal. Subsequently, supplier administrators can create users and selectively assign roles with the API Development Access permission. For more information, see Users and Roles [page 42]. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose Settings Account Registration . 2. Click the API Management tab. 3. In the Ariba Developer Portal (Automatic Sign In) section, click the link Developer Portal. 4. In the SAP Ariba APIs sign-in page, click SAP Business Network Supplier SSO. For more information, see Help for the SAP Ariba Developer Portal. Dun & Bradstreet Integration Dun & Bradstreet (D&B) integration allows you to synchronize your company information from the D&B database and auto-populate it into your company profile. The information that you can synchronize from D&B include: • Company name • Company address • Website URL • Company descriptions  Note To use this feature, your company must be registered with D&B and has a valid Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number. Even though entering the DUNS number is optional, we highly recommend you use the D&B integration to auto-populate the company information from D&B database. This would help maintain accurate and consistent user data across SAP Business Network. 96 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 6 of 10 -- Steps to Synchronize Company Information from D&B • If you don’t have a DUNS number on your profile: 1. Navigate to Account Settings Company Profile . 2. Click the pencil icon to the right of your company name to open the Edit Company Information page. 3. On Basic info tab, fill out the DUNS Number field. 4. If the entered DUNS number is already in use by another account, click Use a different DUNS number. 5. If you don’t know your DUNS number, click Find my DUNS number to search using your company name and address. 6. After you enter or select a DUNS number, the system checks your company name and address against D&B records: • If the details don’t match, you’ll be prompted to accept updates from D&B. • If you choose not to accept the updates, select Remove My DUNS Number to clear it from your profile. 7. Once you accept the updates, your company name and address fields are auto-populated with the information from D&B and become non-editable unless you remove your DUNS number. 8. Optionally, import additional updates (Website URL, Short Description, Long Description) from D&B to enrich your profile. • If you already have a valid DUNS number on your profile: • The system verifies whether your company name and address match D&B’s records. • If the details don’t match: 1. An alert appears on your profile’s Overview page. 2. Click Review and sync now in the alert to open the Edit Company Information page and update your details or DUNS number. 3. Follow steps 3 to 8 from the section above to synchronize your profile. • If you have an invalid DUNS number on your company profile: 1. An alert on the Overview page notifies you of the invalid DUNS number. 2. Click Update your DUNS number now in the alert to open the Edit Company Information page. 3. Follow steps 3 to 8 from the first section to correct your DUNS number and synchronize your profile with D&B. file://SBN/split/SBN Supplier Administra.content: Profile Setting Description Contact My Company The Do not allow buyers to contact my company using Trading Partner Search setting grants you the ability to de- cide whether potential buyers can directly send you messages through the Trading Partner Search results. This secure communication method ensures the confidential- ity of email addresses while monitoring all interactions in a central location. You receive an email notification when a new message arrives. The Allow other suppliers to contact my account administrator setting grants you with the ability to decide whether users who are in the process of registering an SAP Business Network profile can contact your administrator to request an account sign in. During registration, SAP Business Network performs an auto- mated search across all registered suppliers based on the company name, aliases, DUNS number, and tax ID to deter- mine if the registrant’s company is already registered. If SAP Business Network finds your company as a match and you choose this profile visibility option, the registrant can send an email message to your account administrator requesting a user name and password for their SAP Business Network account. Organizational Structure Viewing the organizational hierarchy of suppliers on SAP Business Network enhances visibility and understanding of supplier relationships and can be used to improve collaboration and decision-making with trading partners. You can view your organizational structure on SAP Business Network by navigating to Account Settings > Company Profile and choosing Organization Structure from the left pane. You can view your organizational hierarchy at the following three levels: • Parent organization • Linked child organizations • Additional addresses Clicking an element at the parent or child organization levels displays the following details: • Name of the organization • Address of the organization • Relationship count • SAP Business Network organization ID or BNOID • Account type SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 11 -- 1 of 10 -- Clicking an element at the additional address level displays the following details: • Name of the address • Address of the organization Editing Your Company profile Use this procedure to edit your Company Profile information and ensure that it’s complete and accurate to attract the most qualified customers. Prerequisites You must have the Company Information permission. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose Company Profile. 2. On the Company Profile page, click a pencil icon to edit the information in a section, and enter or revise values as necessary. 3. Click Save. 4. Click Close. How to Add Sustainability Ratings to Your Company Profile Add sustainability ratings to your Company Profile to increase trust and provide transparency on environmental, sustainability, and governance practices to buyers. Context You can now add third-party sustainability ratings in your SAP Business Network Company Profile to increase trust and provide transparency on your environmental, suistaintability, and governance practices to existing and prospective buyers. Buyers can search for and discover trading partners based on these ratings. 12 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 2 of 10 -- Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon and choose Company Profile. 2. In the Sustainability ratings section, click the edit icon. 3. Click Add sustainability rating. 4. Do one of the following: • Click Enter rating to manually enter sustainability rating information, then click Add. • Click Import from EcoVadis to import your sustainability rating directly from EcoVadis. 5. Optionally Browse for and Add an attachment to support your rating.  Note Attachments must be in PDF format and can't exceed 10 MB. 6. Click Done. Showing or Hiding Your Company Profile in Search Results If you want to prevent potential customers on SAP Business Network from finding your company through search, use this procedure to hide your Company Profile in search results. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose Company Profile. The Company Profile page appears. 2. Navigate to the upper right corner of the Company Profile page and choose the  Options button. The Options popover window appears. 3. Toggle the Show my profile in search results option as desired. SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 13 -- 3 of 10 -- Your changes are automatically saved. Adding Economic Activity Code (GIRO) to Your Company Profile Adding economic activity code to your profile is mandatory for Chilean suppliers. You can also view and change the selected economic activity code. When you select the applicable economic activity code, it appears in the GIRO field of your company profile. Field Description GIRO Code related to an activity that involves the production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services. For a list of official economic activity codes and their descriptions, see https://www.sii.cl/ayudas/ ayudas_por_servicios/1956-codigos-1959.html . Procedure Follow these steps to change your selected economic activity code. 1. Click the Account Settings icon and choose Company Profile. 2. Click view details link to view the GIRO description. 3. Click the edit icon to change your GIRO code. 4. Use the drag down option or the search filter to select the applicable GIRO code or description. 5. Click Save. 14 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 4 of 10 -- Showcasing Assessments on Your Company Profile On your SAP Business Network company profile, you can showcase completed assessments related to your products, services, and business practices. This enhances your credibility and makes it easier for buyers to access your assessment responses. To adjust these settings, go to Options Profile settings Profile Visibility and manage the Assessments section. If you choose to show the Assessments section and have shared the assessments with a buyer, they can directly access and view these assessments on your company profile. Even if you haven't shared assessments with a specific buyer, they can still request access to these assessments through the Assessments section on your company profile, irrespective of their current trading or sourcing relationship with you. For added convenience, if you've enabled the Auto share completed assessments with my buyers upon request setting, any assessment sharing requests from buyers with existing trading or sourcing relationships will be automatically handled. However, if a sharing request comes from a buyer without an established relationship, you'll need to manually grant access to your assessments. You'll receive both an in-app notification and an email notification when a buyer initiates an assessment sharing request from your company profile. This ensures you stay informed and can manage these requests promptly. Related Information Self-Assessment Questionnaire Certifications Certifications are essential credentials that highlight your company's expertise, credibility, and compliance with industry standards. Displaying them on your SAP Business Network profile helps demonstrate your commitment to quality and build trust with current and potential customers. SAP Business Network supports a wide range of certification types, including: • Supplier Diversity Certifications for businesses owned and operated by underrepresented groups. Categories include: • Small Business • Women-owned Business • Minority-owned Business • Veteran-owned Business • LGBT-Owned Business • Disability-Owned Business Each category includes specific certification programs. For example, Small Business certfications may include: • Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB) SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 15 -- 5 of 10 -- • 8(a) Business Development Program • HUBZone (Historically Underutilized Business Zone Program)  Note Supplier Diversity certifications are country-specific. Available options are filtered based on your company’s primary address. • Environmental Certifications for businesses that demonstrate environmentally responsible practices, such as reducing waste, conserving energy, and reducing pollution. • Energy Certifications that recognize efforts in energy efficiency and the use of renewable energy sources like solar and wind. • Social Enterprise Certifications for businesses committed to creating positive social or environmental impact in their communities. • Quality Certifications that reflect a commitment to quality management systems and continuous process improvement. • Security Certifications that demonstrate strong information security practices and effective risk management. • Other Certifications that do not fit into the above categories. Managing Certifications on Your Company Profile Adding certifications to your SAP Business Network profile help build trust and credibility with current and potential buyers. Certifications can also improve your visibility, as buyers can search for them when looking for new suppliers. Prerequisites You have the Company Information permission. If you're not an admin user, contact your account administrator to request access. Context You can add a wide range of certification types, including Supplier Diversity, Environmental, Energy, Social Enterprise, Quality, Security, and Other types. For descriptions about each certification type, see Certifications [page 15]. 16 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 6 of 10 -- Procedure Adding a Certification: 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Go to Account Settings Company Profile . 3. Click the Certifications tab. 4. Click Add in the upper-right corner. 5. In the Add New Certification dialog box: • Select a certification from the predefined list. • If your certification isn’t listed, check My certification is not in the list, then enter the certification name and choose the appropriate certification type. • Click Browse to upload your certification document. • Accepted file formats: .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .pdf • Maximum file size: 10 MB 6. Fill in the required certification details: • Effective Date • Expiration Date • Certification Number • Certified By • Certified Location • Additional Information (optional) 7. Click Add to save the certification.  Note Before adding a certification, ensure you have obtained it legitimately and have the right to display it publicly. Managing Existing Certifications 8. Once added, you can manage certifications from the Certifications list page: • Check the certification status: • Self-Reported indicates that the certification is supplier-reported and not verified by SAP Business Network or third parties. • An alert ( ) icon appears if a certification has expired. • Download a certification: Click the Download icon next to the document. • Edit, update, or remove a certification: Click the More options ( ) icon and choose: • Manage Details View and edit certification information. On the certification details page: • Click the Edit ( ) icon to update certification details. • Click Add New Version to upload a new recertified version. SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 17 -- 7 of 10 --  Note You can add up to two versions per certification. To add a new one after reaching the limit, you must delete an older version first. Showing multiple versions highlights your ongoing commitment to quality and helps strengthen buyer confidence. • Click the Delete ( ) icon to delete a specific version. • Click Delete Certification to remove all versions of the certification. • Add New Version Upload another version to show continued certification. • Delete Remove all versions of the certification. Responding to Certification Requests from Buyers Prerequisites To respond to certification requests from buyers, supplier users must have the Company Information permission to edit their company profiles. Context As a supplier, it is essential to promptly respond to certification requests from buyers. Doing so not only helps establish trust with buyers but also provides you with a competitive advantage within the marketplace. Procedure 1. Upon receiving a certification request notification through your SAP Business Network portal, click the Add option within the notification. If the requested certification is not already present in your profile, clicking Add in the notification will open the Add Certification dialog box. This dialog box allows you to input the details of the new certification you want to add. If the requested certification is already part of your profile, clicking Add in the notification will open the Add New Version dialog box. In this dialog box, you can add a new version to the existing certification. 2. Click Browse to add your certification file. Provide details about the certification, including Certification Number, Certified By, Certified Location, Effective Date, Expiration Date, and Additional Information. Once you've entered these details, click Add.  Note Currently, each certification is limited to a maximum of two versions. If you have reached the limit and want to add a new one, you have to delete an older one first. 18 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 8 of 10 -- Results The certification is now added to your profile and is visible to all visiting buyers. An in-app notification is sent to the requester to inform them of the update. Contacts Efficient communication is a cornerstone of successful business interactions, and maintaining accurate contact information is paramount to achieving this goal. Within SAP Business Network, the contact management feature empowers organizations to effectively manage both the main company contact and individual contacts. Main Company Contact: The Main Company Contact includes essential contact information for the company, specifically the general email, phone, and fax numbers. Each account has one main contact, defaulted to the information of the account creator (administrator), and you have the flexibility to edit and update this information as needed. Individual Company Contacts: In addition to the main company contact, you can create multiple individual contacts and assign them one or more roles, such as Sales Representative, Marketing Manager, or Technical Contact. Assigning a role designates the contact as a companywide contact, which is visible to all trading partners on SAP Business Network. If no role is assigned, the contact is considered private. You can later assign them to specific customers. Customer-Specific Contacts: SAP Business Network allows you to assign contacts to specific customers. These contacts are visible only to the designated customer and serve as the primary point of contact for them, improving personalized communication.  Note Your contact information will be available in supplier contact reports that buyers can download, visible on buyers' Supplier Enablement screens, and consumed by other SAP Ariba applications like SAP Ariba Buying, SAP Ariba Sourcing, and SAP Ariba Supplier Lifecycle and Performance. However, your trading partners won’t see it in your company profile. Editing the Main Contact The main company contact includes essential contact information for your company, specifically the general email address, phone number, and fax number. Prerequisites You have the Company Information permission. If you're not an admin user, contact your account administrator to request access. SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 19 -- 9 of 10 -- Context Each account has one main contact, which defaults to the information of the account creator (administrator). You can edit and update this information as needed. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Go to Account Settings Company Profile . 3. Select Contacts from the left navigation pane. 4. Click the Company Contact Information tab, and then click Edit in the upper-right corner of the page. 5. Update Email, Phone, and Fax of your company as needed. Related Information Contacts [page 19] Managing Companywide Contacts [page 20] Managing Customer-Specific Contacts [page 22] Managing Companywide Contacts Designating a contact as companywide makes their information accessible to both current and potential trading partners on SAP Business Network. Prerequisites You have the Company Information permission. If you're not an admin user, contact your account administrator to request access. Context Assigning individuals in your company as companywide contacts ensures your trading partners can easily reach the right people for various issues or inquiries. 20 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SBN Supplier Administra.content: Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Go to Account Settings Company Profile . 3. Select Contacts from the left navigation pane. 4. Scroll down to the Contact Personnel section and click Create in the upper-right corner of the Contact Personnel with Companywide Assignments table. 5. On the Create New Contact with Companywide Assignment page, provide the following details: Basic Information: • Contact Name (mandatory) • Email (mandatory) • Phone (mandatory) • Business Title • Fax • Company Assignment: Assigning a role here designates the contact as a companywide contact.  Note • If you assign a companywide role to the contact, their information will be visible to all trading partners on SAP Business Network. You can assign multiple roles to a contact, if necessary. • If no companywide role is assigned, the contact is considered private and will not be visible to trading partners. You can later assign them to a specific customer. Address Information: • Country/Region • State • City • Address Line 1 • Address Line 2 • Address Line 3 • Postal Code 6. After providing the necessary information, click Create to save the contact. 7. To edit a contact, click Edit in the upper right corner of the table. 8. To delete a contact, Click Delete in the upper right corner of the table. After a contact is deleted, all its assignments will be removed as well. Related Information Contacts [page 19] Managing Customer-Specific Contacts [page 22] SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 21 -- 1 of 10 -- Managing Customer-Specific Contacts Prerequisites • You have the Company Information permission to edit your company profile. If you're not an admin user, contact your account administrator to assign this permission to you. • The individual contact to be assigned to specific customers have been added to the Contact Personnel with Company Assignments table. For details, refer to Managing Companywide Contacts [page 20]. Context Assign individual contacts to specific customers to act as the main point of contact. This helps personalize communication and strengthens relationships. Note that contacts can only be assigned to customers with an existing trading relationship. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Go to Account Settings Company Profile . 3. Select Contacts from the left navigation pane. 4. Scroll down to the Customer-Specific Assignments section, select a customer from the table, and click Edit. 5. On the Edit Customer-Specific Assignment page, select personnel from the drop-down list to assign them as the specified contact for the selected customer, and then click Save.  Note Customers will only see their own customer-specific assignments, along with any companywide contacts you provide. Related Information Contacts [page 19] Managing Companywide Contacts [page 20] 22 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 2 of 10 -- Profile Data Federation This feature enables your company profile data to be replicated across SAP Business Network's global data centers, making your profile visible to trading partners in different regions. For more information, refer to How Profile Data Federation Works [page 23] and Enabling Profile Data Federation [page 23]. How Profile Data Federation Works Profile data federation replicates your company profile data across all global data centers of SAP Business Network, enabling trading partners in different regions to find and view your company profile, thereby facilitating potential business opportunities. To understand how profile data federation works, consider two trading partners located in different regions: • Trading Partner A is based in the United States (US) data center. • Trading Partner B is based in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) data center. For Trading Partner B to view Trading Partner A’s profile, Trading Partner A’s profile data must be replicated from the US data center to the KSA data center. To make this happen, Trading Partner A must enable profile data federation. For details about how to enable profile data federation, refer to Enabling Profile Data Federation [page 23]. Once enabled, an initial replication synchronizes your company profile data across all global data centers of SAP Business Network. Future updates are automatically synchronized to ensure your profile remains consistent and up to date across all data centers.  Note Profile data federation is only available to companies that are not sole proprietors. Enabling Profile Data Federation Profile data federation allows your company profile to be visible across all global data centers of SAP Business Network. This makes it possible for trading partners in different regions to find and view your company profile, facilitating potential business opportunities. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Company Information permission. See Permissions You Can Assign to Users [page 54]. SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 23 -- 3 of 10 -- Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Click the Account Settings icon and choose Company Profile. This opens the Company Profile page. 3. Click the Options menu in the upper-right corner of your profile and select Profile settings. 4. On the Profile Settings page, locate the section labeled Search Results Visibility: a. Optional: Toggle Show my profile in search results to allow your profile appear in search results. This setting determines whether your company profile is visible to trading partners in their search results. To enable global searchability, turn on this setting along with Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network. Currently, this setting is unavailable to buyers. b. Toggle Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network to enable profile data federation. This setting determines whether your profile data will be replicated to other data centers of SAP Business Network. For suppliers, this setting is enabled by default. Buyers need to enable it manually. Once enabled, this setting cannot be reversed. 5. Click Save to confirm your settings. Results • Your company profile will be replicated and visible across all data centers of SAP Business Network. • Future updates to your profile will be automatically synchronized globally. • If Show my profile in search results is enabled, your profile will also become searchable across all global regions. Company Profile Experience for Promote Suppliers with a promote subscription on SAP Business Network enjoy exclusive features that enhance their company profiles and foster trust with potential buyers: • Active Supplier Status Showcase your active platform engagement and readiness for new business opportunities. For more information, refer to Active Supplier Status [page 32]. • Verified Business Badge Confirm your company’s authenticity and legitimacy with trusted third-party partners. By becoming a verified supplier, you gain a competitive advantage over unverified businesses. For more information, refer to Business Verification [page 25]. • Marketing Collateral Promote your company by adding marketing materials such as customer presentations, case studies, and website links. For more information, refer to Marketing Collateral [page 32]. 24 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 4 of 10 -- Related Information Buying the Promote Subscription Business Verification Trust is the foundation of successful business relationships. SAP Business Network is dedicated to creating a secure and reliable platform for suppliers and buyers. To mitigate risks associated with unverified businesses, we’ve introduced the Business Verification feature, designed to foster trustworthy, long-lasting partnerships within the network. Understanding Business Verification Business verification is a crucial process that confirms the authenticity and legitimacy of a supplier company. This process is typically carried out in collaboration with reputable third-party organizations, CDQ and Dun & Bradstreet , which specialize in validating business information. The Verification Process Once you submit the verification request: 1. We first verify your business details with CDQ. If your information matches their record, your business is verified. 2. If there is no match or discrepancies are found with CDQ, we check if you have provided a DUNS number. If available, we use it to verify your business details with Dun & Bradstreet. 3. Once your business is successfully verified through either CDQ or Dun & Bradstreet, a verification badge ( ) will be added to your profile. The business details verified include: • Company Name • Primary Address (Country, State, City, Address Line 1, and Postal Code) • Tax ID or VAT ID • DUNS Number (if Dun & Bradstreet is the verifier) Benefits of Verifying Your Business • Enhanced Credibility SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 25 -- 5 of 10 -- The verification badge demonstrates to prospective buyers that you are who you say you are on the world’s largest B2B network. This can give you a competitive edge over businesses that have not undergone the verification process. • Increased Visibility Verified businesses enjoy increased visibility in search results. • Stronger Trust Verification confirms the accuracy of your business details, reducing fraud risks and building trust with potential customers. Qualifying for Business Verification To qualify for business verification, ensure the following: • You have bought the promote subscription for your SAP Business Network supplier account. • If your organization has a parent-child hierarchy, you must be part of the parent organization, as only parent organizations can initiate business verification. The verification badge is granted exclusively to the parent organization. • You have the Company Information permission to edit your company profile. Only users with this permission can start the verification process. If you don't have this permission, contact your organization’s administrator to assign it to you. Verifying Your Business Maintaining an accurate, up-to-date, and verified profile can significantly enhance your credibility with potential buyers. Here’s a step-by-step guide to help you through the verification process: Prerequisites • Ensure you've bought the promote subscription for your SAP Business Network supplier account. • Ensure you're part of the parent organization if your organization has a parent-child hierarchy. • Ensure you have the Company Information permission to edit the company profile. Only users with this permission can initiate the verification process. Contact your organization’s administrator to assign the necessary permission if needed. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network supplier account. 2. Click the Account Settings icon and choose Company Profile. This opens the Company Profile page. 26 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 6 of 10 -- 3. Click Verify your business under the Promote suggestions section at the top of the Overview page. The system will check for any missing required or recommended information. If any details are missing, a popup will guide you to add the necessary information. 4. Add required and recommended information: Required information: • Number of Employees • Year Founded • Revenue • Legal Form • Business Type Recommended information: • DUNS Number • Adding a DUNS number can increase your chances of successful verification. If your business cannot be verified through CDQ, the system will use the DUNS number for verification with Dun & Bradstreet. Without a DUNS number, Dun & Bradstreet verification will not be attempted. • If you don't know your DUNS number, click Find my DUNS number and use the Lookup DUNS Number service to search based on your company name and address. • If your existing company name and address don't match the records in the D&B database for the DUNS number you’re adding, you need to accept the updates from D&B. Upon acceptance, your company name and address will automatically update to match the D&B records and will become non-editable unless you clear your DUNS number. • In addition to the mandatory updates, you can also import other optional updates such as Website URL and Short Description from D&B to enrich your profile data. 5. Confirm your business details: • Company Name • Primary Address • DUNS Number (if available) 6. Add and confirm your tax information. If you already have a tax ID or VAT ID, double-check to confirm it's correct. Your tax information is used solely for verification and will not be publicly displayed or shared. 7. Click Verify to submit your verification request. Verification Process 1. SAP Business Network verifies your details with CDQ. 2. If CDQ cannot verify, and you’ve provided a DUNS number, verification proceeds with Dun & Bradstreet. Verification Result • Success SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 27 -- 7 of 10 -- • A blue checkmark badge ( ) is displayed against your company name on your profile. • This badge will also appear in search results and SAP applications, like Guided Sourcing. Buyers can search for trading partners by verified status. • Failure Handling Click View Verification Summary on the result page to check the failure cause. To reinitiate the verification process, follow steps in Reverifying Your Business After Verification Failure [page 28]. • Notifications: • You'll receive an in-app notification regarding your verification result. Click the bell icon in the top-right corner of the SAP Business Network portal to view it. • Disclaimer SAP does not verify the accuracy of Third-Party Verification Information and is not responsible for any losses, direct or indirect, that may arise from it. Reverifying Your Business After Verification Failure If your business fails third-party verification, you can reinitiate the process to ensure successful verification. The verification badge boosts your visibility in search rankings, builds trust with buyers, and helps you stand out among competitors. Procedure 1. On the verification result page, click View Verification Summary to access the summary page of your verification. • If the result page is closed, go to your Company Profile and click Verify your business under the Promote suggestions section at the top of the Overview page. This will also open the summary page of your last verification. 2. On the Verification Summary page, review the failure cause and click Edit and Resubmit to return to the business information review page. 3. On the business information review page: 1. Update your tax information. 2. Click Company Profile in the error message strip to update your company name, address, or DUNS number.  Note If you have a DUNS number, we recommend adding it to your profile. This will enable verification with Dun & Bradstreet (D&B) if verification with CDQ is unsuccessful. 4. After resolving all inconsistencies, click Verify to resubmit your verification request. 28 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 8 of 10 -- Business Verification Troubleshooting Business verification issues can occur for various reasons. Below are common scenarios and guidance to resolve them: What Should I Do Upon Verification Failure? [page 29] Why Do I Lose My Verification Badge? [page 31] What Should I Do Upon Verification Failure? Verification through third-party services may fail for various reasons. Below are common causes and the steps you can take to address them: Common Reasons for Verification Failure: • Incomplete or Incorrect Data: The data you provided is incomplete or incorrect, or the reference data has discrepancies due to outdated or incorrect official records. • Data Not Found: The provided identifier is invalid, does not match the business, or is from a country or type not yet supported by the verification service. • Network or Server Error: Temporary technical issues may prevent the verification process from completing. Actions to Take: 1. Review and correct your submitted data. Ensure that the following fields are correct: • Company Name: Make sure it matches the official name on your business registration. • Primary Address: Verify that all address fields are accurate and complete. • VAT or Tax ID: Double-check that your VAT or tax identifiers are valid and match the format required by the system. 2. Cross-check your data with official records. The official data sources that CDQ replies on include: • Business Registers: for example, Companies House (UK), Handelsregister (Germany) • VAT Databases: for example, VIES (EU VAT Information Exchange System) • Tax Authorities: for example, IRS (USA), CRA (Canada) Before resubmitting, refer to your local business register, VAT database, or tax authorities. Make sure the details on your SAP Business Network profile exactly match those found in these official sources. This can include checking any identifiers, registration numbers, or business names that are critical to the verification process. 3. Contact your local authority. If there are any errors in the official records, reach out to your local business registry or tax authority for help. 4. Submit a new verification request. Once you’ve reviewed and corrected any discrepancies, you can resubmit your verification request. Make sure that all the information is up to date and accurate to increase the chances of success. For detailed instructions on resubmitting your verification request, refer to Reverifying Your Business After Verification Failure [page 28]. 5. Escalate the issue. SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 29 -- 9 of 10 -- If your verification continues to fail despite your efforts to correct the data, or if you believe the failure is due to an issue with the verification process, you can escalate the issue to SAP Support. We'll work with the verification partner to investigate and improve the service if needed. Please provide: • The submitted (correct) data (Company Name, Address, and Identifier). • Any official reference sources (for example, business registry extracts) to assist in the investigation. • A brief explanation of the issue. Synthetic Examples for Escalation Cases to CDQ Example 1 Abbreviation Not Recognized • Submitted: Name: ABC Corp, Address: 123 Main St, London, WC2N 5DU, UK. • Reference: Name: ABC Corporation, Address: 123 Main Street, London, WC2N 5DU, UK. • Issue: The abbreviation “Corp” was not recognized as equivalent to “Corporation.” • Resolution: Escalate the case to CDQ to review the fuzzy comparison logic. Example 2 Missing or Incomplete Reference Data • Submitted: Name: XYZ GmbH, VAT Number: DE123456789, Address: Musterstr. 12, 10115, Berlin, Germany. • Reference: The business is not found in the current data source. • Issue: The reference source may not have up-to-date or complete records. • Resolution: Escalate the issue with the input data for analysis and, if needed, review the reference source’s coverage. Example 3 Regional Variations • Submitted: Name: ABC Ltd, Address: Flat 2, 10 Downing Street, London, UK. • Reference: Name: ABC Limited, Address: Flat 2, 10 Downing St, London, UK. • Issue: The matching algorithm fails to reconcile regional address formatting differences. • Resolution: Escalate the case for review and possible algorithm refinement. Example 4 Identifier Not Recognized • Submitted: Name: Tech Innovations Inc., Identifier: US TIN 123456789. • Reference: Name: ABC Limited, Address: Flat 2, 10 Downing St, London, UK. • Issue: The system does not support U.S. Taxpayer Identification Numbers (TIN). • Resolution: Escalate the case to assess expanding identifier support. Detailed Cases of Intended Verification Failure with CDQ 1. VAT Number Issues • Reason: • Invalid VAT number format or structure (for example, missing check digits). • VAT number not found in the database. • Example: A supplier submits VAT Number ESX12345678, which does not follow the correct format for Spain (2 letters + 8 digits). 30 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 10 of 10 --

Address Inconsistencies • Reason: • Missing critical address fields (for example, postal code, street name). • Significant mismatches in address details between the input and reference. • Example: Input address is “Main Road, Berlin, Germany”, but the reference requires the house number and postal code (for example, “123 Main Road, 10115, Berlin, Germany”). • Resolution: Provide a complete address, including postal code and house number. 3. Business Name Discrepancies • Reason: • Placeholder or dummy names (for example, “Unknown Supplier”). • Major differences between the submitted name and reference data. • Example: Submitted: Tech INNVOITASNO, Reference: Tech Innovators GmbH. • Resolution: Ensure that the official name match the business register. 4. Identifier Does Not Match Business • Reason: • The identifier belongs to a different business. • Example: VAT Number DE987654321 is submitted for “XYZ GmbH”, but the reference shows it belongs to “ABC GmbH”. • Resolution: Provide the correct identifier for your business. 5. Data Source Limitations • Reason: • The identifier is from a country or type not yet supported by the verification service. • Example: A supplier provides a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) from the USA, which is not yet supported. • Resolution: Escalate to CDQ if necessary. Why Do I Lose My Verification Badge? Your verification badge can be removed for the following reasons: • Updating Verified Business Information If you update any of the following verified business details, your badge will be removed: • Company name • Primary address (Country, State, City, Address Line 1, and Postal Code) • Tax ID or VAT ID For businesses verified with Dun & Bradstreet, changing or removing your DUNS number will also result in the loss of the verification badge. However, if your business is verified with CDQ, altering your DUNS number will not affect your badge. After making any updates to these details, you must go through the verification process again to regain your badge. SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 31 -- 1 of 10 -- • Expired Promote Subscription If your promote subscription expires and is not set to auto-renew, your badge will be removed. To restore it, you need to renew your subscription and reinitiate the verification process.  Note If your promote subscription is set to auto-renew, you will not lose your badge. To regain your verification badge, follow the steps outlined in Verifying Your Business [page 26] to reinitate the verification process. Active Supplier Status Suppliers who actively engage on SAP Business Network are awarded an icon on their company profile. This status boosts credibility with potential buyers and demonstrates readiness for new business opportunities. Eligibility Criteria To qualify for Active Supplier status, you must have the promote subscription for your SAP Business Network supplier account and meet at least one of the following requirements: • Complete at least one successful transaction (invoice or order) within the last three years. Only transactions within this timeframe are considered. • Maintain at least one active trading relationship. Status Activation and Maintenance • Activation The Active Supplier status is automatically activated when the eligibility criteria are met. The Active Supplier icon is prominently displayed under your company name on your profile, visible to the public. • Maintenance If you no longer meet the criteria, your status will change to Inactive Supplier. The Inactive Supplier icon is not visible to the public. To regain Active Supplier status, you must once again fulfill the eligibility requirements. • Notifications You receive both an in-app and email notifications once the Active Supplier status is activated. Marketing Collateral You can add marketing collateral, including customer presentations, company website, best practices, case studies, and more, in the form of attachments or external links, to your profile to promote your company and attract new business opportunities. The marketing collateral feature is now exclusive to SAP Business Network, promote subscribers. • For promote subscribers, you can add and manage marketing collateral on your company profile to enhance visibility and showcase your expertise. 32 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 2 of 10 -- • For non-promote users, you can only view or delete existing collateral. To continue using the full functionality, you will need to buy the SAP Business Network, promote subscription.  Note Existing marketing collateral will remain visible to buyers, even without a promote subscription. However, you’ll need to subscribe to the promote package in order to upload new assets or make changes to your current collateral. Notifications You specify which notifications you want receive in order to stay informed about different events and activities that affect your SAP Ariba account. You can use notifications to monitor catalog access activity, learn about matching business opportunities on SAP Business Network Discovery, and troubleshoot problems with your account. In-app notifications are categorized into three priority levels: Critical, High-Priority, and Normal. The goal is to offer a more streamlined and focused experience by prioritizing and visually distinguishing notifications based on their urgency. Critical: Urgent and crucial information demanding immediate attention is categorized as Critical. A popup on the homepage, along with a visual indicator  in both the overlay and Notification Center, emphasizes the urgency. Each user with permissions to take necessary actions is granted three sign in sessions to address the issue; failure to do so results in sign in blockage. Once the issue is addressed, normal sign in access resumes. Currently, the system issues only one type of critical notification: "Invalid Payment Method", which is triggered when the payment method is unspecified or invalid. High-Priority: Information of significant importance that requires prompt acknowledgment falls under High-Priority. A visual indicator  in the Notification Center highlights their significance. Normal: General information or updates that are important but not time-sensitive are classified as Normal. There are no specific visual indicators, but these notifications are conveniently visible in the Notification Center for review. Managing Your Notifications [page 34] Enabling Notifications of Changes to Purchase Orders [page 35] Types of Notifications [page 36] SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 33 -- 3 of 10 -- Managing Your Notifications Use this procedure to configure notifications for yourSAP Business Network account. Context By default, only the account administrator has permission to configure all notifications. Other users can configure notifications based on the permissions assigned to them [page 54]. When a user unsubscribes from an SAP Business Network notification or a general notification by clicking the Unsubscribe link in an email notification, SAP Business Network sends a notification to account administrators. The notification informs the administrators of the request to unsubscribe and provides the email address involved. An administrator then fulfills the request, removing the email address from the notification subscription. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose Settings Notifications . Notifications are grouped by solution type. For example, click Discovery to view SAP Business Network Discovery related notification settings. For a list of notifications, see Types of Notifications [page 36]. 2. Enter up to three email addresses, separated by commas, for each notification type you want to activate. For example: johnc@abccompany,natalies@abccompany,nelss@abccompany  Tip To send one notification type to more than three email addresses, create a distribution list in your email system and enter the name of that distribution list in the appropriate field on the Notifications page. 3. Check the box for each notification type you want to receive. If you want SAP Ariba to stop sending a notification type, uncheck the box. SAP Ariba retains your email addresses for your convenience but does not send notifications. 4. Click Save. SAP Ariba displays a confirmation message that your account settings have been successfully updated. 5. Click Close. 34 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 4 of 10 -- Enabling Notifications of Changes to Purchase Orders Use this procedure to enable email notifications of changes in existing purchase orders. Context You receive an email notification displaying up to three changed items in an order (line items and schedule lines) with all changed fields within them (unit price, unit of measure, delivery date, and so on), along with their original values. As this notification displays only a few changes to the order, you are prompted to sign in to SAP Business Network to see if more changes have been made. The email notification of the changed order may contain information about the following fields: • Header • Total amount • Item no. • Customer part no. • Item descriptions • Part no. • Delivery date • Quantity and UOM • Unit price • Schedule line no. • Delivery date • Quantity and UOM  Restriction Only the first three changed items of the updated order will appear in the notification email. Follow the steps below to enable notifications of changes to purchase orders. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose Settings Notifications . 2. Select the Network tab and go to the Electronic Order Routing section. 3. Check the Send notification to suppliers when purchase orders are changed checkbox. 4. Click Save. SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 35 -- 5 of 10 -- Types of Notifications There are four categories of email notifications: general, SAP Business Network, SAP Business Network Discovery, and SAP Ariba Sourcing and SAP Ariba Contracts. General Notifications Notification Type Event That Triggers Notification Customer A customer sends you a relationship request or confirms your registration on SAP Ariba. Trading Relationship Requests A customer has accepted your trading relationship request. Supplier Enablement Activity and Task Reminder A supplier enablement activity is assigned or a task is overdue.  Note This is applicable only for SAP Ariba supplier enablement services. Network Service No triggering event. SAP Business Network notifies customers about planned downtimes or unplanned network service interruptions. New Account A new account matches your email domain.  Note If the domain is non-specific, such as aol.com, SAP Business Network does not send a notification. Certification Expiration Notifica- tions SAP Ariba sends a notification when company certification information has expired. Examples of company certifications include, Small and Disadvantaged Business, Minority-Owned Busi- ness, and Veteran-Owned Business. Reminder of non-shipped order items Order items have not been shipped yet. The buyer specifies the number of days before the delivery date to trigger the reminder. Reminder of non-received order items Order items have not been received yet. The buyer specifies the number of days after the delivery date to trigger the reminder. Other Notifications SAP Ariba sends other important notifications that do not belong to any of the specified notification categories, to the email address specified here.  Note SAP Ariba sends all other important notifications to the email address you specify here. You cannot clear the check box to stop receiving these notifications. Password Reset Notifications SAP Ariba sends the specified email address an email when users reset their password. Subscription Email Notifications SAP Ariba notifies you when there is a problem processing your payment or when your service subscription nears expiration. 36 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 6 of 10 -- Network Notifications Electronic Order Routing Notification Type Event That Triggers Notification Order An order is undeliverable or a change order request is updated. Purchase Order Inquiry A purchase order inquiry is received or is undeliverable. Time Sheet A time sheet is undeliverable. Pending Queue Items delivered through the pending queue aren't acknowledged. Order Confirmation Failure An order confirmation failed to be delivered to the customer. Approval An approval document was received from the buyer for order confirmation deviations that were approved or rejected. Up to 20 items can be included in the email.  Note This notification type is available only for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain suppli- ers. Service Sheet Notification Type Event That Triggers Notification Service Sheet Failure A service sheet was undeliverable, failed, or was rejected by your customer’s ERP system. Service Sheet Status Change A service sheet’s status has changed. This notification does not apply to service sheets that were rejected in your customer’s ERP system; those events trigger a Service Sheet Failure notification. Electronic Invoice Routing Notification Type Event That Triggers Notification Invoice Failure An invoice is undeliverable. Invoice Status Change An invoice’s status has been changed. Invoice Created Automatically An invoice was created automatically on behalf of your company. SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 37 -- 7 of 10 -- Data Deletion Notifications Notification Type Event That Triggers Notification Data Identification and Deletion Transaction documents have been identified for deletion, or they have been deleted. Current Transaction Download Notification Type Event That Triggers Notification Current Transaction Download Requested transaction documents are ready for download. Ship Notice Ship notice status updates are also logged in the History tab of the ship notice details page. Notification Type Event That Triggers Notification Ship Notice Failure A ship notice is undeliverable. Ship Notice Declined A ship notice has been declined. Ship Notice Accepted With Changes A ship notice has been accepted with changes Receipt Notification type Event that triggers notification Receipt A customer sends you a receipt for goods that you have shipped. Broadcast Status Update Request Notification Type Event That Triggers Notification Broadcast A broadcast status update request is received. 38 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 8 of 10 -- Settlement Notification Type Event That Triggers Notification Payment Profile A remittance address or payment profile has changed. Payment Remittance One of the following: • Payment remittance is undeliverable or its status has been changed. • A payment remittance or payment plan has been received. Payment Remittance Status Up- dates One of the following: • Payment remittance status changes to Paid. • Payment remittance status changes to Failed. Customer Catalog Subscriptions Notification Type Event That Triggers Notification Catalog A customer subscribes to a publicly published customer catalog or sends status updates on catalogs, including catalog errors.  Note Only SAP Ariba Procurement solutions customers can send status updates to suppliers. Transport Notification Type Event That Triggers Notification Transport Request A new transport request was received.  Note This notification type is available only for suppliers with a logistics relationship with an SAP Business Network for Supply Chain customer. SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 39 -- 9 of 10 -- Logistics Copies Notification Type Event That Triggers Notification Copy Transport Request A new transport request related to your shipment was sent from the buyer to the logistics provider.  Note This notification type is available only for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain suppli- ers. Copy Transport Confirmation A new transport confirmation related to your shipment was sent from the logistics provider to the buyer.  Note This notification type is available only for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain suppli- ers. Accelerated Payments Notification Type Event That Triggers Notification Buyer-Initiated Early Payment Offers A customer sends you an early payment on a specific invoice.  Note Choosing Send a notification when your buyer initiates an early payment on a specific invoice. requires you to select the frequency of this notification: • Send instantly for each payment • Send a daily summary at a selected time in HH:MM format. If you have not set up such notifications, the Review early payment offer and Scheduled payment: {PPR ID} pages display the prompt To receive offers via email, set up email notification. If you have received more than 5 instant notifications in the last business day, the Review early payment offer and Scheduled payment: {PPR ID} pages display the prompt Set the daily summary to reduce the number of email notifications. Early Payment Offers A customer sends you an early payment request. Standing Early Payment Terms Offers A customer sends you a new standing early payment term. 40 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 10 of 10 --
