file://SBN/split/INT Integration Overvie.content: INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Integration for SAP Business Network -- 1 of 10 -- 2 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Introduction to SAP Business Network Integration: What is Trading Partner Integration? Integration is connecting a trading partner’s ERP to the SAP Business Network by an electronic method via a touchless process. While all of your transactions are submitted to the Network using our native language, cXML, your trading partner may choose to transact using cXML, EDI, or use other methods such as CSV, or using the Network Portal, also known as POFlip. Trading Partner ERP Customer ERP Purchase Orders Invoices Why integrate? When data is transferred from system to system, it is faster, more accurate (45- 60%), more repeatable, less expensive (60-75%), and improves both trading partner and buyer satisfaction. Who should integrate? It’s the trading partner’s choice! Transaction volume can be used to help prioritize but trading partners will confirm whether they wish to integrate a particular buyer relationship on the Network. The image to the left shows how the integration works, focusing on system to system, or B2B, transacting. -- 2 of 10 -- 3 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only How can Trading Partners Transact over the SAP Business Network? Manual Semi-Automated Automated data entry performed by trading partner some set up work required by buyer and trading partner set up work to configure system to system data transmission using the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway Network Portal CSV cXML EDI PIDX OAGIS • The manual conversion of using the Network User Interface to create a order confirmation, advanced ship notice, invoice, credit, or other document from an order, also known as “POFlip” • Comma Separated Value/Variable (CSV) file represents structured way of data stored as plain text file. CSV invoice upload supports the transfer, transformation and loading of comma delimited files representing a trading partner’s order confirmations, ship notices, invoices, and credits to be rendered as cXML invoices for their Customers. • The Commerce eXtensible Markup Language (cXML) is an open language defined by public Document Type Definitions (DTDs). These DTDs define cXML so that it is extremely flexible. It is the Network’s native language, created by SAP Ariba in 1999, intended for the communication of business documents between procurement applications, e- commerce hubs, and trading partners. Electronic data interchange (EDI) is the concept of businesses electronically communicating information that was traditionally communicated on paper, such as purchase orders and invoices. Technical standards for EDI exist to facilitate parties transacting such instruments without having to make special arrangements. • ANSI ASC X12 version 004010 American National Standards Institute Accredited Standards Committee X12 • UN EDIFACT version D96A with syntax version 3 and Syntax levels UNOC United Nations Electronic Data Interchange For Administration Commerce And Transport • Petroleum Industry Data eXchange (PIDX) provides a global forum for delivering the process, information and technology standards that facilitates seamless, efficient digital business within the oil and gas industry and its trading community. • Open Applications Group Integration Specification (OAGIS): OAGIS defines a common content model and common messages for communication between business applications. This includes application- to-application (A2A) and business-to-business (B2B) integration. -- 3 of 10 -- 4 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only What is the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway? The Gateway is the integration engine for the SAP Business Network. getting a trading partner ready for production activity. One resource does not fulfill the function of supporting the Integration workstream activities and deliverables. Remember, we’re trying to get this process to be as automated as possible, so we’re putting in the effort on the front end through testing for you to reap the benefits once you’re operating in production and in a business as usual state. In order to be most successful, carefully consider who you will have engaged to move this process both efficiently and effectively. • While SAP has a large number of resources available, we will scale up or down to best meet your needs. We will staff resources depending on criteria such as region, complexity of project scope, and number of targeted integrated trading partners. The integration management team determines the roles that will be staffed on a per project basis to best support the business outcome objectives. While you’re working through your Systems Integration Testing (SIT), we want to confirm that we have properly identified and understand the requirements for integrated trading partners, so they can be accurately documented. This process is critical in creating a system to best support your business outcome objectives. Testing with buyers Testing with trading partners We test with buyers to validate our understanding of the solution scope and the requirements for integrated trading partners. We test with trading partners to validate the trading partner’s mapping against buyer’s requirements. Integration testing is required. -- 3 of 10 -- 14 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Testing Key Takeaways and Considerations buyer and individual trading partner Who What When Where Why How Solutions Testing •• Buy Side integration resource with buyer resource involvement • Design and Realize Phases • Buyer’s Network TEST Environment • Validate the solution • Identify technical requirements that may be difficult for integrated trading partners to fulfill • Obtain verified samples to use in integrated documentation • Posting integrated documents to the Network Mapping Testing with Trading Partners • Facilitate an integration project using the established process • Explore Phase for initial connectivity testing • Realize Phase for completing test scripts • Buyer’s and Trading Partner’s Business Network TEST Environments • Validate the trading partner mapping to ensure buyer’s requirements are met • Identify technical requirements that may be difficult for specific integrated trading partners to fulfill • Status calls facilitated by Sell Side Integration resource with • Posting integrated documents to the Business Network • Sell Side integration resource with buyer resource involvement • Trading Partners • Buy Side integration resource acts as an integrated trading partner to perform test scripts for validating the solution scope -- 4 of 10 -- 15 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Timing during Project Implementation Prepare Explore & Realize Deploy & Run The work done to set up the integration workstream is in parallel with the overall project deployment and enablement. The integration resources will work with the customer and all of the SAP project team contacts to determine the appropriate roll out for each project. In the case where there are not adequate resources to support an integration workstream in parallel with a project implementation, the set up work prior to engaging trading partners should still take place in order to position the program for integrations in the future. The integration workstream milestones will overlap with the implementation and enablement project plans. Typical timelines for the pilot integration wave, once build is complete and stable includes 4 weeks of buy side work to perform solutions testing and creating the integration specifications for trading partners. After this work is completed, typical timelines for trading partners is 12 weeks. In many cases, the integrated pilot wave will have a later go live date than Portal/POFlip trading partners. -- 5 of 10 -- 16 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Keys to Success How can I have a successful integration program with my trading partners? • Remember that it’s a partnership between you, us, and your trading partner! • Follow our recommended best practices • Mitigate common challenges • Be engaged in meetings to discuss status through accurate and timely reporting • Collaborate with us in establishing project governance and escalation paths Follow Best Practices Mitigation Reporting & Meetings Project Governance -- 6 of 10 -- 17 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Keys to Success: Follow Best Practices Pilot Wave Future Waves During Implementation, you want to include a sampling of integrated trading partners (the “pilots”) by buying channel, business process, and transaction format (cXML, EDI, PIDX, etc.) to verify the requirements. For future waves of trading partners, you want to expand the proven process, best practices, and solution verification of the pilot to larger waves of trading partners. • Integrated Trading Partners • typically represent the bulk of your PO & Invoice transaction volumes. They are key to unlocking your adoption goals to attain business objectives. • require additional lead time to plan and staff their resources to support integration in time for your Go Live. • Have understanding on current business processes with the trading partner • Early business level discussions and engagement are needed to provide the integrated trading partner with visibility into: • Future state of business process • Alignment on scope of spend category, buying channel, business unit • Document choreography and SAP Business Network requirements • Procurement Content (catalogs, contracts) • Timing, Partnership, Expectations, and Alignment • Larger waves of integrations can be managed when adequate planning is conducted and lead time is provided to trading partners • Any new additional changes to Business Network requirements, is considered a change in scope therefore Implementation Team members may need to be re-engaged -- 7 of 10 -- 18 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Keys to Success: Mitigate Common Challenges Resources have day jobs… Resources can’t answer questions… The timeline is too short!
